# WASPNest VirtIO review status

Date: 2026-08-11

This is the durable handoff for the current VirtIO 1.4 and save-state
milestone.  It separates verified implementation from future roadmap work.
A commit is not treated as review evidence.

Updates to this handoff are made alongside the corresponding focused
validation result, so it remains useful after interrupted qualification runs.

Current totals and completion classifications are derived from the TSV
ledgers and summarized in `docs/waspnest-completion-matrix.md`.  All dated
sections below are immutable review snapshots; their historical counts must
not be read as the current inventory.

## Test-readiness replay (2026-08-09)

The pre-live readiness plan is recorded in
`docs/waspnest-test-readiness-plan.md`.  Its inventory pass completed with
238 VirtIO requirement rows, 129 live-activation rows, 110 VirtIO private
interface entries, 433 nested-VMX requirement rows, and 282 nested private
interface entries validated.  The ledger deliberately reports unresolved live
evidence rather than converting it into a pass: 83 Linux and 118 5BSD feature
rows still await their named privileged guest cases or retain an explicit
guest-driver gap.

The full rootless device harness then rebuilt all 98 targets under
AddressSanitizer and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer and published `PASS device
harness all tests passed`.  The full nested model rebuilt its paired
`libvmmapi`, production VMM module, and model suites under the same sanitizer
configuration and published `PASS nested-vmx cases=349`.  The snapshot
portability and runner self-tests, reference corpus validation, requirement
validators, and virtio-lab control-plane self-test also passed.  Plan-only
runs for `qualification`, `soak-smoke`, and `full-qualification` accepted
inert absolute paths without creating host resources.  Finally, `bhyve`
rebuilt with `-Werror`.

This closes one rootless **baseline replay**, not the privileged qualification
phase.  The Intel nested-VMX production entry-owner bridge is now linked and
rootless-validated, but remains disabled pending an all-edge source review and
real Intel L1/L2 qualification.  The activation ledger and qualification
handoff remain the source of the required Linux, rebuilt-5BSD, IOMMU,
checkpoint, soak, and Intel L1/L2 execution evidence.

## Implementation-gate audit (2026-08-09)

The current implementation-first milestone has one concrete production
runtime blocker rather than an implicit collection of test failures:

- 235 of 238 VirtIO requirement rows are host-model implemented and tested;
  the other three are explicit policy outcomes (two topology-inapplicable
  features and block secure erase, which is intentionally unadvertised).
- The separate activation ledger has 129 rows.  Its outstanding entries are
  explicitly classified as a named live case, a guest-driver gap, or a

- `vmx_startup_kernel_actions_ready()` and the public nested stage remain

  source-ordered private inverse and settlement transaction, but that is only

The full ASan/UBSan nested-model replay performed during this audit completed
with `PASS nested-vmx cases=349`.  The subsequent production-bridge replay
also rebuilt `vmm.ko` with `-Werror` and verified the linked owner-adapter
symbols plus the 433-row requirement validator.  These rootless results do not
make guest VMX exposure, kernel-managed startup actions, or Intel L1/L2
execution complete.  The required private inverses and live gates are recorded
in `docs/waspnest-feature-completion-backlog.md`.

## 2026-08-09 retry-environment record

### Focused sound and filesystem lifecycle replays

The source-level retry completed the focused VirtIO sound and filesystem
groups without requiring a privileged guest.  The sound group rebuilt under
`-Werror` and passed 51 ATF cases.  Those cases independently exercise
generation-fenced asynchronous completion, callback ownership while the
device lock is dropped, fragmented playback and capture, lifecycle ordering,
queue reset, guest suspend, backend identity binding, malformed chains, and
portable checkpoint restore.

The filesystem group rebuilt under `-Werror` and passed 88 ATF cases.  It
covers authenticated event-driven backend establishment, descriptor-passing
rejection, queue saturation, cancellation, selective reset, destruction while
requests are retained, freeze/thaw rollback, portable session and backend
state, and the PCI snapshot lock-transfer protocol.  These are rootless model
and device-model results only.  They do not claim production virtio-fs
daemon/export, Linux guest, or 5BSD guest qualification, all of which remain
explicit live gates.

### Focused balloon ownership replay

The balloon tracker and PCI model rebuilt with the current complete `bhyve`
binary under `-Werror`; its 24 focused ATF cases passed.  The replay covers
fragmented little-endian PFNs, duplicate-PFN idempotence, host-page-granule
transitions, tracker release rollback, accounting limits, statistics
retention, free-page hinting/reporting, malformed queue geometry, and repeated
snapshot validation.  The review confirms that host discard and undiscard are
best-effort reclamation hints: a failure cannot reverse the guest-visible
ownership transition after the status-less balloon request has completed.
That separation keeps the common lifecycle correct on hosts with different
memory-reclamation implementations.  Real guest memory-pressure, OOM, and
Linux/5BSD driver activation tests remain live qualification work.

The current non-root execution environment regained source-tree access, so
the IOMMU queue and prepared-restore boundary were rechecked directly.  The
review confirmed the intended distinction between an untrustworthy descriptor
parse (which latches `DEVICE_NEEDS_RESET`) and a known descriptor with an
invalid request shape (which is retired with zero used bytes and cannot be
retried forever).  The prepared-state publication remains validation-thread
scoped and is withdrawn before destruction.

### VirtIO-lab control-plane replay

`virtio-lab-selftest.sh` completed after the nested-source replay.  This
rootless control-plane suite covers the authenticated process-fingerprint

## 2026-08-09 discard live-verifier portability repair

The Linux block live verifier had treated a successful `BLKDISCARD` as proof
that a subsequent read must contain zero bytes.  That is a useful property of
the lab's sparse-file backend, but it is not a general VirtIO discard read
guarantee.  The verifier now proves the negotiated limit and successful
discard submission, then writes a deterministic zero range itself and verifies
the whole-device digest.  Its self-test explicitly fails if the discard helper
tries to inspect post-discard bytes.  This keeps the live test meaningful for
the request path and reboot persistence without rejecting conforming backends
whose deallocated read behavior differs.

`gblock.py --self-test`, the VirtIO lab self-test, the independent
requirements validator, and a source-matched `bhyve` build completed after the
correction.  The privileged Linux discard and reboot lanes remain required
release evidence.

## 2026-08-09 PCI VirtIO snapshot-registration replay

All 16 production PCI VirtIO models currently register the full checkpoint
framework triplet: save, validation, and destination-compatibility callbacks.
That was true by convention but was not previously enforced.  The requirements
audit now rejects a model missing any member of the triplet.  The orchestration
self-test removes the RNG model's validation registration in an isolated
source-tree overlay and proves that the audit refuses the resulting save-only
model.

This preserves the common validate-before-publication architecture as new
devices are added.  It does not imply that all device backends are live
migration-qualified; external-backend reconstruction and real guest
checkpoint cases remain independently tracked.

## 2026-08-09 packed-device activation allow-list replay

The packed-ring activation audit originally checked the known packed PCI
devices one by one, but it did not prove that the list was exhaustive.  A new
`pci_virtio_*.c` model could therefore have opted into `VIRTIO_F_RING_PACKED`
without a per-device release anchor or a Linux/5BSD qualification disposition.
The validator now scans every production VirtIO PCI source after checking the
allow-list and rejects any unledgered packed producer.

The orchestration self-test builds an isolated source-tree overlay with a
minimal extra packed producer and proves that validation fails with the
specific unledgered-producer diagnostic.  This is a ledger and promotion-gate
repair, not a claim that the newly enumerated packed features have live guest
coverage.  The current ledger contains 129 live feature claims; deferred
Linux and 5BSD packed lanes remain root-only qualification work.

## 2026-08-09 nested-VMX architectural-region boundary repair

VMXON and VMCS-region alignment had one remaining host-page dependency in
the production instruction runtime: it rejected a valid architectural
four-KiB VMCS region whenever the host page size differed from the Intel VMX
region size.  The region shift and size are now defined once in the
guest-visible nested-capability contract and used by capability construction,
registry hashing, and the runtime VMXON/VMCS operand check.  The runtime still
uses the host VM mapping API only to hold the four-byte revision field; host
mapping granularity is no longer used as a guest ABI rule.

The public capability header was also made independent of `UINT32_C` and now
includes its own non-kernel `bool` definition, so a standalone consumer or a
kernel translation unit can consume the contract without depending on an
incidental include order.  `vmm.ko` and the standalone architectural state
test rebuild with `-Werror`, and every public nested header now passes an
independent bare-translation-unit compile; the 72 headers which declare
`bool` additionally must include the shared nested-types contract.  The
aggregate rootless nested-model runner executes this header gate after its
requirements ledger and rejects a runner from which that invocation has been
removed.  The nested requirements validator passes, and two separate
rootless nested-model runs completed `PASS nested-vmx cases=349`.
This is source/model evidence only; the existing installed Intel L1/L2 gate
remains required for accelerated nested execution.

## 2026-08-09 VMX bitmap host-page boundary repair

The MSR bitmap buffers used to stage a prospective VMCS02 were still
allocated and cleared using the host `PAGE_SIZE`.  Intel defines these as
fixed 4 KiB bitmap regions; host page granularity is an allocator detail, not
the VMX contract.  Allocation and clearing now use the independently named
architectural MSR-bitmap size, while the host VMX mapping and VMCS allocation
paths retain their host-page requirements where those are genuinely local.

The requirements validator now rejects a host-page-sized MSR staging
allocation or clear in either the vCPU lifetime path or the VMCS02 resource
path.  This makes the distinction mechanically visible for future ports with
a different host base page.  It is Intel-private state and is neither
serialized nor exposed through the common VMM ABI.  Kernel compilation and
the rootless nested model remain the qualification for this change; live
Intel L1/L2 qualification remains separately required.

## 2026-08-09 filesystem teardown publication repair

The filesystem connection destructor drains retained requests through the
normal completion callback.  That callback feeds the PCI device's pressure
telemetry, which queries pending and outgoing queue state.  The queue pointer
was previously left published while the queue destructor ran, so a teardown
completion could follow storage which the destructor had already reclaimed.
The destructor now atomically withdraws the pointer from the connection before
draining it.  Completion-time pressure therefore reports zero after teardown
begins.  The independent connection test creates a retained FUSE request,
queries pressure from its destruction callback, and proves both values are
zero.  The private-interface ledger and source anchor bind this ordering to
the test.  Live virtio-fs export/reconnect and checkpoint qualification remain
root-only gates.

## 2026-08-09 IOMMU prepared-view and provisional-device replay

The VirtIO-IOMMU restore preflight publishes a private, immutable translation
view only to its coordinator thread.  Restore validation runs fabric devices
first, dependent endpoints second, and the matching cleanup loop last in one
serialized call stack before restore commit.  The published owner token is
withdrawn before the prepared state is destroyed, so another thread always
uses the live IOMMU state and the validation thread cannot dereference the
prepared view after cleanup.  The existing cross-thread PCI test exercises
exactly that visibility boundary.  No IOMMU lifecycle repair was required.

The independent IOMMU PCI fixture now also checks its public device ID,
configuration length and bypass-byte offset, every implemented device feature,
and the complete advertised feature mask against the pinned VirtIO 1.4
oracle.  The full IOMMU PCI model suite, including snapshot validation and
cross-thread prepared-state isolation, passes after that coverage expansion.
Those assertions are fixture-led: expected wire values do not come from the
bhyve IOMMU implementation headers.

The PMEM PCI fixture now applies the same rule to device 27: it independently
checks the public device ID, shared-memory region ID, required per-device
feature, and complete advertised feature mask before exercising lifecycle and
snapshot behavior.  The focused PMEM PCI and worker suites pass.

The same lifecycle pass rechecked GPU, virtio-mem, sound, PMEM, and filesystem
state.  GPU keeps resource state under its model mutex and reconstructs only
destination-local presentation objects after portable state publication;
virtio-mem serializes host requested-size notifications with its frozen
configuration and host-model image; sound and PMEM drain event-driven worker
ownership before teardown.  These are source/model conclusions.  They do not
replace the ledgered root-only Linux and 5BSD activation, reset, checkpoint,
and soak runs.

## 2026-08-09 ownership-wait and entropy-state review

The unadvertised administration-owner teardown was reviewed as an explicit
callback-lifetime boundary.  Production destruction closes command admission,
then waits on the event-driven active-command predicate before destroying the
lock or releasing callback arguments.  The associated ATF case now proves
that the destructor has entered that drain state before it releases the
blocked callback; this closes a test scheduling gap that could previously
pass without exercising the ownership wait.  The private-interface ledger
and source validator record the rule as `VIRTIO-PRIVATE-101`.

The RNG save-state boundary was also made explicit as
`VIRTIO-PRIVATE-102`.  It has no device-private snapshot callback or
configuration record: common PCI/queue state may be retained, but the host
random descriptor and generated entropy remain destination-local.  The
validator verifies that the model still uses the common PCI snapshot path and
has no device snapshot hook; the existing RNG ATF assertion checks the same
device contract.  This is deliberately not a claim that two entropy streams
match across restore.

Finally, the PMEM worker test fixture now uses a monotonic condition clock
and monotonic observation deadlines, matching the production worker drain.
This removes wall-clock-adjustment flakiness from bounded lifecycle tests
without changing PMEM behavior.  Focused administration, RNG, and PMEM
builds plus the complete rootless harness passed after these changes.  Live
filesystem, PMEM, RNG, and administration-topology qualification remains
root-only and is still tracked in the activation ledger.

## 2026-08-09 administration/device-group composition review

The administration-virtqueue and device-group foundation received a separate
composition review.  The queue namespace is staged before modern transport
publication, only exposes `ADMIN_VQ` when a binding owns parsing, completion,
queue-local drain, reset, suspend, and snapshot state, and remains
fail-closed otherwise.  The group fabric seals its command topology before a
queue becomes guest-visible; command validation precedes any optional external
membership lease, and snapshot restore verifies the complete group set before
publishing any owner state.

This remains intentionally unadvertised.  There is no real PF/VF
owner/member topology yet, so enabling `ADMIN_VQ` merely because the common
queue and group helpers compile would misrepresent an interoperable device.
The rootless administration PCI/group ATF cases and the complete harness
passed in the current replay.  The required promotion evidence is unchanged:
a concrete PCI ownership topology, live Linux command execution, reset and
suspend under load, and checkpoint/restore of that topology.

## 2026-08-09 lifecycle callback and rootless regression replay

The post-change rootless replay passed the independent VirtIO requirements
validator, the complete device harness, the nested-VMX requirements and
non-standard-interface ledgers, the nested architectural model, and
source-matched `vmm.ko` and `bhyve` builds.  The VirtIO audit reports 237
requirements checked against 683 independent oracle definitions; 16 current
PCI devices advertising Device Suspend and 16 advertising Queue Reset are
ledgered.  These numbers are source/model/build evidence only: the activation
ledger still records the Linux and rebuilt-5BSD device-specific cases that
need privileged execution.

An additional callback-lifetime pass enumerated each VirtIO PCI model with a
host event source, worker, or condition-driven backend.  Every such device
has explicit reset, suspend, resume, and checkpoint ownership.  Balloon,
console, filesystem, input, network, RTC, SCSI, sound, and vsock implement
their own lifecycle boundary; GPU state is internally mutex-protected; RNG
has no independent backend work; and IOMMU callback entry checks the common
quiesce/suspend/checkpoint fence before it can touch a guest ring.  The
stateless no-op callback is therefore an explicit bounded contract, not an
unreviewed inheritance path.  Privileged suspend/reset/checkpoint and soak
cases remain the evidence needed to promote this source result.

The requirements validator now enforces that relationship for the nine
current event/worker-backed PCI models.  It separately checks the
callback-only IOMMU exception for its common quiesce, suspend, checkpoint,
and pending-notification fence.  This prevents a new asynchronous device from
quietly inheriting a stateless lifecycle callback.

## 2026-08-09 balloon asynchronous-statistics fence review

The balloon statistics queue was reviewed as an asynchronous retained-request
path rather than as ordinary synchronous queue work.  Its timer acquires the
common device lock and may complete a retained descriptor only while the
device is runnable.  Guest suspend and checkpoint pause drain the retained
descriptor under their respective ownership fences; selective queue reset
discards it without publishing a completion; a snapshot carrying a live token
fails closed.  The rootless balloon test now exercises quiesce, guest-suspend,
and checkpoint-pause predicates independently, then proves that completion
resumes only after all three fences are clear.  It also retains the existing
stale-generation, reset, snapshot rejection, and repeated-restore coverage.

remaining balloon release evidence is still privileged Linux and rebuilt-5BSD
activation under memory pressure, packed queues, reset, and checkpoint/soak;
this review does not imply that those guest lanes have run.

## 2026-08-09 virtio-fs monotonic checkpoint-wait contract

The filesystem PCI model's asynchronous control and quiesce paths were
reviewed for deadline-clock consistency.  Both construct an absolute
`CLOCK_MONOTONIC` deadline and wait on the same condition variable, which is
initialized with a monotonic condition attribute.  This matters because a
default realtime condition variable paired with a monotonic absolute deadline
would make wall-clock adjustment appear as a spurious immediate or prolonged
checkpoint timeout.

The private-interface ledger now records that host operational contract and
its validator independently checks the ten-second bound, both monotonic
deadline constructors, both timed predicate waits, and the condition-clock
initialization.  The complete rootless harness and requirements validator
passed after adding the guard.  This is source-level lifecycle evidence; live
Linux filesystem checkpoint and backend-failure qualification remain required
before the provisional device can be promoted.

The persistent-memory worker received the same deadline-clock review.  Its
event-driven drain is now separately guarded as a thirty-second monotonic
reset/suspend/destroy contract: timeout preserves the durable-backing owner
and keeps guest admission fenced until retirement.  The guard checks the
private timeout policy, monotonic deadline construction, condition attribute,
timed predicate wait, and the PCI reset/destroy callers.  The rootless replay
passed with 99 private-interface entries.  Live persistent-memory activation
and checkpoint/soak remain qualification gates rather than inferred evidence.

The host block reset drain was corrected during the operational-wait review.
It previously used an absolute realtime deadline because its reset condition
variable used default attributes.  The condition variable is now initialized
with `CLOCK_MONOTONIC` and its bounded drain constructs a matching monotonic
deadline, so host clock correction cannot shorten or prolong the callback
ownership fence.  Timeout still retains the generation fence and marks the
device for reset; delayed backend completion remains discard-only.  The
private ledger records this as entry 100, and the complete rootless harness
plus bhyve build passed after the production change.

## 2026-08-08 FreeBSD guest suspend eligibility replay

The PCI and MMIO guest transport paths were compared directly with VirtIO 1.4
section 3.4.  They already use the required cumulative status writes: the
device clears `DRIVER_OK` after accepting suspend and clears `SUSPEND` after
the driver reasserts `DRIVER_OK`.  The review found one driver-side
conformance gap: a host system suspend could begin that handshake while the
child was not yet `DRIVER_OK`, contrary to the section 3.4.1 recommendation.
Both paths now require a runnable status with neither `FAILED` nor
`DEVICE_NEEDS_RESET` before requesting the optional handshake.  A device that
is merely being suspended by the host bus remains safely fenced; it simply
does not receive an invalid VirtIO status transition.

Each transport also records a host-local handshake transaction only after the
device has completed the suspend half.  Resume consults that transaction bit
instead of merely checking negotiated features, then clears it only after the
matching device-owned resume completion (or a full reset).  Thus a host
suspend that correctly skipped the optional VirtIO exchange cannot cause a
later host resume to manufacture a `DRIVER_OK` write; a completed exchange is
still paired exactly once.

The independent contract test covers runnable, uninitialized, reset-required,
and failed status samples.  The complete rootless harness, requirements
validator, snapshot model, and nested VMX model all pass after the change.
Rebuilt-kernel PCI/MMIO suspend injection remains a later root-only guest
qualification item.

The same transport review found that `VIRTIO_F_NOTIF_CONFIG_DATA` was retained
by the generic MMIO feature filter even though only the PCI path implements a
device-supplied per-queue notification identifier.  VirtIO 1.4 section 2.9
leaves that data and its delivery transport-specific; MMIO supplies neither.
The filter now removes the bit for all MMIO versions, and the independent
guest-contract fixture asserts the modern and legacy outcomes.  This does not
affect MMIO `NOTIFICATION_DATA`, whose required 32-bit queue-notify register
write remains separately implemented and tested.

The host-side status transition was also tightened: a malformed write that
combines driver-owned `FAILED` with `SUSPEND` no longer starts backend suspend
work.  Terminal `FAILED` and `DEVICE_NEEDS_RESET` now take precedence over a
suspend request in the same way they already do during rollback and resume.
The modern device-state regression verifies that no suspend callback occurs
while the failure remains visible to the driver.

After these two lifecycle corrections, the complete rootless device harness
passed (including 505 modern-device checks), the requirements and snapshot
model validators passed, and a fresh `-Werror` bhyve link completed with a
matching freshly built `libvmmapi` archive in an isolated object tree.  The
earlier standalone link failure was stale dependency ordering in that scratch
tree, not a source diagnostic.

## 2026-08-07 nested VMX Linux lifecycle comparison

The pinned Linux 7.2-rc4 VMX reference was reviewed at its nested-entry,
nested-exit, and nested-state boundaries.  The useful behavioural result is
that an L1 VMLAUNCH/VMRESUME remains pending until the authoritative L2 exit:
the entry path explicitly does not report VM-instruction success, while the
exit path cancels pending monitor-trap work, leaves L2, synchronizes VMCS02
into VMCS12, and only then makes the L1-visible result available.  Its state
interface serializes architectural VMCS12 and explicit guest-mode,
run-pending, MTF, and timer state; it does not serialize a hardware VMCS.

The local design agrees with those observable requirements without copying
the reference implementation.  The portable L2 record is fixed-width and
host-resource-free; MTF ownership is generation- and VMCS02-identity-bound,
is acquired only after a real L2 exit proves entry, is consumed only after
publication of its matching exit, and is returned to a strictly newer
portable image on refreeze.  The MTF model includes stale, alias, callback
failure, callback re-entry, and publication-corruption checks.

The remaining deliberate boundary is the common startup entry owner in
`vmx_run_nested()`.  It is still rejected before VMCS02/MSR/EPT acquisition
because its successful, declined, VMfail, cold-refreeze, hot-continuation,
and L2-to-L1 publication inverses have not yet been installed as one
source-ordered production transaction.  Removing that fence or merely
linking the model helper would be incorrect.  Required next implementation:
place the final common owner guard immediately before the real hardware entry,
route every non-entry path through the exact private unwind, and settle the
common owner only after the corresponding hardware or published architectural
outcome.  Intel L1/L2 execution, nested snapshot/restore, fault, and soak
remain privileged qualification gates after that implementation exists.

The nested-entry edge-matrix validator was also tightened in this pass.  Its
mandatory inventory now includes the previously format-checked but not
complete-list-checked unclassified hardware return, final pre-entry residency,
synthetic/rejection, post-entry freeze, and EPT/direct-reflection paths.  The
gate therefore fails if any currently mapped nested ownership edge disappears
from the review matrix.  This improves source-review coverage only; it does
not change nested runtime readiness.

## 2026-08-07 QEMU save-state comparison

The pinned QEMU reference was reviewed at the VirtIO core and modern PCI
save/load boundaries.  QEMU versions its split and packed queue cursors,
feature windows, device-endian state, PCI queue addresses and enable state,
and invokes device-specific extra-state callbacks through a staged load
interface.  That is useful architectural comparison, not a bhyve wire-format
requirement.

The bhyve implementation follows the same safety shape without sharing that
format: its envelope and x86 transaction records are fixed-width
little-endian images; decoders reject wrong versions, lengths, reserved
fields, checksums, overlapping ranges, and invalid destination state before
publication.  Unknown noncritical envelope sections are explicitly skipped;
unknown critical sections fail.  Nested checkpoint decode similarly stages a
complete candidate and validates the capability-bound VMCS registry before
publishing the decoded view.  The rootless envelope and transaction tests
exercise malformed records, staging preservation, destination mismatch, and
unknown-section handling.

This comparison found no new source-level correction.  It does not establish
QEMU migration-format compatibility or live migration readiness: bhyve keeps
its own documented format and requires separate destination/backend identity
qualification before a privileged restore or migration claim.

## 2026-08-07 IOMMU DMA and packed-ring conformance replay

The VirtIO-IOMMU request path was traced against VirtIO 1.4 sections
5.13.6.2 through 5.13.6.7.  The common request-header reserved bytes are
ignored; ATTACH rejects its nonzero reserved field, DETACH and PROBE ignore
their request-specific reserved fields, and UNMAP takes the permitted
deterministic rejection path.  Unknown and unnegotiated request types retain
the specified zero-used-length, no-write result.  The state path uses an
endpoint DMA lease to fence detach, reset, snapshot validation, and restore;
the delayed control request is replayed from the DMA-idle callback rather
than a polling loop.  The common DMA binding keeps both direct and translated
requests accounted until completion, so a domain cannot be installed,
replaced, or detached under a retained mapping.

The packed-ring replay checked the descriptor ownership rule, event
suppression formula, wrap transition, grouped in-order completion publication,
stale completion fence, and portable queue-cursor restore.  A packed chain is
completed by one used descriptor at its head as specified by section 2.8;
payload and descriptor ownership are published before the USED flag.  The
independent requirements, DMA-boundary, snapshot-portability, snapshot-runner
negative self-test, and nested-ledger self-test all completed cleanly.  The
portable snapshot model completed 30 cases with no failure.  This adds
rootless code/model evidence only: installed Linux and 5BSD
ACCESS_PLATFORM/packed activation, active translated-DMA checkpoint, and
bounded long-run soak remain root-only release gates.

The available live host is Intel amd64 hardware.  Intel-specific nested-VMX
work and qualification will use that host, while common VirtIO queue, DMA,
interrupt, lifecycle, and save-state code must remain architecture-neutral.
AMD SVM and future arm64 hosts remain explicit build/model boundaries until
matching hardware is available.

## 2026-08-08 qualification-control PID identity replay

The `virtio-lab` resume and cancellation path now treats a daemon-supervised
case as a three-part identity: supervisor PID, child PID, and a SHA-256 of
each process's start time plus command.  PID/PPID alone is not signal
authority because either value can be recycled after an interrupted manager.
The scheduler records both identities only after the parent/child relationship
is observed; unrecorded or mismatched records remain fail-closed and cannot
be adopted or cancelled.  Cancellation also captures the identities during
its trusted directory scan and revalidates those captured values immediately
before `kill(2)`, without rereading mutable PID files.  Thus a PID-file change
or PID reuse between enumeration and delivery cannot retarget a signal.

The rootless orchestration self-test covers the normal cancellation path,
missing/mismatched fingerprint refusal, and the structural immediate-
revalidation contract.  This is qualification-control correctness only; it
does not replace the pending privileged Linux, 5BSD, checkpoint, soak, or
Intel nested-VMX live gates.

The matching rootless nested model gate completed 349 architectural and
lifecycle cases, including the requirement, evidence, staging, policy-pair,
and live-coverage negative validators.  That is evidence for the model and
the fail-closed boundary only: accelerated L2 entry remains withheld until
the VMCS02 owner transaction is installed in production and qualified on the
Intel host.

The independent rootless VirtIO device harness also completed with its
terminal `PASS device harness all tests passed` record.  Its negative paths
included split and packed malformed chains, invalid snapshot common status,
device configuration bounds, console control records, network backend frames,
and SCSI control/event/request records.  These model results supplement, but
do not replace, installed Linux/5BSD, checkpoint, reset, and soak evidence.

## 2026-08-07 checkpoint callback retry and backend-admission replay

This replay reviewed the direct checkpoint callbacks as a contract separate
from the common VirtIO pause fence.  A callback that returns an error from
pause must already have unwound its private admission state; a callback that
returns an error from resume is invoked again by the common layer without a
new pause, so it must not leave a private mutex or backend admission token
implicitly owned by the failed caller.  Block, SCSI, PMEM, console, 9P,
input, sound, filesystem, and both vsock backends were traced against that

reacquires it explicitly for a retry.  This avoids an implicit same-thread
mutex assumption after a failed event-source enable.  The sound callback now
releases its private mutex after every resume attempt; a defensive asynchronous
worker error can therefore be retried through the common checkpoint lifecycle.
The direct console codec rejects an enabled port without a reconstructible
backend, matching its pause admission rule.  New harness cases cover those
negative paths.  The input test uses portable `pthread_mutex_trylock()` rather
than a FreeBSD-specific mutex-owner probe, so the rootless harness retains
cross-host diagnostic value.

## 2026-08-07 lifecycle failure-fence and virtio-fs backend replay

A lifecycle-ordering review tightened the common modern-transport failed
resume path.  The previous order released the quiesce owner before publishing
`NEEDS_RESET`; `vs_suspended` already kept VirtIO queues closed in that
interval, so this was a defense-in-depth ordering gap rather than a proven
descriptor-admission escape.  `vi_modern_resume()` now publishes the terminal
device state before reopening the common fence, matching the suspend failure
path and making the failure boundary unambiguous to future lockless users.
The independent device harness records the state at the final quiesce release
and rejects the former ordering.

The follow-on virtio-fs replay traced readiness callbacks, queue admission,
QUIESCE/THAW control replies, timeout aborts, rollback, guest suspend, and
checkpoint resume.  Backend control rejection is terminal or transactional as
appropriate: a rejected QUIESCE reopens only its own previously closed queue;
the common suspend callback then quarantines the VirtIO device before the
transport fence opens.  A rejected THAW preserves the quiesced opaque state
for retry and likewise cannot reopen guest admission.  No additional source
defect was found in that path.

The fresh snapshot-enabled bhyve build remains `-Werror` clean.  The rootless
device harness lanes completed 616, 497, 777, 100, and 2 checks with zero
failures; the nested requirements/private-interface ledgers again validated
433 and 282 entries.  Live Intel nested execution and the guest/checkpoint/
translated-DMA/soak qualification remain pending and are deliberately not
claimed by these model results.

This pass reconstructed `vmx_run_nested()` from its first pre-entry stop

The following portability replay then traced the common modern softc,
transport, queue-bank, and administration-controller restore sequence.  The

are destination-local: they are staged and committed only after validation,

## 2026-08-06 exposure, DMA, and AF_VSOCK source replay

An independent source replay started at the nested-VMX CPUID capability and
followed it through the per-VM policy switch and the first guest-entry
boundary.  `VM_CAP_NESTED_VMX` is a VM-wide CPU-model decision: the first
`vmx_run()` atomically locks that decision, so a concurrent configuration
operation either completes before the first guest instruction or receives
`EBUSY`.  CPUID leaf 1 consumes the backend capability rather than the host
tunable directly, so the host policy alone does not expose VMX to a guest.
No exposure, ordering, or capability mismatch was found in this replay.

The separate common-DMA replay followed split and packed queue-ring mappings,

acceptance; cached rings are generation-revalidated.  The deliberate
balloon/PFN and legacy exclusions remain documented rather than silently
falling back to translated DMA.

The AF_VSOCK replay rechecked the receive mbuf construction, fragmented
SEQPACKET handling, provider queue pressure, and blocking send paths.  It
uses direct filling of preallocated mbuf chains, `m_catpkt()` for packet-header
accounting, and event-driven sleeps for credit and queue availability; no
periodic retry loop was found in those paths.  Rootless evidence for this
replay includes the 375-check RX harness, the 1,651-check transport harness,

and Intel nested execution remain required before any release claim.

## 2026-08-06 checkpoint ABI admission and packed-queue transaction replay

The common checkpoint manifest machine ABI advanced from

portable-device wire-format change: version 2 is required because the native
amd64 VMX/nested kernel record changed.  A version-1 manifest is now rejected
by manifest admission before the restore transaction begins, rather than
being allowed to reach a shifted native record decoder.  The manifest model
has a direct rejection assertion for the old ABI.

A separate mutation-first replay traced modern split/packed queue restore.
It confirmed that queue mappings and any newly allocated packed completion
cache are staged before publication; a failed restore frees only staged
storage and restores the destination queue image.  On successful layout or
queue-size replacement, the prior destination cache is retained through the
device-private callback and retired exactly once after that callback commits.
The rootless core tests independently cover packed-cache replacement,
repeated restore, rollback preservation, and a split restore into a previously
packed destination.

The current rootless gate passed the four device-harness lanes (616, 491, 777,
and 99 checks, plus the two-check snapshot lane), the independent requirements
and portability/DMA validators, the nested-VMX model suite, a clean VMM module

nested execution; the root-only Linux, 5BSD, checkpoint, bounded-soak, and

## 2026-08-06 guest-vsock mbuf and attach-lifecycle replay

The guest AF_VSOCK receive path was replayed from transport completion through

not replace installed multi-provider, jail/VNET, checkpoint, or extended-soak

## 2026-08-05 interrupted-qualification CID recovery

The VirtIO lab scheduler originally released a case's CID lease only from its
live manager loop.  If that manager was interrupted after a supervised case
published either a failure or success status, `--resume` could treat the old
lease as a collision, assign a different CID on a retry, or preserve a leaked
lease for a reused pass.  Resume now reattaches a still-live supervisor before
consulting its status, and reclaims only leases whose owner record names the
same completed run and case after the existing liveness checks prove there is
no active case to protect.  Rootless scheduler regressions simulate both
terminal-status cases and prove retries retain the original CID.  This is
orchestration cleanup; it does not broaden provider ownership or permit
concurrent CIDs.

## 2026-08-04 doubled kernel and non-standard-interface review phases

The definition of done now has four independent terminal directions in
addition to the normative, lifecycle, portability, and test-quality passes:
two kernel traversals and two non-standard-interface traversals.  They are
not a single checklist with four names:

* **Kernel-source replay** starts at production entry and retirement points
  (run, reset, suspend, restore, interrupt, callback, detach, and error
  paths), reconstructs ownership and execution context from code, and then
  compares the result with the common VMM and VirtIO contracts.  It must
  account for architecture-neutral state separately from Intel VMX, AMD SVM,
  or device-private residency.
* **Non-standard-interface replay** starts at accepted private inputs and
  observable consumers: bhyve options, ioctls, backend protocols, checkpoint
  records, sysctls/tunables, trace/audit controls, compatibility aliases,
  test controls, and unsupported-feature responses.  It reconstructs each
  contract without importing the previous inventory, and requires an owner,
  lifetime, units/default, authorization, version and reserved-field policy,
  rollback rule, and positive plus rejection evidence.

The second kernel replay starts at live-state mutation, rollback, and
destructive teardown rather than production entry.  The second non-standard
replay starts at emitted diagnostics, unsupported responses, resource limits,
and operator controls rather than accepted input.  Each must use a fresh
traversal; a correction restarts all four directions.  The nested-VMX prompt
records these as terminal Passes 145 and 146, followed by withheld-feature and
independent-test-oracle replays (Passes 147 and 148).  The VirtIO prompt keeps
the equivalent clean-room kernel and private-policy passes in its terminal
cycle.

For VirtIO these are the enforced terminal Passes 41 through 44 in
`VIRTIO_1_4_FULL_REVIEW_PROMPT.md`.  For common VMM/nested work they are the
terminal Passes 145 through 148 in `VMX_NESTED_FULL_REVIEW_PROMPT.md`.
Any production correction restarts all four replays and the affected earlier
requirements, lifecycle, portability, Linux/QEMU comparison, test, and
qualification work.  A source/model result is never substituted for required
root-only Intel, Linux, 5BSD, checkpoint, fault, or soak evidence.

### Applied review result

The first application of the doubled review found one non-standard common
owner-interface leak: deferred post-entry settlement exposed a provisional
loop result while its owner was still non-returnable.  The deferring helper
now retains that result exclusively in the stack-owned transaction; only the
resolver publishes it after private freeze or detach has completed.  The
contract is recorded in `NVMX-EVENT-175` and covered by the common-owner and
amd64 nested-state tests.  This is a rootless contract correction, not a claim
that nested VMX execution has been enabled or live-qualified.

## 2026-08-04 common VirtIO decoder replay

An independent replay of the modern and legacy common VirtIO snapshot
decoders found that the outer checkpoint compatibility envelope rejected an
impossible source contract, but the per-device decoder itself did not.  A
malformed direct device image could therefore present a negotiated feature
which its own saved effective offered-feature word never exposed if the destination
happened to support that feature.  Both decoders now check the saved
negotiated subset before accepting the destination feature comparison.  The
modern record uses the same effective offer as feature negotiation, including
transport-provided bits such as `VERSION_1`, rather than only device-model
features.  The matching source encoders reject an impossible local negotiated
subset before advancing their output cursor, so an internal invariant failure
cannot leave a partially written device record behind.

The focused core ATF case supplies a destination that supports the forged
feature and proves both validation and restore reject it.  The existing
legacy preflight case now covers the same invariant.  This is source-level,
rootless evidence only; it does not replace malformed-image checkpoint runs
against a rebuilt privileged host.

## 2026-08-04 staged common startup-entry ownership

The private `vmmops_run` signature carries a transient startup-owner pointer
for atomic entry-guard conversion.  The common caller now owns admission,
critical/FPU transitions, refreeze, and final retirement.  The ordinary SVM
VMRUN loop and ordinary L1 VMX VMLAUNCH/VMRESUME loop each consume the owner
at their exact interrupt-disabled entry boundary and reverse all local
preparation if it declines entry.  VMX keeps legacy VM-instruction-failure
reporting for userspace.  The historical userspace-owned caller remains
explicitly null.

This is deliberately staged, not activation.  Nested VMX cold/resumed/hot
VMCS02 execution remains fail-closed, as do public readiness controls, until
those distinct entry and unwind paths are converted and pass the separate
Intel live qualification matrix.  SVM additionally awaits AMD-hardware
qualification.

## 2026-08-04 nested lifecycle no-entry boundary

The nested dispatcher has one return before any guest MSR transition, VMCS01
or VMCS02 selection, EPT activation, descriptor/debug preparation, TSC_AUX
transition, or event transaction: a pending suspend, rendezvous, idle, yield,
or debugger stop.  That branch now returns through the common startup owner
as a typed software exit, preserving the existing lifecycle `vm_exit`.

This does not enable nested startup.  Every later nested cold, resumed, and
hot path still rejects a non-null owner before guest-MSR entry because each
can acquire a different combination of portable continuation and CPU-local
VMCS02/EPT/MSR state.  Pass 112 and the source-order validator record that
boundary; Intel live timing and race qualification remain required.

## 2026-08-04 ordinary VMX no-entry result correction

The reverse startup-owner review found that an ordinary VMX owner guard may
decline after all ordinary local preparation has been reversed but before
`vmx_enter_guest()`.  That is a typed replay or error, not a legacy VM exit.
The old post-loop handled/`VM_EXITCODE_BOGUS` assertion nevertheless ran and
could panic because no exit record exists for this path.  `vmx_run()` now
marks only that guard-declined branch and bypasses the legacy assertion there;
the common owner retirement retains the typed result.  Real VM-entry attempts,
VMfail reporting, and lifecycle exits still use the normal assertion.

## 2026-08-04 second kernel and non-standard containment replay

Pass 113 independently retraced every ordinary VMX, SVM, and nested-VMX
machine-entry return from the architecture instruction back to the common
`vm_run()` retirement tail.  It specifically checked that a typed no-entry
result is not confused with a VM exit: ordinary VMX retains its handled/BOGUS
assertion for actual entry attempts, while the one pre-entry owner-decline
path is explicitly marked after its complete local cleanup.  SVM retains its
VMCB re-dirty rule after a declined prepared entry.  No additional shared
Intel/AMD state leak or missing cleanup edge was found in the source/model
scope.

Pass 114 independently reconstructed the non-standard run contracts from
their producers and consumers: stack owner, generation checks, readiness
gates, `EOPNOTSUPP` staging returns, portable checkpoint exclusion, and test
hooks.  The result matches the private-interface ledger (249 entries at that
review point; now 250 after the separately reviewed owner-outcome protocol).
In
particular, a nested L2 owner can be consumed only by the early lifecycle
return before VMCS02/MSR/EPT residency.  Converting initial, resumed, or hot
VMCS02 execution still requires one owner transaction spanning each real
entry, handled re-entry, and residency-specific reverse unwind; it remains
fail-closed rather than being partially enabled.  Rootless model, sanitized
model, snapshot-portability, DMA-boundary, and private-interface validation
passed.  Intel and AMD live qualification is still required.

## 2026-08-04 nested owner-result/unwind composition boundary

Pass 115 found a stricter reason not to partially wire the startup owner into
VMCS02 execution.  The owner makes a declined entry guard immediately
returnable as replay or a specified terminal error.  A later nested
residency-specific unwind may instead need to freeze a continuation or detach
it terminally.  Returning the earlier replay after a destructive detach would
make the common run loop retry state that no longer exists.

`NVMX-EVENT-172`, `NVMX-PRIVATE-250`, and matrix row `EDGE-NVMX-005A` now
require a future nested conversion either to prove that every possible unwind
preserves the guard result or to introduce a single typed result-composition
transaction with terminal unwind error dominance.  Until then the current
pre-residency `EOPNOTSUPP` boundary remains mandatory.  This adds no guest
visible behavior and does not alter readiness.

## 2026-08-04 owner-outcome protocol implementation audit

The prerequisite is now represented by the value-only
`vmx_nested_owner_outcome` protocol.  It accepts a selected nested unwind and
the already-selected guard result, retains the guard result only for clean,
rollback, and refreeze outcomes, and requires a non-replay error to dominate
for fatal or already-detached outcomes.  It rejects fail-stop classification,
invalid error combinations, and aliasing without modifying an existing
output.  The protocol carries neither pointers nor VMCS02/CPU-residency data,
is not serialized, and is not called by `vmx_run_nested()` yet.

The implementation audit found and corrected one documentation drift: the
Pass 114 count was a historical count, not the current ledger size.  The
current 250-entry ledger, requirement mapping, negative model cases, and
module build are clean.  This remains a prerequisite for an atomic live-path
conversion; it does not relax the nested `EOPNOTSUPP` boundary or readiness.

The next conversion therefore needs an architecture-neutral two-phase owner
operation: first observe and retain a pre-entry guard result without making
the stack owner returnable, then commit either that result or the composed
terminal unwind result only after the Intel-private cleanup has completed.
The existing one-phase common guard cannot safely be repurposed for this;
the review explicitly rejects direct Intel mutation of the common owner.

Pass 116 has been added to make that deferred common-owner transaction its
own mandatory review phase.  It requires a consumer-first review of every
existing one-phase guard, independent transition and negative models, and a
proof that no pending owner can reach common retirement.  This keeps the
future integration architecture-neutral even though the motivating resident
state is Intel VMCS02.

The first common prerequisite now exists as a rootless-tested deferred
pre-entry owner result.  It is stack-only, preserves loop provenance, blocks
retirement until exactly one resolve operation, and permits only a
non-replay terminal cleanup override.  It is not connected to a hardware
adapter yet; ordinary VMX and SVM retain their established one-phase paths.

The same review also found the symmetric post-entry condition.  An unhandled
or reflect-to-L1 VMCS02 exit still owns a hot continuation until freeze
publication succeeds; a one-phase post-entry owner guard either becomes
returnable too early or leaves an `IN_GUEST` owner on a freeze failure.  The
new `NVMX-EVENT-173`, `NVMX-PRIVATE-251`, and `EDGE-NVMX-005B` make both
directions mandatory prerequisites for live nested-owner integration.

The nested-VMX review gate now requires every final review phase through

## 2026-08-04 doubled reverse-lifetime and policy replay

The executable nested review gate now carries two further independent phases.
Pass 103 starts at destruction, reset, rollback, cancellation, and no-entry
failure labels and works backward to admission and allocation.  It treats
late callbacks, IPIs, pmap/EPT/VPID residency, VMCS/VMCB workspace retirement,
and release-kernel rollback as proof obligations rather than inferring safety
from a normal teardown or a `KASSERT`.  Pass 104 separately rebuilds every
implementation-defined value from both producers and consumers: diagnostics,
DTrace/audit, sysctls, tunables, private ioctls, checkpoint manifests,
provider protocols, waits, retries, compatibility aliases, and
unsupported-feature gates.  Each is classified as private detail, operator
policy, versioned bhyve contract, or experimental interface and must not leak

These are review phases, not activation permission.  Any correction restarts
the earlier final kernel, non-standard, normative, lifecycle, portability, and

## 2026-08-02 all-vCPU event capture and second kernel replay

The all-vCPU checkpoint capture now enumerates the exact sparse active-vCPU
topology while the VM topology lock is held, requires every active vCPU to be
frozen, captures each complete pending-event value into private kernel
storage, and publishes no caller output unless a VM-wide 64-bit event epoch
and the captured count remain stable.  Exception reservation/publication,
reinjected-event replacement/consumption, NMI, ExtINT, and frozen restore all
advance that epoch while holding the per-vCPU event owner.  The transaction
does not poll or add a VM-wide spin-lock order.  Zero-vCPU capture is valid,
and rejected capacity, alias, wrapping-range, producer-active, count, or epoch
cases leave every caller output unchanged.

This is a consistency detector, not an event-ingress lock.  Its successful
capture has a defined linearization point, but the eventual checkpoint
coordinator must keep device and host event ingress quiesced from that point
through atomic checkpoint publication or source teardown.  A complete 64-bit
same-value ABA within one capture is recorded as a private runtime bound, not
as a serialized guarantee.  All-vCPU restore publication and its ingress
lease remain intentionally unimplemented, so no production `vm-v2` ioctl is
advertised yet.

The independent release-kernel replay also found that the old boolean-only
`vm_entry_intinfo()` compatibility path performed a lock-separated peek and
commit and treated both failures only with `KASSERT`.  An asynchronous
exception could therefore produce `EAGAIN`; a non-INVARIANTS kernel would
then continue with an uncommitted or uninitialized result.  The compatibility
path now plans and consumes the same snapshot in one event-lock critical
section, while the nested entry path retains the error-returning staged
peek/compare-and-commit transaction.  Invalid internal values are preserved
and the compatibility caller enters without consuming them rather than
misreporting success.  Shared locked consumption prevents the two paths from
drifting.

The private-state replay then found that the unadvertised VMS2 x86 record
carried the native `enum vm_exitcode` and the last host exit RIP and decoded
instruction length.  Those values are transient kernel/userspace bookkeeping,
not architectural guest state, and making the native enum a migration field
would couple restore compatibility to future source ordering.  They have been
removed before exposure.  The fixed 80-byte version-1 record remains intact,
but offsets 48 through 79 are now all reserved zero and every nonzero 64-bit
word is rejected without changing the decoded output.  Architectural next PC
continues to live in the common vCPU record.  The private-interface ledger now
records this exclusion and its compatibility rationale explicitly.

The next independent boundary traversal found wrapping-address rejection only
in the outer all-vCPU decoder.  The envelope builder, reader, common-state
codec, and amd64-state codec are independently callable kernel helpers and
could receive an address range that wrapped `uintptr_t`; overflow-safe overlap
subtraction alone did not make dereferencing that range safe.  One
architecture-neutral checked-range primitive now owns nonempty NULL, wrap,
and overlap semantics.  Every public builder, reader, common codec, amd64
codec, and transaction entry validates its complete input and output ranges
before dereference.  Direct tests invoke each layer with top-of-address-space
ranges rather than relying on the outer transaction test.

Focused event-state tests cover stable capture validation, generation drift,
count mismatch, and epoch wrap observation.  The event-state ATF binary and
`vmm.o` compile with warnings as errors, and the 214-entry nested requirement,
45-entry nested private-interface, and 77-entry VirtIO private-interface gates
pass.  Live concurrency, ingress-fence, and restore rollback qualification
still require the rebuilt Intel test kernel.

## 2026-08-02 VMS2 doubled kernel and private-contract replay

The forward kernel pass found that the first all-vCPU decoder contradicted
the canonical envelope ordering.  VMS2 orders sections by type and then
instance, but the decoder required each common-vCPU section to be immediately
followed by its amd64 section.  A one-vCPU fixture therefore passed while
every valid image with two or more vCPUs was rejected.  The decoder now treats
the two type groups as ordered sparse-instance sets, compares the complete
sets during the no-output validation pass, and only then stages both groups.
It also preserves the common format's valid zero-active-vCPU state and rejects
wrapping input or output address ranges before parsing.

The independent private-interface replay did not treat that ordering as an
Intel or VirtIO rule.  It records the grouping, sparse identity, zero-vCPU,
immutability, alias, and transaction behavior as a versioned bhyve checkpoint
contract in both private ledgers.  New tests cover two non-contiguous vCPU
instances, capacity failure with untouched outputs, mismatched type-group
identities with untouched outputs, zero active vCPUs, and wrapping ranges.
The consumer-side replay also added a separate destination preflight which
requires the incoming maximum-vCPU contract and sorted sparse active-vCPU set
to match the destination exactly before an apply adapter can run; it rejects
missing, extra, reordered, out-of-range, or capacity-truncated topology.
The focused ATF cases, amd64 kernel object with `-Werror`, 214-entry nested
requirements gate, 42-entry nested private ledger, 224-entry VirtIO
requirements gate, and 77-entry VirtIO private ledger pass.  Production ioctl
selection remains intentionally blocked on immutable copyin, destination
topology validation, an all-vCPU event publication transaction, and explicit
legacy selection.

## 2026-08-01 double-kernel and non-standard review phases

The rotating gate now includes two additional, independently terminating
passes.  The first repeats the kernel implementation review after the
normative, Linux/QEMU, lifecycle, portability, and test-quality passes have
changed the code.  It retraces allocation, publication, locking, callback,
rollback, reset, detach, suspend, restore, interrupt, DMA, and hot-path
ownership from the production entry points; a clean earlier kernel review is
not carried forward as evidence after a fix.

The second pass inventories behavior outside a normative VirtIO or Intel ABI:
bhyve compatibility interfaces, checkpoint formats, experimental nested-VMX
policy, provider protocols, operator limits, and implementation-specific
defaults.  Each item must be classified as a private implementation detail,
documented compatibility contract, versioned state ABI, or experimental
interface; must remain outside standard wire-value fixtures; must be opt-in or
fail closed where interoperability is not established; and must have direct
negative and compatibility coverage.  Linux and QEMU remain behavioral
comparisons for this pass, not normative sources and not code sources.

The focused vsock review loop now carries the same separation as Passes H and
I.  Its second kernel reading starts from teardown and failure callbacks and
includes unchanged socket, mbuf, provider, cdevpriv, prison/VNET, MAC, poll,
kqueue, and transport code.  Its non-standard pass separately inventories the
provider ioctls, bhyve control protocol, checkpoint records, policy limits,
tracing, audit, and compatibility encodings.  A successful VirtIO wire review
therefore cannot implicitly approve the private host/provider ABI.

The inventory is evaluated as five separate subphases so that a standard-wire
review cannot accidentally sign off a private interface:

1. **Compatibility identities:** legacy/transitional PCI IDs and historical
   guest-visible aliases live in the separate compatibility oracle and may
   never supply expected values to the VirtIO 1.4 oracle.
2. **Host/provider ABIs:** `/dev/vsock`, VMM ioctls, and backend lifecycle
   controls require explicit versions or reserved-zero fields, bounded waits,
   authorization revalidation after sleep, and rollback before publication.
3. **Checkpoint ABIs:** every private record needs a fixed-width endian-defined
   envelope, size and allocation bounds, unknown-version rejection, preserved
   historical decoding, and a preflight parser which cannot mutate the live
   destination.
4. **Experimental guest ABIs:** nested VMX, administration queues/device
   groups, provisional devices, and unqualified accelerations remain
   default-off and must be enabled only by an explicit boot or device policy.
5. **Operational policy:** sysctl limits, rate limits, tracing, audit events,
   and timeout defaults are reviewed for synchronization and denial-of-service
   behavior but are not represented as VirtIO requirements.

Each subphase is rerun after a fix in another subphase.  A value shared with a
Linux or QEMU interface is still classified as compatibility behavior unless
the governing VirtIO, Intel, PCI, ACPI, or platform specification defines it.

The failure-first nested-VMX repetition also found destructive cleanup guarded
only by `KASSERT`.  In a release kernel, an impossible prepared-entry, cold
continuation, reflected-entry, or recovered hot-failure state could therefore
continue into VMCS02, EPT, VPID, or MSR-workspace release after the diagnostic
check had compiled away.  Those ownership checks are now unconditional
fail-stop boundaries, and the source validator pins representative checks at
each release path.  This does not replace live Intel failure injection, but it
prevents a production kernel from silently erasing the last recorded owner.

The non-standard observability subphase now inventories the nested effective-
VPID invalidation statistic and the common kernel-internal-exit DTrace probe.
Both are operational contracts rather than Intel architectural state, so their
names and argument semantics are reviewed separately from the SDM-derived
fixtures.

The second pass, restarted from management and restore entry points, found
that `VM_CAP_NESTED_VMX` accepted every nonzero integer as enabled.  That made
negative values and future flag-shaped values silently change a VM-wide CPU
model.  The private capability now accepts only canonical `0` and `1`, rejects
all other values before inspecting or publishing nested state, and records
that rule in the non-standard interface inventory.

The failure-first repetition found that a rejected backend module
initialization left the common VMM suspend/resume callbacks published and
leaked a successfully allocated common IPI vector.  The Intel backend could
also allocate its posted-interrupt vector and then return from a later EPT or
nested-policy validation without releasing it.  Common initialization now
withdraws both callbacks and releases its vector on backend failure; Intel
rejects an inconsistent nested-VPID tunable before allocation and funnels all
remaining post-allocation failures through one private-vector rollback.  The
non-standard inventory records both callback publication and posted-interrupt
vector ownership, and the source gate plus complete `vmm.ko` warnings-as-errors
build cover the rollback shape.  Live module-load failure injection remains a
root qualification case because this source session does not replace the
running kernel.

The same release-kernel scan removed an older `XXX`/`KASSERT` recovery hole
from VM construction.  With virtual-interrupt delivery enabled, failure to
install the required APIC-access mapping previously stopped only an
INVARIANTS kernel; a release kernel could continue with an internally invalid
VM.  The backend initializer has no error return, so the mapping is now an
unconditional fail-stop invariant, matching the other mandatory VMX
construction resources.  A future fallible common constructor can convert
this to transactional allocation rollback without weakening the invariant.

The first composed Pass 16 run found one unversioned provider operation.
`VSOCK_IOC_TRANSPORT_SET_FEATURES` carried only a bare 64-bit feature mask,
even though ATTACH and FREEZE already used extensible requests.  It now uses a
fixed 32-byte `vsock_transport_features` request with an explicit version,
reserved-zero flags, and two reserved 64-bit fields.  The kernel rejects an
unknown version, nonzero flags, nonzero reserved state, and unsupported device
features before looking up or mutating a provider.  bhyve constructs the
canonical request in one helper, the manual documents the private ABI, and the
provider ATF defines coverage for each rejected expansion field as well as the
valid path.  Its source and the kernel module build cleanly here; execution
against the rebuilt kernel remains an explicit root gate.  Because ioctl
payload size is part of the binary command number, the
kernel also recognizes the old 8-byte encoding as a deprecated compatibility
request and applies the same feature-mask validation; new bhyve never emits
it.  This is a private host/provider ABI correction, not a VirtIO wire-format
change.

Current non-standard inventory and disposition:

| Subphase | Interface | Classification | Default/stability | Direct evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| compatibility identities | explicit legacy input and vsock PCI identities | documented bhyve compatibility contract | selected only by legacy transport | separate `bhyve_virtio_compat.h` oracle plus input and Linux/5BSD identity checks |
| host/provider ABI | `/dev/vsock` attach, feature, reset, freeze and thaw controls | privileged versioned private ABI | fail closed; bounded management waits | kernel provider ATF, bhyve backend harness, Capsicum/MAC ownership tests; stalled-copy timeout remains a root injection gate |
| host/provider ABI | `VM_GET_CPUID` and `VM_GET_CPU_COMPAT` | source-paired kernel/libvmmapi ABI | exact flags/version and reserved-zero validation | production capture-adapter test, ABI layout checks, `vmm.ko` build |
| checkpoint ABI | manifest, compatibility envelope, device and nested records | versioned private state ABI | fixed-width encodings; preflight before publication | codec mutation suites, repeated-restore models, device snapshot harnesses; cross-build live restore remains scheduled |
| experimental guest ABI | nested VMX and nested VPID | explicit experimental Intel interface | loader-only host gate plus per-guest opt-in; VPID separately gated | SDM-derived models and kernel builds; two-boot Linux/KVM-L1 hardware qualification remains pending |
| experimental guest ABI | administration queues, device groups, and provisional devices | opt-in or unadvertised implementation | fail closed until a complete binding and feature gate exist | common transport/device harnesses and activation ledger; incomplete live entries remain non-release gates |
| kernel-private implementation | `virtio_bus_fail` transport method | internal implementation of standard FAILED status | not a guest or userspace ABI; every current PCI/MMIO transport implements it | malformed-ring lifecycle model plus PCI, MMIO, and full VirtIO module builds |
| operational policy | VSOCK limits/timeouts and RTC alarm sysctls | implementation policy | synchronized or device-scoped; not normative VirtIO requirements | focused boundary/race tests and documentation; installed-kernel stress remains pending |

The nested non-standard ABI pass also found that the exposure checkpoint
decoder accepted a version-2 record with the exposure flag clear even though
the encoder defines version 1 as the canonical disabled record and version 2
only as the enabled record.  That undocumented third state could acquire a
different meaning in a later format revision.  Decoding now requires the
version and flag to be a canonical pair: version 1/disabled or version
2/enabled.  The independent wire fixture rejects version 2/disabled while
also proving that a rejected record leaves the caller's prior result intact.

The independent kernel pass then found two Intel adapter cleanup paths which
treated a failed hardware `VMCLEAR` as a recoverable `EIO`.  Both paths could
leave VMCS01 current on the pinned CPU and subsequently permit the caller to
drop that pin, making the per-CPU hardware association escape its ownership
boundary.  Standalone environment capture and staged L2 cleanup now fail stop
on `VMCLEAR` failure and clear their software residency marker only after the
instruction succeeds.  The requirements validator pins these production
ordering and fail-stop conditions; live fault injection still requires the
rebuilt Intel kernel.

The ABI-layout follow-up found that `vsock_wire_test` used the installed
`<sys/vsock.h>` while testing a source tree.  It could therefore report a
clean provider ABI while compiling the previous installed definition.  The
target now includes `${SRCTOP}/sys` explicitly.  A new rootless case pins the
attach, feature-update, and checkpoint sizes and offsets against the sole
current 32-byte versioned request.  All 11 ABI/wire cases pass against the
source header.

The current save-state review found that the prepared incoming VirtIO-IOMMU
translation fabric had production thread scoping but no test that compiled the
snapshot path or observed it from a second thread.  The PCI harness now builds
that path and proves the validation thread sees the prepared fabric while a
peer thread continues to see the live fabric, then proves cleanup removes the
prepared view.  This closes rootless evidence for the concurrency property;
the translated live malformed-checkpoint gate remains pending on the root
qualification host.

The same pass found that the requirements ledger named the amd64 production
CPU-contract capture adapter while tests exercised only its portable codec and
kernel ABI layouts.  A new source-level adapter test now drives the real
capture implementation through deterministic `vm_get_cpuid` and
`vm_get_cpu_compat` boundaries.  It proves bounded canonical subleaf traversal,
the exact TSC/x2APIC/XSAVE/nested signature records, and transactional output
on CPUID, ioctl, and policy-validation failures.  Both focused cases build
with the tree's normal `-Werror` flags and pass.

The second kernel pass then found a VSOCK operator-policy race.  The global
and per-CID connection ceilings were writable without `vtvsock_mtx`, while
admission compared a limit and then subtracted from a second load.  A
concurrent reduction could underflow that subtraction and admit beyond the
new ceiling.  The writable limits now use a lock-aware handler; related buffer
policy updates are serialized and published with release semantics, socket
creation consumes its captured default, and the fragment limit uses the same
serialized policy boundary.  The `vsock.ko` kernel build and focused inbound,
outbound, loopback, global, and per-CID cap tests pass.  Installed-kernel
concurrent sysctl stress remains a privileged live qualification item.

The non-standard provider-control review also found that FREEZE had a bounded
copy-drain wait while SET_FEATURES and RESET could wait indefinitely behind a
stalled userspace copy.  All three management operations now use the same
30-second absolute deadline and return retryable `EWOULDBLOCK` without
publishing the requested transition.  The manual page now documents RESET's
epoch/queue/connection/feature effects and the timeout contract.  The kernel
module remains `-Werror` clean; deliberate stalled-copy timeout injection is
retained as a privileged provider-ABI test.

The repeated kernel portability pass found a packed-ring interrupt race that
was hidden by the current Intel host.  The guest common virtqueue driver wrote
the packed driver-event suppression record, synchronized its DMA map, and then
rechecked for a completion, but the full publish-before-recheck barrier was
compiled only on i386 and amd64.  That barrier is now unconditional, matching
the split-ring and notification paths.  The requirements validator has a
source-level regression which rejects an architecture-guarded packed
enable/recheck barrier.  Every VirtIO guest module, including the new input,
RTC, P9, GPU, and vsock modules, builds with kernel `-Werror` after the fix;
live weakly ordered hardware remains an explicit future architecture gate.

The aggregate sanitizer rerun also caught a test-infrastructure portability
defect rather than a product defect: the new production CPU-capture test used
a source-relative kernel ABI include which became invalid after the sanitizer
runner copied the test into its isolated directory.  The test now includes
the source-tree ABI through explicit compiler include paths in both the normal
ATF and isolated sanitizer builds.  This ensures the independent test cannot
silently fall back to an installed, stale VMM ABI.

## 2026-08-01 layered review contract and administration restore ordering

The rotating review contract now has closed, separately terminating passes
for common save-state/migration and the complete Intel nested-VMX execution
path.  Device conformance, save-state, nested execution, and test integrity
must each be checked against their normative specification and the pinned
Linux reference.  The nested pass additionally requires the pinned Intel SDM
as the guest ABI and keeps model/build results distinct from the still-pending
Linux/KVM-L1 hardware qualification.  A clean device or vsock pass can no
longer implicitly defer either state portability or nested execution.

The save-state-first pass found a cross-component restore transaction defect.
The historical wire format places an optional administration-controller image
after device-private state, and the common restore path therefore committed
the device before asking the external administration controller to restore.
If that final operation failed, common transport and queues rolled back while
device-private state remained from the incoming checkpoint.

Restore now preserves the wire format but validates ahead through the device
section, retains the destination administration image, restores the
controller first, and only then permits device-private publication.  A device
failure compensates the controller; a failed compensation marks restore
incomplete and requires reset.  The focused regression injects the later
device failure, proves the destination controller is unchanged, and then
proves the same immutable image restores successfully.  All 54 common VirtIO
core cases and the 221-entry/683-oracle requirements gate pass.  This is
rootless transaction evidence; the administration feature remains
unadvertised until a concrete production owner and Linux live qualification
exist.

## 2026-08-01 nested-VMX live-ledger completeness review

The production audit confirmed that the Intel source tree contains the
CPU-pinned VMCS02 execution machinery, composed-EPT activation,
destination-local VPID ownership, transactional L1 restoration, and active-L2
checkpoint staging.  Those mechanisms are not a claim of enabled nested
execution: `vmx_run_nested()` deliberately returns `EOPNOTSUPP` for any
startup owner after the one provably pre-residency lifecycle exit.  Converting
that boundary requires one atomic owner/residency transaction spanning VMCS02,
EPT, guest-MSR entry, exit reflection, and reverse unwind.  Guest exposure
therefore remains deliberately default-off pending both that transaction and
real Intel Linux/KVM-L1 qualification with Linux and 5BSD L2 guests.

The audit found one hole in that hardware contract.  `NVMX-EPT-008` was
correctly classified as `experimental-pending-live`, but the EPT/INVEPT live
feature group did not require evidence for its representable-address limit,
non-MBEC EPT02 permission model, and populated-alias lifetime.  A result could
therefore have passed every live group while omitting the requirement that
most directly fences the current amd64 pmap representation.

`EPT-INVEPT` now includes `NVMX-EPT-008`.  A separate cross-ledger validator
requires every pending-live requirement to occur in exactly one hardware
feature group and rejects missing, duplicated, or unknown IDs.  Its rootless
negative fixture is part of the aggregate host regression.  The current
ledger has 196 requirements: 191 foundation-tested experimental entries and
five live-gated entries, all five mapped exactly once across the ten mandatory
hardware feature groups.  This improves the qualification proof; it does not
claim that the pending Intel run has occurred.

The aggregate source-tree regression also exposed an installation/source mode
drift: the nested requirements validator is installed as mode 0555, but its
source inode was mode 0644, so the gate rejected it after completing the full
device harness.  The source mode now matches the installed contract.  The
device prefix completed with zero failed checks, including 1,195,896 packed
ring states, and the repaired nested tail passes the 196-entry validator, the
cross-ledger negative fixture, all 147 ASan/UBSan model cases, the evidence
validator, and the production `vmm.ko` warnings-as-errors build.

## 2026-07-31 production-build and publication-ownership review

The Intel nested-VMX follow-up found that otherwise valid VMCS queries could
publish a field, count, launch state, epoch, or abort indicator through storage
inside the guest VMCS image, the immutable host capability policy, or another
output.  The software-owned MSR list similarly allowed its count to alias the
input bank or output entries, and allowed the output entries to overwrite the
input bank while it was still being read.  A second direct-adapter pass also
found that virtual-MSR reads could publish into their retained context,
capability, control, architectural, or software-MSR objects, and that a
capture destination could overwrite its callback table.  The direct
boundaries now reject the complete ownership graph before publication, VMCS
images and capability policies must be disjoint even for initialization, and
rejected calls leave all inputs and outputs retryable.  Focused negative
coverage is part of the
147-case nested model; the independent 169-entry requirements validator and
live-evidence schema remain green.  This is model/build evidence only: VMX
guest exposure remains disabled until the recorded Intel live gates pass.

The following value-planning pass applied the same rule to VMCS02 control
policy composition, fixed-point nested TSC composition, and resumed-L2
hardware-result classification.  Each implementation already staged a local
candidate, but a successful final assignment could still overwrite an input
policy, control image, time-composition request, raw hardware report, or
captured exit.  Those result ranges are now rejected before calculation, and
