the negative cases prove both source immutability and a later ordinary call.
The complete TSC planner was then checked rather than only its scaling helper:
offset-only and emulated-IA32_TSC-write plans now enforce the same disjoint
publication contract, including the timer-bearing write request.

The final hardware-attempt boundary now applies that contract end to end.  A
raw VMX report cannot be prepared over its captured VMCS02 exit, its
classification cannot overwrite the report, and an initial or resumed attempt
plan cannot overwrite either immutable input.  The negative model case checks
source immutability and then repeats an ordinary classification, preventing an
alias rejection from concealing destructive partial work.

Capability publication received the same ABI review.  Virtual-policy build,
canonical wire encode/decode, signatures, capability-MSR reads, raw hardware
control selection, and virtual `IA32_FEATURE_CONTROL` access now reject output
or mutable-state ranges inside their immutable policy inputs.  The focused
tests preserve every source across rejection and immediately retry the normal
operation, covering both portable state and production control-MSR adapters.

Event arbitration and task-priority publication were the next bounded slice.
Generic and VM-entry event plans, reflected-exit images, transient window
controls, and CR8 reads now reject results inside their retained input or
descriptor objects.  This keeps the event source immutable until the later
entry/exit commit point and prevents a successful query from corrupting the
callback table used to obtain it.

The VMX-instruction capture boundary also had a compound publication hazard:
the capture result or handoff identifier could alias instruction metadata,
capability policy, the live nested context, or one another.  Those ownership
relations are now validated before capture or context mutation.  Tests cover
the permission gate, pure capture, and context-bound publication, including a
normal retry after every rejected alias.

Entry-environment construction exposed the highest-impact alias in this pass.
Its final VMCS02 input is a pointer-bearing borrowed view, so publishing it over
the environment, VMCS12 snapshot, identity, capabilities, entry state, or any
pointed preparation object could destroy an owner and retain pointers into the
destroyed bytes.  Preparation, adapter capture, VMCS12 derivation, and final
binding now validate their complete known ownership graphs before callbacks or
publication.  Opaque callback arguments remain governed by the callback
contract because their extent is intentionally not known to this layer.

Finally, VMX operand decoding now treats its diagnostic enum as a second
publication rather than harmless scratch.  Operand/address results and failure
details must be pairwise disjoint and outside the immutable operand, register,
and segment arrays.  This closes error paths that could otherwise corrupt an
input while claiming merely to describe why decoding failed.

Qualification now compiles the complete 15-module in-tree 5BSD VirtIO guest
stack before accepting live evidence.  The VM-free and nested profiles also
compile the production `vmm.ko` in an isolated object tree, so architectural
nested models cannot hide a compiler or linker regression in the kernel
module that will run on the Intel host.  Both module gates pass with the
tree's mandatory warnings as errors.  They remain build evidence, not guest
activation or accelerated-L2 evidence.

The RTC alarm public boundary had one owner-alias defect.  A direct caller
could place notification output or its completion-length word inside the live
alarm object, causing publication to overwrite the mutex while it was held.
The control helper similarly allowed response or length storage to alias the
request or live alarm.  Both paths now validate the complete ownership graph
before the first write or alarm transition.  Rejection preserves pending
notification, configuration, and completion length so a corrected request is
retryable.  The independent negative case covers live-object, request,
response, and pairwise output aliases; all seven focused RTC alarm cases pass.

The same review lens found queue-publication defects in the provisional GPU
and IOMMU adapters.  Both cleared a caller-owned used-length word before
proving it was disjoint from queue metadata, and their scatter paths allowed
overlapping writable fragments to corrupt traversal state or publish one
response twice.  The IOMMU form also permitted response storage to alias its
request options or live translation tables.  Both adapters now validate the
complete ownership graph before their first write or retained-state change,
permit readable/writable in-place data only because the complete request is
gathered first, and preserve state and completion on rejection.  Focused
negative tests cover metadata, completion, live-state, options, and pairwise
writable aliases followed by a successful unaliased retry.

The next adapter scan found the same early-publication pattern across the
VirtIO-sound control and PCM helpers.  Completion, claim, header, and
payload-length outputs could overlap iovec metadata, live host state, capture
source, or one another; overlapping writable fragments also made a response
order-dependent.  One shared bounded ownership validator now covers every
synchronous and asynchronous sound queue entry, and the PCI composition uses
that same 256-segment limit instead of a private duplicate.  The independent
test rejects every ownership class without changing lifecycle or completion,
then proves a normal completion remains retryable; all sound queue cases pass
with warnings as errors.  The lower host API now independently enforces the
same rule for control, PCM, claims, finishes, and stream-query results, so a
new transport cannot bypass safety by omitting queue staging; all host cases,
including direct live-state and input/output aliases, also pass.

The same public-boundary audit covered the non-DAX VirtIO-fs host shim.
FUSE request-context and completion storage could previously be placed inside
the live session or input request, letting context initialization or the
initial zero used-length publication alter the request before validation.
Acceptance, response completion, and the synchronous backend wrapper now
reject the complete alias graph before INIT changes an incarnation or invokes
the backend.  The independent test proves session, request, context, response,
and completion preservation followed by a successful retry; all host-shim
cases pass.

The audit then followed ownership into the asynchronous filesystem dispatch
and pending table.  Direct header, owner-cookie, count, drain-array, guest
response, and completion publications could alias retained request tables or
one another even though the queue wrapper normally supplied separate storage.
Both layers now reject wrapping, state, input/output, and pairwise output
aliases before accepting INIT, cancelling, pausing, draining, or retiring a
guest chain.  The negative cases prove that rejected submissions and
completions leave the exact request owner retryable, and that a valid retry or
selective drain still completes once.

The VirtIO-memory host API had equivalent direct-call gaps outside its queue
composition: configuration, snapshot-size, response, and used-length storage
could overlap the host or its ownership bitmaps, while request and response
storage could overlap each other.  These extents are now validated before the
first completion write or platform memory callback.  The focused negative
case preserves the completion sentinel and performs no host range operation
for every rejected alias, then plugs the same block successfully on retry.

Balloon PFN tracking and statistics were next.  Inflate/deflate outputs could
alias the retained tracker or bitmap, accounting's changed flag could alias
its counters, and parsed PFN/statistics results could overlap scatter
metadata or readable fragments.  The host helpers now validate the complete
ownership graph before changing a bit or invoking a callback, and independently
bound iovec metadata to the device's 128-entry ring even when every fragment
is empty.  Negative tests cover live-state, bitmap, pairwise output, metadata,
payload, and excessive-vector aliases, followed by valid tracker transitions.

The administration queue adapter already rejected aliasing, but the lower
owner and group APIs did not independently preserve that contract.  Direct
status, qualifier, result, used-length, registration, and snapshot-size
storage can no longer overlap mutex-bearing owners, the fabric, nested owners,
command input, or peer outputs.  Rejection occurs before the one-way topology
seal and before handler or lifecycle callbacks.  The negative case confirms
that rejected calls leave both owner and fabric unsealed, then executes the
same LIST_QUERY successfully through each boundary.

The capability and resource managers now enforce the same rule at their
direct host APIs.  Capability data, size, driver-set, and snapshot-size
results, and resource flags, payload, count, limit, stage, and size results,
must be disjoint from every mutex-bearing manager, retained object, input,
and peer output before publication.  Registration and mutation inputs cannot
borrow live manager storage.  A staged resource query also checks capacity
before publishing flags or size, so `ENOSPC` is transactional.  The negative
cases retain sentinels across manager, retained-payload, pairwise-output,
restore-result, staged-state, and undersized-output failures, then perform a
valid update and query through the same objects.

The device-parts composition and its callback handler were then checked as a
separate ownership boundary rather than relying on the nested managers.
Capability limits, resource objects, member IDs, usage counters, metadata,
captured parts, used lengths, and snapshot sizes are now checked against the
outer composition, handler, nested managers, retained objects, inputs, and
peer outputs before validation callbacks or publication.  This closes the
case where a direct host caller could avoid the lower manager's protections
by aliasing the outer composition mutex.  Focused negative cases retain
sentinels and then complete valid metadata and resource queries.

The adjacent SR-IOV lifecycle wrapper had the same narrow direct-output gap:
state and qualifier publication could target its read/write lock.  Both are
now rejected while holding and then releasing the read lease.  The regression
proves a rejected begin does not strand that lease by completing an exclusive
VF-count update before a valid command lease.

The complete rootless device harness after the RTC, GPU, IOMMU, sound,
filesystem, memory, balloon, and administration publication pass is green.
It includes
1,195,896 independent packed-ring state checks and the final net, SCSI,
console, input, 9P, RTC, memory, balloon, sound, GPU, IOMMU, administration,
and save-state suites; every program reported zero failures.  A source-paired
world build is still required for the
snapshot-enabled bhyve link: the running host's installed `machine/vmm*.h`
predates the tree's CPUID/CPU-compatibility ioctl ABI, and duplicating that ABI
into userspace would conceal rather than solve the deployment mismatch.

## 2026-07-31 guest SCSI and nested-evidence review

The 5BSD VirtIO-SCSI control path no longer contains its unused unbounded
busy-poll completion mode.  Every control request in the driver is
interrupt-driven and supplies an asynchronous completion callback, so the
dead polling flags, loop, and execution selector were removed instead of
retaining an unreachable indefinite wait.  The rebuilt `virtio_scsi.ko`
module compiles and links with warnings as errors.

The command completion path now bounds a device-reported sense length by both
the fixed 96-byte VirtIO response field and the CAM destination.  This closes
an out-of-bounds response read when a malformed device reports a larger
length.  The implementation follows the pinned Linux driver's observable
clamping behavior while also respecting FreeBSD's possibly shorter CAM
buffer.  An independent CS01-derived contract covers zero, exact, one-past,
`UINT32_MAX`, and short-destination cases; the complete guest contract program
passes.  The requirements ledger now contains 191 validated entries.

Nested-VMX live evidence is bound to one qualification invocation by a fresh
opaque run identifier, and every guest assertion and host trace carries
strict UTC start and finish timestamps.  Validation rejects stale or mixed
bundles, malformed times, and reversed intervals.  The host helper suite
passes both the positive bundle and these negative cases.  The separate
nested ledger remains clean at 169 requirements and ten mandatory live
feature groups; hardware execution is still pending rather than inferred
from rootless models.

## 2026-07-31 ACCESS_PLATFORM ownership review

The common DMA-domain lease audit found one device-private exception in the
provisional VirtIO-GPU adapter.  Backing validation acquired a domain lease,
but the later guest-memory read and write callbacks performed a fresh mapping
and copy after that lease had been released.  Both copy operations now hold a
lease from before translation until after the final byte is copied, so IOMMU
detach, endpoint reassignment, reset, and restore cannot retire the provider
under an in-progress transfer.  The independent PCI adapter test covers read,
write, a closed detach gate, mapping failure, and exact acquire/release
accounting; the focused suite passes 7 of 7 cases
(`usr_obj_usr_src_amd64.amd64_tests_sys_kern_vsock_device_harness.
20260731-112609-096285`).

All production VirtIO devices keep a per-instance `virtio_consts` copy before
ACCESS_PLATFORM is added, so feature publication cannot leak between VMs or
between two instances of a device.  Queue enable holds a device-private DMA
lease, descriptor and payload translations inherit a request lease, shared
GPU BAR accesses hold an explicit lease, and checkpoint translation executes
behind the common quiesce fence.  The remaining common-IOMMU work is topology,
fault, invalidation, and restore qualification rather than an accepted
unleased mapping path.

## 2026-07-31 restore-boundary review

The common restore transaction now preserves an explicit runtime-only
restore-incomplete latch.  This closes a cross-layer failure mode where a
device detected that compensation of an external side effect had failed and
set `NEEDS_RESET`, after which the generic rollback restored the old status
byte and hid the inconsistency.  Balloon backing-page transitions, network
backend framing reconstruction, virtio-mem range reconstruction, and
virtio-sound stream reconstruction now mark that latch when their compensating
operation fails.  Common rollback reasserts `NEEDS_RESET`, refuses another
snapshot operation, and requires a successful full device reset before reuse.
Mem and sound reset callbacks republish the latch after common reset when
backend repair or retained-request cancellation fails, so the status-zero
window cannot reopen checkpoint admission over unresolved host ownership.  The
independent core test proves that ordinary device failures remain exactly
transactional while an explicitly incomplete external rollback remains
visible after the common queue/cache rollback.

The kernel snapshot ioctl now also enforces the userspace/kernel operation
boundary before dispatch.  `VM_SNAPSHOT_VALIDATE` exists so bhyve device
codecs can parse an immutable restore image without publication, but it is not
a kernel ABI operation.  Previously an ioctl caller could pass that value into
VM-wide architecture callbacks; leaf buffer operations normally rejected it,
but nested-VMX restore setup may allocate staged destination resources before
the first buffer access.  `vm_snapshot_req()` now accepts only SAVE and
RESTORE, including through the compatibility ioctl, and the independent
`vmm_snapshot_op_test` covers validation and unknown enum values.

The VirtIO-GPU presentation path now captures scanout geometry, format, and
pixels under one state lock.  A concurrent guest resource or scanout change
can no longer mix metadata from one generation with pixels from another.
Capture failure preserves the last valid host frame; only an explicit guest
scanout disable blanks it.  Independent tests cover complete capture,
undersized destinations, concurrent-state boundaries, frame preservation,
and explicit disable.

Portable restore validation now rejects input records that alias the live
object graph before decoding or mutation.  This fail-before-commit rule is
covered for VirtIO memory, sound, GPU, IOMMU, and the administration,
device-group, capability, device-parts, resource, and queue foundations,
including multi-owner administration restore.  The complete rootless
device-harness regression passed 838 of 838 tests after these changes
(`usr_obj_usr_src_amd64.amd64_tests_sys_kern_vsock_device_harness.
20260731-102710-509642`).

A follow-up capability-manager audit extended that boundary to both owned
capability allocations.  Immutable device-policy bytes are protected as well
as mutable driver-selected bytes, so snapshot cannot overwrite destination
policy and restore cannot treat a small internal allocation as a larger
portable record.  The focused capability suite passes 5 of 5 cases.

The same ownership rule now covers the GPU's non-snapshot read boundary.
Resource reads, scanout metadata, full and cropped scanout capture, and cursor
capture reject output storage inside the live GPU state, resource table,
pixels, or backing table.  This prevents overlapping `memcpy` and metadata
corruption even for non-production callers; the focused GPU state and PCI
suites pass 21 of 21 cases and bhyve links cleanly with `-Werror`.  The
complete rootless harness remains green at 838 of 838 tests
(`usr_obj_usr_src_amd64.amd64_tests_sys_kern_vsock_device_harness.
20260731-103633-862165`).

The GPU display adapter no longer treats a native `uint32_t` store as a
portable XRGB byte stream.  Its presentation boundary is explicitly
`B8G8R8X8` (`B,G,R,0`) on every host, cursor composition reads and writes that
same byte contract, and the independent tests assert raw bytes instead of
decoding output with the host's integer endianness.  A production display
backend remains a separate live qualification gate.

The live-activation audit no longer leaves the implemented VirtIO-fs Linux
paths detached from the qualification graph.  The split one- and two-request
queue cases and packed eight-request-queue case are now the explicit pending
gates for session negotiation and queue topology; the two- and eight-queue
lanes also own the read-only backend-isolation contract.  These rows remain
`pending`, not `exercised`, until a root run correlates the guest mount and
queue assertions with the host INIT, queue-class, and audit evidence.

The same test-quality pass found that the VirtIO-fs session checkpoint API
protected only the dispatch allocation from an overlapping output or restore
record.  A caller could instead place that record over the pending-entry
table, pending hash buckets, cancellation tombstones, or tombstone buckets.
The complete immutable ownership graph is now rejected before the session is
read or written.  The focused dispatch suite directly targets every owned
allocation and passes 8 of 8 cases; the production bhyve binary also rebuilds
and links with the tree's mandatory warnings as errors.  The complete
ASan/UBSan harness subsequently passed every stage, including the exhaustive
packed-ring models, and the ordinary ATF regression remains green at 838 of
838 tests
(`usr_obj_usr_src_amd64.amd64_tests_sys_kern_vsock_device_harness.
20260731-104654-136996`).

The adjacent event-driven backend checkpoint copy is now a true multi-output
transaction as well.  It rejects output ranges that overlap the connection,
receive/control buffers, retained backend state, or one another before
publishing the required length or copying any session data.  The focused
connection suite targets each alias class and passes 11 of 11 cases; bhyve
again rebuilds and links cleanly.  The complete post-fix ATF regression passed
838 of 838 tests with no broken or skipped cases
(`usr_obj_usr_src_amd64.amd64_tests_sys_kern_vsock_device_harness.
20260731-105117-444387`).

The activation ledger also distinguishes missing guest support from missing
execution.  Pinned upstream Linux has no VirtIO 1.4 Device Suspend feature,
and the stock 5BSD net and block drivers do not implement RSS/HASH_REPORT or
WRITE_ZEROES despite the block ABI naming the latter.  Those are now explicit
`driver-gap` entries rather than misleading unscheduled `pending` tests.  The
custom 5BSD Device Suspend lane remains scheduled and pending.

The backend transport output boundary now follows the same transactional
ownership rule.  Header, payload, and payload-length destinations for a
received `SOCK_SEQPACKET` frame must be disjoint, and invalid aliases are
rejected before `recvmsg()` consumes the record.  Outbox completion metadata
likewise cannot overwrite the queue object or retained frame.  Focused tests
prove rejection, preservation, and successful retry.

A lifecycle/concurrency pass then found that simultaneous selective
VirtIO-fs queue resets shared post-lock completion scratch.  One reset could
overwrite another reset's remaining guest cookies while its discard callback
was running.  Selective reset now owns a private bounded completion vector,
retaining callback reentrancy without exposing cross-reset state.  A
deterministic two-thread test blocks the first callback, completes a second
queue reset, and proves all four chains are discarded exactly once.

The ACCESS_PLATFORM review applied fail-before-commit to the
VirtIO-IOMMU wire boundary.  Request decoding now uses a local candidate,
preserves the caller's output on every malformed or reserved-field failure,
and rejects input/output aliasing before parsing.  Fault-event encoding stages
the complete 24-byte record before publication, so even an overlapping source
cannot be zeroed before its fields are read.  Independent exact-wire, failure
immutability, and alias tests pass 6 of 6 cases.

The IOMMU request executor is now a disjoint multi-output transaction too.
Guest input, response storage, used-length publication, request options, and
the complete live IOMMU allocation graph are checked before `used_length` is
cleared or any ATTACH/MAP/UNMAP state transition runs.  This prevents a
malformed direct caller from using completion storage to overwrite the
control plane.  The focused request and state suites pass 23 of 23 cases,
including retry-after-rejection and continued endpoint operation.

Sanitizer execution then exposed a false pointer/length contract in the
IOMMU request queue: it intentionally gathered at most the largest 72-byte
request, but passed the guest's potentially megabyte logical length as the
size of that stack buffer.  Decoding and execution now carry available bytes
separately from logical request length.  Oversized known requests still
produce the required invalid status, oversized unknown requests remain
zero-used, and no component invents an addressable extent.  Protocol,
executor, and fragmented/oversized queue tests pass 16 of 16 cases.

Fault-event publication now validates its entire writable iovec graph before
clearing used length or removing a fault from the bounded FIFO.  The iovec
array, used-length word, live IOMMU graph, and every destination fragment must
be disjoint, including pairwise fragment overlap.  A rejected chain therefore
cannot consume or partially publish an event; the focused three-case suite
proves exact retry delivery.

The complete rebuilt ATF regression after the VirtIO-fs concurrency and
VirtIO-IOMMU transaction changes passes 845 of 845 tests, with no failed,
broken, or skipped cases
(`usr_obj_usr_src_amd64.amd64_tests_sys_kern_vsock_device_harness.
20260731-110625-873334`).  This is post-link evidence from newly rebuilt test
programs, not reuse of the earlier 838-test result.

The administration-queue scatter/gather boundary now rejects ownership
aliases before it gathers input, dispatches a command, or clears completion
metadata.  Descriptor metadata, input/output scratch, the used-length word,
and every guest vector must be disjoint from internal publication storage;
writable vectors must also be pairwise disjoint.  Rejected chains leave both
the output and completion word unchanged and can be corrected and retried.
The bank-level portable-state boundary now includes every queue's
preallocated input and output scratch allocation as well as the bank, queue
metadata, fabric, and command owners.  Snapshot and restore therefore reject
scratch aliases before writing or decoding even when the claimed portable
extent is larger than the scratch allocation.  The focused rebuilt
administration suite passes 19 of 19 cases
(`usr_obj_usr_src_amd64.amd64_tests_sys_kern_vsock_device_harness.
20260731-111521-399414`).

The fixed-width checkpoint compatibility envelope is now transactional at
both codec boundaries.  Encoding stages all portable bytes before publishing
them, and decoding validates a local candidate before replacing the caller's
structure.  Exact source/destination overlap is therefore supported without
reading bytes after they have been overwritten, while a malformed envelope
leaves the previous destination contract intact.  Compatibility comparisons
also require canonical zero-filled string tails and use bounded comparisons,
so a direct caller cannot turn a missing terminator into an out-of-bounds
read.  The focused codec and PCI preflight suites pass 13 of 13 cases
(`usr_obj_usr_src_amd64.amd64_tests_sys_kern_vsock_device_harness.
20260731-111705-293160`).

A dependency-complete bhyve rebuild then exposed that the public libvmmapi
prototype for the new CPU compatibility query relied on an installed
`machine/vmm.h` already defining `struct vm_cpu_compat`.  That breaks the
supported source-newer-than-installed-header build and is diagnosed as a
visibility error under `-Werror`.  The public header now carries the required
opaque forward declaration; bhyve subsequently rebuilt every
header-dependent object and linked cleanly.

The settled-source ASan/UBSan harness then completed every stage with zero
failures, including the exhaustive packed-ring state models and the expanded
511-check portability/administration segment.  A dependency-complete ATF
rebuild and run passes 847 of 847 tests with no failed, broken, or skipped
cases
(`usr_obj_usr_src_amd64.amd64_tests_sys_kern_vsock_device_harness.
20260731-112146-581032`).

## Latest production-boundary review

The CTL prerequisite for VirtIO-SCSI events is now implemented.  A versioned
per-open inventory subscription provides an initial RESCAN barrier, monotonic
sequence numbers, bounded queues, poll/kqueue readiness, and explicit loss
boundaries.  bhyve advertises HOTPLUG and CHANGE only after that subscription
succeeds; an older kernel therefore remains fail-closed instead of falling
back to polling.

VirtIO sound backend identity is no longer implicit.  The launch surface,
Linux runner, manifest resume contract, manual pages, independent device test,
and requirements ledger all name `backend=null`; any other name is rejected.
This preserves the deterministic qualification backend and prevents a future
host-audio implementation from silently changing side effects or checkpoint
compatibility.  A real audio backend still requires an asynchronous bounded
ownership layer, because blocking host PCM calls may not execute on a vCPU
notify path.  The release coverage ledger now has 58 contracts and the full
qualification ledger has 71 contracts across 105 cases.

## VirtIO-IOMMU and administration foundation

The rootless VirtIO-IOMMU conformance pass now covers protocol, topology,
request, event, queue, portable-state, VIOT, and Linux live-harness
construction. Unknown request types and unnegotiated PROBE requests complete
with zero used bytes as required by VirtIO 1.4 section 5.13.6; known but
unnegotiated MAP and UNMAP operations retain their specified unsupported
status. Mapping traversal uses a maintained high-water bound instead of
scanning the entire configured table. Linux live and checkpoint cases are
present in `virtio-lab`, but remain a root/updated-host qualification gate and
are not recorded as passed by this rootless review.

The administration/device-parts layer remains deliberately unadvertised while
device-parts capability negotiation, a concrete owner/member model, and PCI
administration-queue composition are incomplete. Its owner now supports
atomic monotonic command-set registration and bounded dispatch outside the
command-list mutex, which lets resource-object handlers remain
transport-neutral and makes restore reject destinations that lack a command
used by the source.

The generic resource-object manager implements CS01 section 2.12.1.3 without
assuming PCI, SR-IOV, or a host architecture. It enforces per-type
driver-selected ID limits, unique and reusable IDs, exact last-successful
query state, no-side-effect failed modification, errno-compatible statuses,
newer-to-older dependency creation, reverse-order `EBUSY` teardown, and
reset-time destruction. Its `ROS1` save-state record is fixed-width
little-endian, checksummed, pointer-free, dependency-validated, and
transactional on an incompatible destination. The independent test oracle
also protects the specification's easy-to-miss opcode assignment: resource
QUERY is `0x0b`, while MODIFY is `0x0c`.

The device-parts wire codec validates each literal PCI common-configuration
selector against the exact field width from VirtIO 1.4 section 2.14,
including notification-data, queue-reset, and administration queue fields.
Focused independent tests cover every one-, two-, and four-byte field and
reject holes, mismatched widths, reserved device-status bits, and invalid
queue-enable values.

## Current milestone

The current tree implements and tests the modern PCI split-ring transport,
the currently advertised common features, net/block/SCSI multiqueue, net RSS
and hash reporting, block write-zeroes and write-cache control, multi-provider
kernel vsock, modern balloon and RTC devices, and versioned save-state for all
supported bhyve VirtIO devices.

Block activation is no longer negotiation-only for DISCARD or CONFIG_WCE.
The Linux verifier writes an independent deterministic pattern, applies
WRITE ZEROES and DISCARD to separate ranges, validates advertised queue
limits and the complete digest, then rechecks its explicit deterministic
post-DISCARD write and the whole-device digest after reboot.  It does not
infer any readback content from DISCARD.  CONFIG_WCE is changed through both
modes repeatedly with a readback after every
transition.  The rootless oracle and manifest gates pass; a privileged
`block-modern-q1` run remains the live acceptance result for this source
state.

A dedicated `block-discard-modern` case owns the backend-dependent DISCARD
requirement.  Ordinary block cases continue to qualify portable mandatory and
unconditionally advertised behavior even when their host filesystem cannot
deallocate ranges.

The common NOTIFICATION_DATA claim now has a dedicated live assertion.  The
guest must negotiate bit 38 and perform block I/O; a debug trace must then
show bhyve decoding a nonzero available index alongside the queue number from
the selected 32-bit doorbell path.  This is scheduled and rootless-validated,
but still awaits the next installed-world release run.

A separate read-only lane now verifies the complete advertised contract:
Linux negotiates RO, declines media-modifying DISCARD and WRITE_ZEROES,
successfully reads the disk, cannot write it, then repeats those assertions
after reset.  This closes the former test-plan gap but is not recorded as a
live pass until the installed-world release matrix runs it.

VirtIO-SCSI now accepts the document's exact REPORT LUNS well-known address
and maps it to CTL's explicit no-LUN command path.  Malformed extended
addresses remain rejected, and task-management commands cannot target that
well-known LUN.  The unit test drives the request through CTL submission and
checks the unmapped target value; live Linux discovery remains a root
qualification gate.

Existing device state is encoded with fixed-width little-endian scalars,
bounded byte strings, explicit magic/version fields, restore validation, and
rollback.  Common modern PCI state includes negotiated feature windows,
status/config generation, ISR/vector state, queue enable/reset state, guest
physical addresses, indices, and queue generations.  Host pointers, mutexes,
condition variables, and file descriptor numbers are not serialized.

The common queue engine now obtains DMA mappings and raises interrupts through
platform operations.  The default operations preserve PCI direct-DMA,
MSI-X/MSI, and INTx behavior; future ACCESS_PLATFORM and non-PCI work can
replace those operations without teaching device models about an IOMMU or
interrupt controller.  The mapping operation deliberately accepts a DMA
address, not a presumed guest physical address.

The endpoint-DMA audit is now executable rather than a prose convention.
`validate-virtio-dma-boundary.sh` rejects direct guest-address mapping from
every VirtIO device model, permits the two reviewed raw mappings only inside
the IOMMU provider, and pins GPU backing reads to `vi_map_dma()`.  Focused
IOMMU tests also prove that changing default bypass affects future
authorizations without invalidating an already leased request. Mutex creation
errors are preserved instead of being incorrectly collapsed to `ENOMEM`.

The pending 5BSD qualification lane now exercises three mechanisms that were
previously Linux-only or unscheduled: a nonzero available index in a 32-bit
`NOTIFICATION_DATA` block doorbell, repeated selective RNG queue reset with a
concurrent entropy reader and paired DTrace reset probes, and a named
virtio-console port carrying distinct tokens in both directions over packed
queues. The release manifest treats both enabled and disabled values as
coverage obligations. These are scheduled gates, not recorded live passes.

Checkpoint publication now uses manifest version 3 with an explicit host
architecture and machine ABI plus canonical SHA-256 digests for the guest-RAM,
kernel/device-state, and JSON-metadata members.  Restore rejects member
mutation before publishing any VM or device state.  Because no checkpoint ABI
has shipped, restore accepts only the current version-3 manifest and rejects
every older manifest before parsing its fields or publishing VM/device state,
as well as unknown host architectures and architecture or machine-ABI
mismatches.

The portable record work does not claim that every older bhyve snapshot
section is a cross-architecture ABI.  Future arm64 work must retain the
portable device records while supplying architecture-specific CPU and
interrupt state behind a richer compatibility contract.

## Rotating review result

### A. Normative conformance

- The pinned OASIS VirtIO 1.4 CS01 source is authoritative.
- The authenticated local corpus is under `/tmp/waspnest-reference`; it
  contains the VirtIO CS01 artifact, Intel SDM volumes 3 and 4 revision 092,
  and the pinned Linux and QEMU source archives.  The catalog validator
  verifies every artifact against its recorded SHA-256.
- The Intel nested-VMX requirements ledger has 166 validated entries.  Its gate
  requires every external authority to be an immutable corpus ID and every
  foundation claim to name a compiled implementation symbol and registered
  ATF case.
- Independent fixtures contain 630 checked oracle definitions.
- Tests reject dependencies on production wire-layout and endian helpers.
- Packed rings remain unadvertised by default while explicit modern split and
  packed qualification lanes cover every current VirtIO device.
  ACCESS_PLATFORM/IOMMU, shared-memory consumers, administration virtqueues,
  and device groups remain unadvertised.  The shared-memory PCI transport
  foundation independently validates the document's exact cap64 layout,
  memory-BAR containment, overflow, and unique region-ID rules; it has no
  consumer and therefore exposes no capability in a live device.

### B. Lifecycle and concurrency

- Queue reset uses generation fencing and per-device quiesce.
- Queue-owned split and packed request leases are consumed exactly once.
  Requests retain their acquisition layout across reset; packed reset drops
  reorder-only state while preserving live backend ownership until a stale
  generation callback retires it.
- ACCESS_PLATFORM domain detachment is fenced by a common active-request
  count, keeping release callbacks valid through late reset completions.
- Checkpoint pause/resume ownership is retryable and rollback-aware.
- Packed restore transactionally replaces a differently-sized empty
  destination reorder cache and retains the old allocation until the complete
  device restore commits; a late device-specific failure restores the original
  queue and allocation.
- SCSI draining and kernel-vsock provider freeze are bounded to 30 seconds.
- Kernel-vsock thaw failure retains ownership for a safe retry.
- Console selective receive-queue reset now clears the exact port's readiness
  latch under the VirtIO mutex and requests disable of its host read source
  before returning.  The backend-neutral disable hook prevents repeated
  level-triggered delivery once the event-loop update is applied; a callback
  selected earlier must acquire the same mutex and observes the cleared latch
  before descriptor or host-byte access.  Other ports remain active, and only
  a guest kick on the replacement queue rearms the source.
- Console receive and transmit callbacks now reject a callback descriptor
  that does not identify the port's current connection.  This closes the
  asynchronous mevent-delete/reconnect window in which an event selected for
  a closed session could otherwise consume bytes or drain output through a
  newer session stored in the same persistent port object.  Same-number
  descriptor reuse cannot bypass the fence because mevent refuses an fd/type
  registration until deletion of the old tuple reaches the event-loop
  boundary.
- 9P refuses non-portable active fid state and now changes negotiated
  connection state atomically.
- Full device reset still waits for guest-buffer/backend ownership to drain.
  Replacing those waits requires a real cancellation contract; arbitrary
  timeouts would permit use-after-reset and are not an accepted workaround.

### C. Portability and state compatibility

- `snapshot_portable.h` has independent unaligned byte-vector and boundary
  tests.
- Manifest parsing has malformed, truncated, reordered, oversized, legacy,
  architecture-mismatch, and machine-mismatch coverage.
- A structural gate rejects native snapshot macros, host page-size
  dependencies, and native scalar-width serialization in converted records.
- Device records have explicit framing and bounded allocations.
- Modern Linux and 5BSD live operation is verified on amd64.  Real arm64 and
  big-endian restore interoperability is not yet verified and remains a
  release requirement for those host ports.
- Modern device-configuration callbacks now cross one explicit little-endian
  byte-to-host-numeric boundary.  Balloon, GPU, input, memory, sound, IOMMU,
  and virtio-fs no longer rely on the Intel host representation for partial
  configuration reads or writable configuration fields.  Literal byte-vector
  tests cover one-, two-, and four-byte unaligned reads and invalid ranges;
  a real big-endian host remains an external qualification gate.
- Virtio-input capability ioctls return native `unsigned long` bitmaps.  The
  device now converts each native bit number into the specification's byte
  bitmap explicitly; it no longer depends on little-endian host word layout.
  The independent ioctl fixture sets properties and keys numerically in host
  words and verifies the exact VirtIO bytes.

### D. Linux and QEMU comparison

- Linux is pinned as the guest-driver and KVM behavior reference.
- QEMU is pinned as the device-model and migration-state comparison.
- Linux's synchronous control-command progress and EVENT_IDX re-arm/recheck
  behavior are represented in the net tests.
- QEMU's versioned feature-window and queue-state approach is reflected in
  the modern transport state.
- QEMU also saves packed-ring wrap state.  bhyve's versioned modern queue
  record now preserves packed available/used cursors and both wrap counters,
  while retaining the prior split-ring byte stream.
- Packed-ring staging has a document-derived independent model and a
  production engine.  Direct and indirect acquisition, completion,
  notification suppression, queue reset, stale-completion fencing, and
  save-state cursor validation pass focused tests.  A bounded common reorder
  table now safely serializes reverse-order asynchronous block and SCSI
  callbacks with unequal descriptor spans, including across the wrap
  boundary.  Group completion preserves a mergeable network packet's
  multi-chain visibility contract in both layouts.  The table is drained
  before checkpoint and excluded from the portable state stream.  Default
  advertisement remains disabled pending the Linux release and checkpoint
  qualification cases.  The conformance review also corrected packed used
  descriptors to set WRITE exactly when the reported used length is nonzero,
  as required by section 2.8.3 for data written anywhere in the complete
  buffer rather than merely in the overwritten head element.
- The modern traditional balloon device defaults to only inflate and deflate
  queues.  Its document-derived PFN parser, 4K/16K/64K native-page
  aggregation, bounded startup target, configuration layout, reset behavior,
  and fixed-width `BAL1` restore record pass independent negative and
  sanitizer tests.  Because PCI reclamation uses deferred `MADV_FREE`, the
  device now advertises MUST_TELL_HOST and cancels the complete native-page
  hint with the architecture-neutral undiscard operation before acknowledging
  deflation; cancellation failure enters `DEVICE_NEEDS_RESET`.  Requests above
  the Linux/FreeBSD 256-PFN compatibility boundary set
  `DEVICE_NEEDS_RESET` instead of being silently acknowledged.
  `deflate_on_oom=true` now exposes the standard guest-stability policy bit
  without bypassing that acknowledgement path.  The independent
  `free_page_reporting=true` option adds queue 4, accepts writable-only
  guest-RAM reports, reverse-resolves them through an architecture-neutral
  platform operation, and opportunistically discards aligned ranges before
  synchronous acknowledgement.  It deliberately leaves PAGE_POISON clear,
  so the guest treats reported pages as uninitialized.  The specification
  comparison also found and closed the non-contiguous optional-queue trap:
  reporting raises `num_queues` through queue 4, but absent free-page-hint
  queue 3 now reports size zero and a defensive notification cannot fall
  through into deflation.
  The qualification manifest now includes Linux split and packed
  balloon operation, target boundaries, combined-device operation,
  deflate-on-OOM negotiation, actual reporting-queue discard, checkpoint, and
  reset soak.  Linux/5BSD live inflation and observable resident-memory
  reduction remain root qualification gates.
- The modern RTC device implements the VirtIO 1.4 section 5.23 baseline with
  one UTC-like clock and an opt-in alarm capability; cross-timestamp remains
  unadvertised.
  It advertises `UTC_MAYBE_SMEARED`, rather than promising unsmeared UTC,
  because host `CLOCK_REALTIME` leap-second policy may step or smear.
  Independent byte-vector tests cover discovery, capability, nanosecond
  readings, reserved bytes, status precedence, short buffers, unsupported
  requests, and host clock failure.  The request engine is synchronous, so
  same-clock responses are read and completed in availability order.  The
  alarm uses one absolute `CLOCK_REALTIME` timerfd rather than periodic
  polling, preserves raised notifications across wall-clock steps, and
  reports timer failures through `DEVICE_NEEDS_RESET`.  Its version-2
  portable `RTC1` record embeds checksummed fixed-width alarm state; restore
  compares its deadline with the destination clock so an alarm elapsed during
  migration is not lost.  The former version-1 development decoder was later
  removed; only the current record is accepted.  A production PCI harness also verifies feature
  advertisement, packed opt-in, descriptor rejection, exact queue bytes,
  timer failure propagation, and `RTC1` snapshot rejection.  Linux comparison
  found that its driver intentionally exposes
  `UTC_MAYBE_SMEARED` through PTP rather than the RTC class; the live oracle
  now accepts exactly one related RTC or PTP clock and reads the actual class
  device instead of assuming an RTC node.  The qualification manifest now
  contains Linux split/packed alarm, reset, checkpoint, and combined RTC
  lanes; root execution remains pending.  Checkpoint pause takes the VirtIO
  device mutex before its final timer disarm, serializing against an
  event-loop callback which had already consumed a timerfd event.
  Resume rearming runs through `vc_resume_complete`, after the common quiesce
  and suspend fences are removed, so an already-expired one-shot alarm cannot
  fire under the fence and be lost.
- The common queue snapshot path now has a behavioral contract test for the
  production mapping helper.  It proves that the portable stream contains the
  canonical guest DMA address rather than a host pointer, that restore maps
  with the descriptor-specific DMA direction, and that duplicate-address,
  truncated, failed-map, and failed-publication cases cannot partially replace
  a live queue mapping.
- Non-DAX virtio-fs now has a registered modern-only PCI composition around
  the isolated protocol boundary.  It advertises the exact tag and request
  queue configuration, one high-priority queue, 1 through 64 request queues,
  packed-ring opt-in, and `VIRTIO_F_RING_RESET` only because cancellation is
  a mandatory backend capability.  The new bounded FUSE
  session validator independently covers little- and big-endian INIT,
  replacement sessions, high-priority queue classification, no-reply
  requests, exact input/output framing, backend disconnect, malformed
  responses, and atomic session-state updates.  Its private backend
  foundation also has fixed-width little-endian framing, bounded negotiation,
  reconnect incarnations, and state-preserving quiesce/thaw/shutdown
  failures.  The nonblocking Unix `SOCK_SEQPACKET` layer authenticates peer
  UID/GID and rejects truncated records and descriptor passing.  Outstanding
  backend connection and HELLO negotiation now run through a serialized
  readiness state machine which reports exact read/write interest, retains
  ownership across `EAGAIN`, fails closed on malformed or rejected
  selections, and transfers its descriptor only with an active bounded
  session.  The filesystem foundation sources are now part of the normal
  bhyve `-Werror` and DTrace build rather than being exercised only through
  isolated test translation units.  An active connection owner now composes
  negotiation, exact readiness interest, one-record-per-callback fairness,
  bounded receive storage, priority writes, validated completion, and atomic
  terminal failure of every retained guest chain.  Outstanding request
  ownership is now fixed-capacity, hashed, internally synchronized,
  cancellation-aware, and incarnation-fenced.  The portable `VFS1` codec
  requires exact backend quiescence and records negotiated backend
  capabilities/limits, identity, and bounded opaque backend state without
  native structures.  Restore also rejects unavailable VirtIO features and a
  destination backend whose quiesced capability or resource contract differs
  from the source.  A transport-neutral dispatcher now reserves ownership
  before publishing FUSE session transitions, defers replacement INIT across
  outstanding requests, validates replies before retirement, maps backend
  failures to portable FUSE EIO, and atomically drains ownership on
  disconnect.  A retained queue engine now copies descriptor metadata and
  request bytes, transactionally couples pending ownership with bounded
  priority-outbox publication, returns the runtime owner cookie atomically
  with retirement, scatters validated replies, completes disconnects with
  portable FUSE EIO, and discards old-generation chains without publishing
  stale used entries during reset.  Guest reset now drains ownership and
  clears the FUSE session without zeroing the authenticated backend
  incarnation, and a regression proves that the same queue accepts a fresh
  INIT afterward; terminal backend failure retains a separate disconnect
  path.  The lifecycle review also found and fixed an INIT half-publication
  bug that would otherwise have appeared when outbox allocation or capacity
  failed after dispatch acceptance.  Retained requests and unsent backend
  frames now have immutable queue identity, allowing an atomic selective
  reset without disturbing other queues.  Successful cancellation and
  cancellation/normal-response races now retire ownership into a
  fixed-capacity, incarnation-fenced FIFO tombstone index.  Full guest reset
  similarly tombstones sent reply-bearing requests, so a bounded late backend
  response is ignored without recovering a freed guest-chain owner or
  terminating the healthy connection.  Selective reset of already-sent
  ownership now publishes one bounded high-priority CANCEL at a time and
  advances from backend acknowledgements; cancellation rejection followed by
  terminal connection failure still discards reset-owned chains instead of
  publishing stale used entries.  The PCI device connects nonblocking backend
  readiness to `mevent`, retains kicks until negotiation completes, and
  reports selective-reset completion asynchronously after cancellation
  retires the final owner.  Rootless PCI, connection, queue, negative, and
  DTrace builds pass.  A production sandboxed backend daemon, backend
  checkpoint bridge now gives control messages a disjoint high-bit request-ID
  namespace, requires an explicit state-transfer capability in addition to
  freeze support, and permits a successful QUIESCE reply to carry one bounded
  opaque backend-state record.  An optional configured backend identity
  enables the snapshot callbacks; without it, normal filesystem operation
  remains compatible while checkpoint returns `ENOTSUP`.  Pause and resume
  hold device ownership across a bounded monotonic-condition wait driven by
  backend readiness, perform a real THAW if capture fails after quiesce, and
  leave rejected restore state retryable rather than silently reopening guest
  admission.  Restore validates the portable `VFS1` envelope, exact VirtIO
  features, backend identity, negotiated limits, and state length before
  replacing the retained session.  A production sandboxed backend daemon,
  live Linux filesystem qualification, and live backend checkpoint operations
  remain required before this can be considered release-qualified.
- Intel nested EPT now has a bounded, caller-sized runtime root cache
  foundation.  Exact EPTP configuration plus the virtual capability signature
  controls reuse, while L1 single-context INVEPT matches every cached
  configuration sharing the EPTRTA in bits 51:12.  Referenced roots cannot be
  evicted or checkpoint-quiesced, stale handles are generation-fenced, and
  runtime tokens are excluded from the portable nested-state envelope.  The
  cache is per-vCPU by contract and all-context invalidation visits nested
  roots only.  A kernel backend constructs empty EPT02 pmaps, removes their
  complete alias range on invalidation, and destroys them without publishing
  a host pointer into portable state.  A generation-checked resolver prevents
  stale or mismatched cache references from selecting a root.  A
  transactional L2-lifetime binding acquires a replacement before releasing
  the prior root, so allocation failure preserves the old execution resource;
  teardown releases that binding before destroying the cache.  The frozen-vCPU
  population path aliases
  the original managed guest-memory object rather than manufacturing an
  uncached physical mapping.  Its private EPT pmap uses software A/D
  bookkeeping, wired 4-KiB leaves, and a dedicated exact R/W/X operation so
  non-executable data is not made executable by the generic VM protection
  API.  A pure transactional fault planner independently checks translated
  page provenance and chooses population, EPT-violation reflection, or
  EPT-misconfiguration reflection.  Live fault publication and entry into L2
  remain intentionally unexposed.
  The ownership review established that nested instruction and EPT-fault
  handling must leave `vmmops_run()` first: that transition returns the vCPU
  to `VCPU_FROZEN` and exits the host critical section, after which the
  existing faulting guest-memory hold API is legal.  Calling
  `vm_gpa_hold()` or allocating EPT02 page tables inside `vmx_run()` would
  violate both contracts.  A generic internal exit and frozen callback now
  provide that architecture-neutral dispatch shape.  The internal exit is
  intentionally operation-neutral because VMX instruction operands and
  EPT12 faults both require potentially faulting guest-memory work outside
  the run critical section.  The Intel side now has
  an epoch-fenced, single-owner handoff state machine that publishes only
  architectural fault data in the VMX critical section, accepts ephemeral
  guest-memory accessors only in the frozen handler, retains retryable
  failures, and returns complete GPA/GLA/qualification reflection state for a
  later VMCS12 commit.  The Intel frozen callback now performs short-lived,
  faulting holds of aligned EPT12 entries, uses atomic 64-bit loads and
  compare/exchange for accessed/dirty updates, validates the held EPT02
  binding, and consumes only successful population plans.  It is initialized
  in every Intel vCPU but remains unreachable while nested exposure and L2
  entry are disabled.  No production entry path installs the active binding
  yet, and reflected plans remain retained until the VMCS12 exit transaction
  is connected.
  The review also found an architectural MBEC collision: EPT user-execute is
  bit 10, which the current amd64 pmap uses as `PG_MANAGED`.  MBEC therefore
  remains explicitly rejected by EPT02 population.  The production virtual
  capability builder now removes MBEC even when the physical CPU advertises
  MBEC and advanced EPT-violation information; the generic value-only model
  retains MBEC validation and walker coverage for a future safe pmap
  representation.  This is a fail-closed implementation boundary, not a
  claim of MBEC runtime support.  EPT supervisor-shadow-stack capability is
  likewise rejected because its EPTP bit-7 and leaf-permission semantics are
  not implemented; the policy can no longer advertise that unsupported
  behavior merely because a physical CPU reports it.
- The nested TSC planner composes the L0-to-L1 and enabled L1-to-L2 offsets
  with Intel's modulo-2^64 arithmetic and retains the VMCS01 offset for exit.
  A separate scaling path follows Intel's 64-by-64 product shifted by the
  48-bit fractional width and the pinned Linux nesting convention: the L1
  offset is signed-scaled by L2's multiplier before adding L2's offset, and
  both multipliers are composed for VMCS02.  It rejects active values behind
  disabled controls, L2 scaling without L2 TSC offsetting, zero active
  multipliers, and composed multipliers that underflow or overflow the
  64-bit VMCS field.  TSC scaling remains unexposed
  until VMCS02 programming, exit reconstruction, and live timer interaction
  are integrated.
- Baseline nested event routing now handles virtual external interrupts and
  NMIs without APICv or posted-interrupt shortcuts.  After higher-priority
  arbitration it defers across pending entry or reinjection, arms an
  L0-owned interrupt/NMI window while L2 blocks delivery, reflects an L1
  window exit before the lower-priority event, reflects intercepted events,
  and otherwise injects into L2.  Reflected external interrupts implement
  Intel's acknowledge-on-exit ownership distinction, while reflected and
  injected NMIs are consumed and establish NMI blocking.  A separate pure
  arbiter selects one eligible SMI, INIT, SIPI, high-priority exception, MTF,
  low-priority exception, preemption-timer, NMI-window, NMI,
  interrupt-window, or external-interrupt event without consuming caller
  state.  RESET and machine check remain L0-owned, hardware TPR-threshold
  handling stays outside this software planner, and the otherwise
  implementation-dependent external-intervention tie is deterministic.
  Live LAPIC integration and hardware exit publication remain required
  stages.
- Virtio-GPU 2D now has a modern PCI device, exact command framing, bounded
  resources and backing descriptors, atomic scatter/gather transfer, clipped
  scanout updates, cursor hotspot lifecycle, portable pixel conversion, and
  transactional restore.  The document-first comparison restored the
  required attach-backing-before-scanout sequence and aligned unknown optional
  commands with the fenced error response used by the reference model.  The
  device now advertises EDID and returns a completely initialized, checksummed
  EDID 1.4 base block whose independently decoded preferred timing matches the
  fixed scanout.  Exact GET_EDID framing, reserved padding, response capacity,
  fragmented scatter, and guest connector validation are represented in
  separate protocol, queue, requirements-ledger, and Linux-live gates.
  Guest-visible queues and interrupts are active; live Linux/5BSD,
  packed-ring, reset, checkpoint, and a registered host display consumer are
  still pending.  The state model uses an architecture-neutral DMA callback
  and fixed-width little-endian records; the available Intel amd64 hardware
  affects live qualification and the later nested-VMX stage, not this common
  contract.
- Virtio-IOMMU now has an opt-in architecture-neutral implementation for
  endpoint/domain ownership, permission-aware IOVA translation, physical-range
  validation, exact feature-gated configuration,
  ATTACH/DETACH/MAP/UNMAP/PROBE decoding, fragmented requestq processing,
  bounded fault-event backpressure, and a checksummed transactional `VIMS`
  restore record.  Translation never invokes a platform callback while
  holding the IOMMU mutex.  The modern PCI function now discovers the complete
  topology after BAR assignment, rejects ambiguous IOMMU topology, binds every
  modern VirtIO endpoint through the common DMA boundary, publishes exact
  ACPI VIOT requester nodes, and only then exposes ACCESS_PLATFORM.  The source
  audit finds no endpoint-private direct GPA mapper.  Checkpoint restore now
  uses a generic PCI fabric-first phase, so IOMMU attachments and mappings are
  published before any ACCESS_PLATFORM endpoint remaps saved virtqueues; this
  removes an implicit PCI slot-order dependency and is independently covered
  by the PCI checkpoint harness.  Linux and 5BSD live discovery,
  translated-DMA, reset, and checkpoint gates remain pending.
- The VirtIO memory-device work now has a provisional modern PCI composition
  around the exact configuration and PLUG, UNPLUG, UNPLUG ALL, and STATE wire
  protocols.  The device uses generic named device-memory segments placed
  outside ordinary RAM, keeps unplugged blocks CPU-accessible because it does
  not offer `UNPLUGGED_INACCESSIBLE`, supports opt-in packed queues, and saves
  both portable control state and generic memory payloads.  A normative pass
  corrected two easy-to-miss rules:
  request padding and unused UNPLUG ALL bytes are ignored, and VirtIO device
  reset preserves plugged memory while a separate platform/system-reset
  operation may unplug it.  Platform mapping callbacks run without the state
  mutex, operation serialization prevents concurrent state publication, and
  the portable `VTM1` record validates identity, bitmap population, tail bits,
  and digest before atomic publication.  Device-level tests cover fragmented
  requests, exact one-completion publication, malformed descriptor ordering,
  configuration-generation changes, and reset-preserved plugged state.
  Linux discovery, real plug activity, anonymous-memory workload,
  reset/rebind, split/packed, and checkpoint cases are present in the lab but
  have not yet passed on a root-capable host.  5BSD currently has no stock
  virtio-mem guest driver, so it remains an explicit unsupported qualification
  gap rather than being counted from PCI discovery alone.
- Administration work now has an unadvertised self-group command core for
  LIST_QUERY and LIST_USE, a generic capability manager, a generic
  resource-object manager, and a separate transport-neutral device-parts
  codec.  All use exact little-endian wire fields, bounded arithmetic, and
  independent document constants.  The
  command core accepts the specified
  short and long buffers, reports exact used lengths, serializes commands,
  resets cleanly, and restores transactionally.  A caller-buffered,
  allocation-free scatter/gather adapter handles fragmented readable and
  writable descriptor regions without touching unused writable tails.  A
  second normative pass corrected two subtle rules: QUERY and USE are assumed
  active after reset, and LIST_USE may disable either command, after which
  the disabled opcode is rejected until an allowed LIST_USE re-enables it or
  the device resets.  The device-parts iterator
  enforces reserved fields, selector forms, fixed value sizes, mandatory
  predecessor order, singleton and selector uniqueness, and forward-compatible
  unknown optional parts.  The capability manager implements the three
  mandatory capability commands using byte-granular tails (including Linux's
  literal 34-byte DRIVER_CAP_SET and 10-byte DEVICE_CAP_GET requests), applies
  driver values transactionally, and has a checksummed pointer-free state
  record whose restore validates destination policy before publishing any
  value.  The device-parts composition now binds that two-byte capability to
  the generic type-zero resource objects, enforces distinct GET and SET
  limits over one globally unique ID space, refuses reductions that strand
  live IDs, and serializes capability changes against object creation through
  one composition lock.  A 1,000-iteration concurrent create/reduce test
  proves the result is either a created object with EBUSY reduction or a
  committed reduction with rejected creation, never an out-of-range object.
  A group fabric now gives each registered group type its own monotonic
  supported-command set, legal-command selection, and reset generation.  It
  preserves the specification's invalid group, then opcode, then member
  precedence; validates LIST command member zero; supports a begin/end lease
  that can hold the PCI SR-IOV lifecycle stable throughout execution; and
  saves all group command state in one checksummed transactional record.
  A reusable SR-IOV lifecycle fence supplies those callbacks and holds
  capability presence, VF Enable, NumVFs, and VF Migration Capable stable
  until command completion.  Conflicting migration state returns TRYAGAIN;
  PCI updates use the exclusive side of the lease instead of polling.
  VirtIO 1.4 currently defines device-parts handling
  commands for the SR-IOV group, so bhyve does not incorrectly expose those
  commands through the self group.  The resource manager covers self-group
  CREATE, QUERY, MODIFY, and DESTROY, including portable state and dependency
  teardown, but is not advertised in isolation because the complete
  device-parts command dependency set is not yet composed.
  A concrete SR-IOV owner/member lifecycle, administration-virtqueue PCI
  composition, and live qualification also remain required before
  VIRTIO_F_ADMIN_VQ can be advertised.  Administration-command and SR-IOV
  lifecycle DTrace probes are present in the unadvertised foundation.
- The Intel nested-VMX phase has begun with an amd64-only, unexposed
  architectural state envelope compiled into `vmm.ko`.  It records VMXON,
  current-VMCS and L2/run-pending state, current launch state, VMCS abort
  state, preemption-timer deadline in L1's scaled virtual-TSC domain,
  canonical sorted VMCS field encodings,
  and optional shadow-VMCS fields.  The format is fixed-width little-endian,
  checksummed, bounded, and tagged with separate guest-visible capability and
  VMCS-schema signatures.  It never serializes a hardware VMCS, pointers, or
  host-page-size state.  Decode is transactional and rejects invalid flag
  dependencies, non-4-KiB-aligned VMX regions, high-half or duplicate field
  encodings, width/value mismatches, truncation, and corruption.  This is
  paired with a separate guest-visible capability policy rather than raw host
  VMX MSRs.  The policy validates Intel required-one/allowed-one control
  masks, CR0/CR4 fixed masks, secondary-control dependencies, VMCS region
  size and memory type, effective physical-address width, and the independent
  32-bit VMX-region restriction.  Its stable signature covers BASIC, MISC,
  VMCS_ENUM, VMFUNC, EPT/VPID, fixed-bit, and true/legacy control inputs.
  An unexposed MSR encoder and destination-compatibility gate have independent
  byte-vector and negative tests.  Inactive state is destination-independent;
  VMXON state requires matching capability/schema signatures; a current VMCS
  additionally requires the same virtual revision ID.
  Restore now validates a complete canonical field image before replacing a
  software VMCS region.  It may reconstruct architectural read-only
  exit-information fields without weakening guest VMWRITE, rejects invalid
  launch epochs and aliased source/destination ranges, and leaves the prior
  destination byte-for-byte unchanged on every validation failure.
  Per-region clear/launched state carries a VMX-operation epoch, which
  distinguishes VMRESUME after an intervening VMXOFF/VMXON (instruction error
  6) from an ordinary non-launched VMCS (error 5).  The pure instruction
  transition layer now covers VMXON, VMXOFF, VMCLEAR, VMPTRLD, VMPTRST,
  VMREAD, VMWRITE, VMLAUNCH, and VMRESUME result conventions and the
  architectural CF/ZF updates without pretending to perform caller-owned
  privilege, decoding, or guest-memory fault checks.
  The first VM-entry validation stage implements the Intel SDM 29.2.1
  control-field checks for required/allowed masks, CR3 targets, bounded
  physical control ranges, NMI/APIC/posted-interrupt dependencies, nonzero
  VPID, EPTP shape and capability bits, preemption-timer coupling,
  overflow-safe MSR areas, event injection (including fixed INT1/INT3/INTO
  vectors and error-code requirements for #CP and #SX), and SMM controls.
  Its diagnostic subreasons are internal; every failure maps to
  architectural instruction error 7.
  Host-state validation covers virtual CR0/CR4 fixed-bit policy, physical
  CR3 width, canonical SYSENTER and segment/descriptor bases, PAT, EFER,
  selector rules, and the host-address-size relationship.  RIP canonicality
  follows the CR4.LA57 value that VM exit will load, while the stable virtual
  capability policy separately records the maximum linear-address width.
  The first guest-state pass covers CR0/CR4 fixed-bit exceptions for
  unrestricted guests, PG/PE consistency, physical CR3 width, debug-control
  width, canonical SYSENTER values, PAT, EFER, and IA-32e dependencies.
  The architectural guest pass now also covers segment selectors, bases,
  limits and access rights, descriptor tables, RIP, RFLAGS, activity,
  interruptibility, pending-debug state, the VMCS link pointer, and PAE
  PDPTEs.  VMX-region and VMCS-referenced control structures honor the
  independent IA32_VMX_BASIC[48] restriction; guest and host CR3 and guest
  paging structures correctly use only the virtual physical-address width.
  VM-entry MSR lists are bounded by the virtual IA32_VMX_MISC recommendation,
  decoded as 16-byte little-endian records, checked without mutating
  architectural state, and report the one-based failing entry required for
  exit qualification.
  A transactional orchestration layer preserves the architectural boundary
  between VMfailValid instruction errors 7 and 8 and late VM-entry failures
  with reasons 33 and 34.  It emits the specified non-zero qualifications
  for PDPTE, STI-blocked NMI, link-pointer, and MSR-record failures.
  VMX instruction operand metadata and effective addresses are decoded from
  Intel Tables 30-14 and 30-15 with address-size, segment, limit, and
  canonicality checks.  An independently tested frozen-vCPU instruction
  handoff now covers VMXON, VMCLEAR, VMPTRLD, VMPTRST, VMREAD, and VMWRITE.
  It preserves Intel's memory-fault versus VMfail ordering, stages machine
  state, VM-instruction error, RFLAGS, and RIP advancement, fences stale
  operations with two generations, and never retains a guest-memory
  callback.  The review also keeps the portable decoded-VMCS checkpoint
  image distinct from the implementation-defined contents of the L1 VMCS
  region.  Intel permits a virtual processor to maintain private VMCS data
  in that region, as hardware and Linux/KVM do, but that backing format is
  not a migration ABI and may not contain host pointers, descriptors, or a
  hardware VMCS.  Revision and shadow metadata remain architectural checks.
  EPT12 faults and VMX-instruction work now share a tagged per-vCPU arbiter,
  which rejects double publication and operation/type confusion before the
  common frozen-vCPU dispatcher is connected.
  Capability validation now rejects reserved EPT/VPID bits and feature data
  whose enabling execution control is unavailable.  It also rejects
  allowed-one controls whose required VMCS state is absent, including
  tertiary controls, VMFUNC/EPTP lists, shadow-VMCS bitmaps, ENCLS and XSS
  bitmaps, PML, #VE information, PASID and sub-page translation state,
  guest-physical PT state, TSC scaling, instruction timeout, secondary
  VM-exit controls, and unsupported entry/exit MSR state.  This follows the
  same architectural rule as Linux's filtered nested capability policy:
  underlying host support is necessary but does not make a feature safe to
  expose.  IA32_VMX_MISC is no longer opaque: reserved and unsupported
  promises are rejected, CR3-target count 256 uses Intel's special encoding,
  unrestricted-guest support implies LMA-on-exit reporting, and VMCS_ENUM is
  bound to the implemented field schema.  Required-one and allowed-one halves
  of every control MSR are checked against Intel's defined-bit tables.
  Legacy control MSR reads now set Intel's historical default-1 low-half
  masks, while the corresponding TRUE control MSRs retain the virtual
  policy's actual required-one bits.  The default-1 controls remain accepted
  in the virtual schema so a legacy reader never receives a must-be-one bit
  that VM-entry would then reject.
  Conditional VMCS MSR fields are hidden unless DEBUGCTL, PAT, EFER, or PERF
  entry/exit controls make them architectural, and serialized state is
  checked against sparse schema membership rather than only encoding shape.
  Reflected exit information rejects reason indicators for unexposed CET,
  bus-lock, enclave, and FRED behavior.  VMFUNC remains rejected entirely
  until its EPTP-list execution and invalidation paths exist.  A first
  VMCS02 control composer requires every bit to be classified as L0-owned,
  L1-owned, merged interception, or software-emulated and validates the
  composed value against hardware controls transactionally.  Policy
  validation also rejects L1-visible controls that would be silently
  discarded or forwarded to incapable hardware, while allowing an explicitly
  software-emulated control to remain absent from VMCS02.  Guest DEBUGCTL is
  checked against the virtual policy when VM entry requests loading debug
  controls, and host CET state requires CR0.WP as specified.  The concrete
  per-feature composition policy and hardware programming path are not yet
  complete, so the guest-state and VMCS02 exposure stages deliberately
  remain unset.
  INVEPT and INVVPID now have a transactional operand-validation layer that
  checks the virtual EPT/VPID capability bits, supported invalidation types,
  EPTP format, the reserved upper half of INVEPT descriptors, VPID reserved
  bits, zero-VPID restrictions, and canonical individual addresses.
  Successful validation produces an
  architecture-neutral invalidation request; it does not execute a hardware
  invalidation or allocate a VPID02.  Hardware VPID namespaces, nested EPT
  roots, invalidation execution, and their checkpoint lifetime therefore
  remain behind the exposure gate.
  A pure VPID02 lifecycle planner now separates L1's virtual VPID12 from
  caller-allocated host tags.  It flushes the effective context when VPID12
  changes, when L1 disables VPID, or whenever a VPID01 fallback lacks a
  caller-proven distinct active EPT tag.  Merely having EPT hardware is not
  sufficient.  L1 INVVPID requests translate only to the effective
  VPID02; even an all-context request cannot flush unrelated host VPIDs.
  Host tags remain runtime resources and are absent from portable state.
  Single-context INVEPT is likewise normalized to EPTP12's EPTRTA
  (bits 51:12), so differing low EPTP configuration bits identify the same
  software-managed nested root.  All-context INVEPT is represented as a
  nested-root-cache operation rather than a host-wide hardware invalidation.
  EPT paging-structure access now has a separate Intel-specific memory
  contract instead of extending the generic read-only VM-entry validator
  interface.  It atomically loads naturally aligned little-endian entries and
  sets accessed/dirty bits with a one-shot compare/exchange.  A concurrent L1
  edit returns an explicit restart condition; there is no polling loop and no
  stale read-modify-write that can overwrite L1 state.  Translation, pinning,
  and fault ownership remain with the runtime caller, and no callback or host
  mapping is retained.  The unexposed EPT12 walker covers four- and five-level
  tables, cumulative read/write/mode-based execute permissions, 4-KiB,
  2-MiB, and 1-GiB leaves, physical-width and reserved-bit checks, and
  separate violation and misconfiguration results.  With A/D enabled it sets
  accessed on each valid used entry and dirty only on an allowed leaf write.
  MBEC supervisor execute (entry bit 2) and user execute (entry bit 10)
  remain independent through every level and are reported separately in EPT
  violation qualification bits 5 and 6; user fetch permission is no longer
  collapsed into the supervisor channel.
  EPT-violation exit qualification is synthesized from the effective access,
  cumulative permissions, and caller-owned linear-address provenance.  When
  advanced information is enabled, the caller must also supply final
  translation, user-mode, guest-writable, and guest execute-disable
  provenance; invalid dependency combinations are rejected transactionally.
  Basic qualification deliberately omits those advanced bits without
  rejecting a legitimate user-mode L2 access; an earlier planner revision
  incorrectly turned that ordinary reflection into `EINVAL`.
  EPT misconfiguration produces the architectural zero qualification.  This
  foundation support does not yet publish the advanced control to guests.
  A bounded, per-vCPU EPT02-root cache now keys runtime roots by the complete
  EPTP configuration, capability signature, and MBEC mode.  References block
  eviction and checkpoint quiesce, generations fence stale handles, and
  nested invalidation cannot affect unrelated host roots.  An EPTP whose root
  page is physical address zero remains valid, and single-context invalidation
  of that root is distinct from all-context invalidation.  The amd64 backend
  allocates and invalidates an empty EPT vmspace through the existing pmap
  interface and deliberately keeps its pointer and hardware EPTP out of
  portable state.  A shared, architecture-neutral frozen-vCPU helper can now
  alias an L1 guest-memory object into a private secondary vmspace while
  retaining the object and its normal cache attributes.  The Intel EPT02
  backend rebuilds and faults one such page at a time; it does not persist a
  host physical address or bypass VM ownership with a raw pmap mapping.
  Dispatching that population remains behind the exposure gate: the operation
  may sleep and therefore cannot run inside `vmx_run()`'s critical section.
  The remaining integration must return the nested fault to the generic
  frozen-vCPU dispatcher and internally restart.
  Nested state encoding rejects every overlap between its destination,
  byte-count output, state object, and sparse VMCS field sources instead of
  relying only on a caller convention; this prevents an aliased encoder from
  checksumming and publishing bytes that it corrupted while constructing
  them.  Decoding rejects an input larger than the maximum representable
  canonical VMCS-plus-shadow image before calculating its integrity digest,
  and every rejection preserves the caller's previous decoded view.  A saved
  preemption-timer deadline is also valid only while L2
  guest-mode state is active.  It is not a host monotonic-clock timestamp;
  it is stored in `(L1 virtual TSC >> IA32_VMX_MISC[4:0])` ticks.
  VM-exit planning now derives the bounded remaining value from that domain,
  writes it back only when the save control is enabled, and forces zero for
  a timer-expiration exit as required by Intel SDM 30.3.4.
  Destination restore reconstructs it against restored L1 virtual-TSC state
  while the capability signature fixes the advertised timer rate.  Pure
  start/remaining helpers cover zero-before-entry expiration, the 32-bit
  architectural horizon, 64-bit TSC wrap, and elapsed deadlines without a
  polling loop.  Destination validation now also applies the destination CPU
  policy to saved VMXON/current-VMCS GPAs instead of trusting signature
  compatibility alone, including physical-width and 32-bit VMX-region
  constraints.
  The first exit-routing layer is also transactional and separates L0-only
  handling, direct L1 reflection, and L0 work followed by L1 reflection.  It
  uses decoded dynamic-intercept decisions for guest bitmaps, attributes EPT
  violations and misconfigurations independently to the L0 or L1 translation
  layer, and distinguishes host physical events from virtual events pending
  for L1 before applying L1's pin controls.  Its baseline interrupt/NMI
  planner now treats a blocked guest with
  an L1-requested window exit as the normal wait state it is: it arms the
  corresponding L0 window even when no interrupt is currently pending, then
  reflects the window exit once L2 becomes interruptible.  APICv and posted
  interrupts remain deliberately outside this unexposed baseline.
  A physical machine check during
  nested VM entry remains L0-owned so the host machine-check path cannot be
  bypassed, while invalid-guest-state and MSR-load late-entry failures are
  explicitly identified and reflected to L1; their reason codes cannot be
