  mistaken for ordinary exits.  Reflected exiting-event and original-event metadata enforce
  Intel's fixed vector/type combinations for INT1, INT3, and INTO rather than
  accepting arbitrary vectors under those software-exception types.  It does
  not assume Linux's APIC or XSAVE composition choices.  Remaining dynamic
  intercept decoders,
  complete exit-state synthesis, and integration with the hardware VM-exit
  path remain pending, so the exit-reflection exposure stage also remains
  unset.  I/O and
  MSR bitmap decoders now cover I/O accesses spanning bitmap A/B and the four
  low/high read/write MSR regions plus VMREAD/VMWRITE bitmaps through
  caller-owned guest memory.  Invalid I/O widths and ranges fail
  transactionally; MSRs and VMCS encodings outside their bitmap ranges
  conservatively request an L1 intercept as Intel specifies.  CR-access
  decoding covers MOV, CLTS, LMSW, guest-host masks, read shadows, exit
  controls, and all active CR3 targets.  VMX-instruction operand decoding
  now also carries the non-64-bit
  segment D/B attribute and applies expand-down data-segment bounds in the
  architectural direction (offset above the limit, ending at the selected
  16- or 32-bit upper bound) instead of treating every segment as expand-up.
  Exit-information preparation now
  preserves Intel's late-entry-failure rule: only reason and qualification
  change for reasons 33, 34, and 41, whereas a true exit validates vectored
  event metadata, clears the pending VM-entry-event valid bit, and marks the
  VMCS launched.  Complete hardware VM-exit integration remains deliberately
  outside the exposure gate.
  A compiled exposure gate enumerates every required implementation stage and
  currently returns `ENOTSUP` before examining a policy.  Thus adding a CPUID
  bit or MSR handler cannot make this partial implementation usable without
  also completing instruction decode/fault ordering, full guest state,
  VMCS02, reflection, nested translation, interrupts, and checkpoint stages.
  This remains unexposed foundation code: VMX stays hidden from guest CPUID
  and VMX instructions remain unsupported until instruction decoding and
  fault ordering, complete guest-state entry checks, VMCS02 composition, exit
  reflection, nested EPT/VPID, interrupt behavior, and live L2 tests are
  complete.
- Reference behavior is compared, not copied; specification requirements
  remain authoritative.

### E. Test quality

- The complete sanitizer harness passes all current device, malformed-chain,
  allocation-failure, rollback, snapshot, and independent-wire tests after the
  balloon discard/undiscard and exact queue-mapping changes.  This includes
  1,189,896 independent packed-ring model checks.
- A focused lib9p ATF regression verifies the minimum negotiated `msize`,
  prevents unsigned payload-size wrap, and proves rejected negotiation leaves
  connection state unchanged.
- Real FreeBSD makefiles build the harness and end-to-end tools.
- The qualification manifest composes host regression, Linux, 5BSD,
  checkpoint, and soak profiles and checks exported option coverage.
- Previous live release and checkpoint matrices passed.  The root
  qualification run below is required again because this review changed
  save-state and 9P negotiation code.

### F. Maintainability and operations

- One `virtio-lab` manifest owns allocation, host preparation, cleanup,
  resumability, coverage contracts, timeouts, and summaries.
- The orchestrator rejects duplicate plain YAML mapping keys before parsing,
  so a repeated executor, gate, timeout, or environment key cannot silently
  replace the reviewed test contract through last-key-wins behavior.
- The root wrapper does not create or modify its work directory before
  `virtio-lab` performs ownership, mode, and symlink validation.
- Per-case logs and a concise summary make unattended runs diagnosable.
- DTrace and rate-limited diagnostic paths remain part of the requirements
  ledger.

No unresolved high- or medium-severity defect was found in the current
milestone by the final synthesized pass.  Future features below are not
silently counted as current conformance.

The subsequent Intel nested-VMX foundation now also has a value-only
VMCS12-to-VMCS02 runtime planner and an explicit one-shot hardware apply
boundary.  It validates the architectural VM-entry pipeline first, composes
L0/L1 controls against pinned virtual and hardware masks, derives EPT, VPID,
TSC, and preemption-timer runtime state, and binds the image to the current
VMCS generation and execution epoch.  No guest-memory callback, host pointer,
file descriptor, runtime EPT root, or hardware VMCS enters that image or the
portable checkpoint format.  Failed or retryable apply callbacks are required
to leave VMCS01 and pre-entry runtime state active.

A renewed Intel SDM pass corrected the TSC helper: setting “use TSC scaling”
while “use TSC offsetting” is clear is legal, although the multiplier has no
architectural effect.  The earlier helper incorrectly rejected that state.
The VMCS02 planner now captures the pre-entry L1 DEBUGCTL, DR7, PAT, and EFER
values and applies Intel's conditional VM-entry semantics instead of copying
unused VMCS12 guest fields.  A separate value-only nested-exit planner saves
those L2 fields only when the corresponding VM-exit controls request it and
computes the effective L1 runtime state after the host-state load.  In
particular, DR7 becomes 400H, DEBUGCTL is cleared, PAT is either retained from
L2 or loaded from the VMCS12 host field, and EFER.LMA/LME follow the host
address-space-size control when EFER is not loaded.  VM-exit event validation
now also follows the advertised IA32_VMX_BASIC[56]=0 policy for #CP and #SX,
matching VM-entry validation.
The exit transaction also consumes valid VM-entry injection and updates the
VMCS12 IA-32e guest bit from L2 EFER.LMA when IA32_VMX_MISC requires that
behavior.

A distinct VMCS02 resource-binding stage now joins the architectural image
with generation-matched L0 host state and reconstructed host-owned EPT,
bitmap, APIC, and MSR-list resources.  The resulting value-only hardware plan
contains no VMCS12 EPTP, bitmap GPA, MSR-list GPA, pointer, callback, or file
descriptor.  It also preserves control-dependent TPR, CR3-target,
posted-interrupt, preemption-timer, VPID, and TSC-scaling values that an
eventual hardware writer must program.  Stale capability tags, stale
execution epochs, and misaligned runtime resources fail transactionally.

The VM-entry MSR-load path now snapshots the complete validated list while
the vCPU is frozen, captures the prior values of every target MSR before
mutation, and rolls completed writes back in reverse order.  VM-exit
MSR-store and MSR-load lists have distinct Intel-rule validators: stores
permit FS_BASE/GS_BASE but reject x2APIC and unreadable MSRs, while loads
reject FS_BASE/GS_BASE, x2APIC, and invalid WRMSR values.  Store processing
builds an immutable target plan before its first write and commits in
architectural order.  Commit revalidates each record header immediately
before its value write so a concurrent L1 index change cannot receive a value
snapshotted for another MSR; a failed or changed entry requests virtual abort
indicator 1 and leaves earlier completed stores visible instead of
overwriting concurrent L1 memory updates.  Host-load WRMSR failure restores
the per-vCPU L1 state and requests indicator 4.  A failed host-state rollback
remains an L0 error instead of being misreported as an ordinary virtual
abort.

The virtual VMCS-region layer now exposes the architectural abort field at
byte offset 4, accepts only Intel-defined indicators 1 through 6, and clears
the field when VMCLEAR reinitializes implementation state.  Portable state
rejects an unknown indicator or an abort record that still claims active L2
execution.  Nested exposure remains fail-closed until the runtime path writes
the indicator and enters the required virtual shutdown state.

The Intel vCPU now owns one runtime-only nested context.  Reset and restore
generations, L2 execution epochs, and internal handoff epochs reject stale
transitions; snapshot quiesce refuses active L2, callback, and VMCS02
transactions.  Instruction and EPT handoff identifiers and machine snapshots
are assigned atomically by that owner.  The frozen internal-exit hook validates
pending work against the owning context before selecting a runtime adapter.
The instruction adapter performs fault-injecting L1 linear access only while
the vCPU is frozen, preserves the VMREAD destination register, and commits
GPR, RFLAGS, RIP, and nested-machine results through a retryable context
boundary.  Opaque active VMCS data is protected by a bounded per-VM registry
with explicit vCPU ownership, hashed GPA lookup, and a processor-owned path
for the read-only VM-instruction-error field.  Capability binding compares
every canonical policy field rather than trusting a digest.  EPT population
now has an atomic frozen-memory adapter and a generation-checked EPT02
binding.  A value-only reflection builder now converts a resolved EPT12
violation or misconfiguration into Intel-defined VMCS12 exit information
without mutating runtime state.  The VMCS registry copy-stages that exit
information and the launched epoch in a disjoint 4 KiB image, then publishes
the image only after every field validates.  A generation-checked context
commit consumes the resolved handoff and changes from L2 to L1 only after a
retryable caller transaction succeeds.  That caller contract deliberately
requires saving L2 state, committing VMCS12, and restoring L1 runtime state
as one operation.  The VMCS02 image now retains the original VMCS12 guest
state and exit policy separately from effective L2 state, and a composite
value-only planner combines those values, a frozen L2 state capture, the
resolved EPT12 fault, and the captured VMCS02 exit information.  The exit
snapshot travels inside the generation/epoch-owned handoff, preventing a
resolved EPT12 walk from being paired with stale exit metadata.  This avoids
incorrectly reconstructing fields whose VM-exit save controls are clear.
VM entry does not install its EPT binding yet, and the
production exit path does not yet implement that complete runtime
transaction.  The complete path remains unreachable because nested exposure
is disabled.  Frozen vCPU destruction has a distinct
leave-and-discard transition, matching Linux's lifecycle shape rather than
treating active L2 state as a quiescent snapshot or panicking during VM
teardown.  The bounded VMCS registry now has a canonical, versioned,
GPA-sorted checkpoint envelope that binds the destination capability and
VMCS-field schemas, preserves complete architectural fields, launch epochs,
and abort indicators, and deliberately omits runtime owners and opaque
region bytes.  Restore builds a temporary registry and swaps it into service
only after complete validation, so malformed, oversized, aliased, duplicate,
or destination-incompatible input preserves the live registry.  Successfully
restored entries are inactive and unowned; per-vCPU ownership is reconstructed
by the runtime context rather than persisted.

The bounded registry feeds a distinct VMCS02 resource-binding boundary and
canonical hardware programming image.  That image contains only values and
L0-owned resource addresses, orders every VMCS write by Intel encoding, and
rejects inconsistent EPT, VPID, posted-interrupt, preemption-timer, TSC
scaling, and currently unrepresented PERF_GLOBAL_CTRL state without
modifying its output.  Independent tests verify the Intel encodings,
conditional fields, EPTP02 substitution, and the architectural LDTR/TR
ordering.  A subordinate apply transaction now requires a private,
unpublished VMCS02, treats commit as the only publication point, and invokes
mandatory rollback after every failed write or failed commit.  Fault
injection covers every write boundary, acquisition failure, commit failure,
malformed ordering, and unchanged result publication.

The focused nested suite now contains 66 passing cases and `vmm.ko` builds
with `-Werror`; nested VMX remains deliberately unexposed pending real VMCS
application, L2 execution, abort/shutdown publication, complete exit
reflection, and live Intel qualification.
The complete post-change rootless regression also passed, including the
independent VirtIO requirements oracle, all sanitizer/fault harnesses, the
1,189,896-case packed-ring model, host helpers, the then-current 76-entry
nested ledger, and all then-current 59 nested cases.  Its result directory is
`/tmp/waspnest-host-regression-nested-runtime`.
The subsequent focused EPT-reflection gate passed all 63 cases, validated the
78-entry ledger, built `vmm.ko` with `-Werror`, and passed
`git diff --check`.
A fresh complete rootless regression after binding the VMCS02 exit snapshot
to the EPT handoff also passed all 63 nested cases and the 78-entry ledger,
along with the independent VirtIO oracle, sanitizer/fault harnesses,
1,189,896-case packed-ring model, and host helpers.  Its result directory is
`/tmp/waspnest-host-regression-ept-exit`.
The subsequent registry-state focused gate passed all 64 nested cases,
validated the 79-entry ledger, rebuilt `vmm.ko` with `-Werror`, and passed
`git diff --check`.
The subsequent VMCS02 programming-image gate passed all 65 nested cases and
validated the 80-entry ledger; the production hardware apply transaction
and live L2 execution remain intentionally unwired.
The subordinate hardware-apply transaction then passed all 66 nested cases
and the 81-entry ledger.  Its real `vmclear`/`vmptrld`/`vmwrite` adapter and
the enclosing VM-entry path remain intentionally unwired.

An Intel-only adapter now compiles behind that portable value boundary.  Each
vCPU owns a distinct page-aligned VMCS02.  The adapter runs inside the
existing VMX critical section, verifies that VMCS01 is current, uses raw VMX
operations so it does not corrupt FreeBSD's critical-section nesting,
restores VMCS01 on every pre-launch failure, and captures the complete
architectural exit-information set before switching back.  Comparison with
Linux 7.2-rc4 confirms the same separate VMCS01/VMCS02 ownership and explicit
switch-back lifecycle; unlike Linux's cached loaded VMCS02, the initial
bhyve path deliberately clears VMCS02 after each exit for simpler launch
state and rollback semantics.  This adapter is build-verified but is not yet
live-qualified or connected to `vmx_run()`, so exposure remains closed.

The complete rootless regression after adding the programming image,
transactional apply boundary, and Intel adapter passed the independent
VirtIO oracle, every sanitizer/fault harness, the 1,189,896-case packed-ring
model, all host helper tests, all 66 nested cases, and all 81 nested ledger
entries.  Its result directory is
`/tmp/waspnest-host-regression-vmcs02-intel`.

The next resource-ownership increment adds a per-vCPU host-owned merged MSR
bitmap and generation-bound leases for VMCS12 virtual-APIC, APIC-access, and
posted-interrupt resources.  Disabling VMCS12 MSR bitmaps is represented as
an all-intercept page, and L0/L1 requests are combined without losing either
intercept.  Guest-memory failure leaves the prior page unchanged.
APIC-related guest physical addresses are resolved by an L0 provider into
temporary hardware addresses; acquisition is transactional, partial failure
releases in reverse order, and stale VMCS or resource generations cannot
release or reuse the mapping.  The VMCS02 planner also canonicalizes an L0
unconditional-I/O policy by removing the hardware I/O-bitmap control while
retaining VMCS12's bitmap policy for software exit reflection.  The focused
gate passes all 68 nested ATF cases, validates all 83 ledger entries, builds
`vmm.ko` with `-Werror`, and passes `git diff --check`.  The Intel
guest-memory mapping provider and enclosing entry/exit transaction remain
unwired, so exposure is still closed.

The frozen VM-entry validator now snapshots the VMCS12 entry MSR-load list
exactly once after all architecturally earlier checks pass.  It distinguishes
bounded L0 storage exhaustion from Intel's late MSR-loading entry failure,
and tests prove that an earlier VM-entry failure performs no list read.
`vmx_nested_vmcs02_prepare_frozen()` now carries that same validation result
into VMCS02 composition instead of invoking the old validate-only path and
rereading guest memory.  Host capability signatures and control policy are
preflighted before the snapshot.  Explicit reverse rollback is also available
when a later hardware-entry stage cannot publish L2 execution.  With
the aliasing and guest-address negative cases added during the follow-up
review, the focused gate passes all 69 nested ATF cases, all 84 ledger
entries, the `vmm.ko` `-Werror` build, and `git diff --check`.

A fresh complete VM-free regression also passed after these changes:
independent VirtIO requirements and oracle checks, every sanitizer/fault
harness, the 1,189,896-case packed-ring model, all host helper tests, all 69
nested cases, and all 84 nested ledger entries.  Privileged kernel/MAC and
live-guest tests were correctly deferred.  Results are retained under
`/tmp/waspnest-host-regression-vmcs02-resources`.

After wiring frozen preparation and the Intel resource provider, another
complete rootless VM-free gate passed under
`/tmp/waspnest-host-regression-frozen-entry-rootless`: all independent
VirtIO ledgers, models, sanitizers, fault harnesses, the 1,189,896-case packed
ring model, host helpers, 69 nested cases, and 84 nested requirements.
Privileged kernel/MAC cases were explicitly deferred.  The root-only
`run_vsock_tests.sh` wrapper now refuses unprivileged direct execution,
because direct ATF invocation cannot honor `require.user` metadata and
previously mislabeled expected permission failures as implementation failures.

The Intel resource adapter now implements the previously missing production
mapping boundary.  With the vCPU frozen it pins VMCS12
virtual-APIC, APIC-access, and posted-interrupt pages through `vm_gpa_hold()`,
derives hardware physical addresses from the held pages, and retains only an
opaque unwire cookie in the runtime lease.  A single Intel resource builder
also materializes the per-vCPU merged MSR bitmap, consumes a separately
captured immutable snapshot of VMCS01's L0-owned MSR auto-load/store areas,
resolves the bound EPT02 root, and acquires every APIC lease under one
resource generation.  VMCS01 capture is confined to a short critical section;
all potentially sleeping guest-page and EPT work occurs after leaving it.
Failure unwinds EPT and partial
leases without publishing output.  A separate scratch page prevents a failed
VMCS12 bitmap read from modifying the prospective hardware bitmap.  These
kernel-only adapters compile with `-Werror`; the common lease and bitmap
semantics remain independently covered by the rootless tests.  They are not
yet invoked from `vmx_run()`: the frozen MSR-list application and the
entry/exit commit transaction must be connected first.

The next entry-publication slice now has a separate value-only per-vCPU
runtime owner.  It fences the immutable VMCS02 identifier and resource
generation across resource acquisition, hardware VMCS02 programming,
software-emulated entry-MSR application, hardware entry, exit capture, and
nested-exit commit.  A raw VMLAUNCH/VMRESUME failure remains distinguishable
from a successful entry that immediately exits with Intel's failed-entry
reason.  Pre-entry failures expose an explicit reverse cleanup plan; a failed
MSR rollback is quarantined instead of silently returning the vCPU to L1.
Snapshot and teardown reject any non-idle transient runtime.  Three new
negative/happy-path tests cover normal exit, every pre-launch cleanup layer,
stale identifiers, and rollback poisoning.  This is still fail-closed
plumbing: production MSR virtualization and the actual `vmx_run()` launch
adapter remain to be connected before CPUID VMX can be exposed.

The next conformance pass added a single frozen VMCS12 capture boundary.
All controls, execution state, guest state, L1 host state, PDPTEs, launch
epoch, timer state, and TSC inputs used by one entry attempt are copied into
one pointer-free value image while the software-VMCS registry owner is
stable.  Validation views are derived from that image; later entry stages
must not reread VMCS12.  The pass also found that the virtual VMCS schema
omitted Intel's TSC-multiplier encoding even though the composition and
hardware-programming layers supported scaling.  Encoding `0x2032` is now
schema- and capability-gated, contributes to VMCS_ENUM and the migration
signature, preserves an explicit zero multiplier for entry validation, and
uses the architectural identity multiplier only when TSC scaling is
unavailable.

A follow-up ownership review found that consuming the successful
VMLAUNCH/VMRESUME instruction also discarded the request copy of the virtual
capability policy.  That policy determines which conditional VMCS fields
exist, so reconstructing it during a later VMCS02 stage would create a
time-of-check/time-of-use boundary.  The frozen entry image now includes the
exact value-only virtual capability contract and its stable signature.
The snapshot has a separate validation boundary which recomputes that
signature, validates the VMCS GPA and launch epoch, cross-checks SMM and
executive-VMCS state, cross-checks host IA-32e mode against the exit controls,
and requires an identity TSC multiplier when scaling is unavailable.  A
corrupt snapshot is rejected without partially publishing a derived
VM-entry image.
Commit-stage retries explicitly reuse an already-resolved instruction result
instead of repeating guest-memory or VMCS callbacks.  The conservative
production control-policy builder now merges L0/L1 execution exits while
emulating L1 VM-entry and VM-exit transition controls around L2, retaining
only L0's transition controls in VMCS02.

The subsequent Linux-comparison pass tightened the architectural MSR-list
boundary.  VM-entry and VM-exit load lists now reject the microcode-update,
microcode-revision, and SMM-monitor MSRs in addition to FS/GS base.  VM-exit
store lists reject SMBASE and the microcode MSRs.  The complete x2APIC MSR
page remains deliberately fail-closed because this boundary does not yet
carry an immutable virtual APIC-mode input; accepting it conditionally would
make restore and retry behavior depend on mutable external state.  Focused
negative tests cover each mandatory exclusion and preserve transactional
output on failure.  The same pass corrected failure priority when an MSR list
exceeds both Intel's architectural count and L0's bounded snapshot capacity:
the architectural L1 error is now reported first, rather than being
misclassified as host resource exhaustion.

The complete rootless gate passed again under
`/tmp/waspnest-host-regression-entry-policy`: all independent VirtIO
requirements and device harnesses, the 1,189,896-case packed-ring model,
helper tests, 86 nested requirements, and 74 nested architectural cases.
`vmm.ko` also builds with `-Werror`.  Privileged kernel/MAC and live nested
execution remain intentionally deferred.

After the mandatory-MSR and architectural-count-priority corrections, the
same complete gate passed under
`/tmp/waspnest-host-regression-msr-priority`: all device and sanitizer
harnesses, the independent VirtIO oracle and packed-ring model, helper
self-tests, all 86 nested requirements, and all 74 nested architectural
cases.  Privileged kernel/MAC tests remain explicitly deferred by the
rootless wrapper.

The first production virtual-MSR adapter is now value-only and independently
tested.  VMCS-managed SYSENTER, DEBUGCTL, PAT, and EFER values are applied to
an explicit prospective guest-control/guest-architecture pair, while
STAR/LSTAR/CSTAR/SFMASK/KGSBASE/TSC_AUX remain in a software-owned
prospective L2 bank.  The adapter no longer requires or points at a mutable
VMCS02 image.  A separate transactional helper derives the exact pre-MSR-load
state from VMCS12 entry controls and the frozen L1 runtime; VMCS02 composition
uses that same helper.  This breaks the former circular dependency in which
MSR validation needed an unpublished hardware image before VM-entry
validation could safely create it.  Canonical-address, reserved
bit, PAT, DEBUGCTL, EFER-LMA, paging/LME, SMM-context, and feature checks are
performed before mutation.  The adapter deliberately separates read support
from write support: FS_BASE and GS_BASE remain forbidden in entry/exit load
lists but can be read from the effective L2 segment image for a legal VM-exit
store.  The generic reverse rollback engine uses these same callbacks, so
neither failure nor rollback requires writing an L1/L2 value to host
hardware.  The adapter compiles into `vmm.ko` with `-Werror`; production
allocation and `vmx_run()` transaction wiring remain outstanding.

That adapter review also corrected the frozen hardware-publication order.
The old state machine programmed VMCS02 before applying the entry-MSR list,
which could not affect VMCS-managed PAT, EFER, DEBUGCTL, or SYSENTER fields
without a fragile second hardware rewrite.  The required order is now
resources, entry-MSR application to the unpublished value image, final
VMCS02 programming, and hardware entry.  A raw entry failure restores VMCS01
before rolling the prospective MSR state back; a failure before programming
needs no VMCS restore.  Successful entry consumes the rollback snapshot and
leaves L2 values as architectural guest state for the nested-exit
transaction.  Nested VMX remains unexposed while production allocation and
the complete `vmx_run()` entry/exit transaction are incomplete.

The MSR transaction now also has a runtime-only workspace contract.  Its two
arrays are externally allocated and reusable, so the eventual per-vCPU owner
can allocate lazily before entering a VMX critical section instead of adding
about 128 KiB to every vCPU.  Capacity is derived from the immutable virtual
IA32_VMX_MISC value (512 through 4096 entries); overlapping, undersized,
partially initialized, stale-capability, stale-generation, and active-unbind
cases are rejected.  Workspace pointers are never portable state.  This
contract is foundation-tested.  `vmx_vcpu` now allocates its single backing
slab lazily at the frozen entry handoff, outside VMX critical sections, and
validates/unbinds/frees it during teardown.  `vmx_run()` does not yet consume
the workspace.

The following Intel Volume 3C/Volume 4 comparison found and corrected two
WRMSR semantic mismatches in that adapter.  VM-entry loading of IA32_EFER now
ignores an attempted LMA change while preserving the prior LMA bit, rather
than reporting an entry failure.  IA32_SYSENTER_CS now accepts and ignores
bits 63:32 while retaining bits 31:0.  Intel's canonical-address failure rule
for SYSENTER_ESP/EIP remains enforced; Linux's common path canonicalizes those
values for cross-vendor reasons, which is not the Intel virtual CPU contract
used here.

The next production boundary is now explicit: one nested entry first captures
L0 controls, execution policy, effective L1 runtime, TSC, VPID, timer, and
capability inputs into a generation-bound, value-only entry environment.
Preparation rejects unsupported L0 controls and stale identifiers, validates
the virtual-to-hardware control policy, and canonicalizes inactive CR3-target,
PLE, APIC EOI, and interrupt-status fields.  Only a synchronous frozen view
may then be bound to the pointer-bearing VMCS02 preparation API.  This removes
the previous risk of composing an entry from values sampled at different
times.  Capture metadata is now validated before any adapter callback, failed
or overflowing reads preserve the previous output, and inactive optional
fields are not sampled.  The Intel adapter pins the short VMCS01 capture to
one CPU, maps semantic fields to VMREAD, sources bhyve's software-owned PAT
from the per-vCPU MSR bank, and leaves VMCS01 clear on every return path.
`vmx_run()` consumption remains deliberately unexposed.

A timing-coherence review then removed the remaining caller-supplied clock
sample from that boundary.  Active VMCS01 TSC offset and multiplier fields
and the host TSC are now sampled while the same VMCS is current on one pinned
CPU; inactive fields are canonicalized without a VMREAD.  The generic layer
derives the L1 virtual TSC from those captured values and rejects callers
that attempt to smuggle mutable L0 offset, multiplier, or scaling state
through the value-only request.  This keeps VMCS02 TSC composition and the
virtual preemption-timer inputs in one coherent entry transaction.  A later
Linux lifecycle comparison found that composing a deadline at this
sleepable preparation boundary started the timer too early.  VMCS02 now
retains an explicitly unarmed initial value, and a separate generation-bound
arm operation computes the L1-virtual-TSC deadline only at the final hardware
launch boundary.  Hardware resource acquisition and validation therefore do
not consume L2's timer budget, and resource binding rejects an enabled but
unarmed timer.
The value-only metadata is now derived transactionally from the frozen
VMCS12 snapshot rather than reconstructed by production call sites.  That
constructor canonicalizes inactive TSC and timer state, preserves malformed
active VMCS12 TSC/VPID values for the architectural VM-entry validator, and
builds the conservative virtual-to-hardware control policy.  Production
publishes the frozen VMCS12 snapshot and coherent VMCS01 environment only
after both construction and the pinned hardware capture succeed; failure
cancels both entry state machines without publishing partial state.
The same portability pass corrected the VPID transition model for Intel
processors on which bhyve runs VMCS01 without hardware VPID.  An all-zero,
untagged transition is now an explicit valid mode; any effective or virtual
VPID in that mode remains rejected.  This avoids turning an optional Intel
facility into an accidental nested-VMX prerequisite.

The frozen production path also now has a bounded Intel guest-physical
memory adapter for VM-entry validation, MSR-list capture, PDPTE/link checks,
and bitmap materialization.  It accepts at most one page of payload, handles
the possible two-page span, acquires every page before copying, and releases
all mappings synchronously.  Failed reads leave the destination untouched,
and failed writes cannot expose a partial update.

The same-generation capture now includes every L0 host-state field consumed
by VMCS02.  The host IA-32e semantic flag is cross-checked against VMCS01's
host-address-space-size exit control, and mismatches reject preparation
without changing the previous output.  VMCS02 resource acquisition may
therefore use the captured host state rather than recapturing it after a
sleepable stage.  The focused and complete gates remain at 80 nested
architectural cases and 90 validated ledger entries, with `vmm.ko` compiling
under `-Werror`.

Hardware control capability selection is now a separate value-only contract.
It follows IA32_VMX_BASIC[55] when choosing legacy versus true-control MSRs,
does not read architecturally absent true or secondary MSRs, rejects malformed
required/allowed masks transactionally, and canonicalizes unavailable
secondary controls to zero.  VMX module initialization caches this immutable
contract and verifies the ordinary L0 VMCS01 controls remain within it.

The complete post-workspace rootless gate passed under
`/tmp/waspnest-host-regression-msr-workspace-final`: all independent VirtIO
requirements and sanitizer harnesses, the 1,189,896-case packed-ring model,
host helper tests, 88 nested-VMX ledger entries, and 76 nested architectural
cases completed successfully.  The subsequent entry-environment focused gate
has 90 ledger entries and 80 nested architectural cases passing, together
with a `vmm.ko` `-Werror` build.  Privileged kernel/MAC and live nested Intel
qualification remain deferred.

## Root qualification still required

Run the command in `docs/waspnest-qualification-handoff.md`.  It executes the
qualification profile (release plus checkpoint plus bounded soak) and writes
the final result to:

```
/tmp/virtio-qualification-current/summary
```

Do not treat this milestone as qualified until that summary reports no
failed or blocked cases.

## Next implementation order

After the root qualification gate passes:

1. finish transport-neutral feature/status/configuration operations and the
   compatibility manifest fields needed for topology and CPU baselines;
2. run the common packed-virtqueue engine's Linux split/packed/checkpoint/reset
   matrix for every current device;
3. run the registered balloon device's Linux split/packed/checkpoint/reset
   gates and add a focused 5BSD balloon resident-memory gate;
4. non-DAX virtio-fs;
5. qualify the new modern-only 2D virtio-gpu PCI composition on Linux and
   5BSD, including split/packed queues, reset, suspend, active checkpoint, and
   its intentionally headless display mode;
6. qualify ACCESS_PLATFORM and virtio-IOMMU with live Linux and 5BSD guests;
7. virtio-memory;
8. administration queues, device groups, and migration compatibility;
9. nested VMX on this Intel host, using Intel SDM revision 092 as the
   normative CPU reference and keeping architectural VMCS12/pending state
   separate from portable device state.  AMD SVM remains an architecture
   boundary and model/build target, not a live qualification claim.

Each item must repeat review passes A through F and add Linux, 5BSD (where a
guest driver exists), checkpoint, fault, and soak evidence before feature
advertisement.

The live evidence is behavioral, not configurational.  A case does not prove
multiqueue, packed rings, queue reset, notification data, translated DMA, or a
device-specific control merely by requesting the option or observing its
feature bit.  It must show the unmodified guest driver activated the feature,
drive its distinguishing path, and correlate that with a host-side trace.  The
release manifest now includes an opt-in FreeBSD virtio-net multiqueue case that
checks `max_vq_pairs` and `act_vq_pairs`, passes real network traffic, and
requires the host to observe the valid MQ control command.

## Nested-VMX continuation (2026-07-27)

The current Intel slice has 109 independently validated requirements and 98
rootless architectural cases.  `vmm.ko` builds with the kernel's normal
`-Werror` flags.  Guest CPUID VMX exposure remains disabled.

Ordinary nested exits now have an allocation-free, generation-fenced VMCS12
staging and publication transaction, complete L2 VMCS02 exit capture, and a
separate L1 processor-state rollback boundary.  Final run-loop integration,
VM-exit MSR abort processing, and reflected-versus-L0-owned exit dispatch are
still required before live qualification.

A fresh Intel field-encoding review found that the common state model orders
TR before LDTR while Intel VMCS encodings order LDTR before TR.  Three
arithmetic adapters had therefore exchanged TR and LDTR during VMCS12
snapshot, ordinary exit publication, and hardware exit capture.  They now use
one explicit checked mapping.  Tests use the SDM numeric values rather than
implementation headers, and the ledger validator rejects reintroduction of
arithmetic guest-segment encoding.

The next hardware-boundary slice raises the rootless inventory to 88
architectural cases and 97 independently mapped requirements.  It adds one
allocation-free coordinator for L2 software-MSR installation, final VMCS02
programming, raw-entry rollback, and successful-entry ownership transfer.
Cleanup obligations are recorded before an adapter can mutate hardware;
transactional programming failure restores VMCS01 before reverse MSR
rollback, and incomplete rollback quarantines the runtime.  The Intel adapter
now has a bounded STAR/LSTAR/CSTAR/SFMASK/KGSBASE/TSC_AUX transition and a
transactional capture of L2's resulting software-owned bank before restoring
L1.  Snapshot and teardown reject the short hardware-MSR transition window.
The focused ATF suite, requirements validator, `git diff --check`, and
`vmm.ko` build pass.  These adapters are deliberately not yet invoked by
`vmx_run()`; interrupt/event commitment and complete ordinary-exit
publication must be connected first, and CPUID VMX remains hidden.

The following entry/exit transaction review raises the rootless inventory to
88 architectural cases and 98 independently mapped requirements.  The
software-owned MSR adapter now records whether hardware is transitioning
toward L2 entry or back toward L1 exit, retains the exact opposite-direction
rollback image, and publishes the new software bank only after every WRMSR
operation succeeds.  Ordinary nested exits use the same complete L1 control,
architectural, and software-MSR image as failed entry, stage VMCS12 updates in
preallocated storage, and publish them last.  An incomplete reverse
transition preserves resource ownership, marks the runtime poisoned, and
requires fail-stop handling rather than allowing execution with mismatched
hardware and software state.

The hardware-entry coordinator now distinguishes three outcomes.  A raw
VMLAUNCH/VMRESUME instruction failure rolls the unpublished hardware image
back.  Intel's failed-entry VM-exit rejects the prospective L2 entry through
the same hardware unwind but follows the architectural failed-entry VMCS12
publication path.  Only a successful L2 entry transfers ownership and may
consume a pending L0 event.  The entry-event validator also enforces Intel
SDM revision 092's rule that zero instruction length for software
interrupts, software exceptions, and privileged software exceptions requires
IA32_VMX_MISC[30].  Focused failure injection covers all three outcomes and
the complete 88-case suite, 98-entry ledger, `vmm.ko` build, and
`git diff --check` pass.  Reflected-versus-L0-owned exit routing and the
non-destructive event peek/commit adapter remain the next production
boundary; no nested execution is advertised yet.

The subsequent exit-ownership review raises the focused inventory to 91
architectural cases and 101 independently mapped requirements.  VMCS02 exit
routing now derives its reason, entry-failure state, vector, interruption
type, and page-fault error from one captured hardware image and combines it
transactionally with one frozen L1 policy image.  Invalid reason bits,
impossible failed-entry reasons, malformed interruption metadata, and
unsupported dynamic exits preserve the prior output.

VMCS12 I/O and MSR interception policy is frozen before L2 entry into
generation-owned host buffers.  Exit routing queries those buffers directly
and never rereads mutable guest memory after L2 has run.  The review found and
fixed a policy bug where unconditional I/O exiting without I/O bitmaps had
been canonicalized as no interception; it is now represented as an all-one
policy image, while no I/O interception is all zero.  Failed preparation and
discard scrub policy and scratch images.  CR, I/O, MSR, VMREAD, VMWRITE, and
APIC dynamic ownership now have a value-only decoder; optional ENCLS and
XSAVES/XRSTORS controls remain L0-owned because they are not advertised.
The 91 focused tests, 101-entry validator, `vmm.ko` build, and
`git diff --check` pass.  The production run loop is still disconnected and
guest VMX exposure remains disabled.

The next exit-capture review raises the inventory to 93 focused cases and 103
mapped requirements.  A width-checked architecture-neutral read transaction
now captures the complete VMCS exit-information field set and publishes
nothing if any read fails.  The Intel VMCS02 adapter uses that same
transaction for both full destructive capture and a new non-destructive
peek, preventing their field lists from drifting.  Classification can
therefore occur while VMCS02 remains current, preserving the option to handle
an L0-owned exit and resume L2 without manufacturing a nested VM exit.

Frozen VMCS12 controls and execution fields are converted to routing policy
by one value-only builder; interrupt, NMI, EPT, timer, and mandatory-L0 facts
remain explicit caller-owned provenance rather than being guessed from L1
controls.  The Intel binding checks the active execution and resource
generations, reads CR operands from the captured L2 register selected by the
exit qualification, and reads the MSR index from L2 RCX.  Failed-entry
contexts now discard irrelevant stale event, EPT, timer, and dynamic-policy
metadata.  All 93 focused cases, the 103-entry validator, `vmm.ko`, and
`git diff --check` pass.  The binding remains intentionally disconnected
until the L0 event, EPT, and preemption-timer handlers have explicit tested
resume/reflect completion contracts; CPUID VMX remains hidden.

The lifecycle pass then found a second, higher-level ownership gap after a
successful reflected exit.  The low-level exit transaction restored L1,
published VMCS12, and returned the entry runtime to its releasable state, but
the architectural context did not move through `EXIT_PENDING` to `ROOT`.
That made failure retry ambiguous and left the only resource-release helper
coupled to cancellation of an entry which had supposedly never run.

The context now binds an exit to the exact state generation, execution epoch,
and VMCS12, enters `EXIT_PENDING` before fallible publication, permits retry
from the same frozen capture, and publishes `ROOT` only after all L1-visible
state commits.  Resource cleanup has separate cancellation and completed-exit
dispositions, so a completed L2 exit cannot call the `ENTRY_PENDING`
cancellation operation.  The focused suite is now 94/94, all 104 nested-VMX
requirements validate, `vmm.ko` links, and `git diff --check` passes.  The
remaining boundary is still the production `vmx_run()` entry/exit loop and
its explicit L0 event, EPT, timer, and interrupt provenance; CPUID VMX remains
hidden until that boundary and live Intel L2 qualification are complete.

The next Linux-comparison pass found three ownership ambiguities at that
boundary.  Successful hardware entry could publish the low-level runtime as
`GUEST` before the architectural context left `ENTRY_PENDING`; those two
state machines now commit as one prevalidated generation/epoch/VMCS12 pair.
Hardware VMfailValid and failed-entry exits now pass through a bounded
value-only converter which accepts only Intel's architecturally meaningful
L1 failures; VMfailInvalid, machine-check-during-entry, and failures in
L0-owned MSR entries remain L0 failures.

Exit routing no longer accepts caller provenance for the forced MTF exit
caused by VM-entry injection of vector-zero `other event`; that condition is
derived from frozen VMCS12 state.  Raw hardware external-interrupt and NMI
exits are also now strictly L0-owned.  L1-visible interrupt/NMI exits use the
separate pre-entry virtual-event planner, including acknowledge-on-exit and
commit-after-publication semantics, rather than reflecting a host interrupt.
The complete focused inventory is 98/98, all 109 ledger entries validate,
`vmm.ko` links, and `git diff --check` passes.

The L0-exit continuation pass establishes the run-loop boundary needed before
an L2 exit can safely reach userspace.  A hot continuation explicitly means
that VMCS02 and L2 CPU-local state are still resident on the current CPU.  A
cold continuation is permitted only after one transactional adapter has
captured all authoritative L2 architectural state, restored L1's CPU-local
state, detached VMCS02, released runtime resources, and returned a nonzero
portable-generation token.  Freeze, thaw, restore, resolution, and fail-stop
reset now publish the continuation and hardware-runtime owners as a checked
pair; incomplete rollback quarantines both.

Cold handle-then-reflect state can publish L1 directly from its portable
image.  A cold resume must first rebuild a hot image, while an in-kernel hot
resume never fabricates a VMCS12 exit.  Failed transactional resolution
preserves the exact hot or cold state for retry.  Export contains only the
generation, epoch, VMCS12 GPA, monotonic exit sequence, portable generation,
and completion decision; hardware VMCS pointers, physical-CPU ownership,
resource generations, and opaque leases are excluded.  Two new negative and
retry lifecycle cases bring the focused inventory to 98/98 and the ledger to
109 requirements.  The full suite, strict test build, `vmm.ko` link, and
whitespace gate pass.  The architecture adapter that produces and consumes
the portable L2 image is the next slice; guest VMX exposure remains disabled.

The portable-L2 image pass now captures the value-owned state needed to
continue an L0-owned exit after VMCS02 has been detached: dynamic L2 control
and architectural state, software-owned MSRs, normalized exit information,
active PDPTEs, the virtual-TSC preemption-timer image, virtual-interrupt
status, and the pending VM-entry event fields.  General-purpose registers
remain in the enclosing portable vCPU image.  Hardware VPIDs are stripped
and a context flush is forced; EPT roots, VMCS pointers, CPU ownership,
resource generations, and backend handles are absent.

The first conformance review caught that VM-entry error-code and instruction
length fields are architecturally ignored, not required to be zero, when the
entry-information VALID bit is clear.  The portable image now preserves those
ignored values exactly.  Stale identities, malformed valid events, invalid
timer combinations, hidden inactive PDPTE data, and mismatched optional
hardware fields are rejected without modifying output.  Capture and apply
also bind the image to the immutable virtual-VMX capability signature and
re-run complete guest-control and guest-architecture validation.  This
structure remains an internal value image rather than a native on-disk
encoding; a future checkpoint record must encode its fields explicitly.

Freeze and thaw now also have architecture-neutral ordered transactions.
Freeze observes the software-owned MSRs before destructively capturing and
clearing VMCS02, validates the complete portable image, restores L1's
software-owned MSRs, and only then releases opaque resources.  A retryable
late failure reconstructs the prior hot L2 image; malformed hardware capture
or incomplete rollback is explicitly fail-stop.  Thaw validates and overlays
the portable image before mutation, acquires a fresh nonzero resource
generation, installs L2 software-owned MSRs, and programs a newly constructed
VMCS02.  Every post-acquire failure rolls back to the same cold image or is
quarantined.

The Intel adapter captures dynamic VMCS guest state, PDPTEs, virtual
interrupt status, pending entry fields, normalized exit facts, and the
preemption timer before restoring VMCS01.  Common capture code is shared with
ordinary nested exits so their field inventories cannot drift.  The focused
thaw path recaptures destination VMCS01 state, recomposes host-derived
controls, reacquires opaque leases and a fresh hardware VPID, and rebases the
preemption timer on destination L1 virtual time.  Fail-stop cleanup still
performs best-effort L1-MSR restoration and releases every recoverable lease.
The focused suite is 101/101 and the ledger contains 111 requirements;
`vmm.ko` links with VMX exposure still disabled.  Continuation-aware register
access and run-loop routing remain the next production boundary.

Continuation-aware register access now has a value-only common layer and a
separately tested amd64 `VM_REG` adapter.  A cold L2 routes its represented
control, architectural, segment, descriptor-table, PDPTE, entry, and
software-MSR fields to the portable image; GPR and debug-register values stay
in the enclosing vCPU image.  Unknown cold mappings fail closed and can no
longer fall through to VMCS01.  A validated cold continuation also has an
explicit teardown path which ends its retained MSR workspace only after all
hardware leases are absent.  TPR/CR8 is deliberately still unmapped because
it needs paired L1/L2 APIC ownership rather than a scalar alias to the L1
vLAPIC.  The focused suite is 102/102 and the ledger contains 112
requirements; nested VMX exposure remains disabled.

## Connected Intel VMCS02 loop and fail-closed unwind

The Intel execution adapter now has a separate `vmx_run_nested()` loop wired
to the value-only run selector.  It covers initial entry, cold continuation
thaw, per-VMCS launch selection, event planning, real and synthetic exits,
composed-EPT handoff, direct L1 reflection, L0-handled hot resume, userspace
freeze, and host-stop freeze.  This is a structural connection only:
`vmx_nested_exposure_validate()` and guest CPUID VMX exposure remain disabled,
so an unqualified guest cannot reach the path.

A review of every error edge found and removed an execution-domain violation:
the host-stop precheck attempted a frozen-resource thaw cancellation from
inside `vm_run()`'s CPU-pinned critical section.  The prepared thaw is now
preserved as explicit CPU-independent state across the stop and may be
resumed on the eventual execution CPU or cancelled by frozen teardown.
The same review also removed an unbounded retry edge after cold thaw: a
missing, stale, or mismatched composed-EPT binding is refrozen to its exact
cold image and the original error is returned.  It is not converted into a
continuation redispatch, because no state transition in that loop could
repair the ownership mismatch.  The distinct EPT A/D compare-exchange race
continues to use its bounded, host-stop-aware retry boundary.

Run-loop failures are selected by a value-only classifier over runtime,
continuation, portable-image, and detached ownership.  It distinguishes an
initial unentered rollback, exact cold-image refreeze, hot live-state freeze,
and fatal no-image detach.  Invalid or mutating combinations are fail-stop.
A raw later VMfail never consumes a pending event or consults stale VM-exit
fields.  Both successful and failed returns assert that VMCS02, nested
software-MSR transitions, and L2 IA32_TSC_AUX residency cannot cross the
outer critical-section boundary.

The pure nested suite is now 129/129.  Its unwind test exhausts every finite
state combination, the 146-entry requirement-to-code-to-test ledger
validates, `vmm.ko` builds with `-Werror`, and `git diff --check` passes.
Live execution is not yet eligible: ordered L1 VM-exit MSR-store/load and
remaining failed-entry host-state forms are explicit blockers.

The first MSR-exit follow-up separates frozen descriptor capture from
CPU-pinned L2 value capture for VM-exit MSR-store lists.  This prevents the
sleepable preparation stage from sampling runtime L2 state and provides the
bounded plan needed by the future ordered exit coordinator.  Existing
partial-store VM-abort behavior remains covered; the production loop still
rejects nonempty exit lists until the complete store/load transaction is
connected.

The ordered-exit review corrected that boundary further.  VM-exit store and
load lists are not frozen at VM entry: another L1 CPU or a DMA agent may
legitimately change their memory while L2 runs.  The exit coordinator must
therefore capture L2's effective MSR values first, sample the current store
list after the exit, commit its entries in order, and only then sample the
load list.  This ordering also makes an overlapping load list observe values
just written by the store list.

A generation-fenced phase machine now records the irreversible store
boundary and makes retries incapable of repeating a committed store.  It
distinguishes abort indicator 1 after a partial store, abort indicator 4
after a fully rolled-back guest host-load failure, and a poisoned L0 state
after an incomplete host rollback.  A separate value-only load planner
constructs prospective VMCS01 and software-owned L1 MSR images without
publishing either on failure.  The Intel L1 restore transaction now includes
that software bank in the same capture, apply, and rollback boundary as
VMCS01 and general registers.

The current rootless inventory is 142/142 pure architectural cases and 166
independently mapped requirements.  The kernel module builds with
warnings-as-errors and the whitespace gate passes.  Ordinary and synthetic
VM exits now process current L1 store records sequentially, preserve earlier
stores on abort 1, sample the load list only after store completion, and
retain the value-only L1 load image across publication retries.  Initial and
resumed failed entries process only the host-load list and publish abort 4
before consuming their handoffs.  Ordinary exits and failed entries now load
and validate 32-bit PAE L1 host PDPTEs in the same ordered transaction and
publish abort 2 before consuming their handoffs.  Guest VMX exposure remains
disabled pending live Intel nested execution qualification.

The nested save-state foundation now has a single versioned, checksummed,
length-delimited checkpoint record joining per-vCPU architectural state to
the VM-wide canonical VMCS registry.  Restore validates destination
capabilities and current-VMCS field, launch, and abort coherence before
atomically replacing the registry.  Whole-record alias checks cover registry
allocations, field arrays, output counts, and borrowed views.  The state
format also preserves virtual `IA32_FEATURE_CONTROL` while VMX is inactive and
requires its lock and outside-SMX enable bits for any VMXON image.

The production `STRUCT_VMCX` path now writes one explicit Intel architecture
header, one VM-wide registry record, and one portable nested state record per
present vCPU.  A new architecture-neutral VM snapshot completion callback
keeps restore data in a destination-local staging registry and candidate
contexts until every ordinary and nested vCPU record validates.  Failure
discards the whole nested stage; success publishes the registry and all
per-vCPU owners, contexts, and virtual control MSRs together while the vCPUs
remain frozen.  The value-only active-L2 image now also has its own 558-byte
fixed-layout, little-endian, versioned and integrity-checked encoding.  It
names every architectural segment, control, event, PDPTE, timer, and
software-MSR value explicitly and rejects aliases, padding-dependent state,
noncanonical booleans, truncation, trailing bytes, and corruption
transactionally.  A separate 666-byte outer envelope binds the exported cold
continuation identity, exit sequence, completion policy, and portable
generation to exactly one inner image; both layers reject corruption and
leave decode outputs unchanged.  A compatible version-2 checkpoint carries
the active continuation as a third bounded section.  Capture now requires
one exact pending internal handoff for the detached cold continuation;
missing, handling, resolved, or mismatched handoffs fail closed.  Restore
reconstructs that same pending handoff, so the frozen run loop routes through
the internal continuation handler and destination resource acquisition before
L2 can resume.  The destination rebuilds a CPU-independent VMCS02 plan from
the immutable VMCS12 entry snapshot and portable post-entry image, acquires
all active per-vCPU MSR workspaces, and replaces the VM-wide registry only
after every workspace is ready.  A late vCPU failure rolls every earlier
workspace back and leaves the live registry unchanged.  The record never
serializes CPU-local VMCS02, EPT, VPID, bitmap, pointer, or file-descriptor
resources.  Linked-shadow restore remains fail-closed until its guest-memory
adapter is connected.  This production path compiles with `BHYVE_SNAPSHOT`
and is rootless-model tested, but remains live-unqualified.  VMX exposure is
therefore default-off and available only through the explicit host and
per-guest experimental qualification gates.  The VM-wide transaction rejects
capability
mismatches, unbound storage, duplicate owners, count overflow, and generation
outputs that alias registry, binding, capability, owner, plan, or rollback
memory.  The `vmm:vmx:nested:restore` DTrace probe reports completion error,
active-L2 count, validated-vCPU count, and published registry size without
adding work to the nested run hot path.

Restore now applies the exposure predicate as an admission gate after wire
decoding and destination-capability validation.  While VMX is hidden, only
the canonical inactive nested record is accepted; VMXON and active-L2
records return `ENOTSUP`.  This closes a checkpoint-only path that could
otherwise reconstruct hidden nested ownership without passing the CPUID,
MSR, and VMX-instruction exposure gates.  The rule is value-only and has
independent inactive/VMXON tests.

The entry coordinator acquires its guest-memory adapter only when the frozen
VMCS12 has an active VMCS link pointer, a 32-bit PAE PDPTE source without
EPT, or a nonempty VM-entry MSR-load list.  The pure entry model defines and
tests that predicate, including memory-free entry and each memory-requiring
branch, so a self-contained entry cannot fail because an unused guest-memory
mapping was unavailable.

The connected-loop host-residency review also aligned VMCS02 exit handling
with the established VMCS01 path: GDTR and IDTR limits plus LDTR are restored
immediately after guest debug and pmap residency ends, before the hardware
result classifier, tracing, failure handling, or interrupt enable.  VM-exit
descriptor side effects therefore cannot leak into ordinary L0 C execution.
Intercepted L2 IA32_PAT writes now update the current VMCS02 guest PAT field
before publishing the software value.  This keeps the forced VM-entry PAT
load, emulated RDMSR value, subsequent execution, and destructive exit
capture consistent.

Intercepted L2 IA32_TSC writes now follow the nested clock composition used
by the pinned Linux reference: the write changes L1's offset in its scaling
domain, VMCS02 retains VMCS12's L2 offset and multiplier, and the nested
preemption timer is reloaded from its unchanged L1 virtual-TSC deadline.
VMCS02 offset, controls, and timer are updated as one rollback-capable hot
transaction.  The matching VMCS01 offset/control pair is retained in the
Intel adapter until VMCS01 becomes current, and software clock ownership is
published only after the hardware update succeeds.

The production virtual secondary-control policy no longer advertises
pause-loop exiting.  Intel defines one PLE gap/window pair in VMCS02, and
arbitrary independent L0 and L1 policies cannot be represented by that one
pair without either missing an owner's exit or adding policy-dependent false
exits.  Linux likewise omits PLE from its nested allowed-one policy.  The
generic value model and VMCS schema retain PLE support for future composition
work, but hardware support alone cannot make the control part of the current
guest ABI.

CR0 and CR4 guest-host-mask composition now follows the separate hardware and
architectural domains used by Linux nested VMX.  VMCS02 masks the union of
L0's hardware-fixed bits and L1's requested intercepts, but L1's read shadow
wins on overlap because that is the value L2 is meant to observe.  The
effective VMCS02 guest CR value still carries L0's forced hardware bits, and
both original mask/shadow policies remain in the immutable execution image
for exit routing.  Differing shadows therefore no longer reject an otherwise
valid nested entry.

The MSR-list boundary review found a separate internal validation gap.
VMCS02 binds only L0-owned hardware MSR areas, while L1's three lists remain
software-emulated in Intel order.  The binder previously checked base
alignment and a count bound but not whether the complete hardware area
wrapped past `UINT64_MAX`.  It now validates the full non-wrapping range and
leaves the caller's plan unchanged on failure.  The independent resource
binding test covers the high-address case; Intel's virtual list limit,
guest-physical last-byte checks, sequential exit stores, retry-persistent
exit loads, and rollback behavior remain covered by the existing MSR-list
tests.

The portable-state decoder now rejects an output view that overlaps its wire
buffer.  Successful views retain pointers into that immutable backing image;
allowing the result structure to overwrite the image made its own field
pointers immediately invalid.  The malformed-state regression verifies that
the aliased decode fails before changing any wire byte.

The L1 restore transaction now also stages the machine-independent next-run
RIP cache and Intel's interruptibility last-RIP cache.  VMCS01 RIP remains
part of the rollback-capable machine-state transaction, while both caches are
published only at final commit.  The commit does not redispatch a register
write through the currently represented architectural owner, which is
essential when a cold detached L2 image still owns ordinary register access
during reflected-exit publication.

Concurrent L1 EPT A/D updates now retain the unresolved handoff and retry at
the ordinary frozen `VM_RUN` boundary.  A compare/exchange race therefore
does not escape as a failed VM run, and retries do not form a private polling
loop that bypasses host stop, rendezvous, or suspend processing.

The connected IA32_TSC_AUX residency contract was corrected to match the
ordinary VMX host boundary.  L1 and paused-L2 values are architectural
software banks; the physical CPU carries its per-CPU host AUX value whenever
L0 may enable interrupts.  L2 is installed only in the final
interrupt-disabled entry interval, captured immediately after exit, and no
guest AUX value is left resident on a host return.

The connected Intel loop now exposes dedicated DTrace probes without adding
unconditional hot-path logging:

- `vmm:kernel:internal_exit:handled` reports the architecture-neutral frozen
  vCPU and final handler result for internal exits that never reach the
  userspace `VM_RUN` loop;
- `vmm:vmx:nested:entry` reports VM, vCPU, VMCS12 GPA, execution epoch, and
  selected launch state immediately before the hardware instruction;
- `vmm:vmx:nested:vmexit` reports the same ownership identity and raw exit
  reason after the complete hardware report is captured;
- `vmm:vmx:nested:failure` reports the error plus entry-runtime and
  continuation states immediately before state-based unwind.

These probes remain dormant while nested VMX exposure is disabled, but they
are compiled into the Intel module for the eventual live qualification.

The exposure boundary now has three fail-closed conditions.  The Intel host
must opt in at boot with `hw.vmm.vmx.nested=1`, the individual guest must
request `x86.nested_vmx=true`, and the complete implementation-stage and
capability predicate must pass.  The guest choice is stored once per VM and
atomically becomes immutable when the first vCPU reaches `vmx_run()`.  It is
not a collection of independent per-vCPU flags, so a libvmm client cannot
produce CPUs which disagree about CPUID VMX.  CPUID, virtual VMX MSRs, VMX
instruction capture, and active nested-state restore all consult the same
VM-wide choice.  Canonical inactive nested state remains portable when the
feature is hidden.

This differs intentionally from pinned Linux 7.2-rc4, whose VMX module has a
read-only `nested` parameter that defaults on.  Linux remains the behavioral
reference for control filtering and runtime semantics, but WASPNest keeps
the host policy default off until its Intel L1/L2 live gate passes.  The
extra per-guest selection also prevents a host qualification setting from
silently changing unrelated guest CPU models.

The rootless transition model covers enable, lock, idempotent repeated
configuration, forbidden late changes, corrupt state, and invalid output.
The complete 141-case nested suite, 165-entry requirements ledger, and
`vmm.ko` `-Werror` build pass with this boundary.  These are architectural
and build results, not substitutes for Linux/KVM L1 execution with Linux and
5BSD L2 guests.

## Common request-ownership and translated-DMA review

The ACCESS_PLATFORM lifetime pass found that mapping validation alone was not
enough to make IOMMU detach and unmap safe.  Every successfully acquired
direct or indirect request now holds one domain lease until exactly one
terminal action.  IOMMU detach, unmap, reset, and snapshot reject an active
lease instead of invalidating memory still owned by a device backend.

The terminal-action review then found two copied-token hazards.  A split-ring
backend could publish one head twice because the split wire format has no
device ownership bit.  A packed-ring backend could rewind its acquisition
cursor twice because rollback deliberately leaves descriptor ownership with
the device.  A boolean in `vi_req` could not solve either problem because
asynchronous backends copy request tokens.

The authority is now queue-owned.  Split queues track each acquired head;
packed queues track each acquired head and wrap value beside the bounded
completion record.  Direct and indirect acquisition claim the owner, while
completion, rollback, grouped completion, and reset discard atomically
consume it.  Copied duplicate actions set DEVICE_NEEDS_RESET without a second
used publication, cursor rewind, or DMA-domain release.  Group failure
examines the complete group so one duplicate cannot leave distinct owners
wedged across reset.  Checkpoint save rejects both layouts while any
queue-owned request or staged packed completion remains.

Reset cancellation now has an explicit `vq_discard_req()` operation.  It
retires host and DMA ownership without publishing a stale used entry or
making the request available again.  Block, 9P, virtio-fs, and the retained
balloon statistics request use that contract on their stale-generation and
no-callback paths.  The sanitizer harness covers duplicate copied tokens,
stale generations, grouped duplicates, direct and indirect acquisition,
successful completion, rollback, discard, and one-to-one domain lease
release.  The independent packed model remains unchanged and passes all
1,189,896 cases.

The SCSI lifecycle pass removed two unbounded selective-operation waits.
Queue reset now has a bounded backend-drain deadline and fails without
recycling queued or active owners.  Task-management completion uses one
device-wide deadline after CTL accepts the operation; if a worker cannot
publish within it, all request queues remain quiesced, the control response
is FAILURE, and DEVICE_NEEDS_RESET is raised.  Full device reset deliberately
retains its drain contract because publishing status zero before CTL has
released guest buffers would be unsafe.  The focused timeout and recovery
tests run with a zero-duration injected deadline.  Production request
conditions and deadlines use `CLOCK_MONOTONIC`, so host wall-clock correction
cannot extend the bound.  The complete rootless device harness remains clean.

The exact VBSD kernel build found two integration defects which focused model
builds could not expose.  The production EPT02-root backend now completes
`struct thread` before including SMR assertions, and the architecture-neutral
internal-exit DTrace probe has an explicit typed definition in the provider
which invokes it.  A focused `vmm.ko` build and the complete `buildkernel`
gate pass after both corrections.

The block lifecycle and portability pass found two defects hidden by normal
guest I/O.  A writethrough completion can need to enqueue its stability flush
after checkpoint quiesce has marked the backend paused.  That continuation is
now admitted as part of the already-owned request while all new data
operations fail closed; the old assertion could abort bhyve during an
active-write checkpoint.  FLUSH on read-only media is now a successful no-op,
which matches the absence of volatile guest writes and avoids calling
`fsync(2)` after Capsicum intentionally removed `CAP_FSYNC`.  The backend
drain now has one 30-second `CLOCK_MONOTONIC` deadline; timeout rolls back the
pause owner instead of hanging orchestration or leaving the VM fenced.

The same pass replaced block snapshot version 1's raw packed-structure copy.
Those fields are host-endian in memory and become guest-endian only in the
configuration-access path, so the old record was not portable despite its
comment.  Version 2 encodes 56 logical configuration bytes field by field in
canonical little-endian form followed by the exact 21-byte identity.
The former version-1 development import path was later removed because no
checkpoint ABI has shipped.  The independent 85-byte fixture,
unknown-version, truncation, backend-drift, and focused lifecycle tests pass.

A later device-suspend review found that the asynchronous block resize
callback could still replace the guest-visible capacity while the common
VirtIO suspend or checkpoint fence was closed.  The callback now retains only
the newest backend capacity during either lifecycle, leaves the frozen
configuration bytes unchanged, and publishes the capacity after
`resume_complete` observes that the common fence is open.  The notification
remains latched while suspended and is delivered after resume.  The focused
test covers ordinary resize, guest suspend, and checkpoint pause boundaries.

The subsequent ACCESS_PLATFORM pass removed another one-command assumption:
a device DMA descriptor may span adjacent IOVA mappings.  The IOMMU translator
now walks the complete requested interval under its state lock and coalesces
separate mappings only when the IOVA and translated GPA ranges are both
contiguous and every segment grants the requested direction.  A hole,
permission transition, arithmetic overflow, or physically discontiguous
result remains one mapping fault because the current common mapper returns one
host pointer rather than a scatter list.  Live mappings are compacted and
kept in canonical domain/IOVA order, so a transaction spanning many adjacent
MAP requests is resolved by one linear walk rather than repeated full-table
scans.  The current reader requires canonical insertion-independent order and
detects adjacent overlap in one bounded pass.  Independent tests cover
successful coalescing, out-of-order insertion, deterministic state, and the
discontiguous fail-closed boundary.

The same portability pass made the complete new IOMMU state image
deterministic.  Endpoint and domain records are now sorted by their
architectural identifiers before encoding, mappings remain in canonical
domain/IOVA order, and the destination-local generation slot is emitted as
zero because that epoch fences translation caches rather than guest state.
The sole current reader requires the zero slot and canonical endpoint, domain,
and mapping order, and advances the live epoch only after atomic publication.  The canonical
state test constructs equivalent fabrics in opposite endpoint, domain, and
mapping order and with different local generation histories, then requires
byte-identical images.

The existing-device callback-lifetime pass found that `mevent_delete()` is an
asynchronous request, not an ownership barrier.  Block resize, console
listener, and input initialization teardown could therefore release a
callback argument before the event loop had removed the corresponding
kevent.  A new acknowledged deletion operation removes the kernel
registration synchronously before dispatch starts and otherwise waits until
the event thread has crossed its callback boundary.  Its independent test
starts dispatch only after deleting a registered event, drives a second
sentinel event through the same kqueue, and proves that the deleted callback
cannot run.

The same review found a virtio-fs reset-generation race.  Readiness events
from the disconnected backend were deleted asynchronously, the connection
was destroyed and replaced, and an already-selected callback could then
operate on the replacement (especially after fd-number reuse).  Reset now
publishes a reconnect fence while holding the device mutex, releases that
mutex so selected callbacks can observe the fence, acknowledges both event
deletions, destroys the old connection, and only then reconnects.  The
focused PCI test proves that both a fenced source and a missing connection
are rejected before backend access.

The follow-up event-loop review found that dispatch readiness was published
before the internal wakeup pipe had been created and registered.  An
acknowledged deletion racing that startup window could consequently notify
uninitialized descriptors.  Readiness is now published only after the wakeup
event exists.  The lifecycle test deletes one event before dispatch and a
second immediately after creating the dispatch thread, then drives a sentinel
through the same kqueue and proves neither deleted callback can run.  Vsock
initialization failure also uses acknowledged deletion for every device-level
event carrying the softc before releasing that softc.  The 94-case focused
vsock suite and exact bhyve build pass; active userspace and kernel connection
checkpoint remain explicit, documented gaps rather than silently lossy state.

The balloon host-memory pass found that PFN ownership was published in the
bitmap before the platform discard or undiscard operation completed.  A host
error could therefore leave saved device state claiming a memory transition
that never occurred.  Tracker transitions now report whether they actually
changed the bit, and the device applies the inverse tracker-only transition
on host-operation failure.  Failed deflation still raises
DEVICE_NEEDS_RESET, but both failure directions preserve their exact
pre-request bitmap.  Focused tests cover changed-bit failure and retry, and
the balloon device/host suites pass 16/16.

The sound lifecycle pass found that a failed backend STOP or RELEASE during
device reset was traced but otherwise discarded.  The common transport must
finish reset with status zero, so the callback now records the failure through
the transport's deferred reset-failure latch.  The next driver initialization
therefore observes DEVICE_NEEDS_RESET instead of running against stale host
stream ownership.  A device-composition test injects RELEASE failure, proves
the recoverable stream state remains intact, observes exactly one reset
failure signal, and verifies a later cleanup retry succeeds.

The RTC reset pass found the corresponding host-resource case: failure to
disarm a POSIX alarm timer was ignored even though its old callback could
remain armed after guest reset.  Reset still clears the portable alarm model,
but host disarm failure now enters the common deferred reset-failure latch.
The focused timer fault-injection test proves the alarm state is cleared,
exactly one failure is reported, and the next driver initialization cannot
silently reuse the stale timer.

The subsequent balloon reset audit found a more direct guest-memory hazard.
Full reset cleared the PFN ownership bitmap without cancelling the host
`MADV_FREE` hints represented by that bitmap.  A page which the guest reused
after reset could therefore remain reclaimable while the device had forgotten
that it owed a `MADV_WILLNEED`.  Reset now sparsely walks only complete native
pages represented in the bitmap, cancels each host hint, and publishes an
empty bitmap plus zero actual count only after every cancellation succeeds.
Failure retains the complete old ownership/accounting record and enters the
common deferred `DEVICE_NEEDS_RESET` path; retry is safe because cancellation
is idempotent.  The independent host test covers low/high-memory holes,
partial native pages, mid-sequence failure, retry, and atomic bitmap
publication, while the device test covers successful and failed reset.

The following balloon restore pass corrected a separate destination-state
defect.  Restore computes the exact complete-host-page difference between the
destination and source bitmaps, undiscards destination-only pages, and
discards source-only pages.  A later platform failure reverses precisely the
successful prefix; an identical repeated restore performs no host memory
operation.  Failure of the compensating operation aborts restore and latches
`DEVICE_NEEDS_RESET` rather than publishing a logical bitmap which claims the
failed reconstruction succeeded.  A follow-up normative review removed an
overly strict bitmap-population comparison: section 5.5.6.1 permits the guest
to batch its `actual` update after multiple completed operations, so exact PFN
ownership and the guest-maintained configuration field are preserved and
validated independently.  Historical empty version-1 records also undiscard
destination ownership before clearing it.

The virtio-fs checkpoint integration pass separates guest ownership from the
external daemon's state-transfer contract.  Dispatch, queue, and connection
layers expose one transactional admission fence: it succeeds only after both
retained requests and unsent backend frames reach zero, returns portable FUSE
plus negotiated backend session values, and permits FUSE-session restore only
while that fence remains closed.  A failed QUIESCE reopens admission internally
because bhyve does not invoke resume for a device whose pause failed.
QUIESCE and THAW use a disjoint high-bit request-ID namespace and exact,
bounded payload rules so ordinary FUSE request ownership cannot collide with
lifecycle replies.  State transfer is a distinct negotiated capability rather
than an inferred consequence of freeze support.

The snapshot-enabled PCI composition now registers pause, resume, and snapshot
callbacks when a stable `identity` is configured.  It waits on a monotonic
condition variable signalled by backend readiness, with a ten-second bound and
no polling.  Successful quiesce captures the backend-produced opaque state;
allocation or local capture failure performs a real saved-state THAW rollback.
Restore validates the complete portable `VFS1` record and destination backend
contract before publishing the restored FUSE session and staging the opaque
state for THAW.  Focused connection tests cover event-driven freeze/thaw,
payload transfer, backend rejection, and admission rollback.  The remaining
release gate is a production daemon implementing the explicit capability and
live Linux checkpoint/repeated-restore qualification.

The pinned QEMU comparison reinforces this separation: current
`vhost-user-fs` checks for explicit backend device-state support and transfers
backend state through a dedicated migration channel; it does not infer
reconstructibility merely from empty guest virtqueues.  WASPNest's private
backend protocol uses a bounded framed blob instead of QEMU's descriptor
channel and now provides the corresponding explicit capability, save, load,
and failure contract.  Production-daemon implementation and interoperability
evidence remain pending.

The same PCI review found that a failed reset-time backend reconnect removes
both mevent registrations, while a subsequent queue-reset cleanup can still
ask the device to synchronize readiness.  The synchronizer now treats a null
connection and null event handles as the disconnected, no-interest state
instead of passing null handles to mevent.  A PCI-composition regression
executes that exact post-reconnect-failure shape.

The VirtIO memory pass found no additional protocol defect.  Request padding
is intentionally ignored as required by sections 5.15.6.3 through 5.15.6.6,
plugged-size changes use the non-interrupting configuration-generation dirty
path, and UNPLUG ALL does not manufacture a configuration interrupt.  The
device-specific persistent-suspend feature remains unadvertised because bhyve
does not expose guest deep-sleep/S3 semantics; the separately negotiated
common suspend feature covers checkpoint quiescence.  Dynamic management of
`requested_size`, Linux split/packed activation, active-memory checkpoint, and
a 5BSD guest driver remain explicit qualification gaps.
