The following sound state review found two production-backend defects hidden
by the null backend.  Restoring a RELEASED stream with retained parameters
used to call SET_PARAMS followed directly by RELEASE, skipping the PCM
lifecycle's PREPARE stage.  Restore now reconstructs
SET_PARAMS--PREPARE--RELEASE.  If a later stream then fails, rollback clears
the already released reconstruction record instead of leaving retained
parameters on an otherwise clean target and making every retry fail with
`EBUSY`.  Independent two-stream tests cover the exact partial-restore failure,
clean retry, and backend-operation-free repeated restore.  The complete
ASan/UBSan device harness passes after both fixes.

The ACCESS_PLATFORM and VirtIO-IOMMU restore pass found that the portable
image's saved translation generation was copied back into the live DMA domain.
That violated the domain's monotonic-epoch contract: a repeated restore could
reuse an old value and let a long-lived split or packed ring mapping appear
current after the translation table changed.  Restore now treats the
generation as destination-local invalidation state and advances it only after
the entire image and endpoint topology validate.  Fault enqueue, loss
accounting, and dequeue no longer advance the translation epoch, avoiding
unrelated full-ring remapping after an ordinary fault.  Independent tests
prove successive restores advance the epoch and fault FIFO traffic leaves it
unchanged.  Live Linux VIOT discovery, translated operation on every device,
active-I/O checkpoint, and fault injection remain privileged qualification
gates; ACCESS_PLATFORM therefore remains opt-in rather than a default.

The checkpoint-manifest publication review then found that the public
publisher trusted its caller to supply a generation-consistent set of member
names.  It now validates the canonical name, data/kernel/metadata roles,
shared 128-bit generation, temporary-manifest generation, path-component
safety, and terminated architecture/machine identities before creating any
file.  Null public arguments are rejected without dereference.  Negative tests
cover path traversal, mixed generations, a mismatched temporary name, an
invalid directory descriptor, and a missing publication-result pointer.  The
complete ASan/UBSan rootless harness passes with this boundary hardened.

The next common-queue review found that the modern snapshot format copied
`vq_generation` from the source image even though this value is a
destination-local asynchronous-ownership epoch.  Repeated restore could
therefore recreate an earlier token and make a late destination callback
appear current.  Because this project format is unreleased, the obsolete wire
slot was removed rather than retained as compatibility baggage.  Modern and
legacy restore both publish the destination generation plus one only after the
complete queue image validates.  Failed and overflowed restores retain the old
generations.  Unit coverage restores the same image repeatedly across both
transport formats and verifies monotonic epochs and overflow rejection.

The administration lifecycle pass found that self-group callbacks executed
outside the owner mutex while `virtio_admin_owner_reset()` could reset the
selected command set and dependent objects concurrently.  Group-fabric users
were incidentally protected by the fabric read lease, but the direct
administration-queue adapter was not.  Owners now count active callbacks,
publish a reset-in-progress state, reject newly arriving commands with the
standard TRYAGAIN qualifier, and wait on a condition variable until the last
callback retires before resetting command state.  A deterministic
condition-variable regression holds a callback active, proves reset cannot
complete underneath it, then releases it and verifies a clean generation
transition.  The mechanism has no polling interval or hot-path allocation.
Snapshot and restore also fail with `EBUSY` while a callback or reset drain is
active, preventing a pre-reset command selection from being captured or
republished through the condition-variable wait window.

The same destination-epoch audit found a device-local copy in the 9P
checkpoint record.  `vsc_generation` fences lib9p completions and therefore
must not be restored from a source image.  The sole current wire record is
accepted, and each successful destination restore advances its local
generation; malformed, incompatible, truncated, and overflowed restores leave
the prior incarnation unchanged.  The atomicity test now covers two restores
of the same image plus the overflow boundary.  Active fid migration remains
deliberately fail-closed because lib9p fids contain backend-private host
descriptors and credentials; a portable object reconstruction protocol is
still required before that gate can be relaxed.

The fresh post-fix ASan/UBSan gate passes in full.  It includes 1,189,896
independent packed-ring model checks, 458 common-core checks, 237
administration checks, 134 9P checks, 289 SCSI checks, and every other device
suite scheduled by the rootless harness.  The requirements validator accepts
154 ledger entries backed by 630 independent specification-oracle
definitions.

A production `bhyve` build was also completed in an isolated object tree with
the FreeBSD build system's normal `-Werror` policy.  The first component-only
attempt selected the running system's older installed `vmmapi.h` and kernel
headers, which do not contain `vm_create_devmem_auto()`, the generic
device-memory identifiers, or nested-VMX capability definitions.  Rebuilding
the source `libvmmapi` and `bhyve` together against the source kernel headers
succeeded, including all new VirtIO PCI devices and DTrace provider linkage.
This was build-environment version skew rather than a source defect; the
privileged qualification must still install a world and kernel from the same
tree before live tests.

The following optional-feature advertisement pass found that enabling balloon
free-page reporting made the fixed queue indices through reporting queue 4
visible, but left statistics queue 2 with a nonzero QueueSize even when
`STATS_VQ` was not offered.  The initialization topology now reports zero for
both absent intervening optional queues and a regression checks the exact
reporting-without-statistics configuration.  The fresh sanitizer harness
passes with 218 balloon-device assertions.

The device-memory API used by VirtIO memory was hardened at the same boundary.
It now rejects null contexts, zero lengths, and guard-region size overflow
before allocating a kernel memory segment, and releases the reserved guard
mapping if the device-memory mmap fails.  Source `libvmmapi` builds cleanly
with `-Werror`; focused rootless calls verify the null and overflow results.

The subsequent optional-device conformance pass corrected Virtio-mem
configuration-notification behavior.  PLUG and UNPLUG change `plugged_size`,
for which VirtIO 1.4 section 5.15.4.2 says the device SHOULD NOT issue a
configuration notification; UNPLUG_ALL is the specification's explicit
exception when it also changes `usable_region_size`.  The request path no
longer marks configuration dirty after every successful command, and the
fragmented-request regression now proves that ordinary PLUG does not produce
a spurious interrupt.  Runtime host control of `requested_size` remains an
explicit completion item because that future control must generate a
configuration interrupt itself.

The same pass found a late-callback boundary in the Virtio-IOMMU PCI adapter.
DMA-idle and fault callbacks can arrive independently of a guest kick and
previously entered request/event queues without checking reset, suspend,
checkpoint pause, quiesce, NEEDS_RESET, or DRIVER_OK.  They now share one
lifecycle predicate.  Reversible blocked edges retain a queue notification
for event-driven replay after resume or DRIVER_OK; fatal/reset edges are
dropped.  A new PCI-composition test covers the normal path and every fence in
14 assertions.  The complete ASan/UBSan harness passes with this test, and the
154-entry requirements ledger again validates against 630 independent
specification definitions.

Finally, the source-paired production build was repeated after these changes.
Source `libvmmapi` and the complete `bhyve` binary, including DTrace linkage
and every provisional VirtIO device, build cleanly with the FreeBSD build
system's `-Werror` flags.  Invoking a separate component build against the
running system's installed headers still reproduces the expected version-skew
failure; it is not accepted as source-build evidence.

The administration teardown review found that owner reset drained dispatched
callbacks but owner destruction relied only on the caller having stopped its
queues.  `virtio_admin_owner_destroy()` now closes admission and waits for
every already-dispatched callback before destroying synchronization state or
permitting callback arguments to be released.  The
`destroy_drains_active_command` concurrency test holds a handler, starts
destruction, proves destruction remains blocked, and then releases the
handler.  This hardening does not advertise `VIRTIO_F_ADMIN_VQ`; concrete PCI
owner/member composition remains a release prerequisite.

The same administration portability pass closed an arithmetic edge in the
capability and resource-object snapshot-size calculators.  They previously
checked the unaligned entry sum but could still wrap when rounding that sum to
the next eight-byte boundary.  Both codecs now reject values above
`SIZE_MAX - 7` before alignment, with direct near-`SIZE_MAX` regressions that
do not depend on allocator failure to enforce the wire-format bound.

The group-state concurrency pass then found that validation and publication
were separate per-owner operations.  Although the fabric write lock excludes
normal group dispatch, a caller holding a registered owner can dispatch
directly between those operations.  A later owner could consequently become
busy after an earlier owner had already accepted restored command state.
Group restore now uses a multi-owner transaction: it locks the immutable
owner set in an internal canonical pointer order, checks every command mask
and lifecycle fence, and only then publishes every owner.  Caller-visible
state order therefore cannot create an overlapping-transaction deadlock.
A condition-variable regression holds the second
group active and proves a failed restore leaves the already-different first
group unchanged, then completes the same image successfully after quiescence.
Group snapshot similarly stages its bounded fixed-size record and copies it
to the caller only after every owner is quiescent; the same regression proves
an `EBUSY` snapshot leaves a sentinel-filled output buffer untouched.

The subsequent administration-queue save-state pass found that the queue bank
previously delegated directly to the group fabric, so an image did not bind
the number of administration queues or its preallocated input/output limits.
The bank now wraps group state in a checksummed, fixed-width little-endian
envelope carrying all three immutable shape values.  Restore rejects a
different queue count or scratch contract before touching group state, and
short, corrupt, or shape-mismatched images leave both the caller buffer and
the live command selection unchanged.

A transport-field review checked common-config offset 56 against VirtIO 1.4
and the pinned Linux driver.  `VIRTIO_F_NOTIF_CONFIG_DATA` (bit 39) is now
implemented independently of `VIRTIO_F_NOTIFICATION_DATA` (bit 38).  bhyve
publishes the specification-permitted trivial queue-index identifier; the
FreeBSD PCI guest stores the device-provided identifier and uses it as the low
16 bits of either notification width.  Independent tests cover field gating,
the bit-39-only 16-bit path, the combined 32-bit path, invalid capability
length, and literal nontrivial identifier selection.

Reset soak is now split into bounded, parallelizable lanes rather than one
ever-growing VM.  The original 100-iteration core-device lane is joined by a
20-iteration input/GPU/memory/sound lane and a 20-iteration translated
net/RNG/block IOMMU-fabric lane, each performing a full functional validation
every five resets.  Both added lanes select packed queues, including the IOMMU
request/event queues and each translated endpoint, while the original core
lane retains split-ring soak coverage.  The input provider is persistent and
forces a fresh LED
transition for each command, so repeated input tests exercise the same live
host device instead of silently becoming one-shot.  IOMMU resets use
dependency order: endpoints unbind, the IOMMU unbinds and rebinds, then
endpoints rebind.  The soak manifest, coverage contracts, parser self-test,
shell syntax, and `-Werror` input-helper build pass rootlessly; live execution
remains in the privileged handoff.

## 2026-07-28 nested-VMX entry and active-restore review

A renewed Intel SDM and pinned Linux 7.2-rc4 VM-entry pass found that the
final L0 event apply boundary revalidated zero-length software events without
retaining the virtual IA32_VMX_MISC[30] decision made by the planner.  The
value-only event plan now carries that capability decision and final apply
rejects a modified or stale plan that attempts zero-length software
injection when the virtual capability forbids it.  The same boundary validates
protected versus unrestricted real mode, the Intel exception-error vectors,
required error delivery, reserved high error-code bits, and software-event
encodings transactionally.

The active-L2 restore review found two destination-generation defects.  An
inactive incoming vCPU could previously replace the VM-wide registry while
the destination retained an older nested plan, portable continuation, or MSR
workspace owner.  Every destination vCPU is now proven pristine before
registry replacement, including inactive incoming records.  Conversely, a
fresh destination had no nested MSR scratch bound, so a valid active-L2
restore could reach final publication and fail.  Frozen staging now allocates
and capability-binds bounded destination-local scratch before shared registry
mutation.  Multi-vCPU restore retains all-or-nothing workspace acquisition
and rollback.

The resulting rootless architectural suite passes 142/142 both normally and
under ASan/UBSan.  The requirements validator accepts 166 nested-VMX entries
and all ten live qualification groups.  Ordinary and `BHYVE_SNAPSHOT`
variants of `vmm.ko` link with kernel `-Werror`, and source-paired
`libvmmapi` plus the complete `bhyve` binary link with the normal userland
`-Werror` policy.  Scoped whitespace validation is clean.  These results
establish model, codec, transaction, and build correctness; they do not
replace VMX execution on this Intel host.

Guest exposure remains experimental and default-off.  Release qualification
still requires Linux/KVM as L1 with Linux and 5BSD L2, instruction and
VM-entry failure cases, interrupt/APIC and timer execution, EPT/VPID and
invalidation, exit reflection, active-L2 checkpoint and restore, repeated
create/destroy, concurrency, fault, and soak tests.

## 2026-07-28 VirtIO checkpoint compatibility preflight

New snapshots now carry a portable compatibility description for every
VirtIO PCI function.  The source transport, queue count and maximum sizes,
MSI-X table shape, device-configuration size, offered and negotiated feature
sets, and shared-memory-region layout are recorded in both diagnostic metadata
and a versioned fixed-width little-endian envelope inside the device payload.
Restore checks that the metadata and payload agree, computes the destination
contract independently, and preflights all PCI devices before the first
device restore callback publishes state.  A destination may add features but
may not remove any source-offered or negotiated feature.

The format requires canonical zero-filled string tails.  This matters because
otherwise ignored bytes after the first NUL would be serialized but excluded
from equality checks.  The independent test mutates those trailing bytes and
proves both encoding and decoding reject the noncanonical form.  Additional
negative cases cover truncation, magic, schema, transport, queue, MSI-X,
configuration-size, shared-memory, and feature mismatches.  A CRC-32 over the
complete device payload is stored in the embedded envelope and diagnostic
metadata, then recomputed during the all-device preflight.  It detects
accidental corruption before device callbacks run; it is deliberately not
described as authentication against a party able to rewrite the checkpoint.

This pass also corrected a pre-existing libxo nesting error: kernel snapshot
records opened an instance under `devices` while closing it under
`kern_structs`.  Kernel records now consistently use the caller-selected
`kern_structs` array key, and the portability gate checks both the call and
the matching close.

The complete ASan/UBSan VirtIO harness passes after this change, including
158 validated requirements, 630 independent oracle definitions, and
1,189,896 packed-ring model assertions.  Source-paired `libvmmapi` and the
complete snapshot-enabled `bhyve` binary link under the FreeBSD `-Werror`
policy.

This is a device-configuration preflight, not yet a globally transactional
restore format.  Historical snapshots without the compatibility version
retain their prior per-device checks.  A later malformed device payload can
still fail after VM memory, kernel state, or an earlier device has been
restored into the new process.  The remaining common-state work is a
two-pass validate/commit contract for every snapshot section plus CPU,
memory-map, and backend compatibility baselines.

## 2026-07-28 checkpoint generation integrity

The outer checkpoint manifest is now format 3.  Publication hashes the
complete guest-RAM, kernel/device-state, and JSON-metadata generation members
only after they have been finalized and flushed, records canonical lowercase
SHA-256 values, and then performs the existing atomic manifest rename.
Restore opens the generation directory without following member symlinks,
opens all three members once, recomputes every digest on those exact
descriptors, and transfers the same descriptors into the restore loaders.
It rejects a missing, non-regular, symlinked, or changed member before loading
guest RAM or invoking any restore callback.  A later current-only-format
cleanup removed the unreleased format-1 and format-2 readers; neither older
manifest is parsed or restored.

The independent manifest test publishes a real three-member generation,
parses it back, verifies all hashes, independently mutates one byte in each
member without changing its length, and requires `EILSEQ` every time.  It
also retains explicit format-1 and format-2 rejection cases, atomic
replacement, interrupted write, manifest-fsync, and post-rename
directory-fsync cases.  The complete
ASan/UBSan VirtIO harness and direct `-Werror` compilation of both
`checkpoint_manifest.c` and `snapshot.c` pass.  SHA-256 here is an accidental
corruption detector and content binding mechanism, not authentication against
an actor who can rewrite both members and their manifest.

The restore coordinator also now validates the exact kernel-record and
device-record topology, requires every record to be present and nonempty, and
runs a metadata-order-independent range check requiring those records to form
one exact partition of the kernel/device-state member.  A gap, overlap,
zero-length range, arithmetic overflow, or unreferenced trailing byte is
rejected before destination mutation.  It then runs the complete VirtIO
destination compatibility preflight before copying
guest RAM.  The checks are repeated at the device restore boundary so a future
caller cannot accidentally bypass them.

CPU topology is now part of that restore contract rather than a late
side-effect.  New metadata records sockets, cores, threads, and total vCPUs;
restore validates the fixed-width bounds and exact product, installs the saved
topology before affinity maps and VM creation, and therefore cannot construct
one kernel topology while allocating a different number of userspace vCPU
objects.  Historical count-only checkpoints are accepted only when the caller
has supplied a destination topology with the same count.  Named topology
arrays are rejected against the already-known destination cardinality before
allocating checkpoint-controlled storage.

The memory member now has the same structural ordering guarantee.  Before the
ordinary RAM copy, a read-only preflight validates the base-memory length and
the complete generic-device-memory extension: canonical names, destination
identity and lengths, fixed-width header and entries, contiguous payload
layout, reserved fields, and every payload digest.  Validation does not write
destination memory.  The copy path deliberately validates again before
publishing generic device memory so an alternate future caller cannot bypass
the check.

The same memory-policy review found that restore parsed the saved `memflags`
and then unconditionally discarded them before `vm_setup_memory_domains()`.
Restore now rejects unknown or negative flag bits and retains the saved
`INCORE` and `WIRED` policy through allocation.  New VMs continue to derive
those flags from their configuration.  This closes an observable restore
contract bug but does not yet encode the complete NUMA/system-memory segment
topology; that remains part of the memory-map compatibility baseline.

The subsequent provisional-device lifecycle pass tightened virtio-mem restore
rollback.  A failed reconstruction now reverses only the contiguous bitmap
ranges that the current attempt successfully applied.  It no longer asks a
platform backend to unplug the entire configured region, which could affect
resources outside the saved bitmap for a backend with richer mapping
semantics.  The independent failure fixture records every touched block and
proves that rollback leaves both logical state and unrelated ranges
unchanged.  The complete ASan/UBSan rootless matrix, including 1,189,896
packed-ring model assertions, passes after this change.

A follow-up failure-recovery review found that the compensation callbacks
themselves could fail.  Virtio-mem now retains a private bitmap of only the
physical ranges reconstructed by the failed attempt, does not publish them as
guest-visible plugged memory, and rejects snapshots, resets, requested-size
changes, and guest requests while compensation remains incomplete.  A later
restore or system reset first retries removal of those exact ranges and may
then safely continue.  The negative fixture forces failure of both the second
reconstruction range and its first compensation, proves the fail-closed
surface, and then proves successful cleanup and reconstruction on retry.

The same recovery lens found that virtio-sound already remembered failed
restore cleanup but did not consult that state on ordinary guest requests.
Control, playback, and capture now return the device-defined I/O failure
without entering the backend until reset or a later restore completes
recovery.  The new fixture leaves a reconstructed stream running by failing
both a later stream and the compensating stop, proves that STOP and PCM output
have no backend side effects, and then proves that a successful reset restores
normal admission.

The RTC state-validation pass tightened the portable alarm record to accept
only states the device can produce.  A record that says no clock reading has
ever been observed may no longer carry an enabled or pending alarm or a
nonzero last reading.  The integrity field is deliberately recomputed in the
negative fixture so the semantic invariant is exercised independently of
corruption detection, and a separate assertion proves that every rejected
record leaves an existing destination alarm unchanged.  The focused RTC alarm
suite passes all five cases after the change.

The administration-virtqueue boundary review found that the unadvertised
queue/core adapters rejected command parts shorter than eight bytes.  VirtIO
1.4 section 2.13.1 instead requires every nonempty short readable structure to
be zero-extended and every nonempty short writable structure to be silently
truncated.  Both adapters now reserve transport failure for a zero-length
part, and the independent test walks lengths one through seven in both
directions, including a one-byte fragmented-chain result.  Rebuilding that
test also exposed Clang's inability to reason about the dynamically sorted
multi-owner restore lock set; the exception is now confined to two balanced
lock helpers while the transaction body remains under thread-safety analysis.
### Administration command extensibility review

The command envelope had already been changed to accept nonempty short
device-readable and device-writable portions, but a second pass against
VirtIO 1.4 section 2.13.1 found stricter behavior in command-specific
handlers.  LIST_USE inspected nonzero extension bytes, capability-list query
rejected an extension despite having no specified input, resource-object
commands required complete fixed headers and exact DESTROY lengths, and the
device-parts adapter required complete fixed fields.

The adapters now apply the specification rule at every layer: missing fixed
fields are zero, omitted fixed-size resource data is zero-filled, registered
variable-size resource data is padded or truncated at its declared bounds,
and bytes beyond specified fixed structures are ignored.  The transport still
rejects a wholly absent readable or writable descriptor part as required by
the driver-facing queue contract.  Independent tests cover nonzero LIST_USE
and capability-list extensions, an entirely omitted resource CREATE
structure, short MODIFY payloads, long QUERY/DESTROY tails, omitted
device-parts CREATE and mode structures, and a short metadata request.

The complete ASan/UBSan rootless device harness passed after these changes,
including 1,189,896 packed-ring model assertions.

### Lifecycle admission and asynchronous-control follow-up

A fresh full-matrix run exposed a test-quality defect after the network
control queue was moved onto the existing transmit worker: the Linux-shaped
indirect-control fixture still assumed that a queue notification completed
the command synchronously.  The fixture now observes the pending-work edge
and explicitly executes the worker callback, including the malformed-command
case.  It can therefore no longer pass by relying on the old callback
architecture.

The virtio-fs PCI fixture was also made complete enough to retain and exercise
the production reset, quiesce, and readiness-driven backend paths.  Its mocks
now model inert event registration, queue ownership, reset, backend progress,
quiesce/thaw control, and connection lifetime rather than allowing the linker
to discard those paths.  An ordinary non-snapshot bhyve compile then found a
snapshot-only helper escaping its feature guard; the condition is now local
to the snapshot callback, so both build configurations remain warning-clean.

Finally, the balloon, GPU, IOMMU, memory, and null-sound fixtures explicitly
pin their current lifecycle contract.  These devices do all accepted work
synchronously under the common device lock, so their private pause/resume
hooks are intentionally no-ops while the common transport fence excludes new
guest work.  This is a tested implementation constraint, not a claim that
their eventual production backends may remain synchronous.

The authoritative ASan/UBSan device-harness run completed with every fixture
passing after these corrections.  The remaining restore issue is unchanged:
global compatibility, record-layout, memory-layout, and payload-integrity
preflight exists, and each modern VirtIO restore has local rollback, but a
later device-specific payload can still be rejected after an earlier device
has committed.  The next common-state slice must introduce a genuinely
side-effect-free payload-validation phase before any device commit; merely
renaming the existing restore callback would not make the operation
transactional.

### Complete VirtIO payload preflight and translated-DMA review

The next common-state slice completed that conversion.  Every VirtIO PCI
device that implements save-state now also implements a validation operation
over the exact same byte representation.  The operation consumes common PCI,
MSI-X, modern transport, split/packed queue, and device-private state, rejects
trailing bytes, and restores all transient destination objects before
returning.  Device-private validators decode into local staging: block
configuration, balloon PFNs, GPU resources, virtio-mem ownership, RTC alarms,
sound streams, filesystem session state, SCSI inventory, console ports, 9P
identity, input frames, network negotiated header state, RNG common state, and
both vsock backends are checked without invoking their external backends or
publishing guest-visible state.

The translated-DMA pass removed the last deliberate exception.  Virtio-IOMMU
validation now constructs a temporary incoming mapping fabric from the
portable state record.  Fabric devices validate first; every endpoint that
negotiated `VIRTIO_F_ACCESS_PLATFORM` then resolves its saved queue addresses
through that prepared mapping set instead of either the old destination
fabric or direct GPA translation.  The prepared fabric suppresses fault and
idle callbacks, never replaces the live fabric, and is destroyed after all
endpoint validators on every success and failure path.  Only after the entire
device set passes preflight does ordinary restore publish the IOMMU fabric
and then restore dependent endpoints in the same phase order.

Focused tests prove that successful and corrupt validation leave live IOMMU
generation, mappings, faults, and device state unchanged, that the prepared
view maps the incoming topology, and that coordinator cleanup is null-safe
and exactly once.  Snapshot-enabled source compilation is warning-clean.
Live malformed multi-device checkpoint rejection and translated split/packed
restore remain privileged qualification gates; rootless tests cannot prove
the installed kernel, PCI topology, or guest driver activation.

## 5BSD virtio-blk multiqueue implementation review

The in-tree 5BSD block driver now negotiates `VIRTIO_BLK_F_MQ`, rejects an
advertised zero queue count, bounds allocation by the device count, CPU
capacity, and a 64-queue driver limit, and allocates one interrupt context per
request queue.  Ordinary requests are distributed round-robin while skipping
full queues.  Ordered requests wait for the entire queue set to empty,
quiesce waits for every queue, completion and detach drain every queue, and
crash-dump polling remains deliberately pinned to queue zero after draining
ordinary traffic.  The active count is observable through
`dev.vtblk.N.num_queues`.

This review also found a pre-existing deferred-busdma notification defect.
The callback cleared `vbr_busdma_wait` before using it to decide whether the
new descriptor required a host notification.  The callback now snapshots the
deferred state before clearing the admission fence and notifies the exact
queue that received the request.  Synchronous submissions notify their chosen
queue in the ordinary dispatch path.

The module builds warning-clean and the lab planner/self-tests include the
new `fivebsd-block-modern-q2` release case.  This is not yet live
qualification: the rebuilt 5BSD guest must report two active queues, complete
concurrent CPU-pinned root-disk I/O, and produce a retained host notification
for each queue.  The driver still serializes queue selection and submission
under its existing device mutex; that limits parallelism but does not make
the multiqueue wire behavior incorrect.  Per-queue locking is a later
performance change and must not be mixed into this correctness gate.

## 5BSD virtio-scsi multiqueue implementation review

The 5BSD SCSI driver now treats configuration `num_queues` as the count of
request queues following the fixed control and event queues.  It rejects
zero, bounds the active set by CPU capacity and a 64-queue implementation
limit, gives each request queue its own interrupt context, and sizes the CAM
request pool from the combined descriptor capacity.  Queue selection is
round-robin but admits a command only where the actual direct descriptor
count fits; indirect commands require one free head.  This avoids a global
CAM freeze caused by selecting a partially occupied queue while another
queue can accept the command.

Polling, timeout completion, reset completion, interrupt enable/disable,
detach draining, and CAM polling now cover every request queue.  Requests
retain their exact queue until completion, while TMF commands remain on the
control queue as required by the device layout.  The existing single driver
mutex still serializes CAM submission and shared sglist construction, which
is correct but not a final scaling optimization.

The module builds warning-clean.  The `fivebsd-scsi-modern-q2` release case
creates a real CTL ramdisk, requires the rebuilt guest driver to activate two
queues, performs concurrent randomized writes to disjoint ranges, reads and
compares those bytes, and correlates notifications on both host request
queues.  Until that root-only case passes, the activation ledger remains
`pending`.

## VirtIO CS01 provenance and administration retry review

The reference-corpus audit fetched the published OASIS VirtIO 1.4 Committee
Specification 01, verified its title and 8 April 2026 publication metadata,
and pinned the reproducible official PDF.  A later audit documented below
identified request-specific Cloudflare substitutions in the HTML
representation, so the catalog deliberately does not authenticate that
unstable representation.  Linux and QEMU remain pinned explanatory
references; neither supplies normative constants to the functional tests.

That source-level review found two related retry-status defects in the
unadvertised administration foundation.  Owner reset and transient SR-IOV
group admission previously paired the `TRYAGAIN` qualifier with `EINVAL`.
Section 2.13.1 defines `EAGAIN` as the retryable status and requires retryable
failures to have no command side effects.  Both paths now produce
`EAGAIN + TRYAGAIN`; permanent invalid-group failures remain
`EINVAL + INVALID_GROUP`.  Independent tests check both 16-bit fields and
prove that rejected group admission neither begins nor ends a command lease.
The focused strict-warning test and the complete ASan/UBSan device harness
pass after the correction.

The following Virtio-IOMMU feature-consistency pass found that the production
device advertised `VIRTIO_IOMMU_F_BYPASS_CONFIG` while its limits object
disabled bypass domains.  That feature defines both the writable bypass
configuration byte and `ATTACH_F_BYPASS`; a valid bypass-domain attachment
was therefore rejected after successful negotiation.  Production policy now
enables bypass domains whenever it exposes bit 6.  One test binds the
advertised feature to the production limits initializer, and the independent
translation fixture proves that an endpoint attached to a bypass domain uses
identity translation while MAP remains invalid for that domain.

## Portable-state structural coverage review

The architecture-neutral state review found a coverage omission rather than
a wire defect.  The structural portability guard enumerated every framed PCI
device whose magic lives in its PCI source, but that convention excluded
virtio-fs and virtio-sound.  Both devices deliberately delegate their private
state to fixed-width codecs (`VFS1` and `SND1`), so their current records were
portable while future native-width changes in either wrapper or codec could
have escaped this guard.

The validator now treats each delegated device as a pair: it checks the PCI
wrapper actually snapshots the codec, checks the codec's explicit magic and
version, scans both sources for native-width snapshot macros, and includes
both in the page/native-scalar structural audit.  Runtime tests continue to
cover literal bytes, corruption, truncation, rollback, and repeat restore.
Transient virtio-fs `owner_cookie` values remain process-local queue ownership
only: checkpoint admission drains every pending request before `VFS1` is
encoded, and the codec contains no owner cookie, pointer, descriptor, lock, or
native structure.  The fresh complete ASan/UBSan harness, including
1,189,896 independent packed-ring model checks, passes after this expansion.

The compatibility-envelope pass then found an independent semantic hole.  A
record whose metadata, embedded envelope, CRC, and outer manifest all agreed
could claim a negotiated feature which its own source offered-feature mask
did not contain.  Restore checked destination support, but that does not make
the alleged source negotiation legal.  Encoding, decoding, and destination
preflight now all reject this impossible source contract.  Independent tests
mutate the literal negotiated-feature bytes, construct an invalid in-memory
source, and distinguish malformed source state (`EINVAL`) from a valid source
whose contract the destination cannot provide (`ENOTSUP`).

A follow-up integration review found that the producer of that envelope used
the device model's raw capability mask rather than the modern transport's
actual offered mask.  The latter also adds `VERSION_1`,
`NOTIFICATION_DATA`, and `NOTIF_CONFIG_DATA` and removes features whose
runtime prerequisites (notably an attached DMA domain or suspend callbacks)
are absent.  A legal modern checkpoint could therefore have failed the new
self-consistency rule.  The modern transport now exposes one authoritative
offered-feature query used by negotiation, queue-layout checks, and
checkpoint compatibility.  The transport tests exercise its runtime
filtering, and the portability guard pins the checkpoint call site to that
same query so these views cannot silently diverge again.

The translated-DMA audit is now an executable structural gate as well as a
manual review.  Every PCI VirtIO device source is rejected if it calls a raw
guest-address mapper; device-private accesses must use descriptor parsing or
`vi_map_dma()`.  The sole exception is the VirtIO-IOMMU function itself,
whose reviewed validation and physical-map callbacks would otherwise recurse
through their own translation service.  The gate pins that exception to
exactly two call sites and separately pins the GPU backing-table command to
the common mapper.  The IOMMU default-bypass transition was also traced
through active request leases: it changes authorization for future
translations and advances the ring-cache generation, while already
authorized guest-RAM mappings remain pinned until their request lease ends.
An independent state test now locks down that linearization policy.

The subsequent cross-guest activation pass strengthened the scheduled 5BSD
common-transport lane.  It no longer infers `NOTIF_CONFIG_DATA` merely from a
doorbell whose configured identifier happens to equal the queue index.  The
rebuilt guest must expose both `NotificationData` and `NotifConfigData` in
the VirtIO PCI transport's negotiated-features sysctl, perform synchronous
root-disk I/O, and produce a host trace containing a nonzero available index
in the 32-bit notification payload.  The same disposable lane exercises a
DTrace-correlated selective entropy-queue reset and a named VirtIO-console
port with distinct bidirectional tokens; packed console qualification also
requires an enabled packed port queue in the retained host trace.

A complete warning-as-error `bhyve` build also passes using the source
world's staged `machine/vmm.h` and the amd64 source include root.  A plain
subdirectory build against the installed headers is not a valid result while
the running host predates `VM_CAP_NESTED_VMX`; that mismatch was diagnosed as
build-environment skew rather than hidden by changing the source ABI.

The block activation review added two independent 5BSD release gates without
touching the disposable root image.  One secondary sparse disk is patterned,
trimmed through FreeBSD `BIO_DELETE`, checked for backend-specific zero
readback and unchanged guard sectors, and correlated with host opcode 11.
Another uniquely sized patterned disk is opened read-only; the stock guest
must negotiate `ReadOnly`, reproduce the host digest, reject a write, and
reproduce the digest again.  The same lane requires `ConfigWCE` on the root
disk, performs synchronous I/O after selecting writethrough and writeback,
restores the original guest setting, and requires both host configuration
writes.  The discard oracle compares equal-length files rather than an
endless `/dev/zero`, avoiding a false EOF failure.  All three claims remain
`pending` in the activation ledger until the rebuilt host and guest complete
the scheduled live case.

The 5BSD SCSI activation lane now distinguishes enumeration from actual
backend use.  In addition to discovering a CAM disk and validating concurrent
data on every configured request queue, it requires the host to observe the
REPORT LUNS opcode and matches later READ/WRITE(10) traffic to the exact CTL
LUN allocated for that run.  This prevents an unrelated preexisting disk from
satisfying the guest-side discovery check.

## Active-I/O checkpoint qualification

A checkpoint test-quality review found that several device cases performed
I/O before and after a snapshot but did not keep work scheduled across the
checkpoint boundary.  They could therefore pass while only serializing idle
queues.  The Alpine runner now installs an independent guest workload helper.
Every checkpoint case keeps a UDP producer alive, while RNG, block, and SCSI
cases also keep one read-only raw-device worker alive.  The same guest PID must
survive and its atomically published progress counter must advance after both
the online checkpoint and the later suspend/restore.  This proves a workload
spans each lifecycle boundary without claiming that a particular descriptor
was necessarily owned at the exact snapshot instruction.

The RNG state contract is now explicit and independently tested: the device
has no private configuration payload and uses only the common queue-state
codec.  Entropy bytes and host entropy-source state are not checkpoint data.
After restore, the surviving guest worker must make new `/dev/hwrng` progress.
The source lifecycle is also explicit: startup and request reads retry
`EINTR`, while EOF, a non-retryable or transient source failure without a
readiness callback, and unexpected source loss retain the guest request and
set `DEVICE_NEEDS_RESET`.  The device never substitutes deterministic bytes.
The Linux live cases remain pending until they run against the rebuilt bhyve;
the source and model tests are not recorded as live activation evidence.

The vsock connection-table review found that the original global ceiling was
consulted only for inbound requests.  Outbound `CONNECTING` sockets and local
loopback pairs could therefore exceed it.  A single locked admission boundary
now covers all three paths, counts both connecting and established PCBs, and
adds a tunable per-remote-CID ceiling.  Loopback reserves both PCB slots before
allocating the accepted child, and teardown makes the capacity immediately
reusable.  The userspace kernel model exercises global and CID rejection,
binding preservation, loopback preallocation, inbound reset, and slot
reclamation; live multi-provider pressure remains a later root gate.

Console and 9P now have explicit external-session policies in the scheduled
live matrix.  The console release case configures two named ports on one
device and performs two complete close/reopen bidirectional exchanges through
each; the
portable state test also covers the second port and rejects a changed
secondary listener without partial publication.  For 9P, live fids remain
deliberately non-portable.  Its checkpoint case must first observe an active
mount rejection and prove the source mount remains usable, then unmount and
complete the idle-session round trip.  Both claims remain pending until the
rebuilt live cases pass.

The 9P export descriptor now also has FreeBSD's sticky
`FD_RESOLVE_BENEATH` policy before its Capsicum rights are reduced.  Every
later relative `openat`, `fstatat`, link, rename, and unlink operation made by
lib9p therefore inherits `O_RESOLVE_BENEATH`; operation capabilities and
pathname confinement are separate enforced properties.  A host regression
opens an in-export file successfully and verifies that an intermediate
symlink targeting the export's parent fails with `ENOTCAPABLE`.  The Linux
mount-level version of that escape test remains a live qualification item.
The follow-up call-site audit converted four process-working-directory paths:
FIFO creation uses `mkfifoat`, Unix sockets always use `bindat`, legacy
truncate opens beneath the export and calls `ftruncate`, and symlink metadata
uses `readlinkat`.  Protocol entry names used by create, link, rename, and
unlink are now exactly one nonempty, non-dot component; direct helper tests
cover the accepted and rejected forms.  Two nearby descriptor leaks on
`fdopendir` and `fstatfs` failure were closed in the same ownership pass.

Virtio-input now has a descriptor-state-sensitive live checkpoint oracle
rather than only before/after traffic.  The host provider can split one input
frame into `down` and `finish` commands.  The runner injects the key-down
without `SYN_REPORT`, requires a debug trace proving bhyve has staged exactly
that event, and takes the checkpoint before sending the frame tail.  After
online checkpoint and again after suspend/restore, the original guest
verifier PID must receive the exact completed keyboard/relative/absolute
sequence, atomically advance its counter, and return LED status to the same
host provider.  Separate split and packed cases are scheduled; neither is
recorded as live evidence until root qualification completes.

The vsock checkpoint policy is also now exercised explicitly instead of being
inferred from an idle round trip.  Each split/packed userspace/kernel case
opens a real host-to-guest stream, proves an initial echo, and then requires
checkpoint admission to reject the non-portable live connection.  A second
token on the same connection proves rollback rearmed the source device and
backend.  Only after both endpoints drain does the case proceed to the
ordinary portable checkpoint.  Existing userspace idle-restore evidence is
retained, while these stronger backend-policy results await the rebuilt live
matrix.

Virtio-console uses the same explicit external-session gate.  Its split and
packed checkpoint cases open the guest port and host Unix connection, require
the host to observe a unique guest-originated token through the actual virtio
port, echo a token, require checkpoint rejection, and echo a second token over
the same session after rollback.  Port-node presence alone is not treated as
readiness because host bytes can be discarded before PORT_READY.  The cases
then drain both endpoints before testing the portable listener-only restore
contract.  This matches the device model's deliberate refusal to serialize
host file descriptors or pending host bytes.

The Linux input release topology now covers device multiplicity rather than
only multiple event types on one function.  It creates two uniquely named
uinput devices, rejects an aliased host event path, attaches two independent
modern PCI functions, locates both through Linux's real virtio-input driver,
and performs the exact event plus reverse LED-status exchange on each.  Both
split and packed release lanes use the two-provider topology, while remaining
separate cases so a failure cannot be hidden by mixing topology and
ring-format results.

The input reset audit also found a timing gap independent of staged-frame
state.  An evdev descriptor could already be readable when the guest reset
and immediately re-enabled its event queue; if mevent had not dispatched yet,
the old host input could be delivered through the new queue.  Full and
selective event-queue reset now drain the nonblocking descriptor
synchronously while the VirtIO mutex still fences reconfiguration.  The
regression queues a complete host frame, resets, models immediate queue
replacement, and proves that the later callback consumes no descriptor and
publishes no interrupt.

The subsequent input loss-recovery pass handled the evdev queue-overrun ABI
explicitly.  On `SYN_DROPPED`, bhyve now abandons any partially staged frame,
ignores all untrustworthy host events through the next `SYN_REPORT`, and
delivers only that two-event loss frame to the guest.  Snapshot version 2
records the pending resynchronization flag, rejects every obsolete version,
and rejects impossible marker/count combinations before publishing
any destination state.  The first validation implementation exposed a
validate-only allocation hole: decoded events were staged only for restore,
although loss-shape validation also inspects them during
`VM_SNAPSHOT_VALIDATE`.  Validation and restore now share the same temporary
decode buffer, with publication still restricted to restore.  Independent
Linux input namespace constants drive tests that prove stale key and absolute
events never cross the loss boundary and that reset and suspend clear it.

The balloon operational review replaced its statistics `SIGEV_THREAD`
interval with bhyve's recurring `EVF_TIMER` event source.  A long reset or
checkpoint can therefore delay at most one event-loop callback instead of
accumulating an unbounded set of callback threads behind the VirtIO mutex.
The timer still refreshes one retained statistics descriptor at each
configured monotonic interval, observes the common quiesce and suspend
fences, and fails device initialization cleanly if event registration fails.
This also matches the single event-loop timer architecture used by the pinned
QEMU comparison without copying its implementation.

The GPU save-state review found that portable resource, scanout, and cursor
state was restored correctly inside the device model but no destination-local
display object was told to rebuild itself.  Successful restore now publishes
all decoded resources first, drops the state lock, repaints the complete
active scanout, and reissues the active cursor.  Validation still has no
observable callback, corrupt records still leave the running destination
unchanged, and the callbacks can safely read the newly restored pixels
without recursively taking the state mutex.

A second presentation-lifecycle pass covered the inverse restore case.
Replacing an active destination with an image that has no scanout or cursor
previously issued no callback, leaving stale pixels and a ghost cursor in a
future host backend.  The state/backend contract now has an explicit
destination-local reset callback.  Device reset and successful restore invoke
it outside the state lock; restore then reconstructs any active scanout and
cursor.  A focused empty-image restore proves that no stale presentation
survives while the guest resource table is atomically replaced.

The follow-up restore pass initially changed the repaint callback to use the
saved resource origin.  A fresh interface-contract and QEMU comparison caught
that as incorrect before handoff: display callbacks are scanout-local, while
`virtio_gpu_2d_state_copy_scanout()` translates those local coordinates through
the saved resource origin.  Restore therefore repaints local
`(0,0,width,height)`.  The portable-state test now uses a nonzero resource
origin and has the callback copy and verify the first displayed pixel, so it
proves the translation instead of merely counting callbacks.

The next conformance pass completed baseline EDID support.  The device now
advertises `VIRTIO_GPU_F_EDID`, accepts only the exact GET_EDID request shape,
returns the specified fixed-size response with zeroed reserved storage, and
builds a deterministic EDID 1.4 base block whose preferred timing matches the
configured scanout.  Independent protocol, queue, PCI-feature, and guest-helper
tests verify the feature bit, header, checksum, timing, response size, and
padding.  Linux live activation remains an explicit pending gate rather than a
rootless claim.

That pass also found that both the command path and restore path accepted a
scanout larger than the configured virtual monitor when the backing resource
was large enough.  Both paths now enforce the configured extent.  The portable
state test constructs a valid oversized resource, proves the oversized command
is rejected, and corrupts an otherwise valid snapshot to prove restore rejects
the same condition.

A separate balloon documentation audit found implementation/documentation
drift rather than a code defect: the statistics queue, deflate-on-OOM,
free-page reporting, and page poisoning were already implemented, while the
design document still listed part of that surface as future work.  The design
and manual now describe those opt-in queues and features while keeping the
distinct free-page-hinting feature explicitly unadvertised.  The
`free_page_reporting` manual entry was also moved from the virtio-net section
to the virtio-balloon section.

The following GPU productionization slice made virtual-monitor geometry an
explicit immutable device option.  Width and height are validated by the same
bounded timing model used to construct EDID, snapshot version 2 records them,
and restore rejects a differently configured destination and every obsolete
record version.  The release manifest
now proves default split-ring and 1920-by-1080 packed-ring monitors, while the
packed checkpoint lane saves the non-default identity.  The Linux oracle takes
the expected dimensions from the independent test manifest, verifies the exact
connector mode and EDID timing, resolves the framebuffer owned by that VirtIO
function, and writes and reads deterministic pixels at both scanout
boundaries.  This makes resource/backing/scanout/transfer/flush activity part
of the pending live gate instead of accepting enumeration alone.

The display-adapter review then added the missing renderer-neutral cursor
primitive.  Every baseline format passes through the existing byte-order
decoder and is composited into XRGB with rounded straight-alpha arithmetic;
transparent and opaque edges, row padding, independent strides, and unaligned
host words have sanitizer-backed tests.  No GUI, RFB, or amd64 assumption was
introduced into retained GPU state.

An orchestrator-contract review found four device-visible controls which the
shell runner accepted without `virtio-lab` governing their coverage: balloon
statistics, balloon deflate/reporting flags, RTC alarms, and virtio-mem
region/request sizes.  They are now public allowed behavior overrides with
release contracts.  Memory has an additional 128 MiB full-capacity lane and
the packed lane requests the full 256 MiB region, so the coverage is not a
single hardcoded geometry.  Input's focused cases were also corrected to
exercise both one- and two-device counts.  The lab self-test now requires 57
release contracts, 70 qualification contracts, and 105 qualification cases.

## Current rootless acceptance evidence

The complete rootless VirtIO release gate passes after the GPU EDID, scanout
containment, and documentation corrections.  It validates 167 independently
tracked VirtIO requirements and 635 specification-oracle definitions, then
runs every rootless device harness, malformed-descriptor and lifecycle fixture,
portable-state fixture, helper self-test, and the nested-VMX model suite.  The
production bhyve build also passes with `-Werror`.

The Intel nested-VMX model is no longer represented only by a prose plan.  The
`vmm.ko` module and `tests/sys/vmm` build successfully, the immutable-authority
validator accepts all 166 ledger entries, and all 142 registered
`vmx_nested_state_test` ATF cases pass.  Of the 166 requirements, 161 are
marked `foundation-tested-experimental`; the five
`experimental-pending-live` entries remain intentionally blocked on real

host soak.  The feature is not exposed merely because its model tests pass.

## Retained device-completion roadmap

The following obligations remain in the active plan and must not be erased by
a passing rootless harness:

- Balloon: Linux and 5BSD pressure/OOM activation, statistics and free-page
  reporting evidence, packed operation, and active restore.
- GPU 2D: a production presentation backend, live scanout/cursor/rectangle
  evidence, execution of the pending Linux EDID connector gate,
  saturation/reset/restore, packed operation, and translated DMA.
- Virtio-fs: production sandboxed backend service, Linux FUSE activation,
  credentials and namespace confinement, cancellation/reconnect, active
  checkpoint, and DAX only after a real shared-memory consumer is qualified.
- Virtio-mem: Linux plug/unplug and busy-memory activation, destination
  capacity policy, packed operation, active restore, and a 5BSD driver before
  making a cross-guest claim.
- Virtio-RTC: live alarm delivery across clock steps, suspend and repeated
  restore, plus Linux and future 5BSD driver activation.
- Virtio-sound: a production audio backend, playback/capture negotiation and
  underrun/overrun behavior, explicit active-PCM checkpoint policy, packed
  Linux activation, and a 5BSD driver before making a 5BSD claim.

Common obligations also remain explicit: real Linux and rebuilt-5BSD packed
qualification per supported device; selective queue reset under active I/O;
indirect and event-index evidence; ACCESS_PLATFORM on every DMA path;
Virtio-IOMMU live attach/map/unmap/fault/invalidation/checkpoint; a consumer
for shared-memory regions; guest-visible suspend; and complete administration
virtqueue/device-group ownership before either is advertised.  SCSI HOTPLUG,
CHANGE, and loss-aware EVENTS_MISSED require a trustworthy CTL event source.
Block secure erase requires a backend operation whose success means secure
erasure rather than discard or ordinary zeroing.  Until those contracts
exist, their optional feature bits remain off.

Additional devices are conditional rather than completeness theater.
Virtio-crypto is next only for a concrete acceleration or isolation workload;
virtio-video requires a media workload and production codec backend; and
Virtio-SCMI belongs to a future ARM/platform-management milestone.  Each must
start with a normative ledger, production backend contract, independent
negative/state tests, and a live guest driver.  No placeholder device is
advertised to make the roadmap appear complete.

## 2026-07-29 provisional-device production-boundary review

The next rotating pass reviewed RTC alarms, virtio-mem geometry, the sound
backend boundary, and SCSI asynchronous-event feasibility.

RTC alarm delivery remains event-driven through one absolute
`CLOCK_REALTIME` timerfd.  The implementation was checked directly against
section 5.23.6.6: a missing alarmq buffer retains one pending expiration,
disable clears service before the control response is published, backward
steps cannot manufacture a notification unless the clock crosses the alarm
again, and checkpoint disarm is serialized against an already selected
event-loop callback.

The virtio-mem review found and fixed one architecture-portability defect.
The bitmap rounding expression added seven while still in `uint32_t`, so the
maximum legal block count could wrap and under-allocate the ownership bitmap.
It now promotes the count to `size_t` before rounding, and the independent
construction test exercises the `UINT32_MAX` boundary without attempting a
huge allocation.

Virtio-sound now has an explicit `backend=null` configuration identity.
Omission remains compatible with that null backend, while every other value
is rejected before device publication.  This prevents a future blocking host
PCM implementation from being silently inserted into the current synchronous
notify path.  A real backend must use a distinct identity, bounded
asynchronous buffer ownership, RELEASE-before-control-completion ordering, and
versioned reconstruction policy.

The subsequent sound queue review found one RELEASE error-ordering defect.
Section 5.14.6.6.5.1 requires every pending stream I/O message to complete
before the RELEASE control request.  A malformed pending PCM chain previously
latched `NEEDS_RESET` and was returned with zero used bytes, but the control
queue still published its already prepared successful RELEASE response.  The
data drain now reports whether it crossed that ordering boundary cleanly,
continues retiring every descriptor that can still be claimed, and withholds
the successful control response when the mandatory flush cannot be
established.  The independent composition test injects the malformed
descriptor at RELEASE and verifies data-before-control completion, zero used
length for both failed chains, and the reset request.  Normal START and
RELEASE ordering remains covered separately.

The RTC checkpoint test-quality pass found that its device-local snapshot
mock implemented only SAVE and RESTORE, whereas production treats VALIDATE as
a loading operation too.  Consequently the historical RTC1 version-1
preflight path had not been executed by that composition suite.  The mock now
uses the production loading predicate for buffer and little-endian decoding,
and the version-1 case first validates an active pending alarm and proves that
preflight leaves its time, enable bit, and pending notification untouched
before the subsequent restore resets it.  All seven RTC composition cases and
the host/alarm model suites pass with the corrected oracle.

The virtio-fs reset/concurrency pass found that full device reset used the
same retained drain and completion arrays as backend failure and selective
queue reset without taking their `failure_mutex`.  A disconnect racing full
reset could overwrite owner cookies while the other path freed or completed
them.  Full reset now participates in the existing failure serializer across
drain, owner retirement, and callback publication.  A deterministic
two-thread test holds that serializer, starts full reset, proves reset cannot
enter the shared scratch region, releases it, and verifies clean completion.
All eight focused virtio-fs queue cases pass.

The earlier CTL feasibility finding is closed by the inventory subscription
described in the latest production-boundary review.  `CTL_TASK_QUERY_ASYNC_EVENT`
retains its original unit-attention purpose and is not reused for inventory
delivery.

After these changes, the complete sanitizer-backed device harness, the
requirements validator (167 entries and 635 independent definitions), the
Werror bhyve build, the nested-VMX ledger, and all 142 nested architectural
ATF cases pass.  Hardware nested qualification and the device live gates
listed above remain pending.
