## 2026-07-29 provisional-device lifecycle and build-integration review

The next lifecycle pass found a reset failure which the virtio-mem PCI
composition discarded.  `virtio_mem_host_reset()` can fail when a previous
restore could not transactionally revoke all newly plugged ranges.  The PCI
reset callback now preserves that condition through the common deferred
`DEVICE_NEEDS_RESET` latch instead of allowing the next guest initialization
to proceed against host ownership which no longer matches the portable
bitmap.  A white-box PCI test forces the incomplete-restore state and proves
that reset retains both the failure indication and the host model.

A clean component build also exposed that bhyve selected the installed
`vmmapi.h` while compiling code which uses the matching source-tree
`vm_create_devmem_auto()` API.  The bhyve Makefile now includes the
source-tree `lib/libvmmapi` directory explicitly.  This keeps incremental and
clean component builds on the same API as buildworld and prevents a stale
installed header from masking source/library integration errors.

The external-resource review rechecked balloon and non-DAX virtio-fs reset,
checkpoint, and reconstruction behavior.  Balloon host-page ownership remains
transactional: a failed reset undiscard retains both the bitmap and actual
accounting and latches `DEVICE_NEEDS_RESET`.  Virtio-fs uses authenticated
backend identity for reconstructible suspend/checkpoint state, fences
readiness callbacks during reconnect, and waits for QUIESCE/THAW completion
with monotonic condition-variable deadlines rather than polling.

The GPU 2D command review was repeated against VirtIO 1.4 sections 5.7.5 and
5.7.6.  The supported unaccelerated 2D command set is synchronous, so the
mandatory fence guarantee is met before a descriptor is returned.  Blob, 3D,
and shared-memory commands are neither implemented nor advertised.  The
current headless scanout model still requires a production presentation
backend before it can graduate from provisional status.

Focused balloon, virtio-fs, GPU, memory, RTC, and sound suites pass 75/75.

## 2026-07-29 RTC autonomous clock-step review

A second RTC pass invalidated an earlier host-timer assumption.  FreeBSD
absolute POSIX timers convert a realtime deadline to a relative callout when
armed.  A backward clock step is noticed at the old callout deadline, but a
forward step does not promptly wake the device.  After a one-shot alarm was
served, no host event remained armed to detect a later backward step and a
second crossing of the still-enabled alarm.  The portable alarm model was
correct when explicitly observed, but the production source did not provide
all observations required by VirtIO 1.4 section 5.23.6.6.

The PCI device now uses one nonblocking `CLOCK_REALTIME` timerfd registered
with bhyve's event loop.  Real deadlines use `TFD_TIMER_ABSTIME` and
`TFD_TIMER_CANCEL_ON_SET`, so `clock_settime(2)` and `settimeofday(2)` wake the
device on both forward and backward discontinuities.  After a notification is
served at or beyond its deadline, a maximum-time cancellation sentinel stays
active: it cannot repeatedly expire the already-served alarm, but a backward
step still cancels it and lets the model rearm the real deadline.  There is no
periodic poll or callback thread.

The focused composition tests independently drive cancellation reads and
clock values.  They prove prompt forward-step delivery, sentinel installation,
backward-step rearming, a second exact crossing notification, and timerfd's
FreeBSD contract where `timerfd_settime(2)` can replace the timer successfully
while reporting an unread `ECANCELED`.  Read, arm, and disarm failures still
request `DEVICE_NEEDS_RESET`.  A follow-up concurrency pass closed the
sample-to-arm window: after activating a cancellation sentinel, the device
samples realtime again, so a backward step immediately before activation is
observed directly while any later step is guaranteed to cancel the active fd.
The independent oracle forces that precise interleaving and proves the real
deadline replaces the sentinel.  The ten RTC composition cases pass, and bhyve
builds with the production `-Werror` flags.  Linux alarm, suspend, clock-step,
and checkpoint lanes remain root-only qualification gates.
The complete bhyve component rebuild passes with `-Werror`.
## 2026-07-29 balloon page-poison conformance pass

The next device-by-device normative pass found that the shared balloon
configuration still stopped at the historical eight-byte prefix even though
VirtIO 1.4 section 5.5.4 defines a 16-byte layout containing
`free_page_hint_cmd_id` and `poison_val`.  The production model and shared ABI
now expose the complete layout.  `page_poison=true` is an explicit,
default-off feature: the guest can write `poison_val` before `DRIVER_OK`, the
device rejects operational mutation, and portable `BAL1` version 4 state
preserves and compatibility-checks the value.

The lifecycle review found an important interaction with page reporting.
Discarding reported backing is only an optional optimization, and a host
discard can replace the guest's negotiated poison pattern.  When
`PAGE_POISON` is negotiated, the reporting queue therefore acknowledges valid
writable ranges without reverse-mapping or discarding them.  The non-poison
path retains the existing bounded discard optimization.

Independent fixture constants now cover feature bit 4 and all four
configuration offsets.  Unit tests cover pre/post-`DRIVER_OK` writes, absent
feature rejection, poison/reporting interaction, snapshot truncation,
feature-mismatched restore, and repeated restore.  The governed Linux lab
adds `BALLOON_PAGE_POISON=no|yes`, requires a 16-byte configuration, and
distinguishes discard evidence from poison-preservation evidence.  Stock
5BSD remains a declared driver gap rather than a false activation claim.

Validation evidence:

- bhyve builds cleanly with `-Werror`;
- all 9 balloon device ATF cases pass;
- the guest verifier self-test and both shell syntax checks pass;
- the VirtIO ledger validates 168 requirements and 638 independent oracle
  definitions;
- the lab self-test passes with 59 release and 72 qualification coverage
  contracts.

The following live-test review found that feature negotiation plus a
reporting log did not prove Linux executed its normative poison configuration
write.  The device now emits a dedicated `virtio:::balloon-poison` probe and
bounded debug record, and both split and packed Linux lanes require that host
event before accepting PAGE_POISON activation.  The activation ledger records
this guest/host correlation explicitly.  The complete sanitizer harness also
passes after the balloon change.

Intel nested VMX now has a first-class, default-off `nested` lab profile.  It
runs the complete architectural host gate before a hardware case, then
requires a reviewed root-owned L1 driver plus distinct immutable Linux/KVM
L1, Linux L2, and 5BSD L2 images.  A separate VM-free validator rejects
missing, duplicate, malformed, or incomplete evidence for the ten mandatory
feature groups, and its positive and negative schema tests pass.  Driver,
image, and source-paired bhyve digests are compared before and after the run;
evidence publishes only after complete validation.  This is orchestration,
not a live qualification claim: the L1 driver/images and real Intel run are
still required, and guest VMX exposure remains default-off.

## 2026-07-29 nested-VMX VMCS ownership review

The hardware-handoff pass traced VMCS01 and VMCS02 ownership through initial
entry, late entry failure, hot resume, refreeze, and run-loop error unwind.
The existing fail-stop policy is intentional: once a hardware rollback cannot
prove VMCS and software-MSR ownership, returning a recoverable error would
allow the pinned thread to migrate with CPU-local L2 state.

One earlier failure window was closed.  The VMCS02 begin adapter used to
validate only `launch.current` before clearing and loading VMCS02.  An
internally inconsistent launch object with `launched` set while `current` was
clear was therefore rejected by `vmx_nested_vmcs_launch_select()` only after
VMCS02 had become current, and the error path did not restore VMCS01.  Begin
now runs the complete launch-state invariant check before its first hardware
mutation.  Corrupt or stale bookkeeping fails with VMCS01 still current.

The focused VMM module rebuild passes, the immutable nested requirements
ledger validates, and all 142 nested architectural ATF cases pass.  The live
Intel/KVM L1 and Linux/5BSD L2 gate remains pending and the feature remains
unexposed by default.

## 2026-07-29 GPU cursor and nested capability integration review

The next GPU wire-format pass compared the 2D cursor commands with VirtIO 1.4
section 5.7.6.10 and the pinned Linux and QEMU references.  MOVE_CURSOR uses
only the position member; every other request field is ignored.  The decoder
previously shared UPDATE_CURSOR validation and rejected nonzero padding, which
created a device-specific wire restriction not present in the specification.
MOVE_CURSOR now decodes and validates only the scanout and coordinates while
ignoring the stale resource, hot-spot, and padding words.  The independent
protocol test deliberately supplies nonzero ignored fields and verifies that
they neither reject the request nor leak into the decoded operation.  All six
focused GPU protocol cases pass.

A clean bhyve component build exposed a separate source-integration problem.
The nested-VMX option referred directly to the new kernel capability enum, so
an otherwise valid source-tree component build failed when the installed
`machine/vmm.h` predated the source.  bhyve now resolves the stable
`nested_vmx` capability name through libvmmapi and fails closed with
`ENOTSUP` when the matching userspace/kernel support is unavailable.  This
keeps the capability mapping in one place, avoids a duplicated numeric
constant, and allows both incremental component builds and full buildworld
builds to enforce the same runtime contract.  The complete clean bhyve build
passes with `-Werror`.

The nested continuation review also traced every freeze/thaw abort path and
the staged hot-commit ownership transfer.  Abort calls which deliberately
discard their return value follow a locally established state and identity
fence and therefore cannot fail for a valid object; all such branches place
both owners in fail-stop quarantine when hardware rollback is not proven.
The staged plan is retained until the runtime transition succeeds, after
which `take` is an infallible ownership move under its checked preconditions.
No additional lifecycle defect was found in this pass.

## 2026-07-29 GPU scanout ownership review

The production-backend boundary review found that internal scanout state and
host presentation ownership were not fully coupled.  Explicit
SET_SCANOUT-with-resource-zero and RESOURCE_UNREF of an active scanout cleared
the model, but no callback told a renderer to release its surface.  This
would permit stale pixels to remain visible even though VirtIO 1.4 section
5.7.6.1 defines resource zero as scanout disable.  The behavior also differed
from the pinned QEMU device model, which disables every scanout referencing a
destroyed resource.

The GPU state interface now has a scanout lifecycle callback distinct from
pixel-damage delivery and whole-device reset.  It publishes bind, rebind,
explicit disable, active-resource destruction, and restored binding; resource
zero always carries a zero rectangle.  This separation lets a production
backend change surface ownership synchronously without treating a mode change
as a flush or a device reset.

The same negative test found that destroying the active cursor cleared its
resource ID but retained nonzero hot-spot fields.  That state violated the
portable snapshot invariant and the synthetic removal callback incorrectly
used zero coordinates from the UNREF request.  Cursor destruction now clears
the hot spot and reports the retained cursor position with resource zero.
All nine focused GPU state cases pass, the independent requirements ledger
maps the new lifecycle assertions, and `git diff --check` is clean.  A real
RFB/window-system adapter and live Linux/5BSD presentation qualification
remain release gates; the callback contract alone is not claimed as a
production display backend.

## 2026-07-29 nested-VMX destination-workspace review

The active-L2 restore transaction was rechecked for VM-wide atomicity and
destination-local ownership.  Registry publication was already staged and
transactional, but two distinct vCPU workspace objects could refer to
overlapping MSR plan or rollback arrays.  Each object passed its own
validation, so the transaction could publish successfully and allow one
vCPU's later nested entry or exit to overwrite another vCPU's scratch state.
The transaction now requires every active plan and rollback range to be
mutually disjoint before acquiring any workspace or replacing the VMCS
registry.  A two-vCPU regression proves rejection leaves both generations
zero, both workspaces inactive, and the old registry visible.

The same pass found that acquisition trusted a stored capacity when it was
merely a valid multiple between 512 and 4096.  The exact bound is derived from
the immutable virtual `IA32_VMX_MISC` contract and determines the allocation
size.  Ordinary acquisition and VM-wide restore now recompute that bound and
reject mismatched metadata; the production vCPU adapter also verifies that
the plan and rollback pointers still name the single allocation it owns.
Malformed workspace validation errors are propagated rather than collapsed
to an argument error.

The focused lifecycle and atomic-restore tests pass, all 142 rootless nested
ATF cases pass, the 166-entry nested requirements ledger validates, and the
VMM module rebuilds with `-Werror`.  Real Intel VMX execution, Linux/KVM L1
with Linux and 5BSD L2, active-L2 restore, and soak remain hardware gates.

## 2026-07-29 nested-VMX restore scratch-containment review

A follow-up pointer-ownership pass widened the active-L2 transaction audit
beyond cross-vCPU aliases.  A caller could bind an otherwise structurally
valid MSR plan or rollback array to bytes occupied by a VMCS registry, the
restore binding table, another workspace object, its capability contract, or
a generation output.  The transaction did not dereference the array during
publication, so it could appear to succeed; a later nested entry or exit would
then use those bytes as MSR scratch and corrupt already-published ownership
state.

The VM-wide preflight now requires every active plan and rollback range to be
disjoint from both registries, the complete binding table, every workspace
object, every immutable capability object, every generation output, and every
other active plan or rollback range.  These checks run before acquiring a
workspace or replacing the registry.  The regression deliberately points a
plan at the destination registry and proves rejection leaves both workspace
generations zero, both owners inactive, and the original VMCS contents
readable.

The focused atomicity case and all 142 rootless nested ATF cases pass, and the
VMM module rebuilds with kernel `-Werror`.  This is an internal containment
fix; it neither expands the exposed VMX capability set nor substitutes for
the outstanding live Intel L1/L2 and active-L2 restore gates.

## 2026-07-29 RTC autonomous clock-step review

The RTC alarm path previously used an absolute POSIX realtime timer.  FreeBSD
implements that interface by converting the deadline to a relative callout,
so an administrator moving the host clock forward could leave an alarm asleep
until the old relative interval elapsed.  Once a one-shot alarm fired, a later
backward step and re-crossing of the alarm deadline was also invisible.

The device now uses a nonblocking realtime timerfd registered with bhyve's
event loop.  Absolute alarms use `TFD_TIMER_CANCEL_ON_SET`; after an alarm has
been served, a far-future cancellation sentinel remains armed so backward
steps are observed without polling.  The callback distinguishes expiration,
clock cancellation, and unread cancellation state, and requests
`NEEDS_RESET` only for an actual timerfd failure.  Reset, suspend, and
checkpoint disarm the timerfd.

A second pass closed the sample-to-arm race in the served-alarm path.  The
device samples realtime again after installing the sentinel; if the clock
moved below the deadline in that window, it records the backward crossing and
reinstalls the real deadline.  Any later clock change cancels the already
active descriptor.

Ten RTC composition cases, five independent alarm-model cases, six host
cases, the clean bhyve `-Werror` build, and the complete sanitizer-backed
device harness pass.  The harness validates 168 requirement entries, 638
independent oracle definitions, 96 live activation claims, and more than a
million exhaustive/model assertions without a failure.  Live Linux alarm,
clock-step, suspend, and checkpoint qualification remains a root gate.

The virtio-mem pass traced geometry validation, bitmap bounds, platform

plugged memory; a separate system-reset operation exists for machine teardown.
All 13 focused host and composition cases pass.  Live Linux plug/unplug under

The provisional virtio-sound pass traced control/data descriptor validation,

cases pass.  This is still a null-backend foundation rather than a production
audio device: a host audio backend, live Linux ALSA operation, a 5BSD driver,
and an explicit active-PCM checkpoint policy remain release work.

## 2026-07-29 balloon and portable-state alias review

The balloon lifecycle pass traced PFN ownership, page-granularity checks,
duplicate handling, host-callback rollback, retained statistics descriptors,
free-page reporting, poison-page negotiation, selective queue reset, and
portable restore.  No new model defect was found.  Statistics, reporting,
poisoning, memory-pressure behavior, and active checkpoint still require live
Linux and 5BSD activation evidence; passing model tests do not close those
gates.

A separate API-boundary pass found that several portable-state writers assumed
their caller-provided output was disjoint from the object graph being encoded.
The virtio-fs writer could erase a tag, backend identity, backend state, or
session object before copying it.  The GPU writer could erase its locked mutex,
resource table, pixels, or backing descriptors.  The virtio-mem,
VirtIO-IOMMU, and virtio-sound writers had the same host-object or retained
storage hazard.  Such aliases are not produced by the normal snapshot
coordinator, but accepting them violated the transactional codec contract and
made internal misuse fail corruptly rather than fail closed.

The reviewed portable codecs now use one overflow-safe range-overlap predicate
and reject source/destination aliasing before mutating output.  This includes
virtio-fs, GPU, memory, IOMMU, sound, administration owners, group fabrics,
queue banks, capability managers, resource managers, and composed device
parts.  A follow-up pass extended the same contract to the RTC alarm codec and
the virtio-fs session snapshot/restore boundary, where aliasing could otherwise
overwrite a live mutex or the dispatch session while it was being copied.  The
same pass made the bounded virtio-fs tag encoder explicitly overlap-safe and
made the variable-length VIOT encoder reject an endpoint array embedded in its
output table before zeroing that table.  The
virtio-fs decoder also
rejects a decoded-result object that overlaps its borrowed input or expected
identity records.  Independent negative tests deliberately present overlapping
state objects, pixel or bitmap storage, backend records, and output-count
storage, then prove the source remains usable and a subsequent disjoint
snapshot succeeds.  The requirements ledger names each regression.

The clean bhyve component build passes with `-Werror`.  The complete
address/undefined-sanitizer device harness passes after the common-header
integration, including the requirements, activation, portability, and DMA
validators.  Live malformed-checkpoint injection remains a root-only gate.

## 2026-07-29 nested VPID/INVVPID instruction review

The Intel SDM instruction pseudocode and the pinned Linux/KVM
`handle_invvpid()` path agree that an unavailable VPID/INVVPID facility raises
`#UD` before CPL and operand checks, while a supported instruction validates
the type register before reading its mandatory 16-byte memory operand.  The
previous nested instruction dispatcher did not recognize INVVPID and therefore
could not prove this priority while the capability remained hidden.

The capture and frozen-handoff models now recognize INVVPID, preserve existing
operation numbers, apply operation-specific INVEPT/INVVPID availability gates,
decode the register type and memory descriptor, validate all four architectural
types, and pass only a virtual invalidation to a runtime callback.  Tests prove
the hidden-capability `#UD` path precedes a bad CPL and noncanonical address,
an unsupported type does not read guest memory, and an all-context descriptor
is still read before successful completion.

A subsequent ownership pass added a dedicated destination-local VPID02 owner
to each vCPU.  Allocation is strict and transactional: it has no VPID01
fallback, rejects zero or colliding results, remains stable for the vCPU
lifetime, releases before the allocator callback, and is never serialized.
Both ordinary VM-entry and active-L2 restore acquire this owner before
constructing the final entry environment.  A reused numeric VPID is not
assumed clean because translations are logical-processor-local.

The production INVVPID callback therefore records an explicit deferred-flush
obligation while the vCPU is frozen.  This also handles legal INVVPID execution
before the first L2 entry, when no VPID02 exists yet.  The obligation is
consumed only after final recomposition on the pinned entry CPU, immediately
before VMCS02 programming, using a single-context invalidation of exactly the
owned VPID02.  Allocation itself creates the same obligation, so allocator
reuse cannot expose stale translations.  Address and all-context virtual
requests are conservatively promoted to the owned whole context and can never
target VPID01 or another vCPU.

The VMM module builds cleanly with `-Werror`, and all 143 value-only nested
architectural cases pass, including allocation rollback, idempotent ownership,
pre-entry invalidation, deferred completion, and malformed-state rejection.
The production adapter also preserves the modeled no-hardware-VPID fallback:
when VMCS01 has no tag, VMCS02 is composed with VPID zero and the optional
acceleration cannot prevent otherwise valid nested execution.

VPID remains intentionally unadvertised.  A follow-up CPU-migration review
replaced the single global invalidation bit with destination-local per-logical-
CPU residency.  Allocation begins with no resident CPU.  The final pinned
entry CPU invalidates before its first use and then records residency; a CPU
migration invalidates lazily on the new CPU.  INVVPID and any VPID12 identity
transition atomically revoke every residency before the current CPU consumes
its obligation, so returning to an earlier CPU cannot observe stale
translations.  The bitmap is runtime-only, bounded to amd64's architectural
CPU limit, cleared before VPID release, and never serialized.  Hidden-VPID
operation remains conservative because an untagged L2 transition still
requests a flush on every entry.

All 143 value-only nested cases pass after adding two-CPU migration,
invalidation-revocation, malformed-residency, and range checks, and the VMM
module rebuilds with kernel `-Werror`.  Capability exposure still requires
real Intel execution covering allocator reuse, CPU migration, every advertised
INVVPID type, reset, active-L2 restore, and
Linux-L1/Linux-and-5BSD-L2 qualification.

The adjacent timer/TSC migration pass confirmed that active VMX
preemption-timer state is captured as a bounded remaining value in L1's
virtual-TSC domain and rebased only after the destination's final-CPU
environment refresh.  It also closed a noncanonical checkpoint case: an
enabled timer can no longer encode zero remaining without being expired, or
expiration with a nonzero remainder.  A shared state validator now guards
portable encoding, IA32_TSC-write recomposition, and final VMCS02 binding, so
freeze/thaw cannot silently reinterpret an ambiguous zero-valued timer.

The following EPT02 ownership pass closed a separate runtime-only aliasing
case.  A cached-root reference previously carried its slot, generation, and
opaque root address but not the cache which issued it.  Distinct per-vCPU
caches can legally reuse all three values, so presenting a reference to the
wrong cache could release or resolve another owner's root.  References now
carry an issuing-cache identity and every release and resolve rejects a
cross-cache reference as stale.  This identity is an L0 runtime pointer, is
discarded with the binding, and is never part of VMCS12 or checkpoint state.
The focused test constructs two deliberately colliding caches and proves that
neither resolve nor reference accounting crosses the ownership boundary.

## 2026-07-29 virtio-mem configuration-notification review

The memory-device pass compared configuration and request behavior with
VirtIO 1.4 sections 5.15.4 through 5.15.6, the pinned Linux driver, and the
pinned QEMU device model.  `UNPLUG_ALL` is deliberately one transactional
platform operation over the complete device region.  This matches the
reference device model, releases all device-memory backing, and avoids a
partially published multi-range operation.  Its successful response clears
the ownership bitmap and may shrink `usable_region_size` without a
configuration interrupt, exactly as the specification permits.

The review did find that the transport-neutral runtime
`requested_size` setter published its new fields without notifying the guest.
VirtIO 1.4 section 5.15.4.2 requires a configuration update when either
`requested_size` or `usable_region_size` changes outside `UNPLUG_ALL`.
The host contract now has an explicit configuration-change callback.  The
setter publishes both fields under the operation/state serializers, drops
both locks, and then invokes the callback; the PCI composition acquires its
concrete lifetime-stable device mutex and uses the common generation-latched
configuration interrupt.  Using the concrete mutex also makes the ownership
contract visible to compiler thread-safety analysis instead of hiding it
behind a nullable generic adapter.  Invalid and idempotent values do not
notify.  Independent tests synchronously read the new configuration outside
the host locks, prove `requested_size <= usable_region_size`, and verify that
the transport notification itself runs while the device mutex is held.

The focused ATF cases and the bhyve `-Werror` component build pass.  A
management-plane command that invokes this runtime setter and live Linux
split/packed plug-unplug activation remain root/live qualification work; the
presence of the model API and interrupt path is not recorded as that evidence.

## 2026-07-29 live VirtIO endpoint-inventory review

The reset and translated-DMA soak lanes no longer select devices for
verification or rebind from assumed PCI slot numbers.  After the guest drivers
are loaded, the Alpine harness now inventories the actual bound VirtIO PCI
functions, independently identifies the network and IOMMU functions by PCI
device identity, verifies the discovered endpoint count against the launch
topology, and uses those discovered BDFs for every later reset.  The
VirtIO-IOMMU guest verifier independently discovers every negotiated
`ACCESS_PLATFORM` endpoint in stable BDF order instead of reconstructing the
list from the requested device names.

This prevents a changed slot layout or newly composed device from silently
resetting or checking the wrong function.  The Python fixture, shell syntax
gate, payload-transfer test, and complete host-helper self-test pass.  A root
Linux run of the IOMMU reset lane remains required before this is live
evidence; feature negotiation and guest I/O still do not by themselves prove
the host translation probe fired for every endpoint DMA path.

## 2026-07-29 nested live-evidence integrity review

The hardware qualification wrapper previously validated ten feature rows and
three distinct evidence labels per row, but those labels did not resolve to
the Linux-L2 output, 5BSD-L2 output, or host trace that allegedly proved the
claim.  A runner could therefore accidentally publish placeholder labels and
still satisfy the schema.

The extended live contract now requires 36 distinct evidence artifacts.  Each token
maps to one owner-controlled regular file with a versioned header, the exact
feature identifier and role, `PASS`, a nonempty assertion, and either a guest
test record or host trace record as appropriate.  Missing, aliased,
group-writable, malformed, role-confused, and extra artifacts fail closed.
The wrapper hashes every named artifact before and after validation, retains
the content-address manifest, and publishes the TSV, artifacts, hashes, and
input identities together with one directory rename.  The VM-free helper
self-test covers the valid 36-artifact transaction plus missing feature,
duplicate token, cross-role alias, missing artifact, and host-without-trace
negatives.  This strengthens the gate without claiming that rootless schema
tests replace the pending Intel Linux/KVM L1 execution.

## 2026-07-29 PCI configuration portability review

The complete device-harness rebuild exposed four native-width pointer casts
in the common PCI configuration accessors.  Although production callers use
architecturally aligned register offsets, the backing configuration image is
a byte array, so the casts were not valid on a strict-alignment host and wrote
the host's native byte order instead of defining the PCI little-endian image.

All widths now delegate to one alignment-safe little-endian image codec.  An
independent test writes literal values, checks every resulting byte, decodes
them again, and repeats a 32-bit operation at an intentionally unaligned byte
offset.  The focused test and the complete bhyve `-Werror` build pass.  The
device-harness install tree was also missing from `BSD.tests.dist`; adding it
makes packaged and `make check` installs create the declared destination
instead of depending on a stale directory.  A real big-endian host remains a
live portability gate; the source and byte-vector tests no longer assume that
the current Intel host is representative.

## 2026-07-29 split-virtqueue byte-order review

The next architecture-neutral pass found that the common split-ring path
treated descriptor, available, used, and EVENT_IDX fields as native-endian C
integers.  The trailing `avail_event` macro also formed a `uint16_t *` beyond
a flexible-array member, which made an alignment promise not supplied by the
guest byte image.  This happened to work on the current little-endian Intel
host but was not a portable VirtIO implementation.

The split consumer now routes the available index, head indices, and every
direct and indirect descriptor field through one transport-aware codec.
VERSION_1 rings are little endian; the explicit legacy compatibility path
retains its guest-native rule, matching the distinction in the specification
and pinned Linux implementation.  Completion entries are encoded before a
release-ordered used-index publication.  Available and used event trailers
use alignment-safe copies; flags are converted at the guest boundary.  The
independent modern EVENT_IDX test checks the literal bytes for `0x1234` and
its disabled-kick predecessor as well as the document-defined modular
suppression formula.  The meta-validation gate now requires both conversion
and acquire/release publication rather than recognizing the old
native-endian source pattern.

Focused direct-chain, EVENT_IDX interrupt, and kick-suppression tests pass,
and bhyve builds cleanly with `-Werror`.  Real big-endian host execution and
the complete root/live matrix remain pending and are not inferred from these
model tests.

A subsequent ownership review found a checkpoint-critical ordering defect in
the first worker composition: it released the ledger entry immediately before
calling the completion callback.  The pause fast path could therefore observe
zero pending requests while used-ring publication was still blocked.  The
same review found that the synthetic lifecycle FLUSH freed its request and
discarded the backend error, allowing a checkpoint to appear durable after a
failed `fsync`.  Ownership now remains active through the entire completion
callback.  Lifecycle completion publishes its exact result under the device
lock; successful stabilization consumes that result, and a timed-out caller
transactionally hands reclamation to the eventual callback without a race or
use-after-free.  A controlled test blocks the completion callback itself and
proves that pause times out with one owner, then succeeds only after response
publication is released.  This failure mode was not covered by the original
blocked-backend test and is now an explicit regression gate.

## 2026-07-29 sanitizer and shared-memory restore review

The full device-harness sanitizer pass found one test-fixture defect which
ordinary assertion accounting had hidden: the console suspend/resume fixture
gave its receive queue a used ring but not its owning `virtio_softc`.  The
transport-aware EVENT_IDX encoder correctly needs that owner to distinguish
modern little-endian from legacy guest-native rings.  The fixture now
establishes the production queue ownership invariant.  The runner also sets
the address- and undefined-behavior sanitizers to halt and abort on their
first report, so a sanitizer diagnostic can no longer be followed by a
misleading zero-failure summary and successful process exit.

The complete undefined-behavior sanitizer matrix then passed, including 212
console checks, and the earlier full address/undefined run had otherwise
completed all device suites.  This is rootless model evidence, not a
substitute for the Linux/5BSD live matrix.

The shared-memory capability review also separated capability construction
from restore compatibility.  Registration remains initialization-only,
bounded by the selected memory BAR, unique by `shmid`, and sorted into a
canonical topology.  The exact restore comparator is now independently
exercised for count, identifier, BAR, offset, and length mismatches before
state mutation.  No device advertises a shared-memory consumer yet, so mapping
lifetime, revocation, and live guest evidence remain open gates.

## 2026-07-30 suspend and administration conformance review

The all-device suspend pass found three lifecycle defects.  Balloon retained
the statistics descriptor across guest-visible suspend even though VirtIO 1.4
requires every device-owned buffer to be completed before the device publishes
SUSPEND.  The guest-suspend callback now completes that descriptor under the
already-published common queue fence, and checkpoint pause reuses the same
operation.  RTC and vsock resume-complete callbacks also assumed checkpoint
resume's unlocked context; guest resume invokes the same callback from the
status-write path with the non-recursive device mutex already held.  Both
callbacks now explicitly support the two lock contexts.  Focused balloon and
RTC/vsock lifecycle tests pass, including locked guest resume.

The administration-command review then compared the unadvertised common model
with sections 2.12 and 2.13.  LIST_QUERY and LIST_USE incorrectly rejected a
nonzero `group_member_id`; the field is unused for those commands and the
device requirement only validates it when a command uses it.  The core now
ignores that field for the two list commands while retaining ordinary member
validation everywhere else.  It also forces the reserved success qualifier to
zero at the common callback boundary, preventing a command-specific handler
bug from emitting a nonconforming successful result.  Independent self-group
and SR-IOV-group cases cover the unused field and an intentionally defective
handler covers qualifier normalization.  All 39 administration tests pass
under the normal `-Werror` build.  `VIRTIO_F_ADMIN_VQ` remains masked: this
foundation is not release evidence for a PCI administration capability,
owner/member composition, or live PF/VF operation.

## 2026-07-30 live device-suspend qualification

The activation-ledger review found that guest-visible device suspend had
strong model coverage but no live case which actually wrote the SUSPEND
status.  Checkpoint pause and whole-guest suspend are different lifecycle
operations and cannot prove that interface.

The rebuilt-5BSD common-lifecycle lane now explicitly requires the modern
transport to negotiate `VIRTIO_F_SUSPEND`, uses `devctl` to suspend and resume
the RNG, root-block, vsock, console, and balloon VirtIO PCI parents, and proves
destination-local data or state after every resume.  The optional net and SCSI
lanes perform the same transition when those devices are present.  Each
transition must also appear in the host's debug-gated common transport log;
the existing DTrace lifecycle probes remain the production tracing boundary.
The common implementation now logs begin, completion, and failure without
adding unconditional hot-path output.

The lab self-tests, 169-entry requirements validator, activation-ledger
validator, `git diff --check`, and bhyve `-Werror` build pass.  The
`fivebsd-modern-common-lifecycle` status remains pending until it is run with
the rebuilt guest and host; no live result is inferred from the rootless
checks.

## 2026-07-30 live common-ring evidence

The common bhyve queue decoder now exposes dormant USDT probes for accepted
descriptor chains and split/packed event-index decisions.  The scheduled
`fivebsd-modern-common-lifecycle` lane attaches a bounded DTrace consumer,
requires the rebuilt guest to negotiate `RingIndirectDesc` and `RingEventIdx`,
then rejects the run unless real workload produces an accepted indirect chain,
an EVENT_IDX-suppressed completion, and an EVENT_IDX-delivered interrupt.
This closes the previous test-design gap where feature negotiation could be
mistaken for actual activation.  The ledger claims remain pending until the
root-only live lane passes.

The same installed trace helper is now enabled by the scheduled Linux
`net-modern-q2` lane.  That lane requires indirect descriptors and EVENT_IDX,
programs the two-pair RSS table (which supplies a known indirect control
request), runs traffic on both transmit queues, and applies the same
accepted-chain, suppressed-completion, and delivered-interrupt gates.  A
VM-free parser self-test accepts the complete evidence tuple and rejects a
direct-only trace, missing suppression, and a mismatched ring layout.  These
changes improve the independence and cross-guest shape of the test, but do
not promote either activation claim before the root-only runs complete.

The packed-net lane now uses the same gate with packed-layout filtering.
During review, the packed event probe was widened from descriptor-threshold
decisions alone to every valid packed suppression mode; enable/disable mode
is real driver behavior and must not disappear from operational evidence.
The Linux parser now also scopes all three required facts to `vtnet`.
Evidence emitted by another VirtIO device in a combined VM cannot qualify the
network feature claim; a mixed-device negative fixture pins that behavior.
The bhyve DTrace build and link complete with `-Werror`.

## 2026-07-30 ACCESS_PLATFORM binding-race review

The common DMA-domain lifecycle had a load-before-accounting race:
`vi_req_dma_acquire()` called the provider acquire callback before publishing
its common active-request count, while `vi_clear_dma_domain()` used that count
to decide when the callback table and argument could be cleared.  A blocking
provider acquire could therefore overlap a successful detach and resume with
stale callbacks and a cleared argument.

The binding pointer is now release-published, detach atomically closes a
separate acquisition gate, and each request publishes its common lease before
calling the provider.  Acquisition rechecks both the gate and binding after
publication; detach clears the binding only after observing zero leases.
Domain publication uses the same mutation gate, so overlapping attach,
detach, or duplicate attach operations cannot lose or partially publish a
binding.  Release continues to hold the lease through the provider callback.
A deterministic pthread regression blocks inside provider acquisition,
proves the common lease is already visible, requires concurrent detach to
return `EBUSY`, then completes and detaches cleanly.  The source-structure
boundary gate now requires the atomic publication and mutation pattern rather
than the obsolete direct callback dereference.  The focused domain tests, the
complete rootless device matrix, and the complete bhyve `-Werror` build pass.
Live Linux translated-DMA qualification remains pending.

## 2026-07-30 existing-device state and isolation review

SCSI checkpoint ownership was traced from the common queue admission fence
through every request worker, CTL call, used-ring publication, timeout
rollback, selective reset, and backend-inventory comparison.  The device uses
one monotonic drain deadline, rolls back queues acquired before a later
failure, and refuses to serialize active CTL ownership.  The later
asynchronous-event milestone below adds the ordered, loss-aware CTL inventory
subscription that this review identified as the prerequisite for HOTPLUG and
CHANGE.

The 9P pass found a policy mismatch below the protocol layer.  A read-only
export correctly rejected mutating 9P requests, but its root directory
descriptor still retained capabilities for write, create, unlink, rename,
metadata changes, and writable extended attributes.  Root descriptor rights
are now derived from the export mode: lookup/read/identity operations remain
available in both modes and mutation rights are added only for a writable
export.  A direct rights-matrix regression checks both configurations.
Active fids and requests remain deliberately rejected at checkpoint because
lib9p backend descriptors and credentials are not portable state.

The standalone `contrib/lib9p` build was then rebuilt from a clean object
directory as an independent source/object-tree check.  That exposed three
build-hygiene defects outside the bhyve-only build: obsolete `LIBADD` library
names in the library, obsolete `LDADD` usage in its example, and Python
self-tests that assumed the object directory was their source directory.
They now use the canonical in-tree library names and `${.CURDIR}` for test
scripts; the library, example server, and all five protocol self-tests build
and pass with the tree's warning policy.  This does not make active fids
portable: `struct l9p_fid` still owns backend-specific `lo_aux`, and the fs
backend state includes host file/directory descriptors, credentials, ACL
state, and mutexes.  A live-fid checkpoint must therefore begin with a
versioned backend-neutral fid identity/reopen contract and request
cancellation/linearization model, rather than serializing those objects.

The same ownership review found that the library's compiled worker count had
drifted from its own fid contract.  `request.c` documents that fids require a
single dispatcher per connection, but `L9P_NUMTHREADS` had created eight
workers, allowing dependent requests to execute out of order or concurrently
alter one fid.  The default is now one worker per connection (plus its
responder); independent connections still run concurrently.  This is a
correctness boundary, not a permanent throughput design: increasing
per-connection parallelism requires explicit fid ownership and a dependency
ordering contract.  The standalone library/example/protocol self-tests and
26 focused lib9p/virtio-9p ATF cases pass after the change.

## 2026-07-30 reset-soak device publication review

The reset soak had a guest-side publication race rather than a block or SCSI
emulation failure.  Linux can republish a bound VirtIO child in sysfs before
`mdev` or `udev` has recreated the corresponding `/dev/vd*` node.  The former
verifiers accepted the sysfs match and immediately opened the absent node,
which produced a misleading `FileNotFoundError` after a successful PCI
rebind.

The block and SCSI verifiers now use a bounded 30-second discovery operation
which requires both a unique, capacity-matched bound child and its device
node.  It uses a monotonic deadline and short waits, so a genuinely missing
device terminates with the last discovery error rather than hanging.  Their
VM-free self-tests construct the complete sysfs and device-node publication
state and exercise the new path.  Both focused self-tests, the complete host
helper self-test suite, and `git diff --check` pass.  Live reset-soak evidence
remains pending; this change does not reclassify the earlier failed run as a
device pass.

## 2026-07-30 shared-memory runtime foundation

The PCI shared-memory capability builder previously described immutable
topology but could not service the BAR it advertised.  The common modern
transport now supports destination-local backing registrations keyed by
`shmid`.  Runtime pointers remain outside the versioned transport record;
restore continues to compare only the portable BAR, offset, length, and ID
topology.  A registration is accepted only before driver activation, must
exactly match the capability length, and must fit the host address space.

BAR reads and writes are bounds checked and explicitly little-endian for
1-, 2-, 4-, and 8-byte accesses.  Read-only regions reject writes.  Reset,
guest suspend, and checkpoint quiesce fence all shared-memory access, and
overlapping region IDs are accepted only when their backings alias the same
PCI bytes.  This prevents registration order from changing observable BAR
contents.  A lifecycle owner can revoke and reconstruct a backing while the
common reset/quiesce fence excludes guest access; an active unfenced device
cannot change the registry.

The focused test covers malformed registration, missing IDs, size mismatch,
duplicate registration, little-endian access, boundary crossing, read-only
behavior, suspend fencing, and consistent/inconsistent overlap.  It passes,
and the complete 28-case modern transport suite, 169-entry requirements
catalog, and bhyve `-Werror` build pass.  No device feature is
advertised yet: GPU blob resources and virtio-fs DAX still require their
device-specific allocation, map/unmap, revocation, and restore contracts plus
live guest qualification.

The follow-up observability pass added a non-hot-path
`virtio:::transport-shared-memory` probe for each successful backing bind and
revocation.  Its arguments carry the device, region identifier, lifecycle
event, length, and writable policy without exposing mapped contents.  This
keeps runtime ownership diagnosable without logging every shared-memory load
or store.  The DTrace-enabled bhyve build passes with `-Werror`, and the
focused modern transport suite remains 28/28.

The GPU comparison also closed an unsafe roadmap ambiguity.  VirtIO 1.4
requires MAP_BLOB and UNMAP_BLOB whenever the host-visible GPU region exists,
and host-only/default blobs depend on rendering-context semantics.  Therefore
the generic shared-memory substrate is not used to publish a dummy GPU BAR:
VIRGL, RESOURCE_BLOB, the host-visible capability, mapping lifetime, and
portable state remain one indivisible future qualification unit.

## 2026-07-30 VirtIO-SCSI asynchronous inventory events

CTL now exposes a fixed-width version-2 subscription ABI on each
`/dev/cam/ctl` open.  Subscription atomically inserts the listener and queues a
RESCAN baseline, closing the inventory-snapshot race without polling.  ADDED,
REMOVED, and capacity CHANGED records use a global nonzero monotonic sequence.
Each subscriber owns a bounded queue; overflow marks the first later accepted
record as missed, or returns a synthetic missed RESCAN after retained records
when no later event arrives.  `poll(2)` and `kqueue(2)` are readiness signals,
not periodic inventory scans, and `destroy_dev()` drains every cdevpriv
subscriber before CTL destroys its mutex.

bhyve subscribes before publishing the device.  HOTPLUG and CHANGE enter the
instance feature set only after successful subscription, so kernels without
the ABI continue to advertise neither feature.  CTL records are strictly
versioned and reserved/unknown fields are rejected.  The initial `UINT32_MAX`
RESCAN sentinel is accepted only for RESCAN; real events retain the 14-bit LUN
limit.  The ABI carries the fixed-width SCSI peripheral type, malformed types
are rejected, and PARAM_CHANGE is suppressed for MMC as section 5.6.6.3.3
requires.  Deliberately filtered MMC records and records for unnegotiated
event features still advance the private CTL sequence cursor, so the next
accepted event is not falsely marked as lost.  Linux/QEMU-compatible
flat-space LUN encoding, capacity-change
ASC/ASCQ, descriptor direction and size checks, sequence-gap detection,
bounded backpressure, selective reset, and `EVENTS_MISSED` are independently
covered.  Pre-DRIVER_OK and full-reset events rely on the driver's normal
inventory discovery rather than manufacturing a missing-buffer event.  Restore
reconstructs the destination subscription and conservatively forces a guest
rescan instead of serializing a file descriptor or replaying stale host
events.

The CTL module, DTrace-enabled bhyve, CTL ABI test, and SCSI harness build with
`-Werror`.  All eight event-state cases and all 24 SCSI device cases pass, as do
the guest-helper self-test, orchestration self-test, and 169-entry requirements
validator.  The release profile now contains `scsi-modern-events`, which
creates, resizes, and removes a unique CTL LUN and requires Linux to observe
all three transitions with HOTPLUG and CHANGE negotiated and without any
manual guest scan.  That root-only live case, a saturation/inventory race
stress, and equivalent 5BSD live activation remain pending evidence.

The 5BSD driver-side pass then found and fixed three independent event-path
defects.  CHANGE is now negotiated and PARAM_CHANGE rescans its addressed LUN;
event and reason fields are converted from device endian; and an event carrying
EVENTS_MISSED is no longer discarded after the recovery scan.  The event
storage is dynamically sized from a bounded, validated `event_info_size`
instead of using that device-controlled length against fixed 16-byte objects.
The size remains an unsigned fixed-width value until after the upper bound is
proved, preventing a hostile value above `INT_MAX` from narrowing negative
before validation.
The release lane `fivebsd-scsi-modern-q2` now schedules no-manual-rescan add,
capacity-change, and removal checks.  Its rebuilt-kernel live result remains
pending.

The CTL ABI suite now also has a root-only live loss-boundary case.  It fills
the real minimum-depth kernel queue, causes one event to be dropped, releases a
slot, and verifies that only the first subsequently accepted record carries
MISSED.  Cleanup tracks and removes every temporary LUN even on failure.

## 2026-07-30 VirtIO-IOMMU runtime/state range consistency

A portability pass compared the translation model's accepted runtime states
with its portable restore validator.  The runtime correctly permits an
inclusive one-byte mapping when bit zero of `page_size_mask` advertises
one-byte granularity, but restore previously rejected the same mapping by
testing `virt_end <= virt_start`.  Such a VM could use and save the mapping but
could never restore it.  Restore now uses the runtime's exact inclusive range
rule and still rejects reversed ranges.

The independent byte-granularity case now checkpoints, restores, translates,
and unmaps that boundary mapping.  All thirteen focused translation-state
cases pass, including active-DMA revocation, deferred reset, bypass policy
changes, canonical images, transactional restore, bounded faults, and snapshot
alias rejection.  The test builds with the tree's `-Werror` policy.  Live
Linux ACCESS_PLATFORM traffic, active-I/O checkpoint, and a 5BSD guest driver
remain pending qualification and are not implied by these model results.

## 2026-07-30 VirtIO-console resume serialization

The lifecycle/concurrency pass found that console resume completion touched
receive virtqueues without consistently owning the VirtIO mutex.  Guest-driven
resume calls the hook from the status-write path with the mutex already held,
whereas checkpoint resume calls it after the common checkpoint fence and
mutex have been released.  The latter could race a host socket callback or a
guest queue operation while inspecting descriptors and rearming receive
sources.

The console callback now follows the established block, RTC, and vsock
dual-caller contract: it detects existing ownership and otherwise acquires the
VirtIO mutex around control and data queue inspection.  Its focused lifecycle
test executes both calling contexts and verifies that the already-locked path
does not relock or drop ownership.  All 22 console harness cases pass with the
tree's warning policy.  Live Linux multiport checkpoint/restore and equivalent
5BSD multiport activation remain pending evidence.

## 2026-07-30 VirtIO-9P bounded suspend

The 9P lifecycle pass found that guest suspend used an unbounded condition
wait for accepted lib9p work.  A backend filesystem operation that never
returns could therefore retain the status-write vCPU indefinitely even though
the common VirtIO admission fence had already stopped new requests.

The per-device condition variable now uses `CLOCK_MONOTONIC`, and suspend has
a single 30-second device-wide deadline.  Expiry returns `ETIMEDOUT`; common
lifecycle rollback reopens admission, while the existing lib9p connection,
fid namespace, and outstanding request remain intact.  The focused negative
case uses a one-second test override and proves that timeout neither closes
nor replaces the session.  All focused 9P harness cases pass.  The separate
lib9p full-reset close path still relies on worker completion because lib9p
does not expose a safe cancellation primitive; long-running reset/close fault
qualification remains a release gate rather than being represented as solved
by the suspend deadline.

## 2026-07-30 VirtIO-input lifecycle recheck

The input pass traced host evdev readiness, frame staging, status writes,
selective and full reset, guest suspend, checkpoint pause, and transactional
restore.  Host input is nonblocking and serialized by the VirtIO mutex;
checkpoint disables its event source before acquiring that mutex and enables
it before releasing the mutex, so an immediately ready callback cannot race
the state image.  Reset drains host events synchronously before a replacement
queue can accept them.  Oversized frames and descriptor starvation drop the
whole frame, while `SYN_DROPPED` retains only the loss marker and terminating
report needed for guest resynchronization.

No additional implementation defect was found in this pass.  The complete
focused input suite passes, including hostile/scatter-gather descriptors,
queue saturation, rapid reset/re-enable, configuration selectors, staged and
loss-frame restore, and event-source resume failure/retry.  Live multiple-input
device activation, packed rings, active checkpoint, and injection/reset soak
remain qualification work.

## 2026-07-30 VirtIO-RNG replay and failure recheck

The entropy pass confirmed that the device has no private checkpoint payload:
the host random descriptor is destination-local, and common queue state is the
only device-visible state carried through restore.  Synchronous descriptor
processing is fenced by the common VirtIO mutex, each host read is bounded to
64 KiB, `EINTR` is retried, and EOF or any unrecoverable/transient source
failure retains the request and publishes `NEEDS_RESET` rather than leaving a
descriptor with no future wakeup.

The focused RNG suite passes hostile descriptor, scatter/gather, partial fill,
source failure, startup, bounded-work, completion-order, packed opt-in, and
common-only save-state cases.  The pass removed an unused per-device scalar
which had no protocol or lifecycle meaning.  Live packed Linux and 5BSD
activation, reset/rebind soak, source-failure injection, and proof that
post-restore requests obtain fresh destination entropy remain qualification
gates.

## 2026-07-30 VirtIO-balloon lifecycle and state recheck

The balloon pass compared feature dependencies and queue numbering with
VirtIO 1.4 section 5.5 and Linux's driver behavior, then traced PFN ownership
through inflate, deflate, reset, reporting, guest suspend, checkpoint, and
transactional restore.  The host-page tracker remains independent of the
host architecture: 4 KiB balloon PFNs are aggregated into the platform's
actual discard granule, and a failed discard, undiscard, or restore transition
rolls ownership back before guest-visible state is published.

One checkpoint-only failure path was corrected.  Releasing a stale retained
statistics descriptor correctly set `DEVICE_NEEDS_RESET`, and guest suspend
already converted that state into a failed suspend, but the balloon's
checkpoint pause wrapper ignored it and returned success.  Checkpoint pause
now returns `EIO`, so the coordinator cannot publish a snapshot after queue
ownership became unprovable.  The focused test constructs that stale
generation and verifies the pause failure and reset latch.  All nine balloon
device cases and all nine independent accounting/tracker/parser cases pass.
Live Linux and 5BSD feature activation, memory-pressure behavior, packed-ring
operation, active checkpoint, and reset/rebind soak remain release evidence.

## 2026-07-30 provisional-device lifecycle recheck

The virtio-fs pass traced connection admission, asynchronous request
ownership, reset cancellation, quiesce, thaw, backend identity, and
transactional restore.  A rejected QUIESCE resumes admission; a rejected THAW
deliberately retains the quiesced state so the same destination can retry
without publishing a partially resumed connection.  No new implementation
defect was found.  All 73 focused backend, I/O, client, chain, pending,
dispatch, outbox, queue, host, state, connection, and PCI cases pass.  A
production sandboxed backend daemon and live Linux operation remain required;
5BSD has no stock virtio-fs guest driver, and DAX remains gated on a qualified
shared-memory consumer.

The virtio-mem, virtio-RTC, and virtio-sound passes likewise found no new
model defect.  Virtio-mem keeps its portable bitmap/range transaction
independent of the destination mapping.  RTC alarms use an event-driven
timerfd path, rearm after backward time changes, and serialize portable alarm
state rather than host timer handles.  Sound remains a synchronous null
backend: its current quiesce and state contract is valid for that backend but
must not be reused for a future asynchronous audio backend without explicit
buffer ownership, cancellation, and drain rules.  The focused totals are
7+8 memory cases, 6+10+6 RTC cases, and 11+3+7 sound cases, all passing.
Their Linux/5BSD activation, packed-ring, active-checkpoint, fault, and soak
evidence remains pending as listed in the requirements catalog.

## 2026-07-30 shared-memory overlap policy recheck

The runtime shared-memory registry formerly allowed two overlapping region
IDs to alias the same BAR bytes while assigning different writable policies.
Because lookup is by region ID, the same guest address could then be writable
or read-only depending on ID ordering.  Overlapping aliases now require both
the same backing bytes and the same writable policy.  The focused negative
case constructs a same-storage, conflicting-policy overlap and requires
`EINVAL`; the complete shared-memory capability case passes.  This is still
common infrastructure only: no device advertises a shared-memory-dependent
feature until its allocation, mapping, revocation, restore, and live guest
contract is independently qualified.

## 2026-07-30 administration/device-group foundation recheck

The administration command, queue, capability, resource, device-parts, group,
and SR-IOV lifecycle helpers were reviewed as one unadvertised composition.
The review traced command leases, member validation, reset, portable state,
and multi-owner restore.  It found and fixed one ordering defect: malformed
opcodes and members are now rejected before acquiring an external SR-IOV
lifecycle lease, preserving the specification's validation precedence and
ensuring invalid commands have no lifecycle side effects.  All 52 focused
cases pass.  There is still no concrete PCI owner/member topology, SR-IOV
capability lifecycle, or PF/VF live qualification, so the common helpers
remain foundation-only and `VIRTIO_F_ADMIN_VQ` remains unadvertised.

## 2026-07-30 Intel nested-VMX rootless qualification recheck

The production `vmm.ko` builds in a clean object tree with the kernel's
`-Werror` policy.  The independently maintained nested-VMX requirements
validator accepts 168 entries and ten mandatory live feature groups.  A clean
ATF build then ran every architectural model case independently: 143/143
passed, covering capability policy, VMX instruction results and operands,
VMCS12 storage and ownership, VM-entry validation, VMCS02 composition,
exit reflection, EPT, invalidation, interrupts, timers, TSC state, lifecycle,
rollback, and portable active-L2 state.

This is foundation evidence, not Intel execution qualification.  The feature
remains default-off behind both `hw.vmm.vmx.nested=1` and the VM-wide
`x86.nested_vmx=true` CPU-model option.  All ten live-ledger groups still
require immutable, distinct Linux-L2, 5BSD-L2, and host-trace artifacts from a
Linux/KVM L1, including active-L2 checkpoint/restore and repeated
create/destroy fault/concurrency soak.  No release claim is made from the
rootless model alone.

The sanitizer rotation then found three defects in the independent model
fixture itself.  Its mock linear-memory and virtual-APIC callbacks added a
guest address to an array pointer and subtracted the fixture base afterward.
Although the final arithmetic value named an in-bounds byte, C pointer
arithmetic had already formed an out-of-range intermediate pointer.  The
callbacks now validate the length before subtraction, calculate one numeric
offset, and add only that checked offset to the array.  The complete nested
suite subsequently passes 143/143 under both AddressSanitizer and
UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer.  This changes test trustworthiness, not the
default-off live qualification status.

## 2026-07-30 VirtIO-GPU blob/shared-memory consumer slice

The first unadvertised consumer slice for shared-memory regions is now in
place for VirtIO-GPU resource blobs.  The GPU protocol decoder understands
and independently tests the exact CREATE_BLOB, MAP_BLOB, and UNMAP_BLOB wire
layouts, including bounded entry arithmetic, memory-entry extents, reserved
fields, unsupported HOST3D memory types, and map offsets.

A normative CS01 recheck corrected the initial test assumption that a guest
blob must carry backing entries: section 5.7.6.8 explicitly permits zero
entries followed by ATTACH_BACKING.  Focused normal and
AddressSanitizer/UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer cases pass.  No blob or
shared-memory feature is advertised yet.  Resource ownership, host-visible
allocation, mapping responses, reset, portable save-state, and live Linux
qualification remain hard gates.

The common modern-PCI layer now also supports callback-backed shared-memory
regions for sparse or dynamically remapped apertures.  Existing direct-pointer
regions retain their fast path.  Callback accesses preserve exact widths and
little-endian values, execute only while the device is outside reset, quiesce,
and suspend fences, and have deterministic failed-access behavior.  Runtime
replacement is lifecycle-owned and callback/direct overlaps are rejected when
aliasing cannot be proven.  The independent transport test exercises
successful and failed reads/writes, replacement, revocation, width handling,
and fencing under both the normal compiler and ASan/UBSan.  This substrate is
deliberately not counted as a production shared-memory consumer until GPU blob
resource ownership and mapping are connected.

The production opt-in GPU composition now connects that substrate to bounded
guest-memory blobs and carries their resource, backing, mapping, scanout,
cursor, and retained-pixel state through the versioned private checkpoint
codec.  Restore validates every saved backing extent through the incoming
architecture-neutral DMA/IOMMU view before publishing any GPU state.  The
decoder also preserves later structural failures after a successful DMA
preflight; the full sanitizer rotation caught and fixed an initial stale
success result on that path.

The live matrix now has distinct split and packed checkpoint lanes for both
ordinary 2D and blob-backed scanouts.  A scheduler invariant rejects a
checkpoint case whose `packed` label disagrees with its device ring option.
The blob lanes additionally require host-side USDT evidence for the normative
`RESOURCE_CREATE_BLOB` and `SET_SCANOUT_BLOB` command numbers, rather than
accepting feature negotiation as proof of activation.  During checkpoint a
guest worker holds the framebuffer open, writes a deterministic boundary
marker, and verifies that exact marker before issuing its first resumed write.
This exercises retained scanout/backing reconstruction across both live
checkpoint and suspend/restore.  Privileged Linux execution of those four
lanes remains pending; rootless helper, parser, ledger, normal, ASan, and
UBSan gates are green.

## 2026-07-29 live-evidence and active-RTC checkpoint review

The packed-ring activation review found that guest feature negotiation alone
did not prove that a particular device actually submitted a packed
descriptor.  Every single-device Linux packed release and checkpoint lane now
starts the common `virtio:::chain` DTrace probe after boot, filters by the
independent expected device name and packed layout value, and requires at
least one successfully decoded chain.  Manifest validation rejects new packed
single-device cases that omit or misname this host-side evidence.

The GPU blob lane has a second device-specific evidence gate.  It records
`virtio:::gpu-command` and independently requires successful
`RESOURCE_CREATE_BLOB` and `SET_SCANOUT_BLOB` commands with nonzero used
lengths.  Its active checkpoint worker keeps the framebuffer descriptor open,
places a deterministic marker at the framebuffer boundary, verifies the
restored marker before changing it, and advances a durable guest-side phase
counter.

The RTC checkpoint lane previously delivered its test alarm before taking the
checkpoint.  That proved the alarm protocol but not portable pending-alarm
state.  Alarm-enabled checkpoint cases now keep `/dev/rtcN` open, arm one
bounded future wake alarm, checkpoint at phase one, and require the restored
descriptor to deliver an `AF|IRQF` event before phase two.  The process remains
alive until the runner verifies and terminates it, so an exited helper or
guest-only stale sysfs value cannot satisfy the gate.  This live evidence is
still recorded as pending until the root-required split and packed lanes run.

The balloon checkpoint review found the same stale-evidence risk in host
statistics logs.  Checkpoint balloon cases are now invalid unless
`BALLOON_STATS_INTERVAL` is nonzero.  Before each checkpoint the runner waits
for a new host-consumed statistics buffer and records its count; after restore
it requires that count to increase again.  This proves the retained
statistics-queue/timer lifecycle resumed instead of accepting a sample from
boot.

Finally, the ACCESS_PLATFORM audit confirmed that endpoint descriptors enter
through the common request translator and the GPU blob aperture takes an
explicit DMA-domain lease.  The IOMMU function itself is the only device
allowed to resolve raw guest mappings because it must read the translation
tables which create endpoint domains.  The requirements validator now rejects
any other `pci_virtio_*` endpoint that directly calls
`paddr_guest2host()` or `vm_map_gpa*()`, turning that architectural rule into
a source gate for future devices.

## 2026-07-29 virtio-mem exhaustive request-state review

The memory-device pass rechecked sections 5.15.4 through 5.15.6 against the
pinned VirtIO 1.4 CS01 text, then compared the observable request and resize
behavior with the pinned Linux driver and QEMU device model.  The existing
implementation correctly ignores request padding, ignores all UNPLUG ALL
payload data, rejects invalid or partially conflicting ranges atomically,
does not overshoot `requested_size`, preserves plugged blocks across ordinary
device reset, and only shrinks `usable_region_size` after UNPLUG ALL or system
reset.

The review found no new production defect, but it found a meaningful proof
gap: the tests covered only selected block layouts.  The host-model suite now
enumerates every bitmap in a four-block independent model, every nonempty
contiguous STATE range, and every PLUG and UNPLUG transition from a fresh
state.  It verifies the exact ACK/ERROR choice, all-or-nothing bitmap
publication, platform callback result, and `plugged_size` accounting without
using production protocol constants for its expectations.  Live Linux split
and packed activation and active-memory checkpoint remain root-required
promotion gates; stock 5BSD still lacks a virtio-mem guest driver and is
reported as a driver gap rather than simulated coverage.

## 2026-07-29 virtio-mem active-page checkpoint qualification

The follow-up test-quality pass found that the dedicated memory checkpoint
lanes preserved the device model but did not independently prove that an
application had live data on pages supplied by the VirtIO memory device.
Those lanes now run with 512 MiB of base RAM, request 128 MiB from
virtio-mem, and allocate enough anonymous memory to force use of the added
region.  A Linux guest helper reads `/proc/self/pagemap`, selects eight PFNs
inside the exact device configuration range, writes independent SHA-256
markers, and pins the pages.

Before and after both live checkpoint and suspend/restore, the worker verifies
the device geometry and sizes, every marker, and every virtual-to-physical
mapping.  The lab manifest validator rejects a dedicated virtio-mem
checkpoint case that does not explicitly enable this workload with a positive
allocation.  The test therefore cannot silently degrade into an ordinary
anonymous-memory or idle-device checkpoint.  Rootless helper, manifest, and
requirements validation pass; the Linux split and packed live lanes remain
recorded as pending until they run on the host.

## 2026-07-29 virtio-fs operational review

The virtio-fs device, retained-request queue, and authenticated backend
connection remain event driven.  Readiness comes from the event loop and
checkpoint coordination uses a bounded monotonic condition wait; no periodic
polling or fixed sleep was introduced.  A new failure-recovery test proves
that a rejected backend THAW leaves the connection quiesced and preserves the
exact opaque state so a later retry can safely complete.

The PCI path now publishes DTrace request-latency and queue-pressure probes.
Latency is measured from a monotonic timestamp captured before backend
submission through normal, stale, and cancelled completion.  Pressure reports
the bounded pending-request and outgoing-frame counts on submission and
selective reset.  The bhyve DTrace build and device harness pass with these
probes.

This does not claim live filesystem qualification.  The tree still lacks a
production sandboxed VFSB filesystem server, so the Linux
mount/read/write/metadata/xattr/rename/fsync and active-restore matrix remains
blocked on that backend.  Stock 5BSD also lacks an unmodified virtio-fs guest
driver; that is reported as a driver gap rather than replaced with a mock.

## 2026-07-29 host-audio prerequisite review

Reviewing a production OSS backend for virtio-sound found a defect in bhyve's
shared audio byte-stream helper before the new backend was connected.  The
playback and capture loops could spin forever when a host descriptor returned
zero bytes, and their `for`-loop increment made a naive EINTR retry move the
buffer cursor backwards.  Both loops now use explicit positive-progress
accounting, retry EINTR without changing the cursor, and fail a zero-progress
operation with EIO.  The API also has an explicit destroy operation that
closes its owned descriptor.

A focused injected-system-call suite covers interrupted plus short playback,
interrupted plus short capture, zero-progress writes, zero-progress reads, and
descriptor destruction.  This hardens existing HDA operation and establishes
a safe low-level prerequisite for virtio-sound.  It does not yet expose an OSS
virtio-sound backend: real playback and capture must be moved off the vCPU
notification path and given bounded reset, suspend, and checkpoint ownership
before that option can be advertised.

The pinned QEMU comparison supports that boundary: its device model retains
PCM virtqueue elements in per-stream queues and advances them from host-audio
callbacks rather than performing backend writes in the queue-kick handler.
That behavior is architectural evidence only; no reference implementation
code is copied.  bhyve's eventual worker must use its own common request
tokens, DMA leases, generation fences, and bounded lifecycle drain.

The live checkpoint gate also no longer accepts a merely surviving `aplay`
process as proof of restored PCM operation.  It records the number of
host-observed playback completions before checkpoint and requires that count
to increase after restore.  A count is used instead of the device's cumulative
byte total because a restored bhyve process reconstructs diagnostic counters
from zero.  This proves that restored guest descriptors reach the production
sound callback while still keeping transient observability counters out of
portable device state.

## 2026-07-30 nested-VMX frozen-dispatch fail-closed review

The frozen internal-dispatch boundary was rechecked against the Intel
revision-092 state model and the pinned Linux nested-VMX implementation.  The
value-only context validator already rejects an invalid cold-continuation
result before commit, but the production commit path still treated an
unexpected result, a failed consume, or an impossible cold-EPT disposition as
a host `panic()`.  Those checks now return `EPROTO` (or preserve a meaningful
non-`EINVAL` consume error) without consuming the resolved handoff.  A future
validation regression or malformed restored transaction therefore fails the
VM operation closed instead of crashing the host.

The independent continuation test now injects an out-of-range disposition,
requires both validation and dispatch to reject it, and proves the caller's
dispatch output remains unchanged.  All 143 architectural model cases pass
normally and under ASan/UBSan, the 166-entry requirements ledger validates,
and `vmm.ko` builds with `-Werror`.  This is not hardware qualification:
guest VMX exposure remains default-off until the root-owned Intel Linux/KVM L1
runner completes the ten-group Linux and 5BSD L2 evidence transaction.

## 2026-07-30 virtio-net packed multiqueue and hash-report review

The Linux packed-ring verifier had an argument-parsing defect: adding the
`packed` selector caused the requested queue-pair count to be ignored, so a
packed two- or eight-pair lane could validate only the default single pair.
Argument parsing is now centralized and independently tests the exact
`modern 2 packed` invocation used by the VM runner, packed-feature
negotiation, malformed forms, and rejection of packed legacy transport.

Hash-report qualification now has packet-level host evidence instead of
inferring metadata publication from feature negotiation plus ordinary
traffic.  A dormant `virtio:::net-rx-hash` probe fires at the exact point
where the device writes the hash value and report into the guest receive
header.  The live multiqueue ring gate requires a nonempty packet on an active
RX queue with one of the independently specified nonzero report values; it
rejects evidence from TX queues, inactive pairs, `HASH_REPORT_NONE`, and
out-of-range packet classes.  The probe adds no logging and is inactive
without a DTrace consumer.

The bhyve DTrace build completes with `-Werror`, and the guest verifier,
shell syntax, trace-parser negatives, and complete host-helper self-test pass.
Promotion still requires the rebuilt Linux live lanes; 5BSD RSS and
hash-report driver support remains a separately reported guest-driver gap.

## 2026-07-30 VirtIO-input dynamic-configuration scope review

The retained roadmap item for input “configuration changes” was checked
against VirtIO 1.4 sections 5.8.4 through 5.8.6.  The device exposes a
driver-selected capability query, but the input chapter defines no feature,
command, or backend event for dynamically replacing that capability table.
The current evdev pass-through instance is identity-bound and queries the same
host device for its lifetime.  Emitting a configuration interrupt for
`SYN_CONFIG` or another guessed evdev condition would invent a guest ABI
rather than implement the standard, so no such behavior was added.

The real remaining input gates are live reset during injection, split and
packed cross-guest activation, and the already scheduled active-frame
checkpoint cases.  The complete rootless device harness passes 538 common,
417 modern-transport, 742 input, and 88 entropy checks with zero failures.

## 2026-07-30 sound backend boundary and SCSI event review

The production-audio review found that the current virtio-sound host callback
contract is synchronous all the way from queue notification through PCM
completion.  Hiding a blocking OSS read or write in a worker and waiting for
that worker in the callback would still stall the vCPU notification path.
Consequently `backend=oss` remains deliberately unavailable.  The required
prerequisite is a bounded deferred-completion interface which owns copied
playback data or pinned capture descriptors until a worker publishes the used
entry, coordinates STOP/RELEASE/reset with in-flight work, and gives
checkpoint validation an explicit backend identity and reconstruction policy.
The existing `backend=null` continues to be a deterministic conformance
backend rather than being mislabeled as production audio.

The SCSI event item was also re-audited because the high-level backlog still
described it as missing.  The implementation already uses the versioned CTL
subscription, advertises HOTPLUG and CHANGE only after subscription succeeds,
converts add/remove/capacity records, preserves source ordering, bounds its
queue, emits loss through EVENTS_MISSED, filters multimedia parameter-change
events, and handles event-queue reset without polling.  All eight independent
event-state cases and all twenty-one composed SCSI device cases pass,
including malformed chains, invalid source records, queue saturation,
sequence gaps and reset continuity.  Remaining SCSI work is live Linux/5BSD
activation, packed operation, active-LUN races and destination CTL identity
qualification—not another event mechanism.
