The following console lifecycle pass found that resume inspected each port's
driver-to-device output queue before rearming host input.  The socket receive
path actually consumes the device-to-driver queue, so a writable buffer queued
before suspend could remain dormant until a later guest kick.  Resume now
checks `vsp_txq`, the same queue used by the socket receive callback.  The
focused test records the exact queue inspected on both checkpoint-driven and
guest-driven resume paths; all nineteen composed console cases pass.

## 2026-07-30 common lifecycle notification rollback review

The cross-device suspend/checkpoint audit found that the common queue callback
discarded a kick whenever quiesce, guest suspend, or checkpoint pause owned the
device.  A kick is only a coalescible hint, but it can race the lifecycle fence
after the driver has published descriptors.  Dropping it can strand those
descriptors indefinitely on synchronous devices and on backends whose drain
has already decided that no work remains.

The common core now latches such a kick in the queue's existing portable
`vq_notify_pending` state.  Guest resume and successful checkpoint resume
already replay that state after reopening queue ownership, while device reset
clears it with the old queue generation.  Failed checkpoint pause is a
separate rollback path: because the source VM remains running, it now replays
the latch immediately after dropping the quiesce fence.

Independent core tests cover nested quiesce, suspended status without
`DRIVER_OK`, checkpoint pause, reset erasure, and a kick injected from inside a
failing backend pause callback.  The modern lifecycle harness additionally
proves that a suspended queue kick is replayed exactly once on guest resume.
Both harnesses pass in full, and the DTrace-enabled bhyve build completes with
`-Werror`.

## 2026-07-30 shared-memory topology and administration review

The modern PCI shared-memory capability registry now has a one-way lifetime
seal.  A device constructor registers its complete topology and seals it before
returning; the GPU constructor does this whether or not its optional blob
aperture is enabled.  Any device-status write also seals the registry, including
a reset write of zero, so a later full device reset cannot make capability
topology mutable again.  Region registration additionally rejects active,
resetting, quiescing, suspended, or checkpoint-paused devices.  This prevents a
late backend action from changing the PCI capability chain after guest
discovery or from making the checkpoint compatibility manifest describe a
topology the guest never enumerated.
`virtio_modern_test:shared_memory_capability` covers explicit sealing and
post-reset immutability in addition to the existing 64-bit offset/length,
overlap, alias, callback, read-only, suspend, revoke, and restore compatibility
cases.

The administration-command, queue-bank, device-parts, resource, group, and
SR-IOV lifecycle modules remain compiled and model-tested but deliberately
unadvertised.  All sixteen direct administration ATF cases pass, including
fragmented I/O, parallel queues, reset drain, transactional snapshot/restore,
corruption, topology mismatch, and concurrency.  No production PCI function
sets `VIRTIO_F_ADMIN_VQ`; live queue-index discovery, owner/member composition,
and Linux-driver activation remain release gates rather than inferred
coverage.

The later PCI integration review completed the ring adapter, extended common
configuration, queue/controller snapshot composition, and nested suspend plus
checkpoint fencing.  It also rejected a proposed ordinary virtio-net owner:
the pinned Linux PCI transport sends its initial command-list query to the
SR-IOV group, while that proposed owner exposed only the self group.  The
feature remains unadvertised until bhyve has a concrete PF/VF topology and
lifecycle.  Resume is now a single binding transaction: it validates retained
ownership, invokes the backend while command admission stays closed, and
releases one nested owner only after callback success, eliminating a path
which could otherwise call a non-idempotent backend resume twice.

## 2026-07-30 sanitizer and queue-ownership review

The complete sanitizer-enabled device harness passes after exercising the
common core, modern transport, split and packed rings, every existing device,
and the provisional device modules.  It exposed one test-fixture defect:
`virtio_net_test` constructed a partial softc without linking `vs_vc` to the
device constants before taking the valid hash-report path.  Production tracing
uses that class name at the point where hash metadata is published.  The
fixture now performs the same class linkage as device initialization, and the
full sanitizer rerun completes with zero failed checks.

The subsequent selective-reset audit distinguishes synchronous queues from
queues with external owners.  Net fences its shared TX/control worker and
serializes RX callbacks; block cancels or generation-fences asynchronous
backend I/O; SCSI parks and drains each independent worker pool; 9P advances a
request generation and completes reset only after lib9p releases all guest
buffers; console disables the reset receive queue's readiness source; input
discards host events staged for the old event-queue incarnation; and vsock
revokes a kernel-backend packet already consumed from the reset TX queue.
Common reset detaches the queue before the callback and validates the
generation again before accepting either synchronous or deferred completion.
RNG and the remaining synchronous command devices retain no queue-local
request ownership after their notification callback returns.

## 2026-07-30 IOMMU strict-range conformance review

A fresh reading of VirtIO 1.4 section 5.13.6.5.1 found that byte alignment and
range length had been conflated.  Setting bit zero in `page_size_mask` permits
byte-aligned endpoints, but the MAP request still requires `virt_end` to be
strictly greater than `virt_start`.  The implementation and its test had
accepted a one-byte inclusive mapping, so the test was reproducing the defect
instead of independently proving the normative boundary.

Runtime MAP validation and portable-state restore now reject equal endpoints.
The replacement test proves that a one-byte range returns RANGE, a two-byte
range remains valid with byte granularity, translation cannot extend beyond
it, and a checksummed state image encoding the prohibited one-byte range is
rejected transactionally.  The requirements ledger now records the strict
range rule rather than the former implementation-derived claim.  All IOMMU
configuration, PCI-lifecycle, state, protocol, request, queue, event,
topology, and VIOT cases pass, and the independent DMA-boundary validator
continues to report no device-private translation bypass.

## 2026-07-30 administration device-status review

The device-parts codec retained the pre-suspend device-status mask and rejected
bit 4 even though VirtIO 1.4 defines it as `SUSPEND`.  A suspended member could
therefore be captured but not represented in a valid device-status part during
portable restore.  The codec now accepts the complete VirtIO 1.4 status set
while continuing to reject reserved bit 5.  The independent literal-wire test
constructs a status containing `SUSPEND` from the specification fixture rather
than a production header.

The complete rootless administration review currently covers 49 direct cases
across command negotiation, capabilities, resource objects, device-parts
composition, independent group state, SR-IOV lifecycle fencing, the
device-parts codec, and transactional handlers.  The foundation remains
unadvertised: real PCI administration-queue discovery, PF/VF owner/member
composition, and live driver activation are still required before exposure.

## 2026-07-30 suspend and GPU shared-memory qualification review

The common suspend path publishes its queue and DMA fence before invoking a
device drain, records suspension independently from checkpoint pause, and
restores device ownership before it republishes `DRIVER_OK`.  Every
snapshot-enabled VirtIO PCI device supplies portable compatibility validation;
asynchronous block and SCSI backends retain their suspended ownership across
restore, while synchronous devices use the common drained-queue contract.
Focused balloon, modern-transport, and core suites pass 81 cases.

The first real shared-memory consumer was then rechecked from PCI capability
construction through GPU blob ownership.  The topology is sealed before
driver activation; runtime aperture access requires a common DMA lease and is
serialized by the GPU state mutex; each mapped range is aligned, bounded, and
non-overlapping; and reset, suspend, and checkpoint fencing deny new access.
Restore validates every retained guest backing through the incoming DMA view
before publishing resources or display state.  The PCI, queue, GPU-state, and
modern-transport suites pass 57 focused cases, including failed lease
acquisition, exact-width little-endian access, malformed chains, mapping
overlap, transactional restore, blob scanout, and blob cursor state.

This qualifies the common shared-memory infrastructure and its opt-in GPU
consumer at the rootless model level.  It does not claim the pending
privileged Linux blob/checkpoint lanes or a production host presentation
backend; those remain GPU release gates.

## 2026-07-30 virtio-mem and virtio-RTC focused requalification

The memory-device review traced configuration mutation, every request type,
host-range ownership, system reset, failed-restore compensation, and repeated
restore.  The operation mutex serializes platform changes without holding the
state mutex across a callback; portable state is fixed-width little-endian and
validates destination geometry, population count, tail bits, and digest before
reconstructing any range.  The PCI device deliberately leaves unplugged memory
CPU-accessible because it does not advertise `UNPLUGGED_INACCESSIBLE`, and
discard uses the destination host mapping rather than persisting a pointer or
host page-size assumption in state.

The RTC review traced request validation, alarm delivery with an initially
empty alarm queue, forward and backward wall-clock steps, timer failure,
device suspend, checkpoint pause, reset, and an elapsed deadline during
restore.  One nonblocking realtime timerfd remains integrated with the bhyve
event loop; no periodic polling or unbounded wait was introduced.  A pending
alarm remains in the portable model until a complete guest buffer consumes
it, and resume rearms only after the common lifecycle fences are removed.

The five focused memory/RTC suites pass 38 cases.  Their governed Linux
split/packed, reset, alarm, active-memory, suspend, and checkpoint cases remain
privileged live gates.  The absence of a stock 5BSD virtio-mem and virtio-RTC
guest driver is recorded as a driver gap rather than inferred from PCI
enumeration.

The qualification-manifest review also found that the generic
`RESET_TEST=yes/no` coverage row proved only that both option values existed
somewhere in the release profile.  It did not require every device to take the
reset path.  A new `reset-devices` contract now enumerates all thirteen
governed device classes.  It initially exposed missing release reset lanes for
net, input, and 9P; their modern cases now enable reset, the complete
qualification coverage report passes 76 contracts, and the orchestrator
self-test passes with the stronger count.

The checkpoint manifest had the same class of blind spot: it required every
device to appear in a checkpoint case, but did not prove that each device was
restored using both split and packed virtqueues.  Fourteen new contracts now
bind the checkpoint lifecycle to both ring formats for net, IOMMU, RNG,
balloon, RTC, block, SCSI, vsock, console, input, 9P, GPU, memory, and sound.
All of those contracts are backed by dedicated cases rather than inferred from
the combined-device lane.  The qualification report now passes 90 contracts
and the orchestrator self-test passes with the strengthened manifest.

A cross-guest lifecycle audit then found that `run-5bsd-auto.sh` implemented
and several release cases exercised `FIVEBSD_DEVICE_SUSPEND`, but the lab
manifest did not declare that switch as a default, public override, governed
behavior, or coverage requirement.  It could therefore silently disappear
from the matrix without failing coverage, and operators could not select it
through the orchestrator's validated `--set` interface.  The option is now
fully governed and the release profile must contain both its disabled
baseline and an enabled modern 5BSD case.  Qualification coverage now passes
91 contracts and the complete orchestrator self-test remains clean.

The portable-state preflight review found one legacy transport mismatch:
`VM_SNAPSHOT_VALIDATE` accepted a source feature set that
`VM_SNAPSHOT_RESTORE` subsequently rejected when the destination lacked a
saved feature.  Feature compatibility is now checked during every loading
operation, so validation remains an exact non-mutating prediction of restore.
The new regression independently serializes the source capability word and
proves rejection by both phases, plus acceptance by a destination superset.
The complete sanitizer-backed rootless harness passes, including 515 common
core checks and 1,189,896 exhaustive packed-ring model checks.

The Intel-only nested VMX model was then rerun independently of the portable
VirtIO work: all 143 model groups pass, both requirement/evidence validators
accept their ledgers, and a fresh source-tree `vmm.ko` build completes under
kernel `-Werror`.  Active-L2 state has a versioned cold continuation and an
atomic destination reconstruction path; it remains default-off because the
real Intel Linux/KVM-L1, Linux/5BSD-L2, active checkpoint, interrupt, EPT/VPID,
and repeated-soak evidence rows are still pending.  This is intentionally an
Intel hardware qualification gap, not a portability dependency in the common
VirtIO implementation.

## 2026-07-30 live-evidence integrity review

The release/checkpoint manifest now refuses to count a Linux VirtIO-IOMMU
case unless `VERIFY_RING_ACTIVITY=yes` is present.  Guest enumeration,
`iommu_group` membership, and negotiation of `ACCESS_PLATFORM` do not by
themselves prove that a request traversed the translation path.  The required
host probe therefore correlates successful translations with every protected
endpoint discovered by the guest.  This applies to split, packed, ordinary,
and checkpoint IOMMU lanes; bounded soak lanes retain their interval-based
checks rather than an unbounded trace.

Checkpoint evidence was tightened similarly.  Every checkpoint case
containing userspace/kernel vsock, virtio-console, or 9P now has to exercise
the corresponding active-backend rejection and rollback check before it may
publish the portable idle checkpoint.  The packed 9P lane and both combined
device lanes previously could prove only the later idle round trip.  They now
must first leave an active connection, port, or fid in place, observe the
expected checkpoint rejection, prove the source remains usable, retire that
non-portable state, and only then save and restore.  Manifest self-tests
include negative fixtures for missing translated-DMA tracing and missing
active packed-9P proof.

The stricter release and checkpoint coverage reports and the complete
`virtio-lab` self-test pass rootlessly.  These changes strengthen the pending
live gates; they do not relabel an unexecuted lane as exercised.

## 2026-07-30 lifecycle fail-closed review

The common checkpoint entry points previously asserted that every registered
VirtIO device supplied both checkpoint pause and resume callbacks.  That made
an integration omission process-fatal: adding a device without the complete
lifecycle contract could terminate bhyve when an operator requested a
checkpoint.  The common layer now rejects either missing callback with
`EOPNOTSUPP` before entering the queue fence or changing checkpoint ownership.
The regression verifies both operations and verifies that quiescing and
checkpoint state remain untouched.

A follow-up request-path audit confirmed that the remaining SCSI LUN
assertions are reached only after the complete eight-byte LUN address has been
copied and validated, while the 9P assertions protect mutex-owned internal
request accounting rather than guest-provided values.  The new fail-closed
regression passes as part of the complete sanitizer-backed device harness
(521 common-core checks and 1,189,896 exhaustive packed-ring model checks),
and a fresh full bhyve build and link completes under `-Werror`.

The cross-guest coverage audit also found that a dedicated rebuilt-5BSD
packed-balloon case existed, but no coverage contract required its split and
packed values.  The release manifest now governs `BALLOON_PACKED` for 5BSD
modern guests explicitly.  This prevents deletion or accidental relabeling of
the split baseline or packed inflate/deflate lane while the higher balloon
features which lack a 5BSD driver remain honestly marked as driver gaps.
The same two existing lanes now explicitly govern 1 MiB and 64 MiB targets,
so cross-guest balloon evidence cannot collapse to a single trivial target
without making release coverage fail.  The manifest now passes 93 explicit
coverage contracts and the complete orchestrator self-test remains clean.

## 2026-07-30 Intel nested-VMX transaction review

The nested-VMX review separated guest-visible validation failures from
hardware-residency failures.  Invalid VMCS12 state, stale generations,
unsupported controls, malformed entry data, and ordinary resource failures
remain recoverable and are rejected or quarantined by the value-owned state
machines.  Failure to restore VMCS01 or to roll back a partially written
architectural register image is deliberately fail-stop: returning from either
condition would let a kernel thread migrate while a private VMCS02 or mixed
L1/L2 processor state remained current.  Those panic sites are therefore
invariant guards, not guest error handling.

The VMCS02 publication regression now also proves that zero state generations,
zero execution epochs, the reserved all-ones VMCS12 GPA, zero resource
generations, empty and oversized programs, and every missing hardware-adapter
operation are rejected before `begin()` can select or mutate VMCS02.  The
transaction result remains unchanged on every rejection.  Production
transaction code now uses the named Intel VMCS encodings for instruction
error, exit reason, and exit qualification instead of repeating raw numeric
values; the independent model tests intentionally retain specification
fixture values.

All 143 rootless nested-VMX model cases pass both normally and under combined
AddressSanitizer/UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer.  The 166-entry requirements
ledger and ten-group live-evidence ledger validate, and a fresh `vmm.ko`
module build completes with the kernel's `-Werror` flags.  This does not clear
the hardware gate: nested exposure remains experimental and default-off until
the pinned Intel Linux/KVM L1 runner supplies Linux and 5BSD L2 evidence for
instructions, entry failures, interrupts and timers, EPT/VPID, active-L2
checkpoint/restore, concurrency, repeated creation/destruction, and soak.

## 2026-07-30 VirtIO-SCSI event saturation review

The CTL subscription-to-eventq path now has an integration-level saturation

monotonic LUN-add records while the guest provides no event buffers, verifies
that the bounded 128-record host queue preserves every accepted event and
source sequence in order, and then requires exactly one trailing
`NO_EVENT|EVENTS_MISSED` record for the dropped suffix.  This covers the real
feature, device-status, CTL-record validation, LUN encoding, bounded enqueue,
and loss-publication path rather than testing only the container.

The focused PCI case and all eight standalone event-state cases pass.  Live
Linux and rebuilt-5BSD add/remove/change races, eventq saturation with actual
guest buffers, and repeated subscription reconstruction remain scheduled
release evidence rather than inferred from this rootless result.

## 2026-07-30 existing-device lifecycle review

The VirtIO console rootless device harness passes all 21 cases.  The review
traced host accept/read/write callbacks, selective receive-queue reset,
multiport announcement retry, suspend rearming, bounded transmit
backpressure, and snapshot validation.  A callback selected for a prior host
connection is fenced by its descriptor identity, queue reset disables the

`EBUSY` rather than serializing an fd or silently dropping the session.  Live
connected-port migration therefore remains a future external-backend

The VirtIO 9P rootless device harness passes all 22 cases.  The review traced

mutex, so a concurrent queue/config access cannot enter the new incarnation
while lib9p drains the old one.  Active requests and backend-private fids are

## 2026-07-30 VirtIO GPU production-presentation review

The 2D device can now opt into the production framebuffer presentation path
without silently replacing bhyve's existing fbuf renderer.  The process-wide
console registration has an explicit stable owner, idempotent same-owner
registration, conflicting-owner rejection, and owner-checked release.
An fbuf device configured with `source=external,vga=off` retains its VNC
storage and server while leaving renderer ownership to
`virtio-gpu,display=true`; dimensions are required to match.

The renderer uses the existing VNC refresh event rather than adding a polling
thread.  It preallocates bounded scanout and cursor staging, atomically copies
the active retained scanout and its format, converts every supported source
format to the architecture-independent B8G8R8X8 presentation bytes, atomically
copies the 64 by 64 cursor with its hotspot, and alpha-composites only the
visible clipped rectangle.  Upper/left clipping avoids unsigned coordinate
underflow and lower/right clipping avoids destination overrun.  Reset,
resource destruction, cursor disable, and restore are observed through the
retained state on the next ordinary refresh.

All 41 GPU protocol/state/queue/display/PCI cases and the new console
ownership case pass, the independent requirements, DMA, snapshot, and
reference-corpus validators pass, and bhyve rebuilds cleanly with `-Werror`.
Live Linux VNC presentation, cursor movement, packed-ring display, reset, and
active checkpoint remain required release evidence.
## 2026-07-30 VirtIO sound lifecycle and queue review

- Corrected the output PCM lifecycle to complete prebuffered data after
  PREPARE and before START, as required by VirtIO 1.4 section 5.14.6.6.1.
  Capture remains gated on RUNNING.
- Negative descriptor-parser results now latch NEEDS_RESET on control and PCM
  queues.  Fatal PCM geometry errors stop at the first bad chain, preventing
  later backend operations after the queue has entered poisoned state.
- Replaced the former deferred-until-START test assumption with independent
  host and PCI tests that prove actual PREPARE-state output completion.
- The synchronous null backend remains the only advertised backend.  The
  existing OSS helper performs blocking I/O and therefore is not suitable for
  direct use from the VirtIO notification path; a production backend requires
  bounded worker queues, cancellation, and explicit suspend/restore policy.

## 2026-07-30 RTC and common scatter/gather review

- RTC request and alarm queues now distinguish an empty queue from a negative
  descriptor-parser result.  A parser failure latches DEVICE_NEEDS_RESET,
  terminates that notification callback, and suppresses later timer scheduling
  after the fatal request path.
- Alarm parser failure preserves the pending notification for reset instead of
  consuming or rearming it.  Existing event-driven CLOCK_REALTIME timerfd,
  discontinuous-clock, suspend, checkpoint, and restore behavior remains
  unchanged.
- Common iovec aggregation no longer relies on an assertion when a mathematical
  length exceeds `size_t`.  It saturates at `SIZE_MAX`, while length validation
  treats overflow as exceeding every representable request.  Exact, short, and
  overflow boundaries are covered independently.
- Focused RTC, sound, and iovec tests pass and bhyve rebuilds with `WARNS=6`.
  Live RTC alarm activation and a real narrower-host build remain release
  evidence rather than claims inferred from this Intel amd64 host.

The OASIS CS01 HTML URL is served through Cloudflare email protection, which
rewrites obfuscated email tokens on every request.  Its byte length and
normative text remain the same, but repeated downloads have different
SHA-256 values, so it is not a reproducible immutable artifact.  The corpus
now pins the official CS01 PDF instead.  Two independent downloads produced
the same 1,788,087-byte file and SHA-256
`497b7b989b5161444e87866c264a46be90911b8f4738eadf4dd4f52eb37c8727`.
The HTML remains useful for document navigation, but no release gate treats
its randomized representation as an authenticated source file.

## 2026-07-30 production OSS sound qualification integration

The completed nonblocking OSS backend exposed a test-oracle defect: the Linux
guest helper treated zero-filled capture as a device-wide VirtIO requirement.
That is true only of the deterministic null backend.  The helper now requires
the exact 192000-byte capture extent for both backends, retains the all-zero
content assertion only for `null`, and independently proves that nonzero OSS
capture is accepted while nonzero null capture is rejected.

`virtio-lab` now has an explicit hardware-dependent `audio` profile with
serialized split and packed OSS cases.  It remains outside the portable
release profile so a machine without audio hardware cannot manufacture a
skip or weaken release coverage.  The runner passes the selected backend into
ordinary and checkpoint guest checks, and host log evidence must identify the
same backend.  The guest-helper self-test, payload-copy self-test, shell
syntax check, release/checkpoint coverage audits, audio plan, and complete lab
self-test pass.  Live OSS playback/capture still requires root qualification
with representative `/dev/dsp` endpoints; OSS provider-loss, underrun,
overrun, and active-checkpoint fault lanes remain follow-on work.

## 2026-07-30 rebuilt-5BSD GPU and FUSE session review

The 5BSD VirtIO GPU driver no longer submits device commands before
`DRIVER_OK`, spins forever in `virtqueue_poll()`, or assumes that each
stack-backed protocol object occupies one physical scatter/gather segment.
Its synchronous control path is interrupt driven with a finite timeout,
serializes requests, validates response type and fence correlation, and resets
and drains an incomplete queue before any stack address can escape.  Display
geometry and rectangles are overflow checked, only an enabled scanout zero is
accepted by the single-scanout VT implementation, and detach fences VT
producers before freeing the framebuffer or request lock.  The driver is now a
standalone `virtio_gpu.ko` module.

The release manifest contains independent split and packed rebuilt-5BSD GPU
lanes.  They require the modern GPU PCI ID, driver attachment, a complete
GET_DISPLAY_INFO/create/attach/set-scanout/transfer/flush command sequence,
and, for the packed lane, negotiated RingPacked state and a packed control
queue.  These remain pending activation evidence until executed with a guest
image containing the rebuilt module.

The full ASan/UBSan device matrix exposed two unrelated virtio-fs defects
during this work.  A FUSE READ fixture failed to initialize its reserved
padding, making a negative reserved-field assertion depend on stack contents;
the fixture now initializes the entire wire request.  More importantly, a
higher-major FUSE INIT correctly established byte order but the session
dispatcher later treated every INIT as byte-order-agnostic.  An
opposite-endian retry could therefore switch the connection before final
negotiation.  Subsequent INIT requests now decode in the already established
order; the existing test proves opposite-endian rejection, same-endian
completion, and rejection of a third INIT.

The GPU module builds with `-Werror`, its independent wire/geometry contract
test passes, the requirements and activation ledgers validate, `virtio-lab`
self-tests pass with the new coverage axes and cases, and the complete
sanitizer matrix passes, including more than 1.2 million packed-ring state
checks.  Live rebuilt-5BSD GPU activation and live Linux virtio-fs
qualification remain privileged gates rather than inferred successes.

## 2026-07-30 rebuilt-5BSD RTC review

A loadable rebuilt-5BSD `virtio_rtc.ko` driver now exposes the baseline
VirtIO 1.4 clock as a read-only system time-of-day source.  The driver
deliberately does not negotiate `VIRTIO_RTC_F_ALARM`: alarm advertisement is
blocked until a guest alarm consumer and notification-queue lifecycle exist.
It waits for DRIVER_OK before issuing requests, validates CFG and CLOCK_CAP
before registration, and then proves the data path with an initial READ.
Requests are serialized and interrupt driven with a finite timeout; an
incomplete stack-backed descriptor is reset and drained before its caller can
return.

The conformance pass compared the driver with CS01 section 5.23, the pinned
Linux driver, and the pinned QEMU device.  It found and fixed two response
validation gaps: the used-ring length is now checked as a common-header-sized
error or an exact full-sized success, and CLOCK_CAP must return a zero flags
field when the alarm feature was not negotiated.  The latter prevents the
guest from concealing a host violation of the alarm capability contract.
Reserved fields, supported UTC-family type, smearing variant, status mapping,
and representable time range are also checked.

The release manifest has distinct split and packed rebuilt-5BSD RTC lanes.
They require modern PCI discovery, `vtrtc0` registration, host-correlated CFG,
CLOCK_CAP, and READ notifications, and packed negotiation plus host ring
layout for the packed case.  The module builds with `-Werror`; its independent
document-derived wire contract, the 176-entry requirements ledger, the
102-claim activation ledger, shell syntax, `virtio-lab` planning/self-tests,
and `git diff --check` pass.  Live execution remains pending an updated guest
image and is not inferred from rootless validation.

## 2026-07-30 rebuilt-5BSD input review

A loadable rebuilt-5BSD `virtio_input.ko` driver now provides the modern
VirtIO input frontend through FreeBSD evdev.  Configuration discovery validates
every returned size and independently decodes byte-stream capability bitmaps,
device identifiers, and absolute-axis metadata.  Event and status buffers are
bounded and preallocated, are not published until `DRIVER_OK`, and are
completed by interrupts rather than polling.  The initial event fill tolerates
descriptor pressure caused by physical page segmentation but refuses an empty
queue.

The lifecycle/error pass made malformed completions fail closed: an invalid
event used length, unsupported event tuple, status completion with a nonzero
used length, or replenishment failure stops further queue publication with one
bounded diagnostic.  Detach prevents new status production, unregisters evdev,
resets the device, and drains both queues.  Comparison with the pinned Linux
driver also found its multitouch `MSC_TIMESTAMP` feedback-loop exception; the
5BSD frontend now applies the same behavioral guard without importing
reference code.

An independent CS01 fixture checks the selectors and every wire structure
size and offset.  A static in-guest verifier locates the named evdev provider,
requires the exact key/SYN/relative/absolute/release sequence, and writes a Caps
Lock LED event back through the status queue. Distinct release cases correlate
that reverse transition at the host provider. The split case proves the
single-device baseline; the packed case attaches two independently named host
providers and guest PCI functions, verifies both event streams and both
reverse status paths, and requires negotiation and event/status queue evidence
for both devices. The helper's
self-test also covers matching, mismatch, terminal-entry, and bounds behavior.
The module and helper build with `-Werror`, their focused self-tests and
contract pass, and the requirements/activation ledgers and lab manifest
validate.  Live promotion still requires a rebuilt guest containing the new
module.

## 2026-07-30 rebuilt-5BSD 9P transport review

The rebuilt-FreeBSD VirtIO-9P transport previously exposed a request buffer to
the device and then returned it to its caller after a timed wait, even though
the descriptor could still be owned by the device. A late completion could
therefore write through freed or reused storage. Timeout and fatal queue paths
now stop and drain the device before waking request owners. Partial attach and
detach paths track initialized resources explicitly; the channel is not
globally visible until `DRIVER_OK`, mount-tag claims are atomic, and duplicate
tags are rejected.

The completion path now retains the used-ring length. The client accepts only
an exact, capacity-bounded 9P response and never trusts a declared length
beyond the returned bytes. The portability pass also found that every
multi-byte protocol scalar was copied in native host order. Production reads
and writes now use shared explicit little-endian helpers, exact range checks
that cannot underflow, allocation-failure handling, exact protocol-version
matching, and bounded mount-option validation. Version negotiation and
partial client construction release their strings, transport claim, pools,
and mutex on every failure path.

Independent rootless tests exercise fixed little-endian byte fixtures,
overflow-safe buffer windows, and all short, oversized, negative, and
mismatched response-length boundaries through the production helper. Both
`p9fs.ko` and `virtio_p9fs.ko` build with `-Werror`. The release manifest now
schedules split and packed rebuilt-FreeBSD cases that mount a private export,
prove guest-to-host and host-to-guest visibility across separate mount
lifetimes, and require guest negotiation plus host ring evidence for packed
mode. Those live cases remain a rebuilt-image promotion gate rather than
inferred evidence.

The final ownership pass added an explicit reference contract to the guest
9P transport registry. A client now holds a locked registry reference from
transport selection through close, and module unload returns `EBUSY` while a
client remains. This closes the mount-versus-unload raw-pointer race instead
of relying on incidental driver detach ordering. The same pass tightened
zero-length read/write semantics, rejects oversized server counts and
directory entries, and reran the complete sanitizer-backed device matrix.
That matrix also exposed and fixed a scheduler-dependent virtiofsd
cancellation test: its synthetic queued job is now installed only after its
workers are joined, so it deterministically tests queued cancellation rather
than occasionally executing the FUSE INIT it intended to cancel.

The rebuilt-5BSD console live lane now has meaningful port-count coverage.
The split case uses one named port; the packed common-lifecycle case creates
two ports on one device and exchanges independent tokens in both directions
through each exact `/dev/vtcon/<name>` alias. The release coverage contract
therefore requires both one and two ports as well as both ring formats.

## 2026-07-30 GPU translated-DMA and SCSI event-completion review

The GPU shared-memory pass found that all retained backing was validated as
bidirectional during restore, even though an ordinary unmapped 2D resource is
only read by the device.  This over-rejected a valid read-only IOMMU mapping.
Conversely, `RESOURCE_MAP_BLOB` published a host-visible aperture without
first proving that every backing extent permitted both device reads and
writes.  The retained-state callback now carries an explicit device-read,
device-write, or bidirectional access contract.  Ordinary restore preflight
uses device-read permission; mapped blobs validate every extent
bidirectionally before publication.  A missing write permission rejects the
map atomically, and imported mapped-blob state cannot become visible through
the destination IOMMU view until both directions are valid.  Dedicated
release and checkpoint GPU-plus-IOMMU cases are now scheduled.

The subsequent rebuilt-FreeBSD SCSI event review found that the interrupt
handler discarded the used-ring length and parsed the zeroed event buffer even
when a device returned fewer than the document-defined 16 bytes.  It also
used diagnostic assertions when event-buffer publication failed during
normal completion or reset reconstruction.  The guest now accepts only a
completion covering the complete base event and no more than the negotiated
buffer.  A malformed completion forces a whole-bus rescan because it may have
replaced a real inventory notification, then returns the zeroed buffer.
Publication failure takes the bounded bus-reset path, and reinitialization
returns an error rather than panicking.

The adjacent console pass found the same trust-boundary defect in the rebuilt
FreeBSD guest: the control task parsed a full port header after any short
completion and accepted an oversized used length as port-name bytes beyond
the published buffer.  It also asserted that returning a dequeued buffer
could never fail.  The driver now validates the complete eight-byte base
header and upper buffer bound before parsing, discards malformed messages,
and returns a zeroed buffer.  Requeue failure frees that one dequeued object,
latches the device failed, stops interrupts, and never reenables the task
path; it no longer panics an INVARIANTS kernel.

The GPU focused tests, the independent SCSI and console used-length boundary
tests, both guest modules with `-Werror`, the requirements and activation
ledgers, the lab self-test, and the complete sanitizer-backed device harness
pass.
Live GPU ACCESS_PLATFORM and rebuilt-FreeBSD malformed-device injection remain
qualification gates; these rootless results do not promote either pending
claim.

The same completion audit found assertion-only request publication in the
rebuilt-FreeBSD entropy driver.  A queue setup or replenishment failure could
therefore panic an INVARIANTS guest even though it is a recoverable transport
failure.  Request publication now returns its real error.  Attach unwinds
before registering the entropy source if the initial buffer cannot be
published; a later replenishment failure makes the source inactive and
returns no bytes, leaving detach to reset and drain the queue before freeing
its DMA storage.  The module builds with `-Werror`; live queue-reset and
source-failure injection remain scheduled qualification work.

That entropy review then found a separate copy bound: a device-supplied used
length was limited by the random subsystem caller's requested size, but not
by the smaller DMA buffer posted to the device.  An oversized completion and
large caller request could therefore read beyond the entropy buffer.  The
softc now retains the exact posted capacity and rejects any larger used
length before copying, deactivating the source until detach resets and drains
the queue.  Independent zero, exact, one-past, and maximum-width boundaries
exercise the production predicate.

The rebuilt-FreeBSD vsock queues had a related boundary mismatch: receive
completions larger than the posted buffer were clipped and then parsed, while
event completions larger than the fixed event were accepted as transport
resets.  Both paths now validate the device-supplied used length against the
exact descriptor shape.  Oversized receive entries are recycled without
entering the socket protocol, and a reset event is accepted only at the
document-defined four-byte length.  Independent short, exact, and oversized
boundary cases use specification literals rather than driver structure
sizes.

The rebuilt-FreeBSD balloon worker also had an assertion-only enqueue and an
unbounded completion sleep.  A device which retained an inflate or deflate
descriptor could therefore prevent driver detach forever, and a queue
publication error could panic an INVARIANTS guest.  Requests now return real
errors and wait at most five seconds; detach cancellation wakes the same
wait.  Any ambiguous completion latches a failed state and performs a full
device reset before returning pages to the VM, which is the ownership edge
that releases every host-side discarded range.  Failed devices neither
republish statistics nor submit deflate work through a stopped queue.
The worker also suppresses its normal `actual` configuration write after that
reset, because feature negotiation and the driver state no longer permit
post-reset configuration access.
Independent classification tests cover successful, wrong-cookie, timeout,
cancellation, and otherwise incomplete requests.  The balloon module builds
with `-Werror`; live withheld-completion and reset injection remains pending.

## 2026-07-30 VirtIO-balloon free-page-hint completion pass

The next balloon pass implemented the previously unadvertised
`VIRTIO_BALLOON_F_FREE_PAGE_HINT` option and then compared it with VirtIO 1.4
CS01 section 5.5.6.5, pinned Linux `virtio_balloon.c`, and pinned QEMU
`virtio-balloon.c`.  That comparison rejected the first parser shape before
live exposure: Linux submits the command and writable page ranges as separate
virtqueue buffers, not one combined chain.  The production parser now accepts
Linux's separate sequence and QEMU's compatible combined form.  It assembles
a possibly fragmented four-byte little-endian command, activates only the
current non-reserved ID, ignores stale IDs and writable buffers received
before activation, and consumes active writable ranges through the common
reverse-RAM and discard operations.

The command lifecycle is explicit.  Command ID 2 starts the first requested
round.  A host mapping or discard failure publishes STOP and generates a
configuration interrupt.  The driver's STOP acknowledgement publishes DONE;
no writable range is modified after DONE.  Malformed command shape fails the
queue closed.  Reset begins a new device lifecycle but no command ID is reused
within a lifecycle.  BAL1 version 6 stores both the architectural command ID
and requested/active phase; impossible, truncated, obsolete, future, and
feature-incompatible records fail transactionally rather than inheriting
destination-local state.

Independent tests cover separate and combined descriptor semantics,
fragmented commands, pre-start and stale pages, successful discard,
device-initiated STOP, guest STOP acknowledgement, DONE, malformed chains,
unnegotiated access, reset, and repeated restore.  A new Linux split case and
the combined packed optional-feature case require feature-bit, configuration,
guest-driver, and host queue evidence.  Stock 5BSD has no free-page-hint
driver support, so that cross-guest claim remains explicitly classified as a
driver gap.

The complete ASan/UBSan device harness, requirements and activation ledgers,
DTrace-wrapper validation, guest-helper self-test, lab self-test, shell
syntax check, and diff whitespace check pass.  Live activation remains
pending installation of the matching bhyve and test suite.

A subsequent command-association review found that a combined hint chain
carrying a stale command could inherit an already active round and discard
its writable ranges under the older command.  The queue handler now marks
page association per chain: Linux-style page-only buffers inherit an active
command, while a combined buffer is accepted only when its own command
matches the current non-reserved ID.  A negative test keeps round 2 active,
submits command 3 with writable pages, and proves that no reverse mapping or
discard occurs.  This directly enforces the section 5.5.6.5.2 requirement to
ignore pages supplied with a mismatched command ID.

## 2026-07-30 5BSD balloon low-memory review pass

The guest driver previously described DEFLATE_ON_OOM but omitted it from the
negotiated feature mask and had no pressure callback.  The implementation now
registers `vm_lowmem` only after successful feature negotiation and
deregisters it before worker teardown.  The callback filters for
`VM_LOW_PAGES`, takes the existing device mutex, coalesces a pending action,
wakes the worker, and never waits for a virtqueue descriptor.  The worker
returns no more than the established 256-PFN request limit and waits one
low-memory interval before normal target-driven reinflation.

The concurrency review removed an unsynchronized callback read of
`current_npages`; only the worker now reads and mutates the page count, while
the mutex-protected flag crosses callback and worker contexts.  Attach failure,
detach, device failure, zero-page state, repeated pressure events, and
reinflation have bounded paths.  A pure contract helper tests zero, exact
limit, one-past-limit, maximum 32-bit count, and zero-limit behavior, and the
module builds with the kernel's normal `-Werror` flags.

The 5BSD live lane uses the supported `debug.vm_lowmem` event rather than
trying to make an unbounded allocation fail.  It requires guest feature
negotiation, a visible drop and recovery in the balloon's current page count,
and a correlated successful host deflate trace.  This qualifies the
event-driven stability path after installation; sustained real-pressure soak
remains pending.

## 2026-07-30 architecture-neutral guest-memory layout pass

A portability review of the common memory setup found unchecked additions in
the NUMA-domain sum, amd64 low/high-memory-hole conversion, two guard regions,
and per-domain GPA progression.  It also found a more subtle ordering defect:
when bhyveload had already created the one permitted kernel memory segment,
libvmmapi replaced the requested domain size only after reserving host address
space from the stale size.

The new pure `vmmapi_memory_layout_calculate()` boundary resolves all layout
arithmetic before mapping, uses an explicit host-span limit, and is independent
of x86 constants.  `vm_setup_memory_domains()` now discovers the authoritative
existing segment first, rejects preexisting multi-domain layouts, calculates
the complete bounded reservation, and only then allocates or maps segments.
Rootless ATF coverage proves below-hole and split-hole layouts plus empty,
zero-sized, invalid-platform, aggregate, GPA, guard, and synthetic 32-bit-host
overflow rejection.  Both focused cases pass with the tree's `-Werror` flags.

The follow-up checkpoint foundation adds an allocation-bounded validator for
guest-visible NUMA identity.  One through eight domains must each own nonzero
memory and at least one vCPU, domain sizes must exactly partition aggregate
RAM, and the vCPU lists must exactly and uniquely partition every identifier.
Focused tests reject missing, duplicate, and out-of-range CPUs, empty domains,
invalid domain counts, size mismatch, and overflow.  Host NUMA allocation
policy is intentionally not classified as portable guest state.  Metadata
encoding and restore-preflight wiring are the next part of this slice.

An isolated full libvmmapi link remains blocked by the already-known installed
kernel-header mismatch (`VM_CAP_NESTED_VMX` and the new device-memory segment
IDs are absent from `/usr/include`).  The new production source itself compiles
cleanly; the matching buildworld/object-world gate remains required.

## 2026-07-30 vsock checkpoint ownership and test-quality pass

A maintainability pass over the aggregate harness warnings found that the
userspace relay's guest-port argument exists solely for the DTrace
`relay-bufsize` probe and therefore appeared unused only when DTrace was
compiled out.  The uninstrumented configuration now documents and consumes
that argument explicitly without changing the instrumented call path.

The same pass made the checkpoint ownership contract executable.  Vsock pause
returns with the device mutex held so the serializer sees an immutable
backend, while resume releases that ownership; runtime assertions now verify
entry ownership, snapshot ownership, retry acquisition after a failed kernel
provider thaw, and the unlocked checkpoint-resume callback path.  Lock-analysis
suppression is limited to the two generic callback boundaries that transfer
ownership across function calls.  The ordinary resume-complete path was split
into explicit locked and unlocked branches and is analyzed normally.

Two snapshot tests had bypassed pause and called the serializer directly.
They now exercise the production pause, validate/restore, and resume sequence
for both userspace and kernel backends.  Linker-wrap declarations were also
made explicit, so the focused translation unit builds with no compiler
warnings.  All 95 vsock-device cases pass, including kernel-provider freeze,
failed-thaw retry, suspend fencing, portable backend identity, truncated state,
transactional restore, and the new ownership assertions.

The comparison pass checked selective queue reset against VirtIO 1.4 CS01
sections 2.6.1 and 4.1.4.3, pinned Linux
`virtio_pci_modern.c`/`virtio_ring.c`, and pinned QEMU
`virtio-pci.c`/`virtio.c`.  bhyve keeps `queue_reset` asserted while an
asynchronous backend drain owns the old incarnation, reports both
`queue_reset=0` and `queue_enable=0` only after completion, clears addresses,
interrupt selection, split cursors, packed cursors and wrap counters, restores
the default queue size, and fences stale completions with a generation.  No
observable conformance difference requiring a code change was found in this
slice.  The complete VirtIO requirement validator remains green at 662
independent oracle definitions, 190 requirements, and 113 live claims.
## 2026-07-30 VirtIO suspend configuration-freeze pass

The rotating Device Suspend review compared the common status state machine
and every asynchronous configuration-change producer with VirtIO 1.4 CS01
section 3.4.  Queue admission, status transitions, failure recovery, ignored
writes, generation latching, and deferred notifications were already
conformant.  The review found one device-level gap: a host
`virtio_mem_host_set_requested_size()` call changed `requested_size` and
`usable_region_size` immediately while only deferring the configuration
interrupt, so a suspended driver could observe fields that the specification
requires the device to leave unchanged.

`pci_virtio_mem.c` now captures the complete little-endian guest-visible
configuration before acknowledging SUSPEND, serves that frozen image until
resume, and then exposes the retained host update together with the common
deferred notification.  The frozen image is part of version 2 of the
device-private snapshot record; every obsolete development record is rejected.
Restore
also reinstates suspend ownership before guest access resumes.

`virtio_mem_test:suspend_freezes_guest_visible_configuration` independently
changes the host requested size during suspension and proves that reads remain
old until resume.
`virtio_mem_test:snapshot_preserves_suspended_configuration` then validates
the literal version-2 envelope, validate/restore behavior, the distinct frozen
and retained values, truncation rejection without mutation, and publication
on resume.  The complete ASan/UBSan device harness passes, including the
updated VirtIO requirements ledger, and all of bhyve builds with `WARNS=6`
and `-Werror` against the staged source-tree headers.

## 2026-07-30 nested-VMX semantic-comparison hardening

The portability pass removed bytewise comparison from the architectural
VMCS02 identity contract.  `vmx_nested_vmcs02_id_equal()` compares the three
defined 64-bit identity fields, all production identity checks use it, and the
requirements validator rejects a future return to `memcmp()` for this value.
The model suite includes a fieldwise-identity case independent of structure
layout.

The same review found a caller-visible padding defect in optional asynchronous
VM-entry event validation.  A semantically absent event was compared against a
zeroed native structure even though the structure contains enum, boolean, and
tail padding.  Validation now checks only defined fields.  Its regression test
poisons the tail padding and proves that an absent event remains valid.  The
follow-up sweep removed the same native-layout dependency from L2 control and
architectural images, PDPTE state, exit information, VM-entry results,
continuation handoffs, late-entry records, and refreeze requests.  A dedicated
test constructs semantically equal values with different poisoned padding and
also proves that real field changes remain distinguishable.

The save-state maintainability pass consolidated five independent pointer
range-overlap predicates into one overflow-safe common helper.  Every nested
state, registry, cold-L2, continuation, and outer-checkpoint encoder uses it;
address-space wrap is conservatively rejected and directly tested.  The outer
checkpoint decoder now rejects records above the absolute maximum possible
wire size before hashing or reading the payload, preventing an invalid
multi-gigabyte digest walk while preserving the destination view.

Pinned Linux nested-VMX behavior was also compared for late VM-entry failure
handling.  Invalid guest state remains reflectable to L1, while MSR-load and
machine-check failures remain owned by L0 because bhyve applies L1's entry
MSRs in software.  Failed entry neither marks VMCS12 launched nor fabricates
unowned exit state.  No actionable difference was found.

The nested requirements validator remains green with 168 requirements and 10
live qualification groups.  The rootless nested model passes all 146 cases
both normally and under ASan/UBSan, and the production `vmm.ko` builds with
`WARNS=6` and `-Werror`.

The subsequent host-word-size pass found that state and outer-checkpoint
alias validation multiplied caller-provided 32-bit field counts before
checking the architectural maximum.  The multiplication cannot wrap on the
current amd64 host, but it could wrap `size_t` on a future 32-bit host and
weaken the no-alias transaction boundary.  State semantics now validate the
counts before any host-sized range calculation, and the checkpoint overlap
predicate fails closed on an out-of-range count.  An independent hostile-count
case proves that neither state sizing nor outer-checkpoint sizing reads the
claimed array or changes its output.  The common range helper also uses a
typed all-bits-one pointer bound so the same header compiles in both the
userspace model and the FreeBSD kernel environment.

After these changes the 168-entry requirements validator, all 146 normal and
ASan/UBSan model cases, diff whitespace gate, and the production `vmm.ko`
`WARNS=6`/`-Werror` build remain clean.

The same arithmetic audit found that VMCS-registry restore calculated its
maximum incoming record from the destination registry limit before
revalidating that in-memory invariant.  Restore now rejects a zero,
over-limit, or count-inconsistent destination before the multiplication.
The registry wire test corrupts the destination limit to `UINT32_MAX`, proves
that restore fails before parsing or allocation, and then restores the
invariant for the remaining transactional cases.

The pinned Linux `KVM_GET_NESTED_STATE`/`KVM_SET_NESTED_STATE` comparison
confirmed the need to represent guest mode and run-pending state separately
and to synchronize authoritative L2 state before export.  WASPNest keeps that
observable distinction but intentionally does not copy Linux's native VMCS12
payload.  Its fieldwise wire records are bounded and endian-defined, and its
restore remains staged until all VM-wide and per-vCPU validation succeeds;
this is stricter than Linux's ioctl path, which may enter VMX operation before
a later nested-state validation failure.  QEMU's pinned VMState comparison
likewise supports explicit versions, bounded subsections, and post-load
validation, without making its GPL structure layout part of bhyve's format.

The requirements validator now also compiles the state, outer checkpoint, and
VMCS-registry wire layers with `-m32`, `-Werror`, and no link step.  This makes
the host-word-size promise executable even on the amd64 development machine.
The model runner rejects the common misspelling `SANITIZE`; the current tree
was rebuilt in a private object directory with the correct
`SANITIZERS=address,undefined`, and all 146 cases passed with sanitizer
instrumentation actually present.

The VM-wide publication follow-up traced the staged registry and every active
vCPU workspace through validation, acquisition, registry exchange,
non-fallible per-vCPU publication, and stage destruction.  The exchange is an
intentional swap: the destination receives the staged registry and the
disposable stage receives the old live registry, which its destructor then
reclaims.  No fallible operation follows that exchange.  One fail-closed gap
was found at the exchange primitive itself: two objects carrying only the
`initialized` marker could still have an invalid limit, count, or virtual
capability shape.  Replacement now validates both complete registry shapes
before touching a list head.  A regression corrupts the replacement count,
requires rejection before any MSR workspace begins, and proves the old
registry remains readable and unchanged.

The pairwise workspace-alias audit also removed an implicit equal-capacity
assumption from range comparisons.  Valid current virtual capabilities do
produce equal capacities, but each side's own byte extent is now used so a
future capability policy cannot weaken overlap rejection accidentally.  The
146-case ASan/UBSan model, 168-entry requirements validator, 32-bit syntax
gate, and production `vmm.ko` build with the tree's mandatory `-Werror` all
pass after this change.

Pinned Linux KVM retains distinct `GUEST_MODE`, `RUN_PENDING`, `MTF_PENDING`,
and absolute preemption-timer flags in its userspace nested-state ABI, then
reconstructs non-root mode during `KVM_SET_NESTED_STATE`.  WASPNest's current
production checkpoint boundary is intentionally narrower: it freezes only a
post-entry active-L2 continuation, stores the preemption timer as a portable
relative timer image, and rejects imported RUN_PENDING, MTF_PENDING, linked
shadow-VMCS, and historical absolute-deadline states until each has an
explicit reconstruction stage.  The wire validator retains those distinct
bits so they cannot be conflated silently, but their presence is not a claim
of production restore support.  Live qualification must include an
entry-boundary checkpoint and an MTF-producing entry before either flag can
be promoted.
# 2026-07-31 nested live-evidence freshness review

The rootless nested architectural suite passes all 146 ATF cases and the
independent traceability validator accepts all 168 requirements plus the ten
mandatory Intel hardware/live groups.  Review of the later root-only runner
found that its 30-artifact transaction was structurally strict but was not
cryptographically or semantically tied to the current invocation.  The host
wrapper now creates and exports a fresh 128-bit textual run identifier; every
Linux-L2, 5BSD-L2, and host-trace artifact must copy it and record ordered UTC
start/finish bounds.  Mixed or stale bundles are rejected before their hashes
are sealed and atomically published.  The host-tools self-test includes a
negative stale-artifact case.  This strengthens orchestration only; none of
the ten live groups is promoted until the Intel L1/L2 run actually completes.

# 2026-07-31 5BSD VirtIO-SCSI response-boundary review

The guest control path contained a dormant polling mode whose only completion
condition was a device response; every production caller already supplied an
interrupt callback.  The unreachable mode and its unbounded busy loop were
removed, and the requirements validator now rejects reintroduction of those
symbols.  Control requests therefore use one interrupt-driven lifecycle.

The command completion path also trusted two device-provided lengths.  Sense
data is now limited by both the 96-byte VirtIO response field and the CAM
destination, while a residual larger than the submitted transfer is rejected
as a malformed response and reported conservatively as a full residual.  An
independent contract exercises zero, exact, one-past, short-destination, and
`UINT32_MAX` boundaries.  The `virtio_scsi.ko` `-Werror` build, focused ATF
case, and the 191-entry requirements validator pass.  The rootless aggregate
`make check` compiled the harness but could not complete its install phase
because it attempted to apply `root:wheel` ownership in the staging tree; that
is recorded as an environment failure rather than a test result.

# 2026-07-31 administration-queue and used-length review

The administration-queue foundation remains intentionally unadvertised.  Its
PCI boundary now has a pre-narrowing validator for the VirtIO 1.4 common
configuration fields: an administration range must be non-empty, start after
the ordinary device queues, fit the 16-bit index/count fields, and remain
within the 65536-queue namespace.  Independent tests cover the exact upper
boundary, overlap with ordinary queues, zero count, one-past field values, and
range overflow.  This does not yet claim a PCI owner/member implementation;
the feature bit and common-configuration fields remain unavailable to guests.

The packed-ring oracle review found that one positive test reported all
descriptor bytes as used even though the VirtIO used length is only the bytes
written into device-writable buffers.  The oracle now expects the independent
literal writable length.  More importantly, the common split/packed parser
records each request's total writable capacity, including indirect chains,
and both single and grouped completion reject a device callback that attempts
to publish a larger used length.  The failure sets NEEDS_RESET and retires the
request without exposing an invalid used entry.

The production bhyve build, focused split/packed and administration tests, the
193-entry independent requirements validator, and the complete ASan/UBSan
device harness pass after these changes.  The aggregate harness emitted only
the expected diagnostics from negative-path cases and exited successfully.

# 2026-07-31 modern VirtIO-MMIO transport review

The architecture-portability pass found that the 5BSD modern MMIO transport
was filtering `VIRTIO_F_SUSPEND` even when a child driver requested it.  It
also retained packed-ring support in the available feature mask without ever
requesting `VIRTIO_F_RING_PACKED`, and validated every queue size using the
split-ring power-of-two rule.  Those three policies made modern MMIO behavior
diverge from both the common guest contract and VirtIO 1.4.

Modern MMIO now requests only transport features offered by the device and
requested by the child, including packed rings, notification data, and device
suspend.  Legacy MMIO continues to reject modern-only suspend and queue-reset
features.  A shared pre-narrowing queue-size predicate accepts every nonzero
size through 32768 for packed rings and retains the power-of-two rule for split
rings in both initial allocation and reinitialization.

Device suspend and resume now perform the document-defined status handshake
around the child lifecycle callbacks.  The wait uses a bounded one-second
deadline with one-millisecond pauses, rejects `NEEDS_RESET` and `FAILED`, and
therefore cannot turn system suspend into an unbounded polling loop.  Focused
independent tests cover modern and legacy feature policy, child opt-in,
offered-feature filtering, split/packed size boundaries, and status
predicates.  The changed MMIO kernel object compiled with `-Werror` in the
amd64 `FIRECRACKER` configuration.  Live modern-MMIO suspend remains a named
5BSD activation gate; the pinned Linux guest does not implement this VirtIO
1.4 feature.

# 2026-07-31 administration exposure boundary review

All six administration foundation suites were rebuilt and their 88 cases ran
cleanly: command and fragmented-queue handling, group dispatch, capabilities,
resource objects, device-parts composition, and SR-IOV lifecycle fencing.  A
line-by-line PCI-boundary review confirmed that this is deliberately common
infrastructure rather than a guest-visible owner device.  No emulated PCI
function currently supplies a real owner/member topology, separate
administration queue range, queue-kick routing, or portable PCI composition
state.  Consequently `VIRTIO_F_ADMIN_VQ`, `admin_queue_index`, and
`admin_queue_num` remain unavailable instead of advertising an unexercisable
interface.  The next implementation slice must add those four pieces as one
transaction; merely exposing the feature bit or common-configuration fields
would violate the queue-range and owner-device requirements.

The secure-erase feature remains intentionally unavailable for the same
reason: ordinary file discard or zero filling is not a secure-erasure
guarantee on sparse, copy-on-write, cached, or remapped storage.  It will only
be exposed behind a backend operation that reports an actual secure-erase
capability and provides the required maximum sectors, segments, and alignment.

# 2026-07-31 console emergency-write live qualification

The console model already accepted the complete 32-bit `emerg_wr` field before
feature negotiation and queue setup, but its release matrix had no real guest
trigger.  The Linux helper now maps bhyve's advertised modern PCI device BAR
through sysfs and writes the independent VirtIO 1.4 console offset while an
ordinary port connection is open.  The host must observe the low byte after a
separately acknowledged queue token, so the case cannot pass from PCI discovery
or queued console traffic alone.  The helper self-test verifies the exact
little-endian bytes against a synthetic BAR.

A `virtio:::console-emergency-write` probe records the value and whether an
attached backend received it.  This keeps successful early output and
best-effort writes without a listener operationally distinguishable without
enabling debug logs.  The focused console ATF case, helper self-test, shell
syntax check, complete requirements validator, DTrace provider generation, and
full bhyve `WARNS=6`/`-Werror` build pass.  Split and packed Linux console cases
are scheduled as the root-required live promotion gate; stock 5BSD currently
has no deliberate emergency-register trigger.

# 2026-07-31 balloon optional-feature conformance pass

The balloon feature/configuration/queue topology was rechecked against
VirtIO 1.4 CS01 section 5.5 and the pinned Linux and QEMU implementations.
Optional queue indices remain fixed, intervening unsupported queues report a
zero size, and PAGE_POISON is correctly independent of PAGE_REPORTING while
changing the latter's permitted host modification policy.  MUST_TELL_HOST,
DEFLATE_ON_OOM, statistics, free-page hinting, reporting, poison configuration,
full reset, selective reset, and portable bitmap reconstruction retain their

No new actionable host-model defect was found in this pass.  In particular,
the one-round free-page-hint policy is permitted by the standard; starting a
later command ID is optional and is not represented as an unimplemented
mandatory feature.  The remaining balloon gates are real Linux/rebuilt-5BSD
activation, pressure/failure injection, packed operation, and active restore,
as recorded in the activation ledger rather than inferred from rootless unit

The cross-guest follow-up closed one of those driver gaps without conflating
it with free-page reporting.  The rebuilt 5BSD balloon driver now negotiates
PAGE_POISON when offered, publishes the portable zero poison value before
DRIVER_OK, and uses the architecture-neutral `pmap_zero_page()` operation on
each acknowledged deflated page before VM reuse.  A saturating read-only
counter makes the live lane prove initialization actually occurred after a
low-memory deflation; negotiated-feature and host pre-DRIVER_OK configuration
traces remain separate required evidence.  The shared public header also now
contains the CS01 huge-page allocation and failure statistic tags 8 and 9,
rather than incorrectly ending the standardized statistic namespace at 7.
The module builds with `-Werror`, and the independent guest contract suite
passes; rebuilt-image live qualification remains pending.

The GPU 2D protocol, queue, state, PCI, display, cursor, blob, shared-memory,

overlay, so it could pass without proving cursor composition.  The oracle now
uses a distinct opaque red cursor and verifies the production render callback

ACCESS_PLATFORM rather than being inferred from the model tests.

descriptor through authenticated backend completion, cancellation, reset,

defense-in-depth authority gap was fixed: the export object now independently
rejects write, read-write, append, and truncate opens with `EROFS`.  It no

negative test covers every rejected access mode, and all eighteen focused
virtio-fs/backend/daemon test programs pass.  Live Linux mount/reset and

# 2026-07-31 virtio-mem and RTC state review

Virtio-mem was reviewed across geometry validation, request serialization,
plugged-block accounting, host-range callbacks, reset, suspension, and
transactional restore.  The separate operation mutex correctly spans each
state transition while platform callbacks run outside the state mutex; failed
restore compensation retains an explicit recovery bitmap, and ordinary
VirtIO reset preserves plugged blocks as section 5.15 requires.  Both focused
memory suites pass.  No new host-model defect was found; Linux activation,
packed operation, active-memory restore, and a future 5BSD driver remain the

RTC review covered request status precedence, reserved bytes, optional alarm
negotiation, timerfd discontinuity handling, the post-sentinel clock-step
race, common suspend/checkpoint ownership, and portable restore.  Its
event-driven timer is disarmed while either lifecycle fence is held and is

notification and active checkpoint, plus rebuilt-5BSD activation, remain the

# 2026-07-31 virtio-sound ownership and save-state review

The sound control, PCM queue, asynchronous owner, OSS readiness, reset,
selective-reset, teardown, and save-state paths were reviewed as one ownership
graph.  A retained PCM request has one stream-local generation, one private
host buffer, and one completion owner.  Progress, cancellation, and callback
completion cannot replace that owner until its callback returns.  The PCI
boundary additionally checks the queue generation before publishing, so reset
discards stale work instead of completing it into a reused ring.  Readiness
events are disabled before cancellation and synchronously deleted before an
OSS descriptor or the enclosing softc can be destroyed.  This pass found and
fixed a narrower replacement race: the event callback used to issue a second
disable after dropping the device mutex.  A guest notification could install
a new retained request and re-enable the source in that interval, then the old
callback could strand it with the late disable.  Terminal completion and
stale-readiness retirement now each disable exactly once while retained
ownership is serialized; the focused test drives both deliveries.

The current checkpoint policy is deliberately bounded: active PCM ownership
causes quiesce/state encoding to fail with `EBUSY`; host audio buffers,
descriptors, callback tokens, and guest addresses are never serialized.
Quiescent stream lifecycle and backend identity use fixed-width,
little-endian state, with transactional reconstruction and explicit
incomplete-rollback recovery.  All focused sound suites pass after the
readiness repair.  Real Linux ALSA activation with the null and OSS
backends, packed-ring operation, teardown while OSS readiness is active, and
live checkpoint of an open but quiescent stream remain required evidence.
5BSD has no stock virtio-sound driver, so it remains an explicit driver gap
rather than a claimed pass.

The complete device harness passes under ASan and UBSan after the GPU and
virtio-fs fixes.  This includes the generated split/packed state space, more
than 1.19 million ring-model checks, malformed descriptor and completion
paths, every provisional device model, the 194-entry requirements ledger, the
113-claim activation ledger, all 56 DTrace wrappers, the private-DMA boundary,
portable modern snapshot structure, and the immutable reference catalog.
Production bhyve and virtiofsd both rebuild with `-Werror`.

A follow-up of the SCSI-event live gate found an obsolete comment rather than
a missing implementation.  The 5BSD driver already negotiates HOTPLUG and
CHANGE, keeps bounded dynamically sized event buffers queued, validates used
lengths, converts device-endian event fields, performs loss-aware rescans, and
repopulates the queue after reset.  The old QEMU-era TODO suggesting that CAM
discovery callbacks should subscribe to events was removed.  Eventq ownership
is driven by negotiated VirtIO features; coupling it to AC_FOUND_DEVICE or
AC_LOST_DEVICE would create a discovery loop and could empty the queue during
removal.  `virtio_scsi.ko` rebuilds cleanly after the clarification.

The Intel nested-VMX architectural model also passes all 146 cases with ASan
and UBSan.  Its 168-entry requirements ledger and ten-group live evidence

default-off until the root-owned Linux/KVM L1 runner produces a fresh,

# 2026-07-31 VirtIO-RNG operational failure visibility

The entropy-source failure path already retained an uncompleted descriptor,
latched `DEVICE_NEEDS_RESET`, and avoided deterministic fallback bytes.  It
did not, however, emit the common VirtIO error probe, leaving production
operators dependent on stderr for source EOF/read failure and malformed-chain
diagnosis.  RNG now emits `virtio:::transport-error` for an unavailable or
failed entropy source and for each malformed descriptor category.  A genuinely
malformed chain is retired with zero used bytes where a head is available,
latches `DEVICE_NEEDS_RESET`, and stops that notification pass, bounding both
work and logging.  A zero return from `vq_getchain()` is an ordinary empty/race
outcome and is no longer mislabeled or logged as malformed.  Entropy contents
and host source state remain excluded from checkpoint data.

The nine focused RNG cases and interrupt-composition case pass after rebuilding
from the production source.  The complete DTrace-enabled bhyve binary builds
with `WARNS=6`, all 57 probe wrappers validate, the independent requirements
and activation ledgers validate, the private-DMA boundary remains clean, and
`git diff --check` reports no whitespace errors.  Live source-failure injection
and long reset/rebind/checkpoint qualification remain explicitly unresolved;
rootless model evidence does not promote those activation claims.

# 2026-07-31 VirtIO-IOMMU descriptor failure review

The production request and event callbacks now distinguish an ordinary empty
queue race from a descriptor parser failure.  A zero result quietly ends the
bounded drain.  A negative result emits the common transport-error probe,
latches `DEVICE_NEEDS_RESET`, and stops processing, preventing a malformed
ring from being silently retried as though it were empty.  Focused tests cover
both request and event queues through the shared callback path; all six PCI
IOMMU lifecycle and parser cases pass.

The fresh aggregate harness passes under ASan and UBSan, including more than
1.19 million packed-ring model checks, all 195 requirements-ledger entries,
all 114 activation claims, and all 57 DTrace wrappers.  The nested-VMX model
also passes all 146 cases.  Nine Intel hardware adapters are intentionally
outside the userspace model and therefore remain build- and live-evidence
gates; this result does not promote the ten pending Linux/KVM L1 live groups.
Live IOMMU fault injection, translated-DMA operation, and active checkpoint
remain required before the device can be described as live-qualified.

# 2026-07-31 Intel nested-VMX adapter rollback and identity review

The kernel-only VMCS02 resource adapter now treats an EPT binding failure as
part of the same reverse-order acquisition transaction as APIC, posted
interrupt, bitmap, and MSR-area resources.  Failure clears every materialized
I/O and MSR bitmap, including the combined hardware MSR bitmap, before
returning the unpublished resource set.  This prevents a later attempt from
observing policy bytes produced for a failed generation.

The outer VMX runtime no longer compares VMCS02 ownership identifiers or
captured exit information through native object representations.  Entry,
exit, continuation, cold-resume, resource rollback, and assertion paths now
use their field-wise architectural equality helpers, avoiding compiler-padding
and future-layout dependencies.  The independent source validator now scans
the outer `vmx.c` runtime for both classes of regression as well as the
architecture-neutral nested components.

`vmm.ko` rebuilds with `-Werror`, the nested requirements validator accepts
all 168 entries and ten live-evidence groups, and the production-source model
passes all 146 cases.  The nine privileged Intel adapters remain outside that
rootless model.  VMX guest exposure therefore remains default-off pending the
root-owned Linux/KVM L1 matrix, Linux and 5BSD L2 execution, hardware fault
injection, active-L2 checkpoint/restore, and repeated lifecycle soak.

The subsequent privileged-adapter pass tightened two more hardware
boundaries.  Deferred EPT12 loads, access/dirty compare-exchanges, and EPT02
population now revalidate frozen-vCPU ownership in release kernels, reject
end-address overflow, and reject a corrupted callback table.  The VMCS01
environment wrapper now stages both outputs until its final `VMCLEAR`
succeeds, so a failed current-VMCS cleanup cannot return error alongside
caller-visible state from an incomplete transaction.  `vmm.ko`, the
168-entry validator, the 146-case model, and the whitespace gate all pass
after these changes; privileged execution evidence is still outstanding.

The same pass found that nested capabilities could expose the processor's
full physical-address width even though the current EPT02 root is bounded by
bhyve's LA48 guest address space.  Capability construction now derives the
exposed width from both limits and rejects invalid hardware widths or
unrepresentable address spaces without changing its output.  Independent
cases cover narrower and wider hardware and both invalid boundaries; the
Werror module build and the 146-case model remain clean.

A VMCS-currentness audit then found two failure edges which were unreachable
under a valid software launch state but unsafe if a hardware operation failed.
Failure to select a freshly initialized VMCS02 now clears it and reloads
VMCS01 instead of returning with VMCS02 current.  Applying a deferred L1 TSC
offset/control pair during detach now captures and restores the old coherent
pair on a partial write, clears the detached adapter transaction on every
recoverable path, and treats rollback failure as fatal rather than allowing a
mixed VMCS01 to resume.  The privileged adapter still requires the live Intel
matrix; the Werror module, 168-entry validator, and 146-case model pass.

# 2026-07-31 PCI administration composition staging

Administration support now has a pointer-free PCI queue namespace which keeps
ordinary `num_queues` indices distinct from the optional administration
range.  Lookup explicitly classifies ordinary queues, gaps, administration
