queues, and every out-of-range selector, preserving the caller's local index
on failure.  A bounded controller composes that namespace with a concrete
immutable self-group owner and the preallocated concurrent queue bank; its
teardown drains queue execution before destroying group ownership.  The new
tests exercise transactional invalid topology, the exact 16-bit boundary,
gapped indices, and a real LIST_QUERY through the second administration
queue.

The controller now owns a versioned little-endian `APC1` state envelope which
binds the ordinary queue count, administration range, and queue-bank payload
under one checksum.  Restore distinguishes malformed bytes from a valid image
whose immutable PCI topology is incompatible.  Snapshot and restore reject
overlap with the controller, queue-bank allocation, every queue scratch area,
and the nested group/owner graph before touching caller or live state.  The
outer overlap check covers the complete envelope, closing the header-only
alias which a payload-only nested check would miss.  Transport-facing process,
whole-device reset, and queue-local drain entry points resolve the global PCI
selector internally, so a future PCI binding cannot accidentally index an
ordinary device queue as an administration queue.  Queue-local drain follows
the processing lock order and waits only for the selected stream; its
concurrency case runs beside a blocked command and a whole-bank reset.

The transport-chain entry point now also requires parser-confirmed lengths,
ordered readable-before-writable descriptors, exact readable/writable counts,
and an independently matching writable-byte total before it can mutate output
or enter the command bank.  This gives the eventual ring callback one strict
boundary rather than duplicating partial descriptor checks in each command.

This is still an unadvertised staging layer.  No guest-visible bit or field is
enabled until modern PCI also owns ring storage, selector/notify routing,
MSI/MSI-X vectors, reset and suspend behavior, and portable queue plus command
state as one composition.  All 24 focused administration cases, the
196-entry independent requirements ledger, and a complete bhyve Werror build
pass at this boundary.

The first modern-PCI binding increment now stages administration queue storage
separately from ordinary device queues.  `num_queues` therefore remains the
ordinary count, gap indices remain invalid, and selectors or notifications
cannot resolve the administration range until `ADMIN_VQ` has actually been
negotiated.  Initialization revalidates the complete 16-bit namespace, queue
identity, queue size, and backing-array consistency rather than trusting the
staging caller.  An accidental feature-mask-only change also fails closed:
administration queue enable is rejected before DMA mapping and before an
ordinary device callback can run.  Reset nevertheless clears every staged
queue so abandoned pre-advertisement state cannot survive a device lifecycle.
The two new focused cases bring the independent ledger to 197 entries.  Ring
execution, controller drain wiring, interrupts, suspend, and composed portable
state remain the advertisement gate.

The next PCI composition pass connected the strict controller to the real
split/packed ring callback.  A malformed descriptor parser result is now
distinct from an empty queue: it latches `DEVICE_NEEDS_RESET` and stops the
notification pass without completing an untrustworthy head.  A controller
rejection of a successfully parsed head instead completes that known head with
zero bytes before latching reset.  Both outcomes, exact successful used length,
queue-local drain, reset, and destruction are exercised through a dedicated
production-source adapter test; that test is also part of the sanitizer
harness.

Modern PCI now contains the 1.4 `admin_queue_index` and `admin_queue_num`
common-configuration fields, but exposes them only when a device-model opt-in,
validated staged storage, and a live adapter binding are all present.  The
capability otherwise remains short and `ADMIN_VQ` remains absent.  When the
gate is complete, the fields occupy independent-oracle offsets 60 and 62 while
`num_queues` remains the ordinary device queue count.  No production owner
device opts in yet: composed portable controller state, suspend and interrupt
qualification, and Linux live activation remain mandatory before release.

The queue-state pass then removed an ordinary-queue-only checkpoint
assumption.  Modern queue serialization is now a reusable bank operation; an
image with negotiated `ADMIN_VQ` appends the administration bank after the
historically stable ordinary bank.  Transport state version 4 binds the
administration range, rejects pre-v4 images claiming the feature, and rejects
a destination with a different immutable namespace.  Restore backup,
packed-cache cleanup, rollback, and commit now iterate all allocated queue
storage, so a failure in a later device section cannot leave administration
cursors partially restored.  A gapped queue-number test proves cursor and
destination-generation behavior.

The administration PCI lifecycle now has its own admission barrier rather
than relying on a sequence of queue-local drains.  A notify callback holds the
shared side while parsing and dispatching a batch; guest suspend and
checkpoint pause close admission on the exclusive side, wait for all active
batches, and retain a counted owner until their matching resume.  This closes
the pre-fence notifier race, preserves its pending kick for replay, and keeps
nested guest-suspend/checkpoint ownership independent.  Focused tests cover
nested closure, rollback of a failed drain, suppression of the ordinary device
callback, and the guest-suspend failure policy.

The controller command bank is now the final common snapshot section whenever
`ADMIN_VQ` was negotiated.  Its exact bounded size is encoded independently,
the binding refuses save or restore without lifecycle ownership, validation
restores a saved controller image and then rolls the destination back, and a
successful restore publishes controller state only after the ordinary device
section has succeeded.  A focused stream test proves save, non-mutating
validation, restore, and incompatible-length rejection.  A production owner,
interrupt-mode qualification, and Linux live activation remain the
advertisement gates.

## 2026-07-31 administration topology sealing

The PCI administration controller now accepts initialization-time dynamic
group registration, including the real SR-IOV lifecycle callbacks, and seals
the complete group plus command topology before a binding publishes queues.
Direct controller execution also seals on its first command.  Sealing is
one-way down through every retained owner pointer, so a subsystem cannot add a
command behind the fabric's immutability contract.  An atomic acquired fast
path preserves cross-queue concurrency after the initial writer transition;
the first implementation attempt was rejected by the parallel-queue test
because taking the writer lock on every idempotent seal could wait behind a
long-running command.

The independent controller case sends the same initial SR-IOV-group
`LIST_QUERY` shape used by the pinned Linux PCI transport through a real
SR-IOV lifecycle object, then proves late group and command registration fail
with `EBUSY`.  The complete administration, PCI adapter, group, and SR-IOV
focused suites pass, as does the bhyve `-Werror` build.  No production device
advertises `VIRTIO_F_ADMIN_VQ`: concrete PF/VF capability and reset ownership,
live Linux discovery, interrupts, suspend, restore, and active-member tests
remain release gates.

## 2026-07-31 virtio-mem destination-geometry review

The next virtio-mem pass compared PLUG/NACK behavior, usable-region changes,
ordinary reset, and migration geometry with VirtIO 1.4 CS01, the pinned Linux
driver, and QEMU's device model.  PLUG overshoot, invalid range, and bitmap
state behavior remain aligned.  Restore deliberately requires the exact
source `addr`, `block_size`, and `region_size`: these are immutable
guest-visible configuration, so merely accepting a larger destination backing
would expose a different ABI after restore.  A smaller destination cannot
represent the source ownership bitmap.  The validation path now documents
that contract, and an independent negative test proves both geometry changes
fail before any host range is reconstructed.  The two focused suites pass
19/19.  A future larger-backing migration policy must first add a separate
restored visible-geometry layer and a compatibility manifest; it cannot be an
unchecked relaxation of this gate.

## 2026-07-31 VirtIO-IOMMU final-IOVA conformance review

The range-boundary pass found a mismatch between the advertised production
`input_range.end` and MAP validation.  The device advertises `UINT64_MAX`, but
runtime and restore paths rejected an inclusive mapping ending at that value.
VirtIO 1.4 defines page alignment through `(virt_end + 1)`; at the final IOVA
page the 64-bit expression wraps to aligned zero, while the mapping length and
physical end remain independently bounded.  Removing the artificial upper-end
rejection makes runtime MAP, translation, snapshot/restore, and UNMAP agree.
An independent test maps the final page to ordinary low guest RAM, translates
both its tail and its complete 4 KiB extent, restores it, and unmaps it.  The
focused IOMMU state suite passes 17/17.  Linux split/packed execution and
translated-DMA trace correlation remain external promotion gates.

A follow-up overflow pass separated that legal final page from the otherwise
aligned inclusive span `0..UINT64_MAX`.  The latter represents 2^64 bytes and
therefore cannot be expressed by the bounded host mapping contract.  Runtime
MAP and portable restore now reject a computed zero length before invoking a
backend validator, while retaining the final 4 KiB page behavior.  The same
independent case covers both sides of this boundary.

## 2026-07-31 5BSD GPU configuration-endian review

The non-x86 portability pass found that the new 5BSD VirtIO-GPU driver read
`num_scanouts` through the common device-configuration API and then applied a
second guest-to-host conversion.  The transport API already returns a
host-endian scalar.  The extra operation is invisible on this little-endian
Intel system but byte-swaps the count on a big-endian guest and prevents the
framebuffer from attaching.  The driver now consumes the decoded value
directly.  The independent requirements validator inspects the production
function and rejects either a reintroduced conversion or failure to use the
transport-decoded field.  Live split/packed 5BSD GPU qualification remains a
rebuilt-guest gate; this source and module check does not claim big-endian live
interoperability.

The post-fix aggregate rootless gate is clean: the sanitizer-backed device
harness, all source-policy validators, 57 DTrace wrappers, snapshot
portability and DMA-boundary checks pass; the 5BSD GPU module and complete
bhyve binary build with `-Werror`; the 27-case guest contract suite and the
virtio-lab manifest self-test also pass.  The activation ledger intentionally
continues to report 71 unresolved Linux and 106 unresolved 5BSD claims.  Those
are explicit privileged live-evidence gates, not silently promoted model
results.

# 2026-07-31 administration exposure and nested evidence review

The pinned Linux PCI transport comparison showed that negotiating an
administration virtqueue is not passive: Linux creates the queue and issues an
initial SR-IOV group query.  Exposing the completed common administration
machinery from an ordinary virtio-net instance with only a self group would
therefore accept feature negotiation and fail the first real Linux command.
The provisional net opt-in was removed.  The queue/controller/group/state
infrastructure remains tested but no production device advertises
`VIRTIO_F_ADMIN_VQ` until a real PF/VF topology owns VF enablement, identity,
FLR, suspend, restore, and member commands.  The requirements and activation
ledgers now describe that gate explicitly.  The bhyve Werror build, 47-case
net suite, 210-entry VirtIO requirements validator, and virtio-lab manifest
self-test pass after the correction.

The nested-VMX live evidence contract was then checked against its own
distinct-artifact rule.  It rejected duplicate token names and symlinks but
did not reject hard-linked regular files.  Every evidence file must now have a
link count of one, preventing a producer from presenting one mutable inode as
multiple Linux-L2, 5BSD-L2, or host-trace artifacts.  A new rootless self-test
first validates a complete 30-file bundle, then replaces one required file
with a hard link and requires the alias-specific rejection.  The self-test is
part of the normal nested model runner; all 146 architectural cases and the
new validator case pass with ASan and UBSan.  This strengthens evidence
integrity but does not change the default-off live qualification status.

A follow-up transaction review now seals the manifest and all 30 artifacts
read-only before validation and requires each to be caller-owned, non-symlink,
and single-linked.  The live runner performs the seal before invoking the
validator, hashes the sealed artifacts on both sides of validation, and only
then atomically publishes the result directory.  Negative self-tests reject a
writable artifact, a writable manifest, a symlink manifest, and a hard-linked
artifact, while the complete valid bundle still passes.

## 2026-07-31 VirtIO-net event-thread fairness review

The operational-progress pass found that transmit and control work used
bounded batches, while receive processing drained a continuously readable
backend without a limit while holding both the VirtIO device mutex and RX
mutex on bhyve's shared event thread.  Sustained ingress, especially a stream
of malformed backend records, could therefore postpone device reset, timer,
console, and unrelated backend callbacks indefinitely.  Receive processing
now acquires at most 64 new backend records per invocation.  The budget is
charged only when a new host record is acquired, so a record already staged
for missing guest buffers is never stranded; level-triggered backend
readiness schedules the remaining records.

Malformed-backend diagnostics now retain a per-device lifetime count and log
only its power-of-two occurrences.  This preserves evidence of a persistent
backend fault without turning the event thread into an unbounded log producer.
An independent continuous-readability test uses no guest descriptors, proves
the callback returns after exactly one batch, and verifies the retained count.
All 48 network cases and the complete bhyve `-Werror` build pass, and the
210-entry requirements ledger maps the new negative case to the receive
contract.  Live sustained-traffic latency and reset-soak evidence remains a
root-owned promotion gate.

## 2026-07-31 VirtIO-input restored-configuration review

The portable-state pass found that input restore bounded `config.size` and
required the five reserved configuration bytes to be zero, but accepted
arbitrary bytes in the remainder of the 128-byte selector payload.  Those
bytes are guest-readable, and every production selector response is built
from a fully zeroed configuration.  A rewritten checkpoint could therefore
publish a configuration image that no live device operation can create.

Restore now validates the entire cached response: the advertised payload is
bounded, reserved bytes are zero, and every byte after the advertised payload
is zero before any state is published.  The snapshot atomicity test corrupts
the first tail byte and proves both validation and restore fail without
changing the destination selector or staged event frame.  All 24 input cases,
the 210-entry requirements ledger, and its 664 independent oracle definitions
pass after the change.  Live split/packed input checkpoint execution remains
the privileged promotion gate.

## 2026-07-31 cross-device notification fairness review

The lifecycle and operational-progress pass found that most synchronous
device callbacks still drained `vq_has_descs()` until the guest stopped
publishing work.  Because these callbacks execute on a guest-vCPU or bhyve
event thread, a concurrently replenished ring could indefinitely postpone
unrelated devices, reset, suspend, and checkpoint.  Every synchronous queue
callback now consumes at most the queue's negotiated size per invocation.
Block, SCSI, console, 9P, input, entropy, vsock, balloon, GPU, virtio-fs,
IOMMU, memory, RTC, sound, and net therefore share the same finite progress
contract.  Completion publication reports the actual remaining availability
instead of falsely claiming an only partially drained ring is empty.

The input evdev readiness callback separately caps each dispatch at one
64-entry guest-ring capacity of host events.  Level-triggered readiness
schedules any remainder, so the change is
event-driven and does not add polling or a periodic timer.  Balloon, entropy,
and RTC composition tests independently hold three descriptors behind a
two-entry modeled queue and require exactly two completions plus one retained
head.  Existing fixtures now initialize real negotiated queue sizes rather
than relying on an impossible active zero-sized queue.  The bhyve production
build passes with `-Werror`; the focused old- and new-device suites pass, and
the 211-entry requirements ledger validates.  Sustained Linux/5BSD
multi-device latency and fairness soak remains a privileged live gate.

A follow-up host-source and completion audit found two more paths outside the
guest-kick callbacks.  CTL LUN notifications and kernel-backed vsock packets
could each consume a continuously replenished provider stream while holding
their device mutex.  CTL now consumes at most its 128-record subscription
capacity per readiness dispatch; kernel vsock consumes at most one negotiated
RX-ring capacity.  Both descriptors are level triggered, so unread suffixes
remain scheduled without timers or sleep loops.  Regression cases prove the
suffix is retained and consumed by the next dispatch.

Input reset draining is now finite as well.  If one 64-event generation-
isolation batch cannot reach `EAGAIN`, the device records a discard fence and
continues draining from subsequent readiness callbacks before admitting any
event to the replacement queue.  A continuously active physical source can
therefore delay new input, but cannot hang reset or leak an event from the old
queue generation.  Finally, single-message RX/event completions for input,
console, SCSI, and vsock report `NOTIFY_ON_EMPTY` from the actual remaining
ring snapshot rather than a constant.  Independent input, SCSI, and vsock
tests retain an extra descriptor and require the non-empty completion state.

The final nested-loop pass found that net RX charged new backend records but
did not charge malformed guest descriptor chains while assembling one staged
record.  A driver that replenished invalid chains could therefore bypass the
outer 64-record limit.  RX assembly now examines at most one negotiated ring
capacity.  Exhausting that capacity without enough writable space is an
invalid driver state: consumed chains are completed with zero bytes, backend
readiness is disabled, and `NEEDS_RESET` is raised instead of retrying the
same staged record forever.  The negative test models a continuously
replenished malformed ring and proves finite return plus the reset signal.

The same nested-loop review then found a smaller console variant.  The socket
RX callback intentionally performs only one host read per readiness event,
but malformed guest receive chains took a `continue` path before that break.
A forged, continuously advanced avail index could consequently keep the
shared mevent thread consuming invalid chains.  Console RX now applies the
negotiated queue capacity as an explicit descriptor budget.  Its negative
test presents twice that many malformed heads, proves exactly one capacity is
completed, verifies the suffix remains pending, and confirms the unread host
byte is preserved.  The focused case and the production console object pass
with `-Werror`.

After these fairness changes, the complete ASan/UBSan device aggregate passes
with zero failures.  That run includes all independent protocol-oracle gates,
the 1,189,896-state packed-ring model, transport and snapshot portability,
all current and provisional devices, net's malformed-chain regression, and
733 SCSI checks.  This remains rootless evidence; live Linux/5BSD latency,
reset, checkpoint, and soak cases are still required for promotion.

## 2026-07-31 VirtIO-sound retained-request progress review

The readiness/lifecycle pass found that a host `EAGAIN` retained one PCM
request correctly, but its later readiness completion did not resume guest
descriptors which were already available behind that request.  Since their
kick had already been consumed, a multi-buffer stream could stop after its
first backend stall.  The readiness owner now remembers the queue before the
completion clears retained state and, while still holding the device mutex,
resumes the available suffix.  Immediate completions stay inside the existing
queue-sized drain loop, so the repair adds neither recursion nor polling.

Completion also reports `NOTIFY_ON_EMPTY` from the actual post-completion ring
snapshot.  The readiness regression now publishes two PCM requests in one
kick, stalls the first, completes it from a host event, and requires both
requests to finish in order with no second guest kick.  Every sound case and
the production object pass with `-Werror`.  Live OSS multibuffer backpressure,
underrun/overrun, reset, and checkpoint qualification remains pending.

The follow-on input-frame pass found a related bound above descriptor
processing.  Physical evdev frames may span multiple readiness callbacks, so
the 64-event callback budget alone did not stop a frame from growing beyond
the 64-entry guest ring before `SYN_REPORT`.  Such a frame cannot be published
atomically.  Input now stops retaining the frame at the negotiated queue
capacity, ignores its untrustworthy suffix, and emits the standard
`SYN_DROPPED`/`SYN_REPORT` resynchronization pair at the terminator.  The new
test uses a four-entry ring and a five-event frame, proving only the two loss
records reach the guest.  Focused overflow tests and the production input
object pass with `-Werror`.

## 2026-07-31 nested-VMX qualification path freshness review

The Intel nested-VMX implementation, exposure policy, connected VMCS02 run
loop, active-L2 state, and requirement ledger were reconciled before the next
hardware qualification cycle.  The ledger contains 168 requirements: 163 are
foundation-tested and five remain explicitly gated on live Intel execution.
VPID/INVVPID remains deliberately unadvertised even though its
destination-local owner and deferred final-CPU invalidation machinery exist;
promotion still requires the pinned Linux/KVM L1 matrix.

The review found that a source-tree model invocation and the aggregate host
gate preferred an older installed nested test binary and installed scripts.
That could report success for stale cases while newer production sources and
ledger checks were never executed.  The model runner now builds the source
ATF binary whenever its source is present, and the aggregate gate resolves
nested scripts relative to its own source or installed tree.  Installed files
remain a fallback only when no source test is available.

Updating that path exposed a stale host-tools evidence fixture: it submitted a
writable manifest and writable artifacts after the evidence contract had been
strengthened to require a sealed transaction.  The valid fixture is now
read-only, and each negative mutation explicitly opens and reseals only its
target before validation.  The host-tools suite passes including all evidence
alias, omission, stale-run, timestamp, and content failures.

Fresh validation passes all 146 nested architectural cases normally and under
ASan/UBSan, the 168-entry requirements and ten-group live ledgers, the complete
host helper suite, `git diff --check`, and a clean source-paired `vmm.ko` build
with kernel `-Werror`.  These results close a qualification-infrastructure
defect; they do not replace the pending root-owned Intel Linux-L2, 5BSD-L2,
active checkpoint, invalidation, migration, and concurrency evidence.

## 2026-07-31 nested interrupt, timer, and invalidation review

The interrupt/APIC, preemption-timer, EPT/VPID invalidation, and exit-routing
lens compared the production path with Intel SDM revision 092 and the pinned
Linux nested-VMX implementation.  Entry events remain value snapshots until a
successful hardware entry or synthetic reflected exit proves the architectural
commit point.  Raw host interrupts remain L0-owned, L1 interrupt/NMI exits are
synthesized from virtual pending state, timer state is armed only on the final
CPU, and EPT02/VPID02 invalidations do not target VMCS01 ownership.

The review found one production observability defect: a valid L1 VMX
preemption-timer expiration was routed for reflection correctly but first fell
through `vmx_exit_process()`'s unknown-exit case.  It now has an explicit
trap-like L0 bookkeeping case, so it neither increments the unknown-exit
counter nor emits a misleading unknown-exit probe before the nested reflection
transaction.  The VPID capability comment was also corrected to describe the
implemented but deliberately unadvertised final-CPU ownership path.

The INVEPT descriptor difference was reviewed rather than silently normalized
to Linux.  Intel's descriptor figure marks bits 127:64 reserved and requires
zero; Linux reads but ignores that half.  The current fail-closed validation
and independent negative test therefore remain tied to the normative SDM until
the Intel live instruction gate records hardware behavior.  No GPL source was
copied.

After these changes, a fresh private-object `vmm.ko` build passed with kernel
`-Werror`; all 146 nested model cases, the evidence-bundle validator, all 168
requirements entries, all ten live-feature groups, and `git diff --check`
passed.  Real interrupt/timer/EPT/VPID execution and concurrent invalidation
remain root-only promotion gates and nested VMX remains default-off.

## 2026-07-31 active-L2 restore resource-atomicity review

The VM-wide active-L2 restore transaction was traced from architecture-record
decode through per-vCPU cold-state reconstruction, VMCS-registry replacement,
MSR-workspace activation, and final publication.  Registry and architectural
state publication were already all-or-nothing, but one host-derived resource
crossed that boundary too early: per-vCPU decode called the production VPID
allocator directly on the destination vCPU.  A later vCPU decode, environment
rebuild, or registry replacement failure therefore left a scarce host VPID
owned by an otherwise unchanged destination.

Active restore now acquires each destination VPID into its unpublished vCPU
stage.  Aborting or freeing the VM-wide stage releases every such VPID; final
publication transfers the validated owner only after registry replacement and
all MSR workspace acquisitions succeed.  The completion pass also rechecks
that the frozen destination did not acquire competing VPID ownership before
commit.  Portable checkpoint data still contains no host VPID, residency mask,
allocator identity, or CPU-local invalidation result; the transferred owner
starts with a mandatory first-final-CPU flush.

The new ownership regression exercises both aborted staging and successful
single-owner transfer.  The complete rootless model now passes 147 cases both
normally and under ASan/UBSan.  A clean private-object `vmm.ko` build passes
with kernel `-Werror`.  Live active-L2 restore, repeated restore into freshly
created destinations, VPID exhaustion, and multi-vCPU failure injection remain
part of the root-owned Intel qualification gate.
## 2026-07-31 whole-machine checkpoint topology seal

The common checkpoint preflight now emits and verifies a versioned canonical
SHA-256 seal for the complete machine device topology.  The order-independent
record binds each PCI device's stable emulator/BDF identity, the
architecture-owned legacy device set, and each VirtIO device's immutable
transport, queue count and sizes, MSI-X table shape, configuration extent, and
shared-memory regions.  It deliberately does not conflate runtime negotiation,
payload integrity, or external-backend identity with immutable topology; those
remain stricter per-device requirements checked independently.

Restore reconstructs the source seal from the fixed-width per-device
compatibility envelopes, verifies the metadata seal, constructs the destination
seal, and rejects any mismatch before payload validation or publication.
Historical images remain readable only when both new fields are absent, while
partial, unknown-version, noncanonical, duplicate, and inconsistent records
fail closed.  The independent model proves order independence, sensitivity to
every sealed field, intentional separation from runtime fields, and ambiguous
input rejection.  Both the model and the snapshot translation unit build with
`-Werror`; live changed-topology restore rejection remains in the privileged
qualification handoff.

The following SCSI checkpoint review confirmed that active-command ownership
was already implemented rather than still a protocol-design gap.  The common
VirtIO fence closes new request admission, all consumed CTL commands drain
normally under one monotonic deadline shared by the complete queue set, and a
failure restores only queue incarnations acquired by that checkpoint owner.
The new two-queue negative case forces the second queue to time out after the
first was parked and proves both queues and ownership flags return to their
original running-source state.  Remaining SCSI work is live qualification,
event/LUN race saturation, repeated subscription reconstruction, packed
cross-guest activation, and translated DMA—not another checkpoint mechanism.

## 2026-07-31 common restore and translated-DMA closure

The common-infrastructure pass traced every device restore callback through
validation, external reconstruction, publication, and rollback.  Device state
which is purely in-memory remains validate-before-publish.  Virtio-IOMMU's
prepared destination mapping view is published with release ordering, consumed
only by the validation owner, retained through all dependent endpoint
validators, and destroyed only after that validation phase completes.  All
endpoint descriptor, indirect-table, payload, and device-private accesses use
the common DMA mapper; balloon's architectural PFN interface and the IOMMU
function itself remain the two documented ACCESS_PLATFORM exceptions.

External reconstruction failure now has one common runtime contract.  A
failed compensation operation latches restore-incomplete state, requests
DEVICE_NEEDS_RESET, and prevents another checkpoint from being admitted.
Balloon, net, memory, and sound propagate their private backend failures into
that common latch.  The remaining device restore callbacks either stage all
state before publication or mutate only reversible in-memory state.

The complete ASan/UBSan device harness passes after this audit, including the
independent requirements/oracle checks and exhaustive small packed-ring model.
Live injected IOMMU/backend rollback and changed-topology restore remain
privileged qualification gates, not rootless claims.

## 2026-07-31 balloon normative and reference comparison

The balloon device was checked against VirtIO 1.4 CS01 sections 5.5.2 through
5.5.6.7, pinned Linux `virtio_balloon.c`, and pinned QEMU
`virtio-balloon.c`.  Fixed optional queue indices, little-endian configuration,
single retained statistics ownership, command-ID free-page hinting,
poison-aware page reporting, and versioned reconstruction agree with the
normative model.  Differences from QEMU are deliberate: optional features are
off until explicitly configured, and checkpoint restores the exact discard
ownership bitmap rather than only the target and actual counters.

This pass found a reset transaction defect.  If cancelling a host discard
failed, the balloon callback requested NEEDS_RESET before `vi_reset_dev()`,
which then erased that indication and reopened checkpoint admission even
though the ownership bitmap was deliberately retained.  Balloon now performs
common reset first and republishes restore-incomplete state afterwards, just
like memory and sound backend repair.  The fixture's reset double now clears
the latch and status as production does, so the regression proves the ordering
rather than merely counting a pre-reset call.

All 12 balloon device cases, all 10 balloon host cases, the focused repeated
restore test, and a production bhyve build pass with `-Werror`.  Linux split
and packed optional-feature activation, 5BSD statistics/page-poison activation,
resident-memory effects, reset under pressure, and active checkpoint remain in
the privileged live matrix.

## 2026-07-31 virtio-GPU 2D state transaction review

The retained GPU model, PCI adapter, queue boundary, display conversion, and
portable state were compared with VirtIO 1.4 section 5.7 and the pinned Linux
and QEMU implementations.  Resource identifiers, backing extents, scanout and
cursor geometry, optional blob commands, DMA permissions, shared-memory
aperture state, and destination reconstruction all remain bounded and
validate-before-publish.  Linux's transfer-before-SET_SCANOUT_BLOB sequence is
supported intentionally; renderer, HOST3D, cross-device blob, and multiplane
behavior remain unadvertised.

The review found that blob `RESOURCE_FLUSH` was the sole pixel import path not
using a transaction.  It copied each DMA row directly into retained pixels, so
a fault reading a later row returned an error after publishing the successful
prefix.  Blob flush now stages the complete rectangle, commits only after all
DMA reads succeed, and reports allocation failure without changing the
resource.  The regression injects a fault on the second row and proves that
the resource and display notification count remain unchanged before a
successful retry.

All 43 GPU protocol, queue, state, display, and PCI cases pass, and the
production bhyve object builds with `-Werror`.  Live Linux/5BSD split and
packed presentation, VNC ownership, blob aperture, ACCESS_PLATFORM, reset,
and active checkpoint evidence remain promotion gates.

## 2026-07-31 virtio-fs protocol, ownership, and migration review

The non-DAX filesystem device was reviewed against VirtIO 1.4 section 5.11,
the pinned Linux `fs/fuse/virtio_fs.c` driver, and QEMU's pinned
`vhost-user-fs` device and backend-state migration boundary.  The device keeps
the specification's hiprio queue distinct from ordinary request queues,
rejects normal operations on hiprio and INTERRUPT/FORGET operations on normal
queues, detects the FUSE session byte order from INIT, and prevents a stale
asynchronous INIT completion from publishing a superseded session.  Multiple
request queues share one incarnation-fenced FUSE session, matching Linux's
driver-visible model.

The backend boundary differs intentionally from QEMU's vhost-user ownership:
it uses an authenticated bounded SOCK_SEQPACKET protocol with explicit
cancellation, freeze, opaque state transfer, and a stable configured backend
identity.  Checkpoint admission closes before requests drain, uses a monotonic
condition-variable deadline instead of polling, and binds the portable image
to the exact tag, queue topology, negotiated features, backend limits, and
identity.  Decode and validation do not publish either the FUSE session or
opaque state; a rejected thaw retains the quiesced state for retry.  Active
FIDs are deliberately a backend-owned freeze concern rather than serialized
host pointers or file descriptors.

All 17 filesystem component suites pass: backend client and framing, backend
protocol, chain, connection, dispatch, export, FUSE codec, handle, host,
outbox, PCI, pending ownership, queue, server, session, and portable state.
This includes malformed frames and chains, priority-capacity reservation,
selective cancellation/reset, bounded late replies, disconnect and destroy
drain, backend identity mismatch, failed freeze rollback, and retryable thaw.
No new rootless correctness defect remained after this pass.  Live Linux
mount/read/mutation rejection, multi-queue activation, split/packed reset,
daemon restart, active-FID checkpoint, ACCESS_PLATFORM, and long reconnect
soak remain explicit privileged promotion gates; DAX remains unadvertised
until the shared-memory and mapping lifecycle is production-qualified.

## 2026-07-31 virtio-mem and RTC normative/reference review

Virtio-mem was compared with VirtIO 1.4 section 5.15, the pinned Linux
`virtio_mem` driver, and QEMU's virtio-mem device model. The device does not
advertise `UNPLUGGED_INACCESSIBLE`, so its direct CPU mapping remains present
and host `MADV_FREE` is a valid discard policy; bytes in unplugged blocks are
not promised across a later plug. Geometry, requested size, block ownership,
and destination reconstruction are fixed-width and validated before publish.
Both memory harness suites pass. Linux split/packed plug and unplug under
pressure, changed-destination capacity, ACCESS_PLATFORM, active checkpoint,
and a real 5BSD driver remain live qualification work.

The RTC device was compared with VirtIO 1.4 section 5.23 and the pinned Linux
RTC driver, with QEMU used as a timer and migration behavior comparison where
applicable. This pass found a reset-ordering defect: failure to disarm the
host timer requested `DEVICE_NEEDS_RESET` before common reset, which erased
the indication and could admit a new driver or checkpoint while an old timer
remained armed. Reset now records the disarm failure, performs common reset,
then republishes the runtime restore-incomplete latch and
`DEVICE_NEEDS_RESET`. The fixture reset now clears both fields like
production, so the regression proves the repaired post-reset state.

All three RTC protocol, alarm, and PCI suites pass, and bhyve builds with
`-Werror`. Live Linux alarm delivery across clock steps, suspend, queue reset,
and repeated checkpoint/restore remain explicit promotion gates; 5BSD RTC
activation requires a guest driver rather than an implementation-derived
mock.

## 2026-07-31 virtio-sound normative/reference review

Virtio-sound was reviewed against VirtIO 1.4 section 5.14, the pinned Linux
ALSA virtio driver, and QEMU's device-side behavior where implemented. The
device exposes exactly the standard control, event, tx, and rx queues, two
honestly described S16 PCM streams, and no jack, channel-map, control, shared
memory, polling, or event feature it cannot implement. Linux's queueing model
confirms the intentionally different admission rules: output may be consumed
after PREPARE for prebuffering, while input does not complete until START.

The lifecycle serializer commits SET_PARAMS, PREPARE, START, STOP, and RELEASE
only after backend success. RELEASE retires retained and available PCM
requests before backend release and before publishing the control response.
One generation-scoped private buffer per stream separates guest DMA from
nonblocking OSS progress; cancellation, readiness completion, selective reset,
full reset, and callback deletion cannot publish through a stale queue
incarnation. Checkpoint rejects active ownership, binds the exact backend kind
and endpoint identity, serializes no descriptor, host pointer, audio handle,
or event registration, and reconstructs stream lifecycle transactionally.
Irrecoverable rollback or reset cleanup remains latched through the common
restore-incomplete mechanism.

No new production defect remained after this pass. The complete ASan/UBSan
device harness passed, including all four sound suites and the independent
wire-value gate, and bhyve linked with `-Werror`. Live Linux ALSA activation
for null and OSS backends, split/packed queues, real playback and capture,
underrun/overrun behavior, active-stream checkpoint policy, repeated teardown,
and ACCESS_PLATFORM remain explicit qualification gates. A 5BSD virtio-sound
driver is required before claiming cross-guest activation.

## 2026-07-31 virtio-block normative/reference review

Virtio-block was compared with VirtIO 1.4 section 5.2, the pinned Linux
virtio-blk driver, and QEMU's virtio-blk device and migration model. The
device advertises optional read-only, FLUSH, CONFIG_WCE, DISCARD,
WRITE_ZEROES, multiqueue, packed-ring, queue-reset, and suspend capabilities
only when their backend and transport contracts exist. Secure erase remains
unadvertised because the ordinary file and device backends cannot promise its
destructive semantics.

Every request is bounded in 512-byte capacity units before submission.
Positive short translated writes are retried without skipping guest bytes,
zero-progress reads and writes fail instead of spinning, and the frontend
converts any incomplete nominally successful transfer into IOERR. FLUSH is a
full scheduler barrier. Guest-selected writethrough and a driver which
declines offered FLUSH both delay successful write completion until the
backend is stable. DISCARD and WRITE_ZEROES accept one bounded specification
segment, validate flags and overflow, and do not advertise media mutation on
a read-only backend.

Multiqueue requests carry both device and queue generations. Selective reset
cancels and drains only the selected queue, while a full reset invalidates all
ring ownership before backend cancellation and waits without holding the lock
needed by completion callbacks. Portable state encodes logical fields rather
than the packed host structure, binds the guest-visible ID and an explicit or
same-object backend identity, freezes resize publication, and rejects
capacity, topology, queue, cache, or destination identity drift before
publish. No new production defect remained after this pass. The block and
block-backend sanitizer suites and the complete shared harness pass, and
bhyve links with `-Werror`.

Remaining live promotion gates are Linux and 5BSD split/packed multiqueue
activation on every queue, queue-local reset during concurrent traffic,
discard and write-zeroes boundary/error operation on real backing stores,
CONFIG_WCE transitions, ACCESS_PLATFORM, backend replacement rejection,
active-I/O repeated checkpoint, and longer reset/persistence soak. A 5BSD
multiqueue guest driver change is required before the host can honestly claim
that cross-guest activation.
## 2026-07-31 virtio-net normative and reference review

The device was reviewed against VirtIO 1.4 CS01 section 5.1, the pinned Linux
virtio-net driver, and the pinned QEMU device model after the packed-ring,
multiqueue, RSS, hash-report, queue-reset, and checkpoint changes.  No new
rootless correctness defect was found.  The review traced RX staging, bounded
mevent work, TX/control fairness, EVENT_IDX rearming, queue-local reset,
multiqueue contraction, feature-dependent header validation, RSS publication,
backend capability changes, suspend, and transactional restore.  The TX
condition variable and its bounded quiesce deadlines use the same monotonic
clock; full reset fences new worker ownership before its intentional unbounded
drain.  Snapshot validation has no external side effects, while restore rolls
back a changed backend framing contract and fails closed through the common
restore-incomplete latch if compensation itself fails.

The sanitizer matrix independently covers malformed chains and offload
metadata, MTU and feature dependencies, RSS/hash parsing and control commands,
fair scheduling, queue-local reset, staged RX, backend faults, and rejected
snapshot images.  Promotion still requires the scheduled Linux and rebuilt
5BSD split/packed lanes to prove real traffic on every enabled queue, MSI and
MSI-X interrupt suppression, queue reset under concurrent traffic, translated
DMA on every descriptor path, active-I/O repeated checkpoint/restore, and the
long reset/traffic soak.  Those live gates remain explicit rather than being
inferred from negotiation or rootless models.
## 2026-07-31 virtio-console normative and reference review

The console implementation was retraced against VirtIO 1.4 CS01 section 5.3
and the pinned Linux and QEMU multiport implementations.  No new rootless
correctness defect was found.  The review covered feature-gated queue
topology, DEVICE_ADD/PORT_READY/PORT_NAME ordering, console nomination,
emergency writes, bounded synchronous completion, per-port queue reset,
stale connection callbacks, buffered nonblocking host output, suspend rearm,
listener reconstruction, and transactional portable state.  A checkpoint is
deliberately rejected while a host connection or buffered host output exists;
the saved listener name/path and queue identity must match the destination,
and port lifecycle state is not published until the complete image validates.

Independent tests cover malformed descriptor directions, partial control
messages, event-buffer exhaustion and retry, multiple ports, host close and
replacement-connection races, bounded callback work, selective reset,
suspend/resume, and malformed or incompatible snapshots.  The remaining
promotion work is live: multiple simultaneous Linux and rebuilt-5BSD ports,
split and packed traffic, blocked readers/writers across selective reset,
host and guest close races, listener reconnect policy, translated DMA, and
active-port migration policy.  Negotiation alone is not accepted as evidence
for any of those gates.
## 2026-07-31 virtio-9P normative and reference review

The 9P device was reviewed against VirtIO 1.4 CS01 section 5.9, the pinned
Linux 9p transport, lib9p ownership rules, and QEMU's device-side behavior.
No new rootless correctness defect was found.  The pass traced request leases
through immediate and asynchronous completion, full-reset connection
replacement, generation-fenced selective queue reset, bounded notifications,
suspend quiesce, export confinement, read-only capability rights, mount-tag
encoding, and destination identity validation.  The last callback draining a
reset generation completes that reset exactly once; ordinary and stale
callbacks never complete one.  Full reset drops the recursive device lock
while lib9p drains, fences replacement with `vsc_resetting`, and does not
replay kicks from the discarded incarnation.

Portable checkpoint currently has an intentionally strict boundary: active
requests or any live fid make the image non-reconstructible and return
`EBUSY`.  An idle image records fixed-width protocol state and requires the
same export path, root device/inode, read-only policy, mount tag, negotiated
features, and queue topology.  Tests independently cover descriptor ordering,
response buffers, immediate completion, reset races, quiesce timeout,
malformed snapshots, export escape attempts, and read-only rights.  Remaining
promotion work is live split/packed Linux and rebuilt-5BSD mount mutation,
reset during requests, long fid/reconnect soak, translated DMA, and—before
claiming active migration—an explicit portable fid/object reconstruction
design rather than serialization of lib9p pointers or host descriptors.
## 2026-07-31 virtio-input normative and reference review

The input device was retraced against VirtIO 1.4 CS01 section 5.8, Linux
virtio-input/evdev behavior, and QEMU's input device model.  The review found
and fixed one host-boundary defect: if timestamp acquisition failed while a
guest status event was forwarded to evdev, the host `input_event` contained
uninitialized timestamp bytes.  The complete host event is now initialized
before its protocol fields are assigned, so even the timestamp-failure path is
deterministic.  The focused ATF program passes every case and bhyve rebuilds
cleanly with `-Werror`.

The remaining review found the configuration selector, native bitmap
translation, atomic SYN_REPORT framing, SYN_DROPPED resynchronization,
queue-sized callback budget, selective reset drain, suspend behavior, event
source lifetime, and portable staged-frame restore consistent with the
specification and pinned references.  Root promotion still requires live
Linux and rebuilt-5BSD split/packed injection and returned-status tests,
multiple devices, queue saturation and loss recovery, reset during injection,
configuration-change observation, translated DMA, active checkpoint, and a
long injection/reset soak.
## 2026-07-31 virtio-rng normative and reference review

The entropy device was reviewed against VirtIO 1.4 CS01 section 5.4, Linux
virtio-rng, and QEMU's entropy backend behavior.  No new rootless correctness
defect was found.  Requests are device-writable only, scatter/gather length is
bounded per host read, EINTR is retried, a short successful read is a valid
partial completion, malformed chains fail closed, and an unavailable or
failed entropy source requests device reset instead of leaving a retained
descriptor with no future wakeup.  Queue processing is synchronous and
ordered, so selective reset and suspend require no device-private worker
state.

Checkpoint saves only common queue ownership and never serializes or replays
entropy bytes.  Independent tests cover hostile descriptors, scatter/gather,
EOF and transient/permanent read failures, bounded requests and batches,
source startup, IN_ORDER, packed opt-in, and the absence of private entropy
state.  Promotion still requires Linux and rebuilt-5BSD split/packed reads,
selective reset/rebind soak, injected source failure and recovery policy,
translated DMA, suspend, and repeated checkpoint proof that restored output
is newly sourced.

## 2026-07-31 virtio-vsock restore-preflight review

The vsock save-state path was rechecked as part of the per-device lifecycle
pass.  The public restore-preflight API can call a device validator without
first transferring checkpoint ownership, but the private codec asserted that
ownership had already been transferred and, for the kernel backend, that the
external provider was already frozen.  Production startup currently pauses
devices before invoking this API, while independent callers and focused
validation do not.  Freezing from the validator would violate the stronger
contract: validation must not mutate an external backend and may later reject
a different device.

Vsock now has a side-effect-free validation wrapper.  It acquires the recursive
device mutex, establishes serializer ownership only for the duration of the
common transactional codec, and restores the prior ownership state on every
exit.  Structural kernel-backend validation is allowed while unfrozen, but
local pending RX/TX and failed state are still rejected.  The commit-time pause
path remains authoritative: it freezes the provider, waits for active copies,
and rechecks that the provider queue and CID-scoped connection set are empty
before any state is published.

A focused ATF case injects a common-validator failure and proves that the mutex
and ownership flag are present during the call, restored afterward, and that
neither FREEZE nor THAW is issued.  All vsock-device cases pass, and bhyve links
cleanly with the tree's `-Werror` flags.  The privileged promotion gate remains
the Linux userspace/kernel split-and-packed checkpoint matrix, including an
image rejected after successful preflight and a provider that becomes busy
between preflight and commit.

## 2026-07-31 virtio-fs restore-preflight review

Extending the same lifecycle audit to virtio-fs found that its private codec
required checkpoint-pause ownership even for `VM_SNAPSHOT_VALIDATE`.
Production restore pauses devices first, but the independently callable
preflight API and focused validation do not; those paths rejected every
identity-bound virtio-fs image with `EBUSY`.  Calling backend QUIESCE from the
validator would violate the all-device preflight contract and could leave a
daemon frozen after another device rejects the image.

The connection layer now exposes a read-only checkpoint compatibility
contract: the authenticated protocol version, capabilities, negotiated
limits, and incarnation are copied without closing admission or emitting a
control frame, with only the copy's phase normalized to the necessarily
quiesced image phase.  The PCI validation wrapper reuses checkpoint ownership
when the current thread already holds the non-recursive device mutex, and
otherwise acquires it while the common transactional codec compares the
incoming image with that copy.
Restore commit still requires the ordinary pause path, which drains ownership,
performs the real QUIESCE exchange, captures the exact FUSE and opaque backend
state, and rechecks the contract before publication.

The connection test now proves the normalized contract is available before
pause and that the subsequent real pause still reports the live active phase.
The PCI test directly exercises serializer entry both without ownership and
with the non-recursive mutex already retained by pause, proving that exit
releases only ownership acquired by preflight.  This test exposed a stale-build
mistake in the first draft: the private mutex-ownership API requires
`pthread_np.h` and the ATF target requires libpthread.  Both production and
test build declarations are now explicit.  All focused connection and PCI
tests pass, and the complete bhyve target rebuilds with `-Werror`.  Live
promotion requires a state-transfer-capable daemon and a test in which the
daemon contract changes both before preflight and between preflight and
commit.

## 2026-07-31 rotating common-code review

The final common-code cycle used all six roadmap lenses after the per-device
passes.  The requirements validator accepts 213 requirements backed by 664
independent oracle definitions and resolves every scheduled case and
`VIRTIO_ACTIVATION_ASSERTION` reference.  The separate activation ledger has
117 claims.  It intentionally reports 71 unresolved Linux obligations and
106 unresolved 5BSD obligations; running with
`VIRTIO_ACTIVATION_GATE=linux` fails closed on those rows.  A model, a driver
attachment, or feature negotiation alone was not promoted to live evidence.

The packed-ring comparison used the pinned Linux `virtio_ring.c` and QEMU
`hw/virtio/virtio.c` revisions from the reference corpus.  All three models
start packed availability and used wrap counters at one, publish a used head
only after the rest of its chain, reset queue-local cursors and wraps without
resetting unrelated queues, and retain packed cursors in migration state.
bhyve additionally retains a destination-local generation owner for each
asynchronous request.  That is an intentional backend-lifetime fence rather
than a guest-visible difference; source generations are consumed for format
compatibility but never republished on restore.

The portability scan found no native pointer, descriptor, `long`, page-size,
or host-endian value in the modern portable records.  Remaining raw snapshot
buffers are either exact guest-visible configuration byte strings or
fixed-size arrays whose multibyte members are encoded separately.  The
`sizeof(long)` uses in the input device describe the host evdev ioctl bitmap,
not a VirtIO wire or save-state layout.  Constants equal to 4096 are bounded
protocol/resource limits or the specification's balloon page unit, not a host
page-size assumption.  Device progress contains no manual sleep loop; queue,
backend, timer, and readiness progress remains event driven with bounded
monotonic lifecycle deadlines.

No new common correctness defect was found in this cycle.  The remaining
high-value gaps are live activation: selective queue reset on real guest
drivers, translated ACCESS_PLATFORM I/O, split/packed active checkpoint and
repeated restore, rebuilt-5BSD drivers, external-backend races, and Intel
nested execution.  They remain pending in the activation ledger and the
qualification handoff rather than being inferred from rootless coverage.

A clean `MK_BHYVE_SNAPSHOT=yes` rebuild was also used specifically to compile
the conditional restore path.  The changed virtio-fs snapshot object compiles
with `-Werror`.  The standalone aggregate build then stops, as expected on
this not-yet-upgraded host, when checkpoint CPU code sees the installed
pre-change `machine/vmm*.h` ABI instead of this tree's
`VM_CPUID_F_BASELINE` and `vm_cpu_compat` definitions.  The source-paired
world/kernel/package build in the qualification handoff is the valid
integration gate; duplicating those kernel ABI definitions in bhyve merely to
make a mismatched standalone build link would hide a real deployment error.

## 2026-07-31 nested virtual-CPUID consistency review

The Intel capability pass found one cross-layer defect on LA57-capable hosts.
The ordinary bhyve CPUID policy masks `CPUID.7.0:ECX.LA57`, but nested-VMX
initialization previously derived its virtual linear-address width directly
from the unfiltered host feature word.  An L1 could therefore observe LA48 in
CPUID while the virtual VMX contract accepted 57-bit host/guest addresses and
permitted `CR4.LA57` through `IA32_VMX_CR4_FIXED1`.

The leaf-7 ECX allowlist is now a shared, value-only CPU-model function used
by both CPUID emulation and nested capability construction.  Nested linear
width is derived from the filtered guest feature word.  The capability model
also clears `CR4.LA57` from `IA32_VMX_CR4_FIXED1` for an LA48 virtual CPU and
fails closed if a hardware policy ever requires that bit.  Independent tests
cover host-LA57 filtering, width selection, fixed-bit shaping, transactional
failure, and the future LA57 value path.  The focused tests, 147-case nested
model, 168-entry ledger, and `vmm.ko` `-Werror` build pass.  This is rootless
conformance evidence only; all ten live Intel qualification groups remain
required before guest VMX exposure can be promoted.

The nested requirements validator now resolves the LA57/guest-CPUID policy
case from its dedicated x86 CPUID ATF binary as well as the nested-state
binary.  It still requires both declaration and registration and no longer
encourages duplicating a cross-layer policy test merely to satisfy a one-file
inventory assumption.

The following qualification-manifest audit found separate fail-open test
coverage declarations.  Split and packed virtio-fs reset and checkpoint cases
existed, but the authoritative `reset-devices` and `checkpoint-devices` value
domains omitted `fs`; removal of those filesystem lifecycle cases could
therefore leave both coverage lines green.  Both domains now include `fs`, and
the lab self-test pins the checkpoint invariant.  The checkpoint coverage
command resolves the filesystem active-policy, split/packed ring, and complete
device-domain contracts together.

VirtIO-IOMMU had a related but distinct omission: its packed release case ran
the reset path, while no coverage contract required reset and
`VIRTIO_IOMMU=yes` in the same case.  The new `iommu-reset-lifecycle` contract
binds those values, so endpoint reset alone can no longer masquerade as an
IOMMU lifecycle result.

The shared-memory consumer had the same composition risk.  GPU blob activity,
generic GPU reset, and generic GPU checkpoint could previously be satisfied by
different cases.  `gpu-blob-reset-lifecycle` and
`gpu-blob-checkpoint-lifecycle` now require the blob feature, the lifecycle
operation, and the GPU device in one scheduled case; the existing split,
packed, and translated-DMA cases supply the evidence.

RTC alarm reset and checkpoint evidence is now similarly bound by
`rtc-alarm-reset-lifecycle` and `rtc-alarm-checkpoint-lifecycle`.  A plain
clock read after reset/restore cannot satisfy either contract; the scheduled
case must enable the alarm feature while exercising the lifecycle path.

The two existing block checkpoint boots now also prove optional media-policy
state without extending the profile: the split lane enables discard on a
writable image and the packed lane uses read-only media.  New checkpoint
coverage contracts require both values of `BLOCK_DISCARD` and
`BLOCK_READONLY`; each lane retains active read I/O across restore, while the
ordinary device verifier performs the discard or rejected-write assertions.

The split SCSI checkpoint lane now enables asynchronous events while the
packed lane keeps them disabled, and `checkpoint-scsi-events` requires both
states.  This promotes destination CTL subscription reconstruction, forced
rescan, and event/request coexistence into the restore matrix instead of
testing them only during a non-checkpoint boot.

The split console checkpoint lane now negotiates MULTIPORT while the packed
lane retains the single-port baseline.  `checkpoint-console-port-counts`
requires both states, so the active-session rejection and post-restore control
queue checks cover port discovery and per-port state rather than only port 0.

The split input checkpoint lane now launches two input functions and the
packed lane one.  `checkpoint-input-device-counts` requires both values, so
the active injection and restore checks demonstrate per-device queue/event
ownership instead of extrapolating from one function.

Virtio-fs checkpoint coverage now also requires request-queue counts 2 and 8,
matching the existing split and packed idle/active-rejection lanes.  The
external-backend contract is therefore exercised across a queue-boundary
change as well as both ring layouts.

The checkpoint profile's four vsock lanes are now guarded by
`checkpoint-vsock-backends` as well as the ring-format contract.  Userspace
and kernel providers must each complete checkpoint qualification; the two
userspace cases alone can no longer satisfy the device's restore coverage.
### 2026-07-31 checkpoint feature-composition review

- Checkpoint coverage now binds active restore to two queues for network,
  block, and SCSI instead of allowing the packed/split lanes to satisfy only
  the ring-format dimension.  The same audit binds block discard/read-only,
  SCSI asynchronous events, console multiport, two input devices,
  virtio-fs queue boundaries, and both vsock backends to checkpoint cases.
- The GPU presentation release case and GPU active-checkpoint case previously
  formed two disconnected proofs.  `checkpoint-gpu-modern` now enables the
  external display backend, reconnects to RFB after restore, and verifies the
  independently derived framebuffer marker written after restored execution.
  This covers resource state, active guest progress, backend reconstruction,
  and observable presentation in one lane.
- Rootless manifest, shell, helper compilation, and helper self-tests pass.
  The new live checkpoint cases remain root-only qualification evidence.
- Balloon packed checkpoint now restores statistics, deflate-on-OOM,
  free-page hinting, reporting, and poison together and reruns guest and host
  activity checks after each restore.  A hardware-dependent
  `audio-qualification` profile similarly adds active OSS playback/capture
  checkpoint in both ring formats while portable qualification keeps the
  deterministic null backend.
- ACCESS_PLATFORM release and checkpoint contracts now enumerate every
  eligible endpoint through an opt-in tokenized `DEVICES` domain.  The packed
  combined IOMMU lanes add virtio-fs, and live translation tracing must
  correlate activity for every guest-enumerated endpoint.  Balloon remains
  explicitly ineligible because the Linux PFN/reporting ABI does not use the
  DMA API; it does not advertise ACCESS_PLATFORM.

### 2026-07-31 restore-contract and reference comparison

- The common restore coordinator was retraced from metadata and topology
  validation through fabric-first payload validation and commit.  Device
  topology, record layout and presence, the machine seal, every compatibility
  envelope, the incoming IOMMU view, and every endpoint payload are validated
  before the first device publishes restored state.
- The sanitizer harness carried a stale copy of the compatibility predicate.
  Its mock now matches production canonical-tail and impossible-source-feature
  checks.  An independent VirtIO 1.4 fixture explicitly proves that a source
  which negotiated `ACCESS_PLATFORM` cannot restore onto a destination that
  would silently use direct DMA; queue geometry and shared-memory drift are
  rejected by the same matrix.
- The shared backend-identity codec now uses a maximum-bounded scan instead of
  `strlen()`, preflights the entire save record, and stages aliased input before
  publishing bytes.  The identity ATF program is now part of the ASan/UBSan
  harness, with mismatch, unterminated-input, short-output, and exact-overlap
  cases.
- At pinned QEMU commit `300438ffbb8d9430cac2fcc15cba6f482b2c0587`, VirtIO
  migration preserves negotiated features, queue count and size, modern queue
  enable/address state, packed cursors, status, ISR, and transport selectors;
  the WASPNest records cover the corresponding architectural state but use a
  separate preflight envelope and reject configuration-size drift rather than
  QEMU's bounded truncate/skip compatibility behavior.  This stricter policy
  is intentional for the first bhyve portable format.
- At pinned Linux commit `1590cf0329716306e948a8fc29f1d3ee87d3989f`, the
  VirtIO core requires both VERSION_1 and ACCESS_PLATFORM whenever its memory
  access callback is active.  That observable driver contract agrees with the
  fail-closed destination feature check; Linux and QEMU formats remain
  behavioral references only and no GPL implementation text is reused.

### 2026-07-31 live restore mutation and SCSI state review

- The checkpoint runner now performs two real destination mutations before
  the control restore.  The split-net lane changes queue geometry, while the
  packed-net lane removes the source's negotiated PACKED feature.  Each
  mutation must make bhyve exit during restore preflight with an explicit
  incompatibility diagnostic; a process which remains alive without opening
  its console is killed and counted as a failure rather than turning the
  qualification job into an unbounded wait.  The original configuration is
  then restored and its post-restore workload remains the positive control.
- The packed activation audit confirmed that every device for which Linux and
  rebuilt 5BSD currently provide a guest driver has a matrix case requiring
  packed negotiation, a host-observed packed queue, and real device I/O.
  Devices without a 5BSD driver remain explicit activation-ledger gaps rather
  than attachment-only passes.
- The SCSI private-state test now mutates the CTL initiator, request-queue
  count, negotiated feature set, immutable queue limits, event record size,
  CDB size, and CTL inventory independently.  Every mismatch fails before
  publication, and validation is also required to preserve a queued
  destination-local event.  The complete ASan/UBSan harness passes, including
  751 SCSI checks and the 1,195,896-check packed-ring state exploration.
- A standalone snapshot-enabled bhyve build on the running host continues to
  fail closed because installed `machine/vmm*.h` predates this tree's CPUID
  and CPU-compatibility ioctls.  This is intentional ABI-skew detection; the
  source-paired buildworld/kernel/package transaction remains the integration
  gate, and the ABI is not duplicated into bhyve to manufacture a mismatched
  binary.
- Console restore retains an explicit reconnect policy: listener identity and
  logical multiport lifecycle are portable, while a connected host socket or
  buffered host output makes checkpoint fail with `EBUSY`.  No descriptor or
  socket is serialized.  Independent mutations now prove that an image cannot
  claim an active host connection and cannot restore onto a differently named
  logical port, with destination state unchanged.  The refreshed sanitizer
  run passes 265 console checks.
- The 9P state audit distinguishes safety from completion.  The current
  versioned record restores an idle connection contract, mount tag, export
  identity, negotiated limits, and a destination-local completion generation.
  It intentionally rejects active requests and every fid-bearing session,
  because lib9p fids retain host descriptors, credentials, and backend-private
  objects.  Active-fid migration therefore remains a roadmap item requiring a
  portable fid/object replay contract and backend reconstruction; the current
  rejection tests must not be counted as that feature.

### 2026-07-31 vsock provider reconstruction review

- Kernel-backed restore uses the exclusively attached guest CID as its stable
  provider identity.  Commit-time pause fences that exact file/provider,
  requires zero queued packets and CID-scoped connections, reconstructs the
  negotiated feature epoch while admission remains closed, and only then
  thaws.  Detach or CID replacement between preflight and commit therefore
  fails the owning descriptor rather than silently selecting another provider.
- The freeze response is now treated as a versioned ABI in both directions:
  bhyve rejects a changed response version, nonzero reserved words, unexpected
  flags, or nonempty counts and attempts an immediate thaw/rollback.  The
  focused harness injects future-version and reserved-field responses and
  proves the lifecycle and checkpoint mutex are released without marking the
  provider frozen.
- The kernel snapshot negative matrix now mutates backend kind, guest CID,
  negotiated features, port allocator, path length, reserved bytes, and the
  canonical path tail independently.  Every rejected restore leaves the
  destination provider state unchanged before the final positive restore.
- The checkpoint qualification profile now contains a two-VM kernel-provider
  lane.  Distinct-CID barriers keep both providers attached across each VM's
  active-connection rejection/rollback and portable checkpoint/restore, so
  single-provider checkpoint success cannot satisfy the multi-provider claim.

### 2026-07-31 translated-DMA binding review

- The domain lifetime audit found that request leases were counted only after
  a DMA domain existed.  A direct-DMA request accepted before device reset
  could therefore remain incomplete while a later topology operation observed
  status zero and installed ACCESS_PLATFORM, changing the address-space
  interpretation underneath that completion.
- Common DMA leases now increment the binding-use count before observing
  either a translated or direct binding.  Domain publication first closes the
  same atomic gate and requires that count to be zero; release invokes a
  provider callback only when the stable lease actually has one.  This keeps
  direct-to-translated attachment, translated detach, sparse shared-memory
  access, queue mapping, and asynchronous completion under one architecture-
  neutral ownership rule.
- Lease acquisition now also saturates at `UINT32_MAX` instead of wrapping the
  active-use count to zero.  The boundary case fails without changing either
  the lease or counter, so an impossible amount of concurrent work cannot
  make domain publication or detach observe a false idle state.
- The independent core case holds a direct lease with status zero, requires
  domain installation to return `EBUSY`, releases it, and then proves attach
  and detach succeed.  Existing callback-blocked detach and request-completion
  tests remain the translated-domain counterparts.

The following administration transaction pass found a cross-index alias gap
in multi-owner restore.  Duplicate owner pointers were rejected and each input
record was disallowed from aliasing its corresponding owner, but record zero
could still point into owner one.  Publishing an earlier destination could
then rewrite bytes that a later publication had not consumed.  Preflight now
checks every record against every destination owner before parsing or locking;
both cross permutations have focused negative coverage and no owner is
modified.

### 2026-07-31 nested exit and cold-thaw publication review

- The value-only EPT-exit builder and VMCS02 hardware-resource binder now
  reject a result buffer overlapping any retained architectural, runtime,
  fault, host, or resource input.  Focused tests cover each input class and
  prove rejection leaves it byte-for-byte unchanged.
- Cold-L2 thaw now validates the complete public result graph before writing
  even its rollback status.  The plan, resource generation, and rollback
  result must be pairwise disjoint and must not overlap the input wrapper,
  callback table, portable L2 image, virtual capability contract, or frozen
  plan.  The callback-private argument remains an explicitly opaque adapter
  contract because its extent is not available to the common layer.
- The later staged handoff applies the same rule when transferring a ready
  thaw: neither output may overlap the retained staged owner or the other
  output.  Rejected aliases preserve the ready transaction so a correctly
  separated caller can retry and consume it exactly once.
- The normal 147-case model, the ASan/UBSan variant, the 169-entry
  requirements ledger, the ten-group live-evidence validator, and a fresh
  private-object `vmm.ko` build with kernel `-Werror` all pass.  VMX remains
  default-off; these publication checks are rootless model evidence rather
  than Intel L1/L2 hardware qualification.

### 2026-07-31 nested handoff consumption review

- Every value-returning handoff now rejects destination storage overlapping
  its retained owner, generation identity, or another output before copying
  or clearing state.  The per-vCPU tagged wrapper applies the same whole-owner
  rule, including continuation request/result separation, so a child-union
  output cannot be erased by the wrapper's final reset.
- Publication through the tagged wrapper likewise rejects a request sourced
  from the wrapper it is about to initialize.  Refreeze consumption rejects
  its retained request as an apparent caller-owned identity rather than
  accepting equality and then clearing the caller's bytes.
- Focused EPT, VMCS02-commit, and continuation regressions snapshot the owner,
  attempt the aliased transfer, require `EINVAL`, verify byte-for-byte
  preservation, and then complete a normal one-shot take.  The normal and
  ASan/UBSan 147-case model suites, the 170-entry evidence ledger, and the
  production `vmm.ko` kernel `-Werror` build pass.  Live Intel nested-guest
  qualification remains pending and is not implied by these model gates.

The following cold-owner pass found that EPT completion published its
disposition after mutating the context, continuation, and runtime.  A caller
could place that output inside any one of those owners and turn an otherwise
successful transition into state corruption.  Cold EPT completion and cold
reflection now require the context, continuation, runtime, portable image,
and any output to be pairwise disjoint before validation or mutation.  The
negative regression aliases the disposition with the context, verifies all
mutable owners are unchanged, and then completes the same pending operation
with separated storage.

### 2026-07-31 nested EPT02 cache ownership review

- Cache initialization now rejects an entry array or callback table
  overlapping the cache owner before either region is cleared.  Acquire,
  release, and resolve likewise keep keys, references, results, the owner, and
  its bounded entry storage separated, preventing a final result publication
  from overwriting live cache metadata.
- Backend create, invalidate, and destroy callbacks execute behind an explicit
  callback-active fence.  Recursive cache operations return `EBUSY`; callback
  failures cannot leave the fence set, and negative non-errno create results
  are normalized to `EPROTO` just like invalidation results.
- The rootless lifecycle case now covers overlapping initialization,
  overlapping acquire output, callback reentry, negative callback results,
  byte-for-byte preservation, and successful retry.  These runtime roots stay
  destination-local and remain excluded from portable checkpoint state.

### 2026-07-31 nested VMCS02 resource-lease review

- VMCS02 APIC-page, APIC-access-page, and posted-interrupt leases now keep the
  retained owner, VMCS identity, entry controls, callback table, fixed host
  resources, and result publication in disjoint storage.  Invalid aliases are
  rejected before a provider callback or owner mutation.
- Acquire and reverse-order release callbacks execute behind one explicit
  callback-active fence.  Recursive provider operations return `EBUSY`, a
  negative provider status is normalized to `EPROTO`, and partial acquisition
  still unwinds without publishing a resource generation.
- The focused lifecycle regression proves acquire-output alias preservation,
  acquire and release callback reentry rejection, negative-status handling,
  reverse rollback, and a normal retry.  The 147-case normal and ASan/UBSan
  model suites and a production `vmm.ko` kernel `-Werror` build pass.  This is
  rootless ownership evidence; live Intel L1/L2 execution remains pending.

### 2026-07-31 nested EPT and VPID backend-transfer review

- A successful EPT02 create callback must now return one non-null root that is
  distinct from every root already owned by the cache.  A duplicate cannot be
  destroyed safely because it may be the retained root itself, so it is
  rejected as `EPROTO` without eviction; the focused case proves the old root
  remains releasable.  The production root allocator also rejects a result
  slot overlapping its immutable backend or cache key before allocating.
- VPID02 allocation and release now use a callback-active owner fence.  A
  recursive allocator or releaser sees `EBUSY`, negative allocator status is
  normalized to `EPROTO`, an overlapping callback table is rejected before
  dereference, and release keeps the active owner published until the
  provider has relinquished the hardware tag.
- Rootless tests cover duplicate EPT roots, VPID allocation/release reentry,
  callback-table alias preservation, failure normalization, and successful
  retry.  The 147-case normal and ASan/UBSan suites, evidence validator, and
  production `vmm.ko` kernel `-Werror` build pass; they do not claim live
  Intel proof.

### 2026-07-31 nested MSR-workspace ownership review

- Binding now keeps the workspace owner, virtual capability contract, and
  complete plan/rollback arrays mutually disjoint.  Beginning a transaction
  also rejects a generation result inside any retained region before changing
  the owner.
- Generation `UINT64_MAX` is an explicit `EOVERFLOW` terminal condition.  It
  no longer wraps to one and risks accepting an ancient entry/exit MSR-list
  identity as current after an extreme uptime or fault-injection sequence.
- Focused tests snapshot the capability and workspace owners across aliased
  capacity, binding, and generation outputs and across exhaustion.  The normal
  and ASan/UBSan 147-case models and production `vmm.ko` kernel `-Werror`
  build pass.

### 2026-07-31 nested VMCS-registry ownership review

- Registry initialization, field import, exit preparation/publication,
  entry-failure commit, reads, snapshots, launched-state queries, and abort
  queries now reject storage inside either the registry object or any of its
  separately allocated VMCS regions.  Multi-output queries also require
  disjoint caller-owned destinations.
- VM-wide replacement rejects shallow copies that share even one entry
  allocation.  Without this check, swapping list heads could create two
  owners for one region and lead to cross-registry mutation or double free.
