- Focused regressions preserve the registry across aliased outputs, reject
  overlapping launched/epoch results, and construct a bounded shared-entry
  replacement to prove it fails before publication.  The normal and
  ASan/UBSan 147-case models and production `vmm.ko` kernel `-Werror` build
  pass.

The monotonic-identity sweep also found the value-model VMXON epoch wrapping
from `UINT64_MAX` back to one.  Because launched VMCS state uses that epoch to
reject VMRESUME across VMXOFF/VMXON sessions, recycling it defeats the stale
session fence.  VMXON now fails without mutation at exhaustion, with a focused
byte-preservation regression.

The same pass moved VMCS02 lease-generation exhaustion ahead of every backend
callback, so a transaction known to be unpublishable has no provider side
effects.  It also requires the final sorted VMCS02 hardware-write program to
be published outside its immutable composed plan; the alias regression keeps
the full plan byte-identical.

The registry checkpoint follow-up now treats the decoded current-VMCS view
and both of its borrowed wire ranges as part of the immutable transaction.
Restore rejects oversized or missing ranges and any overlap with the registry
record, destination registry, view descriptor, or sibling range before
parsing or publication.  The focused regression places the view descriptor
inside the live registry and proves rejection leaves the canonical registry
image unchanged.

The decoded-state field accessor now enforces the same borrowed-view contract.
It validates both complete field ranges, rejects overlapping ranges, and
publishes through a local candidate only when the result is disjoint from the
view and immutable wire image.  Direct result-over-view and result-over-wire
regressions preserve both sources byte for byte.

The cold-L2 architectural accessors now keep scalar, segment, descriptor-table,
PDPTE, and amd64 descriptor input/output storage outside the portable owner.
This removes overlapping structure assignments and prevents a query result
from corrupting the detached state which later restore or VM-exit publication
still owns.  The focused access test exercises both generic and amd64 adapter
aliases and verifies the complete portable image remains unchanged.

The atomic EPT12 memory helper now rejects its loaded or updated value output
inside the retained callback descriptor before invoking memory or taking the
already-set A/D fast path.  The regression aliases both operations with the
descriptor and verifies its function pointers and opaque argument are not
overwritten.

Frozen VMCS12 capture now publishes its pointer-free snapshot outside both
the opaque VMCS region and virtual capability policy.  Building the later
pointer-bearing VM-entry view likewise keeps the result outside its snapshot
and optional memory/MSR-policy descriptors.  Focused aliases preserve the
complete VMCS region and snapshot, preventing a successful query from
invalidating the exact entry image it returns pointers into.

Preemption-timer exit publication now rejects a save plan inside the
immutable exit-time observation.  The focused alias case leaves the complete
TSC, deadline, rate, and expiration input unchanged rather than allowing the
final small plan write to corrupt a later retry or diagnostic.

### 2026-08-01 5BSD virtio-net RSS and hash-report qualification slice

- The 5BSD `vtnet` driver now understands the VirtIO 1.4 extended 20-byte
  receive header, the six basic hash-report values, and the RSS device
  configuration fields.  RSS and hash reporting are negotiated independently:
  both require the control virtqueue, while only RSS requires multiqueue.  The
  driver validates the advertised key and hash-type limits for both modes and
  the table limit only for RSS, then removes only the invalid dependent
  features before finalizing negotiation.
- The default RSS command uses the document-defined 128-entry table and
  40-byte Toeplitz key, device byte order, the kernel RSS indirection policy
  when available, and a deterministic queue distribution otherwise.  A
  rejected command falls back to one active pair instead of publishing a
  partially configured multiqueue state.
- A one-pair device uses the document-defined 53-byte `HASH_CONFIG` command,
  including four zero reserved words and the same 40-byte key.  If RSS setup
  fails but hash reporting was also negotiated, the driver falls back to one
  pair and still attempts the independent hash configuration; failure leaves
  packet delivery intact with `HASH_REPORT_NONE` metadata.
- Receive processing preserves mergeable-buffer semantics when hash reporting
  is also negotiated, strips the negotiated header length, validates the
  reserved field and report range, ignores the unspecified hash value carried
  with `NONE`, maps valid reports to native mbuf hash types, and exposes
  accepted and invalid metadata counters per receive queue.
  Netmap's shared header storage was enlarged to the maximum negotiated header
  so the same feature combination cannot overwrite the fixed object.
- The live 5BSD q1 case requires hash reporting without RSS and accepted
  `HASH_CONFIG` command 2.  Split and packed q2 require RSS plus hash reporting
  and accepted `RSS_CONFIG` command 1.  All three require real receive hash
  metadata, guest-side mbuf consumption, and device-specific
  indirect/event-index evidence for the actual ring layout.  They remain
  `pending` until a rebuilt guest runs them; no rootless result is promoted to
  live evidence.
- Rootless verification passes the 15-module 5BSD VirtIO build, the normal and
  `DEV_NETMAP` `if_vtnet.ko` kernel `-Werror` builds, the 218-entry independent
  requirements/activation validators, the orchestration self-tests, and the
  host helper/parser self-tests.  Comparison with pinned Linux commit
  `1590cf0329716306e948a8fc29f1d3ee87d3989f` confirmed the header selection,
  RSS and hash command shapes, configuration timing, and command-failure
  fallback.  A follow-up completed the guest-side standard surface for
  extension-aware IPv6 report types 7 through 9, mapping them to FreeBSD's
  existing `_EX` mbuf RSS types.  bhyve continues to advertise only the six
  basic types because those are the algorithms its device model computes.

#### Independent one-pair hash configuration follow-up

The host-side topology review found that bhyve previously created a control
virtqueue only when more than one RX/TX pair was configured.  That coupling
was correct for MQ and RSS but not for `HASH_REPORT`: VirtIO 1.4 defines the
independent `HASH_CONFIG` command for a one-pair device.  Modern q1 net devices
now expose queues 0/1 plus control queue 2 and advertise `CTRL_VQ` with
`HASH_REPORT`; MQ and RSS remain restricted to configurations with multiple
pairs.  Legacy q1 retains its historical two-queue topology and does not
advertise these modern high feature bits.

Control scheduling, selective queue reset, resume discovery, and TX/control
fairness now test actual control-queue presence rather than inferring it from
the pair count.  The host unit suite independently proves modern q1, modern
q2, and legacy queue/feature topologies and sends a real q1 `HASH_CONFIG`
through control queue 2 without MQ or RSS.  All 49 virtio-net ATF cases pass.
The complete rootless VirtIO release gate also passes, including the
1,195,896-check ring model, all device harnesses, host helper/parser controls,
the 196-entry nested-VMX requirements ledger, and 147 ASan/UBSan nested-state
cases.  Live q1/q2 split/packed evidence still requires a rebuilt 5BSD guest
and remains pending in the activation ledger.

### 2026-08-01 virtio-SCSI event and state review follow-up

The post-network rotating review revisited the production CTL event source,
event queue, request-worker ownership, selective reset, guest suspend, and
checkpoint paths.  No new high- or medium-severity defect was found.  The CTL
callback is queue-bounded and level-triggered, retains source records while
the common lifecycle fence is closed, and drains guest descriptors only after
the final resume owner releases that fence.  Full reset deliberately discards
pre-ready source history because guest discovery observes current inventory;
event-queue reset and restore instead force loss-aware rediscovery.

The review also confirmed that request queues use a single bounded ownership
deadline, selective reset cannot publish a stale CTL completion, and portable
restore validates queue shape plus CTL inventory before publication.  These
claims remain backed by the event ordering/saturation, malformed-record,
lifecycle-fence, multiqueue rollback, and transactional snapshot harnesses.
The live active-I/O checkpoint lane remains pending root execution and was not
promoted by this source review.

### 2026-08-01 virtio-console lifecycle and state review follow-up

The console review traced every port and socket object through accept,
read/write readiness, disconnect, queue reset, device reset, guest suspend,
checkpoint pause, restore, and destruction.  No new high- or medium-severity
defect was found.  Host output is bounded and retains partial writes; stale
read and write callbacks are rejected by connection-descriptor identity; and
destruction synchronously retires all callback registrations before freeing
their persistent port object.  Selective receive-queue reset disables the
external read source, while resume explicitly rearms descriptors which were
available before the lifecycle fence.

The versioned snapshot validates negotiated features, port topology, port and
listener identities, and multiport announcement ordering before publishing
state.  A live host connection or pending host byte stream is intentionally
rejected because neither is portable.  Consequently, reconnectable active
port migration is still a roadmap item rather than an implemented claim; the
existing negative checkpoint policy and its unit tests are correct for the
current backend contract.

### 2026-08-01 virtio-9P lifecycle and state review follow-up

The 9P review traced lib9p request ownership across synchronous and worker
completion, full reset, selective queue reset, suspend, and checkpoint.  No
new high- or medium-severity defect was found.  Per-request queue-generation
tokens prevent stale callbacks from publishing into a reset ring, the last
asynchronous owner completes selective reset exactly once, and full reset
serializes connection replacement while lib9p drains its worker callbacks.
The request callback's response-vector copy is bounded by lib9p's documented
fixed `L9P_MAX_IOV` transport contract.

Checkpoint state is little-endian and transactional, and validates the export
path, root device/inode identity, read-only policy, mount tag, protocol
version, and negotiated sizes.  Active requests and lib9p fids are
intentionally rejected because current fids retain backend-private host
descriptors and credentials.  Portable active-fid reconstruction and backend
restart/reconnect therefore remain pending features; neither is claimed by
the current save-state implementation.

### 2026-08-01 virtio-input lifecycle and state review follow-up

The input review found no new high- or medium-severity issue.  Host event
dispatch is bounded, complete evdev frames are published atomically, oversized
or overrun frames generate the standard `SYN_DROPPED` resynchronization
sequence, and inactive/reset queues drain stale host input instead of carrying
it into a later queue incarnation.  Selective reset and suspend discard only
incomplete frames; status-queue failures still retire every guest descriptor.

Snapshot version 2 stores a pointer-free partial frame and resynchronization
state, validates the complete cached configuration response and evdev
path/device identity before publication.  A later current-only-format cleanup
removed the unreleased version-1 compatibility decoder.
The focused harness rebuilt with `-Werror` and all 26 cases passed.  Dynamic
host capability-change notification, multiple simultaneous input devices,
and live packed/checkpoint qualification remain pending roadmap coverage.

### 2026-08-01 virtio-vsock checkpoint rollback review follow-up

The provider and device-model review found and fixed a failed-checkpoint
rollback defect in the kernel-backed transport.  A failed provider `FREEZE`
left the private lifecycle fence asserted, so the nominal rollback could not
rearm host sources.  A malformed freeze reply also ignored a failing `THAW`,
which could leave the provider frozen while the source VM continued without
declaring the device failed.

Rollback now restores the private fence to the independently negotiated guest
suspend state and rearms sources only when that state permits it.  A malformed
reply records the provider as frozen until `THAW` succeeds; a failed thaw marks
the backend failed and raises `DEVICE_NEEDS_RESET` instead of silently
continuing.  A successful provider reset clears the frozen state explicitly.
Focused tests cover direct freeze failure, malformed reply with successful
rollback, and malformed reply with thaw failure.  The rebuilt device-model
suite passes all 98 cases.  Active-connection portable migration and backend
reconstruction remain pending; the present snapshot contract continues to
require an empty connection table.

### 2026-08-01 VirtIO-IOMMU and ACCESS_PLATFORM review follow-up

The translated-DMA review traced topology discovery, endpoint binding,
request and event queues, attach/detach domain lifetime, MAP/UNMAP,
permission checks, fault delivery, reset deferral, queue-ring revalidation,
and phased checkpoint restore.  The behavior agrees with VirtIO 1.4 section
5.13 and the pinned Linux and QEMU references: moving an endpoint destroys an
empty old domain, UNMAP removes only complete mappings, unattached endpoints
fail closed unless configured for bypass, and revocation waits for every
accepted endpoint DMA lease without inventing a nonstandard wire status.

The production build exposed a missing direct include in
`virtio_iommu_queue.c`: the queue boundary used the state's storage-overlap
API without including `virtio_iommu_state.h`.  Target-only harness
composition had supplied the declaration indirectly.  The dependency is now
explicit, and coherent bhyve builds pass with and without snapshot support.
The snapshot-enabled local build must use the rebuilt source-world headers
and `libvmmapi`; otherwise an installed pre-upgrade ABI naturally lacks the
new CPU compatibility entry point.

The state regression suite now removes three mappings in one UNMAP while
running under AddressSanitizer, proving compaction clears exactly the vacated
allocation rather than crossing its bound.  The complete rootless VirtIO
gate passes again, including the independent requirement validators,
split/packed queue models, all device harnesses, and 1,195,896 exhaustive ring
checks.  Live Linux VIOT discovery, split and packed translated endpoint I/O,
fault recovery, and active checkpoint remain pending in the activation
ledger.  Stock 5BSD presently has no VirtIO-IOMMU guest driver, so that side
requires the planned driver before it can become live evidence.

### 2026-08-01 suspend, administration, and shared-memory review follow-up

The common lifecycle review traced guest-requested suspend, checkpoint pause,
selective and full reset, failed drain rollback, deferred configuration
notification, and nested administration-queue ownership.  No new high- or
medium-severity defect was found.  `VIRTIO_F_SUSPEND` is exposed only when a
device supplies both lifecycle callbacks; completion fences all queues before
the backend drains, reports `SUSPEND=1/DRIVER_OK=0` only after every accepted
buffer is returned, and reports `DEVICE_NEEDS_RESET` on either suspend or
resume failure.  Administration queues share that fence and retain independent
ownership depths for overlapping guest suspend and host checkpoint operations.

Shared-memory capability construction is permanently sealed on the first
status access, validates each 64-bit range against its containing BAR, rejects
duplicate IDs, and records the exact immutable layout in the machine-topology
seal.  Runtime backing replacement is permitted only behind reset or quiesce;
direct aliases must resolve to identical bytes and access policy, while
callback aliases fail closed because their identity cannot be proven.  BAR
access is width-bounded and disabled throughout reset, suspend, and checkpoint
publication.  Existing sanitizer tests cover boundary accesses, read-only and
callback backings, failed callbacks, lifecycle revocation, alias ordering, and
restore-layout mismatch.

The administration controller independently covers short command structures,
zero-filled missing input, truncated output, descriptor direction and ordering,
queue-local concurrency, saturation, reset, and transactional versioned state.
No production device advertises `VIRTIO_F_ADMIN_VQ`: live Linux qualification
remains blocked on a real SR-IOV PF/VF owner and its device-group lifecycle,
which prevents the tested common machinery from being mistaken for a shipping
guest-visible feature.

### 2026-08-02 doubled kernel/private review: guest suspend rollback

The independent post-private kernel replay compared the FreeBSD PCI and MMIO
guest suspend paths with VirtIO 1.4 section 3.4 and the bhyve device status
machine.  Cumulative status writes are correct: the device owns clearing
`DRIVER_OK` after suspend and clearing `SUSPEND` after the driver reasserts
`DRIVER_OK`.  The failure rollback was not correct.  Both transports resumed
their function child immediately after any timeout or `NEEDS_RESET`, including
when the final status sample showed an actually suspended or indeterminate
device.  Network and block resume paths can enqueue work immediately, so this
could expose buffers to a device for which normal operation was still
forbidden.

The final paths use one shared, independently tested status classifier with
failure precedence.  A device which remained running reopens the child.  A
device which completed suspend at the deadline boundary must complete the
standard resume handshake first.  `NEEDS_RESET`, `FAILED`, an indeterminate
transition, or a failed transport rollback leaves the function child fenced;
an otherwise unclassified protocol failure sets driver `FAILED`.  Bhyve now
accepts the cumulative driver-owned `FAILED` bit while suspended and refuses
to interpret `FAILED|DRIVER_OK` as a resume request.  The one-second deadline
and rollback policy are inventoried as private contract 78, while the
normative behavior is requirement 225 with a pending rebuilt-5BSD live
fault-injection disposition.

Focused PCI-device-model and guest-contract ATF cases pass, the PCI kernel
module builds with warnings as errors, the modern-MMIO object cross-builds
warning-clean for arm64, and the complete requirement and private-interface
validators pass with 225 requirements, 125 activation claims, and 78 private
contracts.  Live PCI/MMIO timeout, `NEEDS_RESET`, child-resume-failure, and
exact completion-boundary injection remain root qualification gates.

The final independent sanitizer replay also covered the full device harness
under AddressSanitizer/UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer and ThreadSanitizer.  The
first ThreadSanitizer run exposed a scheduler-dependent assertion in the block
reset test: a completion thread could acquire the deliberately dropped device
mutex before the cancellation mock observed it.  The production cancellation
path was correct; the test now uses an explicit condition-variable barrier to
observe the unlocked interval before permitting completion.  The focused ATF
case builds warning-clean and passes, and the complete ThreadSanitizer replay
then completed with zero harness failures.

### 2026-08-01 packed-ring publication and portability review follow-up

The packed-ring pass compared descriptor acquisition, indirect tables, used
publication, event suppression, wrap arithmetic, queue reset, and saved cursor
state with VirtIO 1.4 sections 2.8 through 2.8.14 and the pinned Linux and QEMU
implementations.  No new high- or medium-severity defect was found.  The device
acquires ownership from the head flags before reading descriptor payload,
publishes length and buffer ID before a release store transfers ownership, and
publishes grouped buffers tail-to-head so a polling driver cannot observe a
partial multi-buffer request.  Interrupt and kick suppression use an explicit
full barrier across the publish/recheck race.  Queue-part alignment is checked
at enable time, and queue-ring translations are replaced only after one stable
IOMMU generation spans the entire mapping transaction.

VirtIO 1.4 defines `WRITE` in a used packed descriptor as evidence that the
device wrote any part of the complete buffer, rather than a copy of the
available head's direction.  The implementation already derived that flag
from the nonzero used length.  A new independent regression now proves the
previously uncovered zero-byte half of the rule: a writable available buffer
completed without data has zero length and clears `WRITE`.  The complete
ASan/UBSan rootless gate passes, including 607 core checks and 1,195,896
exhaustive split/packed cursor and event comparisons.  Rebuilt Linux and 5BSD
live qualification across every opted-in device remains an activation gate,
not a claim inferred from the unit model.

### 2026-08-01 balloon optional-feature review follow-up

The balloon pass compared the complete optional queue surface with VirtIO 1.4
section 5.5 and the pinned Linux and QEMU implementations.  No new high- or
medium-severity defect was found.  Fixed queue indices remain discoverable
only when their defining features are offered, intervening optional queues
report size zero, statistics retains at most one driver-readable chain, and
selective reset revokes that ownership without reconstructing a host token.
Free-page hinting accepts the Linux command-plus-pages shape, rejects malformed
command framing, ignores stale command IDs, and reaches DONE only after the
driver's STOP acknowledgement.  Reporting preserves poison bytes when
PAGE_POISON is negotiated and otherwise treats host discard as an optional
optimization.

Inflate, deflate, reset, and restore keep the guest-PFN bitmap synchronized
with architecture-neutral discard/undiscard side effects, including rollback
and a persistent incomplete-restore latch when compensation cannot be proven.
The state is fixed-width and pointer-free; queue ownership is drained instead
of serialized.  Deflate-on-OOM, statistics, hinting, reporting, poison, packed
rings, active checkpoint, and rebuilt-5BSD page-poison/statistics activation
remain separate live gates in the qualification profile rather than being
promoted by this rootless review.

### 2026-08-01 provisional-device lifecycle review follow-up

The GPU, virtio-fs, memory, RTC, and sound implementations were reviewed again
with the lifecycle, portability, and test-independence lenses.  The GPU cursor
renderer cannot underflow its crop arithmetic: command processing and restore
both reject hotspots outside the fixed 64-by-64 source before publication, and
the renderer rejects an off-screen destination before framebuffer addressing.
Blob BAR reads and writes accept only PCI widths, convert values explicitly at
the little-endian boundary, and hold the common DMA-domain lease across the
state-locked backing copy.  GPU restore revalidates every guest backing extent
through the destination DMA view before publishing retained resources.

The virtio-fs request path remains event-driven and bounded.  Cancellation,
selective reset, backend disconnect, stale reply retirement, quiesce, thaw,
backend identity, and rollback are explicit transactions.  Its production
read-only backend deliberately refuses state transfer while non-root lookup or
open-handle objects exist; active-FID reconstruction is therefore a recorded
qualification limitation rather than silently incomplete migration.

Virtio-mem validates address, block, region, request, and bitmap arithmetic at
construction and restore, keeps device reset distinct from system reset, and
uses compensating platform operations for partial restore failure.  Its
independent four-block model covers every bitmap and contiguous request range.
The RTC uses one nonblocking absolute timer with clock-step cancellation,
covers forward and backward discontinuities including the arm-time window,
and stores no host timer or sampled clock state.  Sound serializes lifecycle
and asynchronous claims, completes retained data before RELEASE tears down the
backend, fences callbacks through return, and reconstructs or rolls back the
backend lifecycle during restore.  No new high- or medium-severity correctness
issue was found in this pass.  The remaining gaps are the manifest-recorded
live Linux, rebuilt-5BSD where a driver exists, packed-ring, ACCESS_PLATFORM,
active-checkpoint, presentation/audio-backend, and long-soak gates.

The final operational review found that the portable, Intel nested, and OSS

### 2026-08-01 VirtIO PMEM foundation review

VirtIO PMEM device 27 was selected as the next high-value device because the
local VirtIO 1.4 CS01, pinned Linux driver ABI, and pinned QEMU device model all
define a small interface with a demanding persistence boundary.  The new code
is intentionally unadvertised.  Its independent oracle covers the device and
queue IDs, feature zero, shared-memory region zero, exact 16-byte
configuration, four-byte FLUSH request, and literal zero/minus-one response.
The protocol decoder rejects truncated or aliased storage before invoking the
persistence callback and writes only the documented response length.

The first boundary review found and fixed an exclusive-end arithmetic mistake:
a one-byte region beginning at `UINT64_MAX` is representable, so validation now
checks the last addressed byte while still rejecting a two-byte range there.
The persistence slice opens only a non-symlink regular file, takes a
nonblocking exclusive lock, maps it shared, and retains runtime-only device,
inode, and size identity.  FLUSH revalidates that identity, performs a
synchronous mapping flush followed by file synchronization, and reports any
failure as the specification's minus one.  Focused Werror tests cover the top
address, competing devices, empty and resized files, durable data visibility,
callback integration, malformed requests, and transactional alias rejection.

At this foundation checkpoint this was not yet a guest-visible PMEM device.
The then-next implementation gates were
an event-driven PCI flush worker and completion wakeup,
device-memory placement, a portable backend identity manifest, explicit
checkpoint durability and rollback policy, DTrace/rate-limited diagnostics,
and Linux split/packed live qualification.  QEMU currently normalizes a flush
failure to positive one, while VirtIO 1.4 requires minus one; bhyve follows the
normative specification and records that comparison rather than copying it.

The second lifecycle pass added the bounded FIFO owner ledger that the future
worker will consume.  Admission closes atomically before pause or reset while
already-owned jobs remain acquirable for event-driven drain.  Only one backend
flush is active, duplicate guest tokens and capacity overflow fail closed,
completion requires the exact token and reset epoch, and destruction and an
ordinary synchronous reset refuse live owners.  Reset epoch rollover occurs
only after the ownership count reaches zero, so wrapping to one cannot alias a
live old owner; reset completed under suspend leaves admission closed until an
explicit resume.  Focused Werror and ASan/UBSan lifecycle tests cover FIFO
wrap, backpressure, pause/drain, token reuse across reset, stale completion,
busy destruction, and suspended reset.

The contention follow-up starts four producers at one barrier and admits 64
unique owners without sleeps, then proves every token is returned exactly once.
It also removed a reference-derived limit: QEMU's choice of a 128-entry PMEM
queue is not a VirtIO requirement, so the generic ledger now accepts any
caller-selected capacity through the modern transport's documented 32768-entry
maximum.  The eventual PCI device must advertise its queue size explicitly and
test that boundary rather than inheriting a reference implementation constant.

The third pass added the actual dedicated persistence worker.  Submission
transfers ownership into the ledger and signals a condition variable; the
worker serially acquires, flushes, invokes the exact completion callback while
ownership remains active, releases ledger ownership after publication, and
only then wakes lifecycle waiters.  Pause, reset, and
destroy share one monotonic deadline and never poll.  A blocked backend times
out with admission still closed, can finish later, and can then be drained or
resumed without losing its guest token.  Controlled tests prove FIFO callback
ordering, flush-error publication exactly once, bounded blocked-backend pause,
reset epoch rotation, and a reset that intentionally remains suspended.  At
this worker checkpoint it remained unreachable from guests until the PCI
descriptor/interrupt composition was completed in the following pass.

The fourth pass completed that composition as the modern-only `virtio-pmem`
PCI device.  Device 27 publishes its exact backing through shared-memory
region zero when feature zero is negotiated and otherwise reports the same
range through the mandatory physical-address configuration fallback; the
shared-memory configuration is canonically all zeroes.
Every shared-memory BAR access and queue notification is serialized by the
common VirtIO lock, so writes completed before a FLUSH notification precede
the worker's `msync(MS_SYNC)` and `fsync` persistence boundary.  Descriptor
parsing independently enforces readable-before-writable order, copies the
possibly fragmented four-byte request before retaining only the exact first
four writable bytes, detects aggregate-length overflow, and revalidates the
retained response shape at asynchronous completion.  Unknown commands return
literal minus one; malformed chains fail closed with NEEDS_RESET.

Reset and selective queue reset drain the sole bounded owner domain and rotate
its epoch before queue generation can be reused.  Suspend and checkpoint first
drain guest requests, then enqueue and drain a synthetic final FLUSH while the
common queue/shared-memory fence remains published.  A checkpoint failure
reopens admission for the still-running source, while reset or suspend failure
remains fail closed.  Snapshot state is fixed-width little-endian and carries
only magic, version, exact size, and a stable operator identity; the host path,
inode, descriptor, mapping, locks, thread, and guest pointers never enter the
stream.  Restore therefore treats the persistent file as an explicit external
backend and rejects a different declared identity or size.

Focused Werror ATF coverage now exercises protocol/configuration boundaries,
durability and competing opens, fragmented and malformed descriptor chains,
overflow, exact response publication, FIFO ownership and backpressure,
timeout rollback, stale epochs, worker ordering, and flush-error publication.
The snapshot-enabled bhyve build passes with DTrace enabled, and the new
`virtio:::pmem-flush` probe reports submit, lifecycle-submit, and completion
without exposing host pointers.  Linux and 5BSD split/packed live activation,
guest-visible DAX I/O, reset, suspend, and repeated checkpoint evidence remain
root-required qualification gates; no such result is claimed by the rootless
model tests.

The Linux qualification plumbing is now scheduled rather than merely planned.
`pmem-modern` and `pmem-packed-modern` bind Alpine's upstream VirtIO PMEM
driver, check the independently defined feature contract, write and flush a
fixed-offset marker, and compare the guest digest with the host backing file.
Both cases repeat that proof after device reset.  The checkpoint profile adds
split and packed PMEM cases and requires a fresh marker after restore while
the stable identity and exact capacity match.  These are root-required gates;
their presence in the lab plan is not recorded as a pass until executed on the
updated host.  Stock 5BSD has no PMEM guest driver, so its activation row stays
an explicit driver gap.

The fifth PMEM review rotated through normative descriptor semantics,
snapshot portability, test independence, and lab-contract consistency.  It
found that the queue helper rejected zero-length descriptors even though the
VirtIO descriptor formats permit semantically empty segments.  The helper now
ignores zero-byte readable and writable segments while still requiring an
aggregate four-byte request and four-byte response; a null pointer is accepted
only when its length is zero.  An independent fragmented-chain test proves
that empty segments neither consume response slots nor alter the exact used
length.

The actual `pci_vtpmem_snapshot` callback now runs under the sanitizer harness,
not merely the shared identity helper.  Its tests compare every emitted byte
with an independent little-endian fixture, validate and restore the same image
repeatedly, reject changed magic, version, capacity, and identity, and reject
every truncated record length.  Runtime size and identity remain unchanged
after every failed or validation-only parse.  The same pass found that the
optional-device soak case had gained PMEM but four coverage selectors had not;
the selectors now match the executable case, making all eleven soak contracts
covered and raising the complete qualification coverage count accordingly.
The snapshot-enabled Werror bhyve build, requirements validator, lab
self-tests, and full ASan/UBSan device harness pass after these corrections.
The split and packed live checkpoint lanes now also mutate the configured PMEM
identity and enlarge the backing by one page, require both preflight restores
to fail, restore the exact destination contract, and only then perform two
independent accepted restores of the same checkpoint.  Each destination must
advance the restored same-PID workload and pass the exact backing comparison.
Correlated DTrace evidence remains root-required rather than being inferred
from the model tests.

The sixth PMEM review concentrated on the full-reset timeout boundary.  The
common VirtIO callback has no error return and publishes status zero after the
device reset callback returns, so simply replacing the bounded wait with an
unbounded wait would make a stalled host filesystem hang a vCPU indefinitely.
Returning after the existing timeout was memory-safe—the worker has already
copied the request, touches only the host mapping, and the queue-generation
check makes its late callback discard-only—but it left worker admission closed
forever.  The owner ledger now supports a deferred reset: timeout keeps the old
epoch closed, the common reset advances the queue generation, and the last old
completion atomically advances (or safely wraps) the worker epoch and reopens
admission.  Selective reset, suspend, and checkpoint remain bounded and
fallible.  New ledger and worker tests hold the completion callback, prove the
reset timeout cannot admit a new token, release the callback, and require
automatic admission under a distinct epoch.  The full ASan/UBSan device
harness passes after this change.

## VirtIO-SCSI selective-reset ownership review

The SCSI lifecycle pass found a common-queue ownership leak in selective
request-queue reset.  A request that had been removed from the available ring
but had not yet been submitted to CTL was recycled directly into the
device-private free list.  That cleared the saved `vi_req` without retiring
it through the common virtqueue layer, so a packed-ring descriptor owner and
an ACCESS_PLATFORM DMA lease could survive the reset even though the old
queue incarnation would never publish a used entry.

Selective reset now calls `vq_discard_req()` while holding the same
publication mutex used by concurrent request completions, and only then
recycles the SCSI request object.  It deliberately does not write the used
ring.  The regression constructs an outstanding common request, verifies that
discard observes the owner before it is cleared, verifies the queue mutex is
held, and verifies that no completion is published.  Split and packed queues
therefore share the same retirement path, including translated-DMA release.

Full device reset intentionally remains different.  CTL receives the guest
iovecs directly and may still be reading or writing them while its ioctl is in
progress.  A full reset therefore waits for every active CTL command before
returning `VIRTIO_SCSI_S_RESET` for consumed but unsubmitted requests and
allowing the common transport to reset guest-visible queue state.  Replacing
that wait with a timeout would require a real CTL cancellation/ownership
protocol; merely generation-fencing the eventual used-ring completion would
not prevent late payload DMA into guest memory.  Selective reset retains its
bounded failure behavior: on timeout the old incarnation stays fenced and the
common transport requires a full reset.

The same pass rechecked the device-wide monotonic checkpoint deadline,
rollback of partially acquired queue owners, destination-local CTL event
subscription, loss-aware rescan after restore, fixed-width configuration
encoding, and the bounded opaque CTL inventory identity.  No second
actionable rootless defect was found in those paths.  The focused SCSI ATF
suite, snapshot-enabled Werror bhyve build, and full ASan/UBSan device harness
pass with the ownership regression.  Active-command checkpoint, CTL identity
change rejection, event overflow/rescan, multiqueue activation, packed rings,
and translated DMA remain explicit Linux and 5BSD live qualification gates;
they are not inferred from the harness.

## VirtIO-console control-message validation follow-up

A fresh console pass found that the driver-to-device control path decoded the
first complete eight-byte header even when the descriptor chain contained
trailing bytes.  In this direction the VirtIO console protocol defines only
the fixed control header; payload belongs to device-to-driver events such as
`PORT_NAME`.  Accepting a valid prefix made malformed guest input capable of
changing DEVICE_READY or PORT_READY lifecycle state.

The decoder now checks the complete iovec aggregate before copying or decoding
any field.  Exactly eight bytes are required.  Fragmentation and zero-length
descriptor segments remain valid when their aggregate is exact, while short,
overflowed, and oversized messages fail without changing readiness.  The
independent control test covers each of those shapes.  All console ATF cases
and the snapshot-enabled Werror bhyve build pass after the change.

The reconnect and migration boundary remains explicit: listeners are
reconstructible, but an accepted host stream and its pending bytes are not a
portable socket protocol.  Checkpoint therefore fails with `EBUSY` while a
connection is active instead of serializing a host descriptor or silently
dropping source data.  Active-port migration needs a versioned reconnectable
proxy/backend contract before that gate can honestly be relaxed; the current
strict policy is retained as a release-visible limitation rather than hidden
by an unsafe one-off.

## VirtIO-input status framing and lifecycle follow-up

The input-device review re-traced host-event staging, loss recovery,
selective event-queue reset, suspend, snapshot validation, and the reverse
status path.  A guest status chain was previously accepted once its first
eight bytes formed a `virtio_input_event`; trailing readable bytes were
silently ignored before the event was written to the host evdev descriptor.
The production path now requires an overflow-safe exact aggregate size of
eight bytes.  Fragmented events remain valid, while short, overlong, wrongly
directed, and invalid chains complete without reaching the host device.

The event queue deliberately has a different rule: each device-writable
buffer may be larger than one event, and bhyve publishes an eight-byte used
length.  Keeping those two rules separate avoids imposing the status
message's exact-size requirement on guest receive capacity.  The focused ATF
suite now includes an overlong status-chain regression in addition to short,
NULL, direction, scatter/gather, ordering, loss-resynchronization, reset,
suspend, and atomic snapshot cases.  The complete input ATF case list and a
snapshot-enabled `-Werror` bhyve build pass after the change.

## Kernel-vsock checkpoint admission follow-up

The userspace and kernel bhyve backends were re-traced through guest suspend,
checkpoint pause, backend identity validation, feature reconstruction, reset,
queue-local reset, callback rearming, and failed-resume retry.  The bhyve
device model's empty-backend checkpoint boundary remains intentional: active
Unix connections and buffered userspace relay state are rejected, while the
kernel provider must report no queued packets or CID-scoped AF_VSOCK
connections under its checkpoint fence.

The provider FREEZE ioctl had an admission-order defect.  It waited for
existing read/write copies before setting `frozen`; every sleep released the
domain mutex, allowing sustained VMM traffic to replace a completing copy
with a new one.  Each wake also restarted a relative timeout.  FREEZE now
publishes the provider fence before waiting, wakes blocked participants so
they observe it, and uses one absolute thirty-second deadline.  An interrupted,
timed-out, or busy checkpoint restores the prior admission state and wakes
provider and socket waiters.  Repeated FREEZE on an already frozen provider
remains idempotent.

The kernel module, root ATF binary, and complete rootless bhyve vsock-device
case list compile or pass with the change.  The installed-kernel
`kernel_transport_checkpoint_fence` case now additionally proves that an
`EBUSY` checkpoint reopens POLLOUT; running that case requires the rebuilt
kernel and root and remains in the live qualification queue.
