### 2026-08-02 — second kernel replay: console completion ownership

The destructor-first guest-driver pass found that the FreeBSD VirtIO-console
control task classified a used length outside its published 128-byte buffer as
malformed but then zeroed and republished that same buffer.  A faulty device
could therefore produce an unbounded completion/task/log loop.  The final
driver frees the one locally dequeued buffer, latches its failed state, stops
the device to revoke every remaining posted DMA buffer, and leaves interrupts
disabled.  It also rechecks detach and failure after the control processor
drops and reacquires the child mutex, so a buffer cannot be published into a
queue which detach reset in that interval.  The independent length oracle and
the console module's warnings-as-errors build pass.  A rebuilt-5BSD malformed
device lane remains a live qualification gate.

### 2026-08-02 — second kernel/private replay: block deferred-DMA owner

The reverse block-driver trace found an owner outside both the software queues
and every virtqueue: a request retained by an asynchronous busdma callback.
The old suspend predicate could report quiescence while that callback was
still able to publish a descriptor, and detach could proceed toward DMA-tag,
request-pool, and mutex destruction without explicitly draining it.  Detach
now closes callback admission, waits for the retained callback, and makes that
callback unload its mapping and return the request to the software queue
without device publication.  Suspend includes the same retained-owner bit in
its existing absolute deadline, and the callback wakes both suspend and
detach after ownership is returned.  The no-deadline detach wait is recorded
as private ownership policy rather than a VirtIO timeout: safely bounding it
would require a cancellable busdma contract.  The private ledger and source
gate pin the predicate and rollback ordering, and `virtio_blk.ko` builds with
kernel `-Werror`; injected deferred-callback suspend/detach remains a live
kernel test gate.

### 2026-08-02 — second kernel replay: RTC asynchronous failure ownership

The RTC guest-driver replay found that malformed alarm completions and alarm
buffer replenishment failures only latched an internal failed bit.  With no
synchronous request in flight, no thread performed the reset, so request and
alarm descriptors could remain published to a device which the driver had
already declared unusable.  The interrupt path now only closes admission and
schedules the existing task; task context performs a common full device stop,
disables both queues, drains every device-owned descriptor, and wakes any
stack-backed synchronous request owner.  Synchronous timeout and validation
failures use the same helper, and an alarm follow-up read which returns a
protocol error also performs the drain directly from task context.  The RTC
module builds with kernel `-Werror`.  A rebuilt-5BSD malformed-alarm injection
lane remains the live qualification gate.

The final-source replay then closed the detach/task composition race in that
change: because parent interrupt teardown follows child detach, a late alarm
interrupt could otherwise enqueue the failure task after detach had drained
it.  The detach flag is now an admission fence checked under the interrupt's
queue mutex before any dequeue or task publication; an interrupt already past
that fence necessarily finishes before detach can acquire the same mutex and
begin its task drain.  The source gate pins both halves of this ordering.

### 2026-08-02 — second kernel replay: input failure reclamation

The input guest driver had the same logical-failure versus DMA-ownership gap:
an invalid event, invalid status completion, or event-buffer replenishment
failure set `failed`, but other writable event buffers remained posted.  The
interrupt handlers now close admission and enqueue one retained failure task;
that task disables both queues, performs the full reset, drains every posted
event and status descriptor, and releases status-slot ownership.  Detach sets
its admission fence first and drains the task before its own reset and mutex
destruction.  `virtio_input.ko` builds with kernel `-Werror`; malformed live
device injection on a rebuilt 5BSD image remains the promotion gate.

### 2026-08-02 — consumer-led private inventory: block dump polling

The second non-standard inventory, starting from the block dump callbacks
rather than the existing ledger, found one undocumented wait policy.  Crash
dump I/O intentionally cannot depend on scheduler-driven interrupts and uses
the dedicated preallocated request, so it drains preexisting requests and
then polls each dump completion without a deadline.  This can stall a dump if
the device never completes, but a local timeout would abandon device-owned DMA
and still could not complete the destination dump.  `VIRTIO-PRIVATE-079` now
records that tradeoff separately from normal I/O and suspend deadlines, and a
source gate pins queue quiescence before dump-request publication.

The same consumer-led pass found that the RTC alarm wire protocol was already
ledgered but its FreeBSD management mapping was not.  `alarm_time_ns` is now
classified as a privileged, private device sysctl in absolute UTC
nanoseconds, with zero meaning disable; its two counters are explicitly
read-only observations.  `VIRTIO-PRIVATE-080` records serialization and
rollback: the cached deadline changes only after an exact successful device
response, while a failed write preserves the previous value.

### 2026-08-02 — doubled INIT/SIPI and withheld-MTF boundary review

The next forward and reverse kernel passes traced virtual INIT/SIPI from the

### 2026-08-02 — coordinator-owned startup provenance

The common event coordinator now owns one startup-event state per vCPU under
its existing entry spin lock.  Creation binds the state to the VM incarnation
and vCPU, reset transactionally advances both ingress and startup generations,
and destruction validates both owners.  Checkpoint begin holds the complete
selected lock set and rejects a pending startup value with `EBUSY`; this is a
deliberate loss-prevention gate until the portable checkpoint schema can carry
INIT/SIPI provenance.

The first kernel pass found a finite-identity leak in that rejection path: the
checkpoint transaction owner was allocated before pending startup state was
examined.  Repeated rejected checkpoints could therefore exhaust the global
nonreused owner domain without ever creating a transaction.  The allocator is
now spin-owned and is called only after caller credentials and every selected
startup state pass under their entry locks.  Transaction state is published
immediately before the value-layer begin, and every rejection clears staged
membership and any temporary entry state pointers.

The independent kernel pass then traced lock order from transaction lock to
ascending entry locks to the global owner spin lock, and searched every owner
allocator call for an inverse path.  None exists.  The independent private-
policy pass confirmed these owner IDs, storage cookies, receipts, locks, and
pending bits are transient kernel implementation state: they are absent from
ioctls, sysctls, tunables, DTrace records, guest features, and checkpoint wire
formats.  The nested validator now accepts 254 requirements and 90 private
contracts, the rootless model passes 167 cases, and both default and snapshot-
enabled `vmm.ko` builds pass with `-Werror`.

The review also rejected premature LAPIC wiring.  The existing rendezvous path
has no architecture decision or event-driven wake contract for a retained
receipt.  Publishing there without a commit consumer would strand ordinary
INIT/SIPI and permanently block checkpoints; immediately consuming would lose
the nested retry boundary.  The next slice must model and test explicit
APPLY-L0, REFLECT-L1, and RETAIN-AND-RETRY outcomes before production delivery
changes.  Nested INIT/SIPI and monitor-trap exiting remain withheld.

A second, reverse review of the consumer boundary found another unsafe shape
before it acquired callers.  Separate coordinator `peek` and `consume` calls
release the entry lock between selection and the external side effect.  A
newer INIT/SIPI can then invalidate the receipt after LAPIC or nested state is
already changed, leaving either a duplicate delivery or a permanently pending
value.  Those unused wrappers have been removed and the source validator
forbids their return.  The required replacement is a claim lease with exact
finish or abort semantics that preserves later publications behind the
claimed event.  This finding restarts the doubled review and remains part of
the withheld-feature gate.

### 2026-08-02 — exact startup claim ownership

The common startup value layer now has the missing external-side-effect
transaction.  Claim begin removes exactly the oldest pending value and issues
a nonreused credential bound to the VM owner, vCPU, state storage, claim
storage, and claim identity.  The coordinator then releases its spin lock, so
an architecture adapter may perform a rendezvous without spinning or polling.
New INIT/SIPI publications remain pending behind the active claim.

Finish consumes only the exact claim after an irrevocable side effect.  Abort
restores an older INIT unless a newer INIT already superseded it, and restores
an older SIPI only when no newer startup event exists.  Reset and checkpoint
reject active claims.  Cancellation closes new claims but permits the exact
owner to finish or abort; teardown drains active claims using the existing
sleepqueue predicate interlock before freeing coordinator storage.

Four additional rootless cases cover later publication behind a claim,
age-aware abort coalescing, copied/stale credentials, reset exclusion, and
overflow failure atomicity.  The nested model now passes 170 cases, while the
ledgers contain 255 requirements and 91 private contracts.  The default kernel
module builds with `-Werror`.  LAPIC publication, target-vCPU notification,
architecture decision, and Intel no-entry retry remain unconnected and are the
next reviewed boundary; no withheld feature was exposed.

The restarted final-source kernel traversal then found that claim completion
originally consumed a second event generation.  A publication could advance
an active claim to `UINT64_MAX`, after which both finish and abort returned
`EOVERFLOW` forever and teardown could not drain the claim.  Claim begin has
already invalidated every older receipt, so completion now releases the exact

must not; validation previously allowed INIT with that marker cleared even

generation exhaustion, validation, and coalescing, and commits live states

under spin ownership; the VM adapter preflights every target before publication
and performs every notification after the coordinator releases all entry
owners.  Because pending values live in the coordinator,
they survive return of an interrupted initiating stack and are claimed only

### 2026-08-02 — architectural INIT/SIPI value-plan boundary

The pinned Intel SDM revision 092 Table 12-1 and note 2, pinned Linux
7.2-rc4, and pinned QEMU 300438 comparison exposed an important boundary:
INIT is not a cold reset and SIPI is not another reset.  INIT preserves CR0
CD/NW, forces ET, clears the represented integer/control/debug/segment state,
and leaves several x87, vector, performance, time, and MSR domains unchanged.
SIPI changes only RIP and the CS startup vector state.  Linux implements the
same split and QEMU preserves its explicitly delimited INIT-unchanged region.

The new pointer-free `vmm_x86_init_state_plan()` and
`vmm_x86_sipi_state_plan()` therefore do not reuse bhyve's historical
userspace `vcpu_reset()` plus `spinup_ap()` sequence.  The old sequence keeps
its established CR0.NE Windows compatibility policy and its existing ABI.
The kernel-owned mode instead has independent hard-coded specification tests
for CR0 cache-bit preservation, the reset values, SIPI vector arithmetic, and
failure atomicity.  The plans deliberately exclude LAPIC reset, pending-event
clearing, TLB invalidation, wait-for-SIPI/resume, backend writes, and every
architecturally unchanged state domain.  Those operations are now an explicit
pending transactional Intel/AMD adapter gate (`NVMX-EVENT-050`) rather than
implicit side effects hidden inside a value helper.

Fresh rootless evidence is the 180-case model under both the ordinary build
and ASan+UBSan, the requirements/evidence/staging/policy validators, and
warnings-as-errors `vmm.ko` builds in both default and
`MK_BHYVE_SNAPSHOT=yes` configurations.  The default object tree is
`/tmp/nvmx-startup-default.Iw7JRx`; the snapshot object tree is
`/tmp/nvmx-startup-snapshot2.6SctFT`.  An initial snapshot command which
overrode rather than appended the kernel CFLAGS was discarded; the recorded
snapshot result uses the supported make option and includes the snapshot
sources.

from the virtual APIC-base BSP property, not duplicate the current vCPU-zero
initialization convention.  The same private-boundary replay also rejected a
negative owner enum and overlapping policy/output storage which the original
value helper accepted.

Independent tests cover both owners, BSP and AP INIT outcomes, every wait
transition, immutable selection, negative and reserved values, unlocked use,
alias rejection, and byte-identical failure.  Production wiring remains gated
on the complete Intel and AMD transactional state adapters and target-context
live qualification.

publication back through LAPIC reset, translation invalidation, pending-event
clearing, backend descriptor/register writes, and capture.  It found that the
existing event restore operation cannot safely be used as rollback after a
clear: by design it rejects a nonempty destination so it never overwrites an
event that arrived after preflight.  `NVMX-EVENT-053` therefore fixes the
required order.  Every fallible backend mutation and its rollback precedes an

### 2026-08-03 — frozen-entry notification and doubled final-source review

The next kernel traversal found a notification race that the typed machine
adapter alone could not close.  `vcpu_notify_event()` intentionally performs
no wakeup for a FROZEN target, so a startup event published after an idle
dispatch observation but before RUNNING publication could otherwise remain
pending until an unrelated exit.  A new pointer-free runtime token captures
the coordinator owner, vCPU, generation, next and active claim identities,
pending event, SIPI vector, and active claim kind/vector under the per-vCPU
spin owner.  Exact validation after RUNNING publication returns `ESTALE` for a
different owner or vCPU and `EAGAIN` for same-owner mutable drift.  Active
claim fields are included because exact claim release does not advance the
event generation.  Capture and validation reject aliasing and malformed or
reserved values without mutating either owner or caller output.

The independent final-source replay then found that the coordinator wrapper
used the full readiness predicate during capture but only structural ingress
validation during check.  An unchanged event token could therefore validate
after ingress entered checkpoint quiesce or after coordinator cancellation.
Both sides now require the same uncancelled, OPEN-ingress readiness predicate;
`EBUSY` or `ECANCELED` forces the future entry consumer to unwind instead of
entering hardware across teardown or snapshot quiescence.

The common value layer also now models two-stage entry arbitration.  A
canonical lifecycle snapshot prioritizes rendezvous, suspend, reqidle, and
debugger work before machine dispatch.  When none is present it dispatches
before deciding whether an AP waits for SIPI, allowing pending INIT to reach
an already-waiting AP.  A CONSUMED result replays all predicates; IDLE waits
only when the captured wait predicate is set; RETAINED and nonwaiting IDLE
permit guest entry.  RETAINED cannot wait because running the guest is the
only guaranteed way to remove the live architectural blocker that retained
the claim.  Exhaustive tests cover all 32 lifecycle/wait combinations
against every typed dispatch result, plus malformed, alias, and
failure-atomic rejection.

Review Passes 41 and 42 and roadmap phases 33 and 34 capture the forward and
reverse notification/FPU analysis.  At the operator's request, Passes 43 and
44 plus roadmap phases 35 and 36 add another independent final-source kernel
review and a definition-first/consumer-first inventory of all non-SDM
behavior.  The executable validator requires every phase.  The second pass
must prove FROZEN/RUNNING and host/guest-FPU unwind, pre-entry interrupt timing,
bounded replay fairness, lock order, and teardown before production wiring.

NVMX-EVENT-143/144 and NVMX-PRIVATE-205/206 record these contracts.  Final
rootless evidence is clean: `vmm.ko` links with kernel `-Werror`; the validator
accepts 369 requirements, 206 non-standard interfaces, and 11 live groups;

pair checks.  No `vm_run()` consumer was added, both machine readiness
providers remain false, AMD remains `EOPNOTSUPP`, and Intel architectural apply
remains `ENOTSUP`.  Installed before/during/after-RUNNING race qualification is
therefore still a release gate rather than an inferred result.

### 2026-08-03 — doubled outer-owner kernel and non-standard review

Roadmap phases 56 through 59 and review Passes 64 through 67 now make the
entry-owner review four independent traversals.  The first kernel pass walks
forward from the admitted post-dispatch BOUND state through common critical

Those passes found three correctness defects in the dormant model.  First,
separately valid runtime and loop values could be combined into an impossible
outer lifetime.  Second, RUNNING with a nonzero entry history and CHECKED with
no entry history were accepted even though no operation can produce either
tuple.  Third, a zero-entry completion could claim RETURN_VMEXIT, falsely
asserting that hardware had returned an exit.  The owner now has exact
cross-member relations for BOUND, CRITICAL, GUEST_FPU, RUNNING, IN_GUEST,
RECHECK, RETURNABLE, REFROZEN, HOST_FPU, and COMPLETE.  Named operations
advance a complete local copy and publish it only after full validation;
retirement composes the owned backend disposition with final coordinator and
notification observations, publishes a disjoint result, and clears the owner
exactly once.

An independent exhaustive test enumerates every outer phase, runtime phase,
loop phase, zero/nonzero history, and disposition class and compares the
production validator with a separate reachability model.  Mechanical source
checks reject outer-phase writes outside the owner implementation and still
reject consumers in common `vm_run()`, VMX, or SVM.  Fresh evidence passes
296 rootless model cases and the same 296 cases under AddressSanitizer plus
UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer; the executable ledgers validate 383 requirements,
220 private/non-standard contracts, and 11 live-qualification groups; the
amd64 `vmm.ko` build passes with warnings as errors; and the scoped diff is
format-clean.  This is still dormant model evidence.  Production placement,

or advertised behavior changes.

The next actual-kernel traversal immediately refined that result rather than

without incrementing the entry count.  Software exit requires zero error;

other values to terminal error.  Final arbitration preserves the software

### 2026-08-03 — second machine-entry and non-standard activation review

The new doubled review starts from the presently inert `NULL` owner argument,

The review-runner portability replay also replaced a fragile pipeline-plus-

### 2026-08-04 — doubled kernel and non-standard seam replay

The review process now has an additional independent kernel-source replay and
a separate implementation-defined seam replay.  The kernel replay starts
from production PCI, DMA, interrupt, socket, VMM, snapshot, module, and MAC
entry points, then separately from cancellation, reset, suspend, restore, and
teardown.  The seam replay independently inventories bhyve-only configuration,
private protocols, checkpoint envelopes, provider/backend contracts, policy,
limits, retry/polling behavior, diagnostics, test hooks, and dormant
interfaces from both their definitions and consumers.  Neither may use a
passing standard conformance result as a substitute for a private-contract
proof; a correction restarts the final common and private passes.

This replay found one concrete common-path portability defect.  Legacy
`QueuePFN` layout derives aligned guest offsets, but a future translated DMA
implementation is not required to return a host pointer that is naturally
aligned for `struct vring_desc`, `struct vring_avail`, or `struct vring_used`.
The old code cast that pointer directly and could therefore publish invalid
typed pointers on a strict-alignment host.  `vi_vq_init()` now validates all
three typed addresses before publication; failure clears the queue and sets
`NEEDS_RESET`.  The independent legacy mapping test injects an intentionally
unaligned mapping and proves that no ring pointer or QueuePFN becomes live,
then proves a separate aligned mapping still initializes correctly.  This is
rootless source-level evidence; translated-DMA and strict-alignment live-host
qualification remain required.

The reverse setup replay also found that allocation failure for the split-ring
owner store took a shorter path than a DMA-map failure.  Both rejected setup
paths now use the same queue-clear transition: QueuePFN, allocation, pending
notification, ring pointers, and cursors are reset before `NEEDS_RESET` is
published.  The independent test begins with deliberately stale queue-visible
fields and a zero queue size that makes owner-store initialization fail; it
proves every field is cleared.  The normal, address/undefined, and thread
sanitizer rootless harnesses plus the strict bhyve and VMM builds remain
clean.  Installed translated-DMA, strict-alignment, and live guest coverage
remain separate qualification gates.

The second VMM-only pass traced the staged kernel-owned INIT/SIPI path from
the common frozen dispatcher and independently backward from every machine
entry instruction and no-entry return.  It confirmed that the common stack
owner is a value-only protocol, not yet a live ownership transfer: historical
`vm_run()` originally supplied `NULL`; the staged common caller now passes its
local owner through the ordinary L1 VMX and SVM loops.  Nested VMX still
rejects the owner before machine-state acquisition; VMX's frozen startup
adapter ends in an explicit `ENOTSUP`; and SVM has no startup dispatcher.
This is intentional staged behavior, not supported nested-startup execution.
The activation-completeness validator makes all remaining gates part of one
reviewed contract.  Any readiness change must first convert the cold/resumed/
hot nested VMX edges and every path-specific unwind, then replace structural
assertions with installed-kernel race and failure evidence.

### 2026-08-04 — startup-owner transfer boundary rechecked

The common `vm_run()` path was rechecked against the ordinary VMX, nested
VMX, and SVM machine-entry loops.  The common path currently enters the
critical section, restores guest FPU state, publishes `VCPU_RUNNING`, invokes
the backend, then refreezes, saves FPU state, and leaves the critical section.
Each backend has additional no-entry, initial-entry, handled re-entry, and
terminal-unwind edges.  Consequently, changing only the `vmmops_run()`
argument from `NULL` to a startup owner would either duplicate or omit one of
those state transitions; it is not a safe incremental activation.

The required production conversion is therefore one ownership transfer with
an exact, tested disposition for all of these edges: common pre-dispatch,
ordinary VMX no-entry and re-entry, cold/resumed/hot nested VMX no-entry and
unwind, SVM no-entry and re-entry, and the common terminal return.  The
transition must also preserve existing guest-MSR, descriptor, pmap/EPT, debug,
interrupt, and FPU ordering.  The first staged conversion now passes the
owner through the ordinary L1 VMX and SVM loops only.  Nested VMX still
rejects a non-NULL owner with `EOPNOTSUPP`, and public readiness stays false
until its cold/resumed/hot paths and installed-kernel Intel qualification are
complete.  This remains a deliberate release blocker, not an optional
compatibility fallback.

### 2026-08-04 — independent common-decoder and non-standard contract replay

The additional replay began at the compatibility-envelope and direct
device-decoder consumers rather than at feature producers.  It confirmed that
the checkpoint envelope, the modern device-local record, and the live modern
transport all use the same effective feature offer: negotiated features must
be a subset of the image's own offered word, and the saved offer must be a
subset of the destination offer.  Thus a feature-rich destination cannot make
an impossible source negotiation valid during a direct payload preflight.
The fixed-width BVC1 codec independently rejects malformed shape tails and
preserves caller output on decode failure; portable compatibility, PCI
checkpoint, and common-VirtIO model suites passed 7, 7, and 57 cases
respectively.

The non-standard replay also revalidated the private-interface ledger,
snapshot-portability structure, and nested-VMX requirement ledger.  The
machine-checked inventories now cover 82 VirtIO private contracts and 240
nested/private VMX contracts, while 228 VirtIO requirements remain mapped to
independent oracle-based tests.  No new source defect was found in this pass.
This is not live-device, installed-kernel, migration, translated-DMA, or
Intel nested-entry evidence; those remain explicit root-only qualification
gates.

The common VMS2 envelope and amd64 composition decoder were reviewed in both

The review found no implementation defect: the transaction decoder validates

### 2026-08-04 — checkpoint ingress and group-reopen double review

The architecture-neutral checkpoint ingress protocol was reviewed

The independent group-checkpoint test now proves that failed finish operations

### 2026-08-04 — startup-owner private-state and persistence review

The second non-standard review traced the proposed kernel-startup entry owner
from admission through each phase transition and searched every snapshot and

### 2026-08-04 — portable address-range replay

The second common-kernel replay found that three variable-length checkpoint
and startup-storage paths independently mixed `size_t` lengths with

only by accident: a future target may represent object lengths more widely
than object addresses.  The common VMM address-range helper now rejects a
non-empty length that cannot be represented by `uintptr_t`, validates the
last byte by subtraction, and tests overlap using ordered subtraction rather
than an end-address sum.  The public snapshot envelope deliberately reports
an invalid range as invalid; private alias guards conservatively treat it as
overlap and reject the operation.

handshake paths use that shared contract.  Boundary, alias/overflow, and
transactional handshake model cases were rebuilt and passed, as did the VMM
module under `-Werror`.  The nested requirements validator now checks for the
shared range contract instead of matching the former amd64-width-dependent
expression.  This is portable lifecycle hardening; it does not serialize an
address, change a device wire ABI, or claim live checkpoint qualification.

The portable startup entry-owner state machine was included in the replay as
well.  Its alias checks now use the same helper, so a non-standard owner
transition cannot retain an independent, width-dependent range rule.  The
rootless hardware-attempt/no-guest-entry and exact state-product models pass;
the real VMX path remains fail closed after the point at which nested private
residency could be acquired.

The Intel-private nested state helper now delegates its non-empty arithmetic
to that same common helper while preserving the private codec convention that
NULL and zero-length inputs do not themselves denote an alias.  The 32-bit
syntax portability gate was corrected to use the kernel's normal `sys`
include root, then passed for the nested state, checkpoint, and registry
codecs.  This confirms the checked address arithmetic is portable value-code
in both common and Intel-private layers; it is not evidence of hardware VMX

The AC non-standard-interface replay traced the amd64-only startup management

The event-state model test now exercises wrapping and null nonempty ranges;
the nested requirement validator makes all five private users, and those
negative cases, a permanent requirement.  The rootless nested VMM model was
rebuilt with undefined-behavior instrumentation after the change.  This is a
portable source/model correction, not a claim of live Intel VMX execution.

### 2026-08-04 — portable dirty-log value-contract review

The migration review now has a deliberately small, architecture-neutral
dirty-log value foundation.  It defines a 4 KiB *logical guest-physical*
unit, canonical byte/bit ordering, validated bitmap size, and a
non-wrapping generation value.  It does not inspect EPT, NPT, pmap state, a
host page size, native bitmap words, host pointers, or a device-specific
backend.  It also has no ioctl or claim that dirty tracking is active.

The first common-kernel pass found that representing a range's exclusive end
in `uint64_t` incorrectly rejected the valid final 4 KiB of the GPA space.
The validator now uses inclusive-end and subtraction arithmetic, so a range
may end exactly at 2^64 without permitting any wrapped GPA.  Independent
tests prove the top-of-space case, malformed/partial inputs, unmodified
outputs on rejection, canonical low-GPA/low-bit layout, and generation
overflow.  The focused ATF binary and `vmm.ko` build pass with `-Werror`.

This is only the first prerequisite for stop-and-copy dirty logging.  A
frozen memory-map transaction, backend collector contract, generation
invalidation, and root-only active-I/O/checkpoint qualification remain
required before an ABI or pre-copy capability can be exposed.

### 2026-08-04 — frozen-map dirty-log boundary review

The next common review isolated frozen-map semantics from both `vm_mem` and
hardware collection.  A map snapshot is now a bounded (by
`VM_MAX_MEMMAPS`), by-value, ascending list of logical GPA ranges plus only a
collectability bit.  It intentionally
does not carry a `vm_mem_map`, segment ID, object, protection, host address,
host page size, EPT/NPT entry, callback, or retained pointer.  A requested
range can span adjacent collectable entries; a gap returns `EFAULT`, while a
valid but uncollectable mapping returns `EOPNOTSUPP`.  This lets a later
frozen transaction reject MMIO and holes before it asks a backend to collect
anything.

The independent map model covers adjacency, holes, uncollectable mappings,
overlap, unsupported flags, and the final legal GPA page.  The review also
found and corrected a portability defect in the original common header: its
`UINT*_C` macros were available accidentally in one kernel build path but are
not provided by the freestanding kernel headers.  The shared interfaces now
use typed C integer literals and the VMM module builds with `-Werror`.
Neither helper enables dirty tracking nor establishes a public ABI; backend
collection, lifecycle invalidation, and live qualification remain withheld.

A second pass made the bounded-input guarantee executable.  A caller-supplied
entry count beyond `VM_MAX_MEMMAPS` is rejected before entries are read, and
the covering operation preserves that `E2BIG` result instead of collapsing it
to a generic malformed-input error.  The rootless model runner now discovers
both the range/bitmap and frozen-map ATF cases in ordinary and UBSan runs.

### 2026-08-04 — dirty-log collection-owner lifecycle review

The next common VMM pass adds only the portable lifecycle owner required by a
future collector.  It retains a logical tracked range, a caller-owned frozen
map generation, a nonwrapping dirty generation, and one immutable collection
ticket.  It does not retain a map pointer or accept EPT/NPT, pmap, host page,
backend, or userspace values.  Observation retains the dirty generation;
clear-after-publication advances it only on successful finish; abort retains
it.  Reset, map change, checkpoint abort, restore, destroy, and backend
detach will all use the same invalidation path and therefore revoke an active
ticket.

The first source/test replay found a real owner-state defect: the ticket was
compared with the tracking range rather than its narrower collection range.
The owner now retains and checks the exact collection range and mode.  A
second replay removed native-structure comparison from that check, rejects a
ticket output aliasing the owner, distinguishes malformed arguments from stale
tickets, validates private phase values, and makes identity exhaustion
permanently fail closed.  Rootless ATF tests cover observe versus clear,
failed/stale settlement, abort preservation, alias rejection, map-generation
drift, invalidation, and exhaustion.  The `vmm.ko` warning-as-error build and
ordinary rootless model pass.  Binding that owner to a real `vm_mem` map
generation, VMX/EPT and SVM/NPT collectors, an ABI, and live migration
qualification remained deliberately unimplemented at this review point.

### 2026-08-04 — common vm_mem generation/snapshot review

The common memory layer now owns the map-generation source and private owner
for the portable dirty-log transaction.  A successful map or actual unmap
advances a nonwrapping generation and revokes any active ticket; reset and
destroy revoke even when the system-memory map itself does not change.
Exhaustion disables only future dirty-log capture, never ordinary VM map
changes.  Under `mem_segs_lock`, the snapshot API returns a bounded,
ascending, by-value logical map with the common collectability bit and the
exact generation.  It rejects malformed internal map state, output aliases to
live memory state or to another output, no-map and insufficient-capacity
requests, and values that cannot be represented in the portable 64-bit GPA
contract.

The second common/non-standard replay found that the original header implied
that a frozen vCPU alone made this safe.  The real invariant is
`mem_segs_lock`; vCPU freezing is the higher-level collection lifecycle that
makes the snapshot generation retainable.  The API and implementation now say
that explicitly.  The same replay found that owner operations were incorrectly
permitted with a shared map lock; they now require the exclusive lifecycle
lock, while read-only map snapshots retain the shared-lock contract.  The
snapshot has no public ioctl, hardware collector, VMX/SVM type, host pointer
retention, or architecture-specific page-size assumption.  `vmm.ko`, the
ordinary model, UBSan model, requirements and non-standard-interface
validators pass.  A root-only test that exercises map mutation versus a frozen
dirty-log transaction, plus matched EPT/NPT collection, remains required
before this foundation can expose an ABI.

### 2026-08-04 — snapshot transaction invalidation review

Snapshot ioctls already freeze all vCPUs but had no connection to the new
private dirty-log transaction.  Kernel save and restore dispatch now revokes a
live ticket under the exclusive memory lifecycle lock and releases that lock
before invoking arbitrary architecture or device snapshot callbacks.  The
review found and corrected a side-effect error in the first version: a bad
snapshot selector would have revoked a ticket before returning `EINVAL`.
Selectors are now fully validated before the revocation boundary, preserving
the normal malformed-request no-change rule.

This is lifecycle fencing only.  It does not serialize a dirty-log record,
collect any hardware dirty bits, enable a feature, or change the public
snapshot ABI.  Root-only tests must still prove an active collection ticket is
rejected after save, restore, failed callback, reset, and map-change paths;
the eventual VMX/EPT and SVM/NPT collectors must be tested against the same
transaction contract.

### 2026-08-04 — nested-page dirty-bit boundary review

The second kernel/private-boundary review found that the existing pmap APIs
were unsuitable as a future dirty-log collector: `pmap_clear_modify()` works
by host physical page across mappings, while emulated EPT A/D uses write
permission as its apparent modified bit.  A narrow amd64-private
`pmap_guest_query_dirty()` seam now accepts only guest EPT/NPT pmaps with
hardware A/D, returns a by-value description of the actual 4 KiB, 2 MiB, or
1 GiB leaf, and rejects emulated A/D without changing caller output.  Clear
uses a compare-and-set against asynchronous hardware A/D updates and advances
the existing nested translation invalidation generation after success.

The helper intentionally does not report a dirty superpage as one 4 KiB page,
retain a pmap or VM pointer, expose a native bitmap, or enable a public
dirty-log or pre-copy interface.  Its caller must freeze relevant vCPUs before
clear; otherwise no API can make a stable write-generation claim.  The
configured amd64 kernel pmap object, `vmm.ko`, ordinary/UBSan model suites,
and requirement validators build/pass.  Root-only EPT/NPT tests for all leaf
sizes, emulated-A/D rejection, and clear/rewrite invalidation remain required
before this can be connected to the portable owner transaction.

The portable bitmap layer now has the paired
`vmm_dirty_log_bitmap_mark_range()` operation.  It validates an entire dirty
leaf and tracked range before mutation, clips their intersection, and marks
each canonical logical 4 KiB unit in low-GPA/low-bit order.  Independent
tests cover a clipped partial leaf, a 1 GiB leaf clipped to a small tracked
range, the final legal GPA page, and malformed inputs with byte-for-byte
unchanged bitmap output.  This is a value conversion only; it still neither
queries a pmap nor exposes dirty tracking.

### 2026-08-04 — backend ticket-fence review

The common dirty-log owner now exposes one read-only ticket check for a future
architecture backend.  It validates the active collection identity,
frozen-map generation, dirty generation, requested range, and mode without
mutating owner state.  This is the fence immediately before an EPT or NPT
collector observes or clears A/D bits: reset, map replacement, snapshot
cancellation, or a competing collection makes the ticket stale and requires
the backend to do nothing.  The focused owner test covers a live ticket and
stale/null ticket rejection with byte-for-byte owner stability; malformed
arguments are `EINVAL` while revoked valid tickets are `ESTALE`; `vmm.ko`
builds with `-Werror`.

This deliberately does not add a common collector callback, public dirty-log
ABI, or pre-copy migration.  Those still require matched VMX/SVM backend
operations plus root-only leaf, race, and clear-after-publication evidence.

### 2026-08-04 — staged dirty-log observation review

The portable layer now has a small `vmm_dirty_log_collect()` value contract.
It first checks the immutable collection ticket, scans only abstract
guest-physical dirty leaves into a caller-owned staging bitmap, and copies
that bitmap to the result only after every query and range conversion succeeds.
The contract rejects stale tickets before calling a backend, aliases between
staging and result, malformed/uncovered leaves, and incorrect canonical bitmap
sizes.  It intentionally has no EPT/NPT/pmap dependency and no clear callback:
clearing A/D bits before the published observation is durable would make a
failed checkpoint lose write evidence.

Focused ordinary and UBSan model tests cover a full multi-leaf scan, a failed
second query, stale-ticket rejection without a backend call, malformed leaves,
and output/staging alias rejection.  The static requirement gate additionally
pins the staged-before-copy ordering and prevents an architecture-private or
clear operation from entering this common layer.  The VMM module builds with
`-Werror`.  A paired VMX/EPT and SVM/NPT clear transaction, its frozen-vCPU
live qualification, and any public dirty-log or migration ABI remain deferred.

The final review cycle now has two explicit independent terminal passes in
both review prompts.  Pass 35 rebuilds the final kernel and device lifecycle
from public entry points and from teardown paths without reusing the earlier

accepted inputs and consumers, including CLI and ioctl values, backend and
CID selection, checkpoint compatibility, limits, timeouts, tracing, and
test-only controls.  Each pass requires a positive and negative proof for
every private behavior and must restart the affected lifecycle, portability,
reference-comparison, and qualification passes after a correction.

The nested-VMX review has matching terminal phases for checkpoint/guest-memory
transaction replay and non-standard host-policy/resource-boundary replay.
The rootless validator now rejects a missing terminal phase, an unmapped
production nested source, or an incomplete private-interface ledger.  The
VirtIO validator similarly checks the doubled kernel/private phases, the
final-source replay record, independent test oracles, and the private

requirements and 271 nested private interfaces, and 228 VirtIO requirements
and 82 VirtIO private interfaces.

The independent dirty-log collector review also added a failure-atomicity

### 2026-08-04 — dirty-log collection-owner invariant replay

A fresh portability and private-contract replay found that the common
read-only ticket fence compared an incoming ticket with a collecting owner
without validating the owner's stored collection representation itself.  A
corrupted owner could therefore look current and supply an invalid range,
generation, or mode to a future architecture callback.  The fence now
requires a valid containing tracked/collection range, nonzero generations and
identity, and a defined collection mode before it accepts a matching ticket.
Malformed internal owner state is `EPROTO`; a normal invalidated or
non-collecting ticket remains `ESTALE`.

New direct negative coverage corrupts the mode, collection range, and map
generation of an otherwise matching owner and proves that check, finish, and
abort do not mutate it.  All owner and collector model cases pass, and
`vmm.ko` builds with and without `BHYVE_SNAPSHOT`.  The complete nested model
was then rerun and recorded `PASS nested-vmx cases=342`; its ASan/UBSan rerun
also recorded `PASS nested-vmx cases=342 sanitizers=address,undefined`.  This
strengthens the common transaction contract only; it does not expose dirty
logging, clear hardware A/D state, or qualify EPT/NPT collection without the
existing live gate.

### 2026-08-04 — dirty-log lifecycle representation replay

The ticket-fence correction was intentionally reviewed a second time from the
opposite direction: every public owner transition was checked for an implicit
trust of its phase field.  `enable`, `begin`, and `invalidate` could otherwise
consume a malformed but phase-labelled owner, even though a later ticket check
would reject it.  The common owner now validates the complete representation
before every transition: OFF and EXHAUSTED are canonical empty states,
TRACKING has exactly one valid tracked range and no collection state, and
COLLECTING has a valid contained range, nonzero epochs, identity, and defined
mode.  A bad phase remains `EINVAL`; a malformed representation is `EPROTO`;
a valid stale ticket remains `ESTALE`.

New direct tests prove that malformed TRACKING and OFF owners cannot begin,
enable, or invalidate and remain byte-for-byte unchanged.  The existing
malformed COLLECTING cases continue to cover finish and abort.  Focused owner
tests and normal/snapshot `vmm.ko` builds pass.  The complete normal nested
model records `PASS nested-vmx cases=343`, and its ASan/UBSan counterpart
records `PASS nested-vmx cases=343 sanitizers=address,undefined`.  This closes
the portable model gate for this change only; Intel hardware collection and
live nested execution remain separately default-off qualification work.

### 2026-08-04 — dirty-log callback-publication replay

The next common collector review started from its only externally visible
operation, copying a completed staging bitmap to the caller.  The collector
checked a collecting ticket before querying backend leaves, but it did not
recheck before that final copy.  The documented frozen map/vCPU owner makes
concurrent invalidation unsupported today, but a future architecture callback
or detach path must not be able to publish a bitmap for a ticket it revoked
while answering a query.  The common collector therefore fences the same
ticket immediately before publication; failure leaves the caller bitmap
unchanged.

The direct model has a callback return a valid leaf, invalidate the owner, and
return normally.  It proves the collector returns `ESTALE`, makes exactly one
query, leaves the owner OFF, and preserves the prior bitmap.  Focused collector
tests, the requirements validator, and normal/snapshot `vmm.ko` builds pass.
The complete normal nested-model replay records `PASS nested-vmx cases=344`,
and the ASan/UBSan replay records
`PASS nested-vmx cases=344 sanitizers=address,undefined`.  This validates the
portable callback/publication contract; it does not replace the separately
gated live hardware dirty-log qualification.

The privileged nested-VMX wrapper was reviewed from the completed result

### 2026-08-04 — doubled kernel and implementation-defined review phases

The review protocol now has explicit terminal mutation/rollback and
implementation-defined-behavior replays.  The kernel pass starts from live
writes and destructive helpers, and requires an admission condition, final
fallible boundary, rollback or derived-cache invalidation rule, and an
independent negative proof.  The policy pass starts from accepted operator
inputs and emitted diagnostics, then traces authority, lifetime, failure,
persistence, and observability before consulting a prior ledger.

The first restore-path replay confirmed that nested checkpoint restores keep
architectural VMCS rollback images through registry publication.  It also
confirmed that nested-EPT cache destruction is a quiescent, derived-cache

### 2026-08-04 — dirty-log completed-clear exhaustion replay

The mutation-first lifecycle review found a terminal counter case not covered
by identity exhaustion.  `finish(CLEAR)` runs only after the bitmap was
published and the architecture backend cleared that dirty generation.  If the
dirty-generation increment then overflowed, the previous implementation
returned `EOVERFLOW` while leaving a completed transaction in `COLLECTING`.
The caller could not safely retry the already-completed clear, and the owner
could remain pinned until an unrelated abort.

The common owner now converts that completed-clear overflow directly to the
canonical `EXHAUSTED` state: all range/generation/collection fields are
cleared and the identity becomes `UINT64_MAX`.  The direct owner model proves
the completed ticket is stale, the terminal representation is canonical, and
future enables are rejected.  The requirements validator pins both the
transition and the regression.  Normal and ASan/UBSan complete nested-model
replays passed after the change, as did both normal and `BHYVE_SNAPSHOT`
`vmm.ko` builds.  This is portable lifecycle evidence only; hardware
dirty-bit clear and live migration qualification remain root-only gates.

### 2026-08-04 — VirtIO terminal mutation and non-standard seam replay

Passes 37 and 38 of the VirtIO review protocol were applied independently to
the final common transport and its non-standard seams.  The mutation-first
pass traced DMA-domain installation and detach, direct and translated request
leases, persistent ring remapping, split and packed ownership stores,
administration-queue pause/resume, snapshot queue staging, and rollback of
device-private state.  In particular, an acquire increments the common lease
before consulting a provider callback; detach publishes its fence before
checking the lease count; and release cannot observe a withdrawn callback
because detach waits for that count to reach zero.  Packed-cache replacement
and administration-controller restore retain the old destination state until
the enclosing transaction commits.

The separate consumer-first pass started at private host inputs and outputs:
DMA-domain topology binding, modern-only ACCESS_PLATFORM policy, queue-reset
and notification latches, checkpoint pause/resume, administration-controller
records, snapshot compatibility rejection, and DTrace diagnostics.  It found
no additional actionable defect in that reviewed source/model scope.  This is
not a claim that those optional features are live-qualified: Linux and 5BSD
translated-DMA, packed-ring, checkpoint, reset, multi-queue, and soak cases
remain the independent root-only evidence recorded by the qualification
handoff.

The ASan/UBSan rootless device harness passed all three executed suites (604,
491, and 777 checks) after the replay.  The requirements validator also
passed with 228 requirements, 683 independent oracle definitions, 125 live
feature claims, and 82 private-interface entries checked.  The snapshot
enabled bhyve source build requires a coherently rebuilt world/object tree;
a standalone build against the current mixed object tree stopped at stale
`libvmmapi` snapshot symbols, rather than at a source compilation diagnostic.

### 2026-08-04 — historical snapshot event-owner replay

The second mutation-first kernel traversal found a legacy-path defect in
`STRUCT_VM` restore.  Its fixed historical wire record stages pending-event
fields, but the old commit wrote them under only `rendezvous_mtx`; normal
event publishers and the VMS2 restore path use each vCPU's event owner.  A
management-plane event arriving while the historical input was decoded could
therefore be overwritten.

The historical ABI is unchanged.  Capture now reads those fields under the
event owner.  Restore records a transient destination event-generation fence,
then commits under the established rendezvous-to-ascending-event lock order.
It returns `EAGAIN` for a changed destination generation and `EBUSY` for an
occupied destination event owner before its first write; successful
publication advances the generation for every restored vCPU.  The generation
is kernel-private staging, never part of the historical record.  The
requirements ledger and validator now pin this boundary.  The rootless VMM
module build completed under `-Werror`, and the requirements validator passed
with 419 mapped entries and 271 non-standard interfaces.  Installed-kernel
historical restore racing event injection remains a root-only qualification
gate.

### 2026-08-04 — historical PIT snapshot transaction replay

The compatibility-path review also found that `vatpit_snapshot()` copied
directly to live timer fields and printed that restore did not reset timers.
That allowed a failed copyin to leave a partial PIT image and a successful
restore to retain no scheduled channel-zero timer.  The historical field order
is retained, but save now captures a lock-protected value candidate and
restore decodes the whole record into temporary storage before publication.
Commit stops the prior channel-zero callout, replaces the candidate under the
PIT owner, and rearms it from restored counter state; the old source-relative
deadline is deliberately reanchored on the destination clock.  The stale
diagnostic was removed.  Rootless `vmm.ko` compiled under `-Werror`; a live
checkpoint proving PIT interrupt timing remains a root-only gate.

A second pass now rejects a candidate with a mismatched fixed PIT frequency,
an unsupported mode, or an out-of-range port-I/O latch cursor before it takes
the PIT owner.  This keeps malformed compatibility input from reaching the
live counter path.  The latch is decoded through an explicitly one-byte
temporary rather than a raw C `bool`, with a compile-time width assertion;
the historical record layout remains unchanged.

The follow-up rootless gates passed: the nested requirements validator (420
mapped requirements and 271 non-standard interfaces), the 345-case nested
model suite, and `vmm.ko` with `-Werror`.  The full VirtIO harness also passed
its independent requirements, private-interface, DMA-boundary, snapshot
portability, and model suites.  Installed-kernel checkpoint timing, hardware
VMX execution, and guest-matrix/soak qualification remain intentionally
separate root-only evidence.

### 2026-08-04 — historical PIC snapshot transaction replay

The next compatibility-path replay found the same direct-live-decode pattern
in the fixed VATPIC record.  It now captures under the PIC owner, decodes into

selector, vector-base alignment, priority index, and boolean bytes, then
publishes once under the PIC owner.  Failed copyin and malformed input leave

### 2026-08-04 — historical RTC snapshot transaction replay

The next timer compatibility record, `STRUCT_VRTC`, also decoded directly
into live RTC fields.  A short or otherwise failed input could therefore
leave a changed register image, NVRAM, or destination uptime before returning
an error.  It now captures one locked value candidate for save and fully
decodes a temporary candidate for restore.  Only then does a single RTC-owner
commit replace the image, reanchor source-relative uptime on the destination,
and recompute the callout.  The record field sequence and widths are
unchanged.  An installed checkpoint that proves active periodic/alarm timing
remains a root-only gate.

### 2026-08-04 — historical HPET snapshot transaction replay

`STRUCT_VHPET` also decoded its entire fixed record directly into the live
counter and timer fields.  In addition to partial-input mutation, a restored
disabled HPET could leave destination callouts from its pre-restore state
armed.  Save now captures a locked candidate; restore decodes and verifies
the immutable nonzero device tick duration before a single HPET-owner commit.
That commit stops stale callouts, and the existing restore-time phase
reanchors enabled timers under the same owner.  The historical field sequence
and widths are unchanged.  Installed checkpoint timing and interrupt-delivery
qualification remains a root-only gate.

### 2026-08-04 — historical interrupt and PM-timer replay

The I/O APIC compatibility record had the same direct-live-decode shape: a

The common VirtIO snapshot review found a destination-local lifetime leak at a

cache has no split-ring meaning and could survive until a later unrelated

staged queue commit, allowing the existing outer transaction to retire the old

### 2026-08-05 — bounded virtio-block reset drain

The full virtio-block reset path invalidates the guest ring before it asks the
backend to cancel active I/O, so a late completion is generation-fenced and
cannot publish into a reset queue.  It previously waited indefinitely for
those callbacks.  The drain now uses the existing completion condition
variable with one absolute `CLOCK_REALTIME` deadline (the condition variable
uses its default clock).  A normal reset still waits until every backend-owned
buffer is retired.  If a backend does not respond within five seconds, bhyve
releases reset ownership and marks the device `NEEDS_RESET`; it does not report
that condition as a successful drain.  The outstanding slots remain
generation-fenced until their callbacks return.  The focused harness injects
an expired deadline and proves there is no polling wait and no stale
`reset_waiting` state; the ordinary active-I/O reset case still proves that a
completion is drained before reset succeeds.  A deliberately stalled real
backend remains a privileged live/soak qualification item.

### 2026-08-05 — bounded virtio-SCSI full-reset drain

The SCSI selective-queue reset already used its bounded CTL drain, but a full
device reset selected an unbounded wait and ignored any result.  That allowed
one nonresponsive CTL command to hold a guest vCPU in reset indefinitely.  A
full reset now uses the same bounded, condition-variable-driven quiesce path,
with one monotonic deadline shared by every request queue rather than one
full timeout per queue.  On timeout it advances the common queue generation,
leaves the private worker quiesced, and records `NEEDS_RESET`; a delayed worker
therefore cannot publish into a replacement queue.  The normal path still
completes consumed requests with the VirtIO-defined RESET response before the
common ring reset.  The focused harness forces the zero-second test deadline,
proves the device is marked failed with the active worker retained and
quiesced, and retains the ordinary full- and selective-reset coverage.  A live
intentionally-stalled CTL operation remains part of the privileged SCSI/reset
soak gate.

### 2026-08-05 — 9P reset backend boundary review

The 9P full-reset path already advances its private generation and resets the
common VirtIO queues before it drops the device mutex to close the old lib9p
connection.  Competing reset/reconnect callers wait on the reset condition,
not a polling loop, and notifications observed during the close are not replayed
into the replacement connection.  The lib9p close API has no cancellable or
deadline-bearing operation, however, so adding a synthetic timeout would free
or replace a connection while its worker callbacks might still own it.  The
correct current contract is therefore generation-fenced, serialized teardown;
an intentionally stalled backend close is recorded for the privileged 9P soak
gate and requires a real backend cancellation interface before it can become a
bounded reset path.

continues to allow only the initial lifecycle return and rejects every later
non-NULL owner before VMCS02 residency.  The edge matrix, requirements
validator, sanitized nested model, and VMM build cover this rootless boundary;
Intel L1/L2 execution remains a later privileged qualification gate.

### 2026-08-05 — checkpoint manifest candidate-state atomicity

The checkpoint manifest parser and generation/publication helpers were

### 2026-08-05 — checkpoint manifest path-resolution review

The manifest payload names its data, kernel, and metadata members relative to

guarantees that `is_manifest` is cleared and the caller's manifest remains

removes an ambiguous path-resolution case; it does not replace the privileged

### 2026-08-05 — ACCESS_PLATFORM DMA lifetime review

The common VirtIO DMA path and the VirtIO-IOMMU provider were reviewed as one
ownership protocol.  A request lease is acquired before descriptor or cached
ring translation, including direct-DMA requests, and is retained until normal
completion, cancellation, reset retirement, or grouped completion releases
the request.  Installing or clearing a domain first closes a detach gate and
then requires that no request lease remains; it cannot replace the address
space underneath a completion.  The IOMMU provider pins an endpoint's domain
or bypass selection across all overlapping leases.  ATTACH, DETACH, UNMAP,
reset, and snapshot changes which would revoke that selection return busy and
are retried only from the provider's idle callback when the final lease drains.
This is deliberately event-driven rather than a polling loop.

Cached split and packed ring mappings carry a translation generation.  They
are rebuilt through temporary pointers only when the generation is stable
before and after all mappings; four unstable observations fail closed with
NEEDS_RESET rather than spinning.  Payload and indirect tables are translated
per request.  The review found no path that clears a provider while its
callback table or selected endpoint can still be used.

All individually enumerated `virtio_iommu_state_test`,
`virtio_iommu_request_test`, `virtio_iommu_event_test`, and
`virtio_core_test` ATF cases passed.  Those cover permission and range
matrices, active-DMA unmap and domain revocation, concurrent linearization,
bypass changes, bounded faults, transactional portable state, packed-ring
mapping, and common domain detach races.  This is rootless component evidence;
translated-DMA live Linux/5BSD and destination-host checkpoint qualification
remain ledger work.

### 2026-08-05 — AF_VSOCK record and transport review

The kernel receive path was rechecked at the mbuf-to-socket boundary.  The
allocation helper uses `m_getm2()` only for storage allocation and directly
fills each preallocated element, setting each `m_len` and the sole packet
header length.  It does not use `m_copyback()` on a zero-length chain, so it
cannot silently append unaccounted M_NOWAIT allocations.  Fragmented
SEQPACKET reassembly combines packet chains with `m_catpkt()`, preserving the
single packet-header invariant; EOM delivers one record and EOR is attached
to its final mbuf.  Reassembly remains bounded by both connection credit and
the fragment cap, and its incomplete bytes remain part of receive-credit
accounting until delivery.

The transport path was also checked for event-driven progress: full software
reply queues retain packets and restart from TX completion, and blocked socket
writability is registered under the same lock that publishes a credit wakeup.
The rootless RX and direct transport harnesses passed with 370 and 1651
checks respectively.  These results validate mocked kernel logic and the
driver transport contract; installed-kernel multi-provider, jail/VNET, and
long-running live guest qualification remain separate privileged gates.

### 2026-08-05 — Qualification scheduler lifecycle review

The rootless qualification scheduler now treats its own lifecycle contracts as
testable behavior.  A help request is a successful, side-effect-free command,
rather than a usage error.  CID allocation is based on whether a case uses a
vsock endpoint, not on a particular VM executor name, so scheduler probes
exercise the same generated-CID and lease path as real-VM cases.  Explicit CIDs

case, so it cannot expose a seemingly clean reset device over an unrecoverable

### 2026-08-05 — packed completion and notification reference replay

The packed completion path was compared again with VirtIO 1.4 sections
2.8.6 through 2.8.10, 2.8.15 through 2.8.19, and 2.8.21, plus the pinned
Linux and QEMU reference revisions.  The review confirms that a direct
multi-descriptor request is made visible by publishing its first descriptor
last, with the buffer ID from the list's final descriptor.  The remaining
descriptors are accounted for by the completion span; this is the same
head-publication representation used by QEMU's packed queue.  It is not the
separate `VIRTIO_F_IN_ORDER` batch-completion optimization, which applies to
ordered batches of independent requests.  Consequently the core does not
advertise or depend on `IN_ORDER` merely to complete a normal chained request.

The event-suppression implementation was also checked against the document's
exact-descriptor wording.  Its independently modelled interval is the set of
descriptors completed from the previous used cursor through, but not
including, the new cursor.  Exhaustive small-ring tests cover the two wrap
values, zero progress, full queue progress, and every event offset; the
production helper is not used to calculate the expected result.  Publication
writes completion data before the release-store of descriptor ownership, and
event-control writes are ordered before the availability recheck.  This is
source/model evidence only: packed negotiation and traffic with installed
Linux and rebuilt 5BSD guests remain required privileged qualification lanes.

active softc before unregistering it, waits for the explicitly counted RX and

not replace the installed multi-provider, jail/VNET, checkpoint, and extended
