VMCS02, MSR, EPT, VPID, and continuation state after initial admission.  Its
full residency/no-entry rollback is not yet one common-owner transaction.
Accordingly, `vmx_run_nested()` accepts a non-null owner only for the early
pre-entry software-exit path; every later L2 attempt fails with
`EOPNOTSUPP` before guest-MSR entry or VMCS02 selection.  The management
readiness predicate likewise remains false.  This is deliberate fail-closed
behavior, not a claim that nested execution, INIT/SIPI dispatch, or
save/restore of a running L2 is ready for activation.

The review also checked that portable nested structures are separate from
Intel runtime artifacts: opaque VMCS02, EPT-root, VPID, and CPU-local MSR
ownership remain destination-local and are not serialized.  Existing
sanitizer model coverage validates the staged state machines, but the
remaining atomic L2 owner conversion and Intel-host L1/L2 qualification are
still mandatory before enabling nested VMX exposure.

### 2026-08-05 — virtio-lab interruption and cleanup replay

The test orchestrator was reviewed as part of the operational-correctness
gate.  Each case runs under a recorded daemon supervisor and a separate
case-wrapper child.  `cancel` verifies the run-directory ownership before it
signals only a live child whose parent is the recorded supervisor; the wrapper
then terminates its runner descendants, waits for their cleanup traps, writes
an atomic terminal status, and lets the scheduler release only that case's CID
lease.  Resume rejects a different manifest/configuration, a competing
manager, an untracked live process, or a missing active CID lease.  This
keeps an interrupted VM lane from silently reusing a CID or deleting a
resource it does not own.  The rootless `virtio-lab-selftest.sh` completed
cleanly, including malformed ownership, inactive cancellation, active
cancellation, resume, stale-process, and lease-recovery coverage.

The short timed descendant check is deliberately cleanup-only, bounded, and
followed by a direct wait; normal device progress is event/status driven
rather than busy polling.  Real-VM cancellation and host-bridge cleanup
remain privileged qualification lanes.

### 2026-08-05 — aarch64 checkpoint source-selection correction

The common bhyve Makefile selects machine-dependent sources through
`${MACHINE_CPUARCH}`.  On ARM64 that spelling is `aarch64`, while the existing
fail-closed checkpoint CPU-contract callback had been placed in an `arm64`
directory and therefore could not satisfy a snapshot-enabled aarch64 bhyve
build.  The architecture-selected `aarch64/checkpoint_cpu_machdep.c` now
returns `EOPNOTSUPP` explicitly until an ARM64 CPU-contract format is defined.
The portable-snapshot validator now requires that selected source and a
cross-selection make dry run resolves exactly that file.  This is deliberately
not an attempt to serialize Intel CPU state on a different architecture;
portable device envelopes remain independent while CPU checkpoint support
continues to fail closed per architecture.

### 2026-08-05 — nested L2 owner-conversion integration review

A source-ordered review rechecked the relationship between the common
startup-entry owner and `vmx_run_nested()`.  The Intel-private outcome bridge
has an independent, sanitizer-backed state model for initial entry, resumed
entry, completed private rollback/refreeze, terminal inverse failure, and
post-entry EPT/reflection deferral.  It intentionally has no power to select
VMCS02, publish an exit, or perform cleanup itself.  The production L2 runner
does not yet call that bridge: after its sole provably pre-residency
software-exit branch it returns `EOPNOTSUPP` for a supplied common owner,
before guest MSRs, VMCS02 selection, EPT activation, VPID use, or a nested
event transaction.

This boundary is retained.  Wiring the model at only the final VMLAUNCH or
VMRESUME instruction would be wrong: initial-entry rejection has a distinct
VMCS02/MSR rollback, resumed rejection needs a continuation refreeze, and
post-entry EPT/reflection routes must finish their private publication or
freeze before resolving a common result.  The outstanding work is therefore
one source-ordered atomic conversion covering every early synthetic exit,
initial/retry failure, hardware result, hot L0 re-entry, EPT walk, reflection,
freeze, and terminal detach path, followed by live Intel L1/L2 qualification.
Until then the owner outcome source remains a deliberately dormant,
non-serialized private value protocol—not evidence that kernel-owned L2
startup or active-L2 checkpoint/restore is supported.

### 2026-08-05 — installed validation-payload replay

The device-test packaging review compared the ATF registration, the rootless
`run.sh` source inputs, and the installed validation payload rather than
assuming that a source-tree run represented the package.  It found that
`virtio_snd_async_test` was registered and run in the source tree but its C
source was absent from `VIRTIO_VALIDATION_FILES`.  An installed harness would
therefore fail before it could rebuild the advertised asynchronous sound lane.
The payload now includes that source.  The complete source-input versus
package-payload cross-check has no omissions, and the sanitizer-backed device
harness completed all groups cleanly (1,973 checks, zero failures).  This is
test-package completeness only; it does not convert the null/OSS sound model
or any provisional device into live-guest release evidence.

The requirements validator now performs that comparison on every rootless and
installed-suite invocation, parsing the `VIRTIO_VALIDATION_FILES` and
`SANITIZER_HARNESS_FILES` package payloads rather than accepting a coincidental
source-name mention in a compiler or clean rule.  Any C fixture rebuilt by
`run.sh` but absent from those payloads is now a deterministic validation
failure.

The portability replay also now protects both currently non-x86 bhyve
machine-directory selections.  ARM64 (`aarch64`) and RISC-V (`riscv`) each
must provide the architecture-selected `checkpoint_cpu_contract_capture()`
callback and explicitly return `EOPNOTSUPP` until a native versioned CPU
contract exists.  That keeps portable device envelopes usable without
accidentally treating Intel CPUID state as a cross-architecture checkpoint
format.

### 2026-08-05 — save-state and nested-owner review replay

The shared VirtIO lifecycle review rechecked the device suspend/checkpoint
fence against GPU command execution and presentation state.  GPU command
processing enters only through the common queue gate, while the independently
locked 2D state object serializes command, renderer, and snapshot access.  The
GPU lifecycle callbacks consequently require no device-specific drain today;
the common fence prevents a command from starting during save/restore and the
state codec uses a bounded transactional copy.  This remains a host-model
claim only: a live Linux scanout/presentation lane is still required before
promoting GPU support.

The second nested-VMX replay traced `vmx_run_nested()` from the outer
startup-owner admission through every private outcome.  The ordinary L1
runner can commit or abort its owner directly because it has one VMCS and one
post-exit route.  The L2 runner cannot: it has distinct initial rollback,
resumed-continuation refreeze, hot-continuation freeze, EPT-walk publication,
reflected-exit publication, and terminal-detach routes.  The outcome adapter
and its sanitizer model cover those value combinations, but production still
does not invoke it.  Retaining the pre-residency `EOPNOTSUPP` boundary is the
correct behavior until one implementation binds each source-ordered private
inverse to exactly one owner settlement.  This review found no reason to
weaken that boundary.

Rootless replay after the review passed the independent VirtIO requirements,
snapshot-portability, nested-VMX requirements, and sanitizer-backed
nested-state model gates.  They validate source and model behavior, not
hardware VMX execution; the installed Linux/5BSD, checkpoint, soak, and Intel
L1/L2 qualification gates remain pending.

### 2026-08-05 — reset-soak re-enumeration diagnostic

The prior reset-soak observation where a re-bound block device briefly lacked
`/dev/vda` is an ordinary guest device-manager publication race, not evidence
of a block data-path checksum failure.  The block guest helper already waits
for the exact expected VirtIO PCI child, its `virtio_blk` binding, and its
resulting block node before it performs an I/O command.  Its independent
self-test now also removes that node and proves that the helper emits the
bounded, specific “device node is not ready” failure rather than returning an
unusable pathname.  This wait is a re-enumeration boundary with a finite
deadline; normal queue/device progress remains interrupt and event driven.

### 2026-08-05 — provisional-device lifecycle capability audit

A fresh feature-exposure pass compared the common modern transport's
`VIRTIO_F_SUSPEND` gate with the lifecycle implementations for balloon, GPU,
filesystem, IOMMU, memory, RTC, and sound.  The transport exposes SUSPEND only
when both suspend and resume callbacks exist, enters its common queue-admission
fence before the device callback, and does not clear that fence until the
resumed device is ready.  The models with external or timed state take their
own action: balloon completes a retained statistics buffer, virtio-fs freezes
its identified backend, virtio-mem captures its configuration, RTC disarms and
later rearms alarms, and sound quiesces its async state.

GPU and IOMMU currently use explicit no-op lifecycle callbacks.  That is
intentional and safe only for their present synchronous host models: GPU 2D
state and backing copies are serialized under the model lock, and IOMMU state
mutation and foreign endpoint callbacks pass through the common lifecycle
fence.  Their independent PCI tests assert this premise and state that a
future display/renderer or asynchronous invalidation worker must replace the
no-op with an ownership drain.  This audit found no feature bit that was
advertised without a matching current lifecycle contract.  It does not qualify
those provisional models for a live guest; their Linux/5BSD activation entries
remain pending in the feature-activation ledger.

### 2026-08-05 — checkpoint canonical-base-case replay

The common machine-topology seal was reread as a portable wire boundary rather
than as a device-specific helper.  It orders only bounded device names, writes
all numeric fields in fixed-width little-endian form, rejects duplicate names
and noncanonical fixed-capacity shapes before publishing the digest, and never
serializes a pointer or native structure image.  Its zero-device input is also
valid: it represents the canonical empty topology used while a machine is
being assembled.  A new independent ATF case proves that this base case
produces the same canonical digest on repeated calls.  This makes the
`calloc(0)`-permitted implementation detail unobservable to the checkpoint
format.  The targeted ATF binary and the requirements/payload validator both
pass after the addition.

### 2026-08-05 — existing-device snapshot transaction replay

The common `vi_pci_snapshot()` transaction and the callbacks for balloon,
console, 9P, input, memory, RTC, and sound were traced together.  The common
layer stages generic queue/transport state, holds a destination queue backup,
and retires a replaced packed completion cache only after the model callback
has committed.  On validate or an error it restores the generic destination
image; models that own external state either validate before publication or
quarantine the device with `restore_incomplete` if an external rollback cannot
be proven.  Console and 9P preserve only reconnectable identities and publish
their mutable state after the complete record has been consumed.  Input stages
the event frame before replacing the live queue.  Balloon, memory, RTC, and
sound use their model-specific bounded state codecs and retain the common
failure boundary.

This source pass found no generic callback that silently publishes an
unvalidated record.  It also does not claim cross-host behavior for any
external backend: live changed-backend, active-I/O, packed, Linux, and 5BSD
qualification stays explicitly pending in the requirements ledger.

### 2026-08-05 — nested owner transaction model replay

The Intel-private nested owner model was replayed against the real
`vmx_run_nested()` entry ordering.  The only production path permitted to
consume a supplied owner remains the early lifecycle stop before guest MSRs,
VMCS02 selection, EPT activation, or nested event acquisition.  Every later
path rejects that owner with `EOPNOTSUPP`.  Focused model cases passed for
initial and resumed attempts, hardware rejection, terminal L0 failure,
deferred pre-entry resolution, post-entry EPT/reflection/unhandled routes,
and the full owner transaction graph.

This proves the value-level prerequisites and the fail-closed boundary; it
does not authorize a partial call-site conversion.  A production conversion
must still bind each modeled result to its exact VMCS02 rollback, continuation
refreeze, hot freeze, or terminal detach before it settles the common owner,
then pass live Intel L1/L2 qualification.

### 2026-08-05 — nested run-loop branch-to-edge reconciliation

`vmx_run_nested()` was checked branch-by-branch against the startup-entry edge
matrix.  Its early cold lifecycle return, resumed thaw/refreeze, hot freeze,
initial synthetic event, resumed/hot synthetic event, initial hardware
rejection, resumed no-entry result, EPT walk, direct reflection, handled
re-entry, unhandled/reflect freeze, and terminal unwind all map to an explicit
matrix edge.  No additional VMCS02 return path was found.  In particular, the
EPT and direct-reflection branches follow a real L2 exit even though they
bypass `vmx_exit_process()`, so they correctly remain post-entry routes in the
future transaction rather than being misclassified as synthetic no-entry
returns.

The review confirms the existing boundary is intentional: adding an owner
guard only before `vmx_enter_guest()` would leave earlier synthetic/rejection
and later post-entry publication edges without a safe owner settlement.  The
matrix and model are therefore complete enough to constrain a future atomic
conversion, but the production gate remains closed until that conversion and
Intel live qualification are available.

### 2026-08-05 — live-evidence reachability audit

The feature-activation ledger previously verified that every named live case
existed in the manifest and that every exercised claim named a source-level
assertion marker.  A further independent check now requires each case backing
an `exercised` Linux or 5BSD claim to be reachable from the complete
qualification graph: the release, checkpoint, or soak profiles.  This closes
the metadata-only gap where a historical claim could otherwise be attached to
a smoke-only or ad-hoc case that the full qualification run never selects.

The audit intentionally does not promote pending entries and does not treat a
scheduled case as evidence of a passed live run.  The current ledger still
reports 125 claims, with 79 Linux and 114 5BSD entries unresolved; those
remain explicit root-only qualification work.  The requirements validator and
the orchestrator self-test pass with the new reachability check.

### 2026-08-05 — qualification cancellation ownership replay

The lab cancellation path was reviewed as an ownership problem rather than a
mere manager status update.  The case wrapper previously asked `pgrep -P` only
for the direct child of its timeout supervisor.  A runner can start a device
model and helper processes below that child; once the runner exits, such
processes can be reparented and are no longer visible to a new direct-parent
lookup.  Cancellation now captures the complete descendant tree, with a
start-time-and-command fingerprint for every PID, before it asks the runner to
perform its normal cleanup.  It waits a bounded five-second grace period, then
terminates and finally kills only survivors whose fingerprint still matches;
it never acts on a bare PID that might have been reused.  The case status is
still published atomically only after this bounded teardown.

`virtio-lab-selftest.sh` passes its active-cancellation scenario with this
path.  This improves cleanup determinism for interrupted qualification runs;
it does not turn an interrupted soak into evidence of a completed soak gate.
The scenario now also launches an intentionally untrapped helper below the
runner and asserts that its recorded PID is gone after cancellation.  Thus the
test proves descendant teardown rather than inferring it solely from the
manager's terminal status and lease removal.

### 2026-08-05 — checkpoint CPU-contract publication audit

The portable snapshot metadata path was reviewed together with the selected
amd64, aarch64, and riscv CPU-contract callbacks.  The non-amd64 callbacks
correctly report `EOPNOTSUPP` until their native execution-contract codecs
exist, but the generic writer had treated that result as non-fatal and could
therefore publish a new checkpoint without a CPU contract.  Restore would
then mistake that newly incomplete image for an intentionally supported
historical pre-contract image.

New checkpoint creation now propagates every CPU-contract capture error,
including `EOPNOTSUPP`.  Historical restore remains deliberately compatible
only when the entire field is absent from an existing image.  The portability
validator asserts that the old exception cannot return, and the snapshot-mode
bhyve build, snapshot portability validator, requirements validator, and
whitespace check all pass.  This is a fail-closed portability boundary, not a
claim that aarch64 or riscv CPU checkpointing is implemented.

### 2026-08-05 — nested owner call-site reconciliation

The common startup owner was traced against the ordinary VMX runner and every
`vmx_run_nested()` return route.  The ordinary runner can guard immediately
before an entry instruction, commit only after a real VM exit, and resolve its
single post-entry result directly.  The nested runner has materially different
routes: an initial rejection completes a VMCS02/MSR rollback, a resumed
rejection refreezes a retained continuation, a synthetic L2-visible exit never
attempts entry, and EPT walk, direct reflection, and unhandled exits each
publish or freeze private state before a common result may escape.

The existing Intel-private outcome model covers those distinct result domains,
but production retains the pre-residency `EOPNOTSUPP` boundary for a supplied
owner.  This is intentionally stricter than attempting to reuse the ordinary
one-VMCS sequence: a partial integration could commit guest residency after
an unentered VMLAUNCH/VMRESUME or return a result while VMCS02 state remained
CPU-local.  The next implementation unit must wire all of the mapped edges as
one transaction, with focused model and Intel L1/L2 qualification before the
readiness gate is enabled.

The complete sanitizer-backed device harness was replayed after this audit:
1,973 checks passed with zero failures.  Its intentionally noisy malformed
descriptor, short I/O, provider failure, reset, and entropy-source cases are
expected fault-injection coverage.  This rootless result validates host-model
and wire contracts only; the feature-activation ledger continues to mark the
Linux and 5BSD live gates as pending rather than treating it as guest evidence.

### 2026-08-05 — CPU-contract capture errno hardening

The amd64 contract adapter relies on libvmmapi's documented failure convention
of returning an error with `errno` set.  A defensive review found that directly
returning `errno` could nevertheless turn a faulty wrapper's failure with a
clear `errno` into apparent success and permit a record derived from stale
input registers.  The adapter now clears `errno` immediately before each
query and maps a failing query with no errno to `EIO`.  The output remains
unchanged on every failure.

The capture fixture injects both ordinary errno-bearing failures and failures
with no errno for CPUID and compatibility queries.  The normal `-Werror`
fixture build, ASan/UBSan 1,973-check harness, snapshot-enabled bhyve build,
and whitespace check pass.  This is a local defensive boundary; it does not
change the kernel or libvmmapi ABI.

### 2026-08-05 — CPU-contract topology completeness

The amd64 checkpoint contract initially captured CPUID topology leaves
`0x0b` and `0x1f` through a fixed subleaf count.  That was sufficient for
the common SMT/core hierarchy but was not the architectural rule: the Intel
CPUID interface terminates those leaves when `EBX[15:0]` is zero, and valid
machines can report additional hierarchy levels.  A contract which omitted
one of those guest-visible levels could incorrectly regard distinct CPU
topologies as compatible across restore.

Capture now follows the documented terminator, includes that terminating
subleaf in the canonical record set, and rejects a nonterminating response at
the existing bounded contract limit.  The independent libvmmapi fixture now
models four topology levels plus a terminator for both leaves and proves that
the extra levels, terminators, and no-beyond-terminator boundary are encoded.
The normal `-Werror` fixture build, ASan/UBSan 1,973-check harness,
snapshot-enabled bhyve build, portability validation, nested-ledger
validation, and whitespace check pass.  This improves the portable CPU
compatibility contract; it does not constitute Intel hardware migration or
nested-L2 execution evidence.

### 2026-08-05 — nested stop-classification snapshot

The nested VMX runner checks suspension, rendezvous, requested-idle,
scheduler-yield, and debug state at the two points where it can return before
entry or freeze a hot L2 continuation.  These predicates are intentionally
lockless observations.  The prior code used them once to decide that it must
stop, then reread them to choose the reported exit.  A scheduler AST can clear
between those reads, making an already selected yield stop appear as a debug
exit.

Each nested stop decision now takes one local snapshot of all five predicates
and uses that immutable set both for admission and for the priority-ordered
exit classification.  The hot path still publishes/fences its continuation
before enabling interrupts and reporting the selected stop.  The nested edge
matrix and requirement validator were updated to assert that explicit
single-observation shape.  This does not enable owner-backed L2 execution:
all paths after the sole pre-residency lifecycle return remain fail-closed
until their complete owner/residency transaction is converted and live tested.

### 2026-08-05 — CPU-contract cache-leaf termination

The CPU-contract review found the same termination-boundary error in the
deterministic-cache CPUID leaves (`0x04` and `0x8000001d`): after recording
subleaf zero, capture would always request subleaf one even when zero already
reported the architectural cache-type terminator.  Those extra values are not
an architectural cache record and could unnecessarily make two compatible
CPU contracts differ.

The cache enumerator now checks the already captured zero subleaf before
issuing a further CPUID query.  It continues to retain a nonzero sequence's
terminator, so the full guest-visible response remains canonical.  The
independent mock now exercises both a multi-record cache sequence and an
empty-at-zero sequence, asserting that no subleaf one is requested in the
latter case.  The `-Werror` fixture, ASan/UBSan 1,973-check harness, and
snapshot-enabled bhyve build pass.  This is contract correctness only; it is
not live migration qualification.

Both cache and topology enumeration now use the explicit
`CHECKPOINT_CPU_MAX_RECORDS` capacity instead of an unrelated 64-subleaf
policy limit.  Thus a nonterminating response fails at the same bounded
contract limit used by every other record, while a valid larger hierarchy is
not rejected only because of a hidden local constant.

### 2026-08-05 — CPU-contract extended-leaf validation

The maximum-leaf value returned by CPUID `0x80000000` is part of the
execution contract.  The capture path previously accepted a value below the
extended-leaf base and treated it as an empty range.  That is malformed CPUID
output, not a valid no-extended-leaves representation, and could produce a
contract from an incoherent kernel query.

Capture now rejects such a response with `EPROTO` before it can publish the
candidate.  The independent libvmmapi fixture injects the invalid maximum and
proves that the caller's output remains byte-for-byte unchanged.  The strict
fixture build, ASan/UBSan harness, snapshot-enabled bhyve build, and
whitespace check pass.  This remains rootless contract validation; live
checkpoint migration is still an explicit later gate.

### 2026-08-05 — checkpoint publication event-fence visibility

The checkpoint manifest is the sole publication edge.  A directory `fsync()`
can report a durability failure only after the manifest rename has made the
new generation visible.  The snapshot path now commits, rather than aborts,
the exact kernel event-fence session whenever that visibility edge occurred.
The command still returns the durability error and does not remove the new
members, but the visible image retains one coherent capture-side event cut.
The rootless manifest fault-injection test covers the post-rename error, and
the portability gate separately prevents the source transaction from
regressing to an error-gated abort.

### 2026-08-05 — packed used-descriptor completion audit

The packed-ring completion publisher was checked directly against VirtIO 1.4
sections 2.8.3 through 2.8.6 and 2.8.21 through 2.8.22.  It deliberately
overwrites the first available descriptor in a completed chain with the used
descriptor's length, buffer ID, WRITE result, and AVAIL/USED ownership bits.
In that used representation WRITE reports whether the device initialized any
part of the complete buffer; it is not the original writable-capacity flag.
NEXT is reserved in a used descriptor and drivers must ignore it.  Therefore
preserving the old head flags would have been incorrect.

The common completion path already has independent checks for a wrapping
direct chain with nonzero output and for a zero-byte completion.  Those tests
use only the specification fixture values, verify the exact used flags and
length, and ensure a zero-byte result clears WRITE even when the original
available descriptor was device-writable.  The sanitizer-backed harness and
the nested requirement/model gates passed after this review.  This is
rootless wire and ownership evidence only; packed Linux and rebuilt-5BSD live
feature activation remains ledger-gated.

### 2026-08-05 — AF_VSOCK transport and mbuf lifecycle replay

The receive, fragmentation, attach-completion, and detach paths were replayed
against the current source.  Packet construction fills the preallocated
`m_getm2()` chain directly and fails if it cannot account for every byte; it
does not use `m_copyback()` on zero-length preallocated mbufs.  Fragmented
SEQPACKET records use `m_catpkt()`, preserving packet-header semantics before
the completed record reaches the socket buffer.  These are the two operations
that the earlier simple userspace mbuf mock could not validate.

The VirtIO transport publishes its softc only after registration succeeds,
each interrupt/recycle path rechecks the exact global-softc identity after a
lock drop, and detach removes that identity before waiting for inflight work
and draining queues.  The PCI, legacy PCI, and MMIO buses each check a
driver's `attach_completed()` return value and detach/fail the device on an
error.  Both `vsock.ko` and `virtio_vsock.ko` rebuild cleanly.  This source
and module-build replay does not replace the existing installed-kernel
multiple-provider, reset, checkpoint, and long-run qualification gates.

### 2026-08-05 — non-standard ABI and nested owner replay

The extra portability pass examined host-ABI-sensitive paths rather than
assuming every use of a native type is a guest ABI leak.  In particular,
VirtIO input uses `unsigned long` only to size the host evdev ioctl buffer;
`pci_vtinput_get_bitmap()` then translates each native bit number into the
specified VirtIO byte bitmap before exposing configuration to a guest.  The
guest-visible length is derived from that byte representation, not the host
word width or byte order.  No change was made because replacing that ioctl
buffer sizing with a wire-layout calculation would be wrong for the host
evdev ABI.

The nested entry-owner path was replayed source-order against the ordinary
VMX transaction.  The latter proves the necessary pattern: observe/admit,
prepare every CPU-pinned resource, guard immediately before the instruction,
commit only a real VM exit, undo preparation before publishing any declined
result, then defer an unhandled exit until the private inverse completes.
`vmx_run_nested()` does not yet satisfy that complete pattern across its
initial, resumed, hot, reflected-exit, EPT, refreeze, and terminal-error
branches.  It therefore retains the explicit `EOPNOTSUPP` boundary for every
non-null owner after the one cold pre-residency lifecycle return.  Enabling
that owner incrementally would create an unsound residency/rollback path, so
the required next change remains one atomic Intel-private transaction plus
model and live-L2 qualification.

The requirements validator (431 entries), non-standard-interface ledger (276
entries), sanitizer-backed nested model suite, snapshot-enabled `bhyve`
build, both vsock module builds, and the sanitizer-backed VirtIO harness all
pass.  These are rootless design and model results; installed-kernel Linux,
5BSD, active checkpoint, soak, and real Intel L1/L2 evidence remain separate
promotion gates.

### 2026-08-05 — isolated checkpoint sanitizer lane

The focused checkpoint-model runner accepted `SANITIZERS` but previously
invoked an ordinary object-directory build.  That meant its success message
could overstate sanitizer coverage.  The runner now creates a private object
directory, materializes only the checkpoint DUT sources required by the quote
include harness, and supplies the sanitizer flags through the build
environment so each program retains its Makefile-provided include paths and
linker wrappers.  It rejects the ambiguous `SANITIZE` spelling rather than
silently ignoring an operator request.

The normal and ASan/UBSan lanes each execute all 30 independently enumerated
checkpoint-model cases successfully.  The gate still does not claim live
checkpoint, device-backend reconstruction, or cross-host migration evidence;
those remain privileged qualification work.

### 2026-08-05 — lifecycle callback and nested-owner replay

The common checkpoint contract was replayed from `vi_pci_pause()` through
`vi_pci_resume()` and the individual SCSI, console, 9P, input, and vsock
callbacks.  The reviewed devices either drain request workers before taking a
checkpoint owner or reject backend state that cannot be represented without
host descriptors, pointers, or live sockets.  The common fence remains held
when a callback resume fails, so a caller can retry without reopening guest
queues.  Input intentionally retains its device mutex if `mevent_enable()`
fails; its tested retry path reuses that owner and releases it only after the
event source is successfully re-enabled.

The Intel nested-owner outcome model was also replayed alongside the hardware
entry finisher.  It validates an immutable report classification before
settling the portable owner, distinguishes entered, rolled-back software
rejection, and rolled-back host-error outcomes, and rejects overlapping
value/output storage.  Production nested execution remains explicitly
fail-closed for a non-null startup owner after the cold no-entry return.  No
partial wiring was added: a real enablement change must cover all VMCS02,
MSR, EPT, event, reflected-exit, refreeze, and error exits as one transaction.

The rootless device harness passed 604, 491, 777, 99, and 2-check lanes with
zero failures, including 229 requirements, 683 independent oracle values,
125 activation claims, snapshot portability/DMA/DTrace validators, normal
and ASan/UBSan checkpoint models, and the VMX nested model.  This is not a
claim of live guest or hardware-nested execution; those retain their separate
privileged Linux, 5BSD, checkpoint, and Intel L1/L2 gates.

### 2026-08-05 — virtio-fs readiness and completion callback replay

The virtio-fs PCI adapter was replayed through connection establishment,
readiness callbacks, queue reset, quiesce, thaw, and completion.  Readiness
registration is now an error-returning operation: each arm or disarm is still
attempted so the two registrations converge, but the first failure is carried
back to connect, reset, quiesce, and thaw callers.  Those callers either
disconnect the incomplete backend or retain the checkpoint/reset fence and
set NEEDS_RESET; they no longer wait for an event source that failed to arm.
The underlying connection API explicitly treats a null connection as having
no events, so the disconnected cleanup path remains a tested no-op.

The same replay found that `pci_vtfs_complete()` discarded its callback
context and then passed that null value to the pressure probe, despite the
probe requiring the device softc.  A normal asynchronous backend completion
could therefore dereference null after publishing a used chain.  The callback
now retains and supplies its real softc.  The PCI composition harness injects
both readiness-arm failures and a successful asynchronous completion, checks
that the first of two distinct arm failures is retained after both operations
are attempted, verifies per-event counters so the second registration cannot
be skipped by an early return, checks the used-chain publication, and reaches
the pressure probe with a valid context.  The snapshot-enabled bhyve build
and rootless harness pass after the fix.  Live virtio-fs backend, packed-ring,
and checkpoint qualification remain pending privileged gates.

### 2026-08-05 — RTC and virtio-mem lifecycle replay

The RTC alarm and virtio-mem device paths were replayed across request
processing, reset, suspend, checkpoint, restore, and their host-owned
resources.  RTC uses one nonblocking absolute `CLOCK_REALTIME` timerfd with
`CANCEL_ON_SET`; after delivery it uses a far-future cancellation sentinel and
a post-arm clock sample, so backward wall-clock steps remain observable
without a polling loop.  Its portable alarm record contains only fixed-width
little-endian logical state and a digest; timer descriptors, wall-clock
samples, pointers, and native timer state are not serialized.  The unit
tests cover exact wire replies, malformed requests, short alarm buffers,
notification and storage aliases, forward/backward crossings, reset, corrupt
state, and a destination where the alarm deadline elapsed while stopped.

Virtio-mem validates an entire incoming portable bitmap before acquiring the
restore operation, reconstructs only ranges described by that image, and
records each reconstructed range before a later failure can need to undo it.
If that precise compensation cannot complete, the backend exposes a
restore-incomplete latch; the PCI adapter republishes it after reset, keeping
further checkpoint admission closed rather than claiming an unknown backing
state is valid.  Normal reset intentionally retains plugged memory, while the
frozen configuration is encoded separately for suspend/resume.  No new
correctness issue was found in these rootless source/model replays.  Linux and
5BSD packed, activation, memory-pressure, and checkpoint runs remain
privileged qualification rather than completed evidence.

### 2026-08-05 — vsock backend checkpoint replay

The userspace and kernel-backed virtio-vsock checkpoint paths were replayed
with their callback, reset, and provider ownership contracts in scope.  The
userspace backend has no portable connection, descriptor, buffer, or listener
state: save and restore require all of those runtime lists and accounting
counters to be empty, and retain only a bounded configured listener identity.
The kernel backend freezes its provider before committed save/restore state is
used, verifies the complete versioned empty-provider reply, restores the
negotiated feature epoch while the provider remains fenced, then thaws it.
Malformed FREEZE replies, feature replay failures, and THAW failures either
roll back to a running source or retain a closed, retryable fence; an
unrecoverable malformed-reply THAW failure also publishes NEEDS_RESET.

All host readiness callbacks take the device mutex and test the lifecycle
fence after disabling races have been accounted for.  Full reset drains both
ordinary and control connection lists and decrements the control-list count
once for each removed object; the initially suspected double-decrement was
not present in the production source.  The rootless device harness,
address/undefined-behaviour snapshot lane, snapshot-enabled bhyve build, and
diff-whitespace validation pass.  Live split/packed Linux and 5BSD
checkpoint/reconstruction cases remain explicitly root-only qualification.

### 2026-08-05 — SCSI worker and checkpoint replay

Virtio-SCSI was replayed through request acquisition, CTL execution,
completion, queue reset, full reset, guest suspend, checkpoint pause, and
restore.  The common admission fence stops new descriptor acquisition before
the device takes its own queue owners.  Existing workers drain under one
monotonic device deadline; a selective queue reset retires its old common
request owner without publishing a used entry, while a full device reset
completes queued-but-unsubmitted commands with the VirtIO-SCSI reset response.
Timeout leaves the private queue parked, resets the common incarnation, and
sets NEEDS_RESET rather than allowing a late CTL completion into replacement
guest memory.

The checkpoint record contains only fixed-width logical configuration plus an
opaque, bounded CTL LUN-inventory identity.  Decode and topology checks occur
before a destination inventory query, and all destination state remains
unchanged on malformed, truncated, incompatible, or changed-backend input.
CTL event subscriptions and their source sequence are deliberately
destination-local: restore discards old records and produces the documented
loss-aware rescan marker only when event delivery is available.  Focused
model cases cover this behavior, queue ownership preservation, multiqueue
rollback, TMF interaction, and suspended/checkpoint nesting.  No new
rootless correctness issue was found; active-command Linux/5BSD restore,
HOTPLUG/CHANGE races, packed, and translated-DMA runs remain promotion gates.

### 2026-08-05 — console and 9P lifecycle replay

Virtio-console and virtio-9P were reviewed across host I/O callbacks, queue
reset, guest suspend, checkpoint, restore, and reconnect.  Console accepts a
checkpoint only when every enabled port has its configured listener but no
connected host descriptor, pending output, or live connection event source.
Its portable record uses fixed-width logical port state and bounded configured
port/listener identities; restore forces ports closed, validates every state
dependency before publication, and re-arms receive work only after the common
queue fence opens.  Stale host callbacks identify their connection descriptor
under the device lock, so a deferred event cannot consume descriptors from a
later connection.

9P deliberately rejects active requests, queue-reset transitions, and every
live fid because those carry backend-owned objects.  Its restore identity is
the already-open confined export path plus device/inode, readonly policy, tag,
and negotiated connection geometry; the source generation is consumed only as
a historical compatibility slot and is never imported as an asynchronous
completion token.  Full reset drains and replaces the lib9p connection, while
selective reset retains the mounted fid namespace but advances a destination
generation and completes only after the old callbacks retire.  Rootless tests
cover stale notify suppression, generation fencing, identity mismatch,
malformed records, suspend ownership, and reconnect failure.  No new
correctness issue was found.  Active Linux/5BSD packed, reset-under-load,
reconnect, and checkpoint qualification remain privileged gates.

### 2026-08-05 — IOMMU prepared-fabric rollback replay

The VirtIO-IOMMU checkpoint adapter was replayed through save, validation,
validation cleanup, restore, DMA leasing, and endpoint callback delivery.  A
real reversibility defect was corrected: validation used to discard a prior
prepared destination fabric before the replacement image had passed complete
decode, topology, and destination-GPA validation.  A malformed later
validation could therefore erase a still-valid prepared view.  Preparation now
happens first and the prepared view is atomically replaced only after success;
the old view is retired only after publication.  The live fabric remains
untouched on every failed validation.

The review also confirmed that active endpoint DMA fences state save and
restore, that mapping revocation is retried from an idle edge rather than a
polling loop, and that portable state contains endpoint/domain/mapping/fault
records rather than host pointers or mapper results.  The rootless device
harness passed all 604 core checks plus the 491, 777, and 99 focused lanes
after this correction.  Live translated-DMA, Linux packed IOMMU, destination
topology mismatch, and long-running concurrent invalidation qualification
remain privileged gates.

### 2026-08-05 — common transport and checkpoint final replay

The common VirtIO transport/checkpoint path was replayed across split and
packed queue banks, administration queue composition, lifecycle pause/resume,
DMA-domain generation changes, compatibility validation, and rollback.
Portable records retain only explicit little-endian device features, queue
cursors, guest addresses, MSI-X selections, and fixed-width compatibility
metadata.  Host mappings, completion caches, request ownership, queue
generations, mapper pointers, and external backend handles are rebuilt or
fenced as destination-local state.

Checkpoint pause first closes common queue admission, then acquires the
device and optional administration fences; failed pause reopens those fences
and replays a coalesced notification edge.  Resume only releases ownership
that the particular device acquired and replays deferred configuration and
queue notifications after the common fence opens.  Queue mapping refresh uses
a bounded stable-generation retry and fails closed rather than polling
indefinitely.  No additional rootless correctness defect was found in this
pass.  The remaining evidence required for promotion is privileged live
Linux/5BSD split-and-packed operation, translated DMA, checkpoint/restore,
fault injection, and soak execution.

### 2026-08-05 — nested VMX startup-owner integration review

The Intel nested-VMX path was independently replayed against the ordinary
VMX startup-owner transaction and the Intel-private VMCS02 lifecycle.  The
ordinary path has one entry instruction and one audited inverse, so its
common owner can be guarded immediately before entry and settled on the
matching post-entry path.  Nested VMX has three materially different entry
residencies: cold VMCS02 preparation, thawed continuation resume, and hot
L0-exit re-entry.  They require respectively an initial hardware rollback,
an unentered cold refreeze, and a hot continuation freeze.  A shared owner
must not be committed, aborted, or resolved until the matching inverse has
completed.

The existing `vmx_run_nested()` `EOPNOTSUPP` boundary is therefore retained
deliberately for every owner-bearing nested entry after the one proven
no-side-effect lifecycle-stop return.  It executes before guest MSRs, VMCS02
selection, EPT activation, or nested event ownership.  The owner-outcome
model and its tests define the required order, but production has not yet
connected all cold, resumed, hot, reflected-exit, EPT, and terminal-error
branches.  Enabling it partially would permit a common startup owner to
outlive or misrepresent Intel-private residency.  This is a tracked
integration gap, not an enabled feature or a test-only limitation.

The requirement validator and nested model tests pass with the boundary in
place.  The next implementation gate is a source-level owner adapter proving
the exact inverse and settlement order for each of the three entry modes,
followed by real Intel L1/L2, snapshot, repeated-create/destroy, and fault
qualification.  AMD and common VMM paths remain fail-closed and portable.

### 2026-08-05 — second kernel and portable-state replay

The kernel VirtIO-vsock receive and ownership paths were replayed a second
time.  Receive construction fills the preallocated mbuf chain directly rather
than allocating through `m_copyback()`, and fragmented SEQPACKET records use
`m_catpkt()` so only the head carries a packet header.  The receive harness
checks positive segment lengths, byte-exact reconstruction, and exactly one
packet header.  Driver attachment registers the transport while the global
softc slot is still empty, publishes that slot only after registration
succeeds, and clears it only when detach owns that same object.  Modern PCI,
legacy PCI, and MMIO all propagate `attach_completed()` failure through
cleanup to FAILED; RX and event-buffer recycling recheck pointer identity
after their unlocked work.  No additional lifecycle, ownership, or
attachment defect was found in this pass.

Nested and device checkpoint records were also replayed for host-independent
state.  The nested active-L2 envelope is fixed-width little-endian, versioned,
digest-protected, and validates every section and capability signature before
registry publication.  Its portable L2 image deliberately excludes VMCS
hardware identity, EPT roots, VPID leases, pointers, and backend handles.
The rootless snapshot model and portability validator pass.  A CPU-contract
harness defect was corrected: its mock had placed extended deterministic cache
enumeration at the basic `0x1d` leaf rather than `0x8000001d`.  The test now
captures the real extended leaf and independently verifies the expected
subleaves; this was an oracle/count defect, not a production checkpoint
capture defect.

The full nested startup-owner adapter remains intentionally unintegrated.
After the one pre-residency lifecycle return, `vmx_run_nested()` still rejects
an owner with `EOPNOTSUPP` because cold initial entry, resumed thaw, and hot
re-entry each require a different completed inverse before owner settlement.
The next implementation must bind the tested owner-outcome model across all
of those branches, including synthetic/reflected exits, EPT handoffs, and
terminal errors, as one transaction.  It must not replace this fail-closed
boundary with partial handling.  Rootless evidence does not substitute for
the pending Intel L1/L2 and active-checkpoint qualification.

The nested entry/return matrix was replayed against the common startup owner.

needs refreeze, and a hot continuation needs either freeze publication or a

deferred owner resolution after their route-specific private publication.
The current source therefore continues to reject owner-bearing nested runs
after the sole proven pre-residency lifecycle exit.  This is the reviewed,
fail-closed implementation boundary until all of those inverses and their
settlements are installed as one source-ordered transaction.

The rootless verification lanes were rerun without relying on privileged
guest execution: the VMX nested model, its requirements and private-interface
ledgers, the sanitizer-backed VirtIO device harness, the snapshot model, the
snapshot portability validator, and a snapshot-enabled bhyve build all
passed.  The device harness exercised 604 core, 491 transport, 777 input,
and 99 RNG checks, including expected malformed-request and resource-failure
paths.  These are evidence for source/model correctness only; the handoff
continues to require root-run Linux and 5BSD split/packed, translated-DMA,

### 2026-08-06 — shared-memory callback and translated-DMA replay

The callback-backed shared-memory contract was traced through the modern BAR
read/write path, the GPU blob aperture, and the common DMA lease.  BAR access
holds the device mutex while locating a sealed backing; a callback must not
take that mutex again or change transport, queue, or lifecycle state.  The
contract now explicitly permits only the lock-free `vi_dma_acquire()`,
`vi_dma_release()`, and `vi_map_dma()` trio, which is the GPU's required
lease around its sparse-aperture state access.  The lease's atomic active
counter prevents a DMA-domain detach from clearing its provider while that
access is in flight, and the lifecycle fence prevents BAR callbacks during
reset, quiesce, suspend, or checkpoint pause.

The independent private-interface ledger, common harness, and a fresh

### 2026-08-06 — common checkpoint/suspend ownership replay

The shared modern-transport lifecycle was replayed from status negotiation
through guest suspend, nested checkpoint pause, restore validation, and final
resume.  `VIRTIO_F_SUSPEND` is offered only when a device supplies both drain
and restart callbacks.  The suspend transition first fences queue admission,
then drains the administration and device backends, and only afterwards
publishes `SUSPEND` while removing `DRIVER_OK`.  A failed drain sets
`NEEDS_RESET` before reopening admission; it cannot leave a briefly runnable
partially-drained device.

Checkpoint ownership is separate from guest suspend ownership.  A checkpoint
resume releases only its owner: it neither restarts backend sources nor emits
deferred configuration/queue notifications while the guest remains suspended.
Modern and common deferred-configuration latches are snapshot-validated as a
consistent pair, and malformed restored status combinations (including
SUSPEND without the negotiated feature, or SUSPEND with `DRIVER_OK`) are
rejected before publication.  The harness exercises successful and failed
drains/resumes, administration-fence failures, queue-notification fencing,
and deferred configuration delivery across the nested lifecycle order.

The common device harness, portable snapshot model, private-interface
validator, and warnings-as-errors bhyve build passed for this source state.
This does not replace privileged active-I/O suspend/checkpoint qualification
for each backend; those remain explicit Linux/5BSD release gates.

The common harness now also invokes `vi_pci_resume()` directly with a retained
guest-suspend owner.  It verifies that checkpoint release does not invoke the
post-resume source callback or notify a queue while guest suspension remains
active; the deferred configuration event is handed back to the transport
callback.  The modern-transport test separately verifies its paired latch.
This closes the prior test-only gap where that nested ownership case
was modeled at the modern-transport layer rather than exercising the common
checkpoint resume implementation.

The stateful existing-device paths were replayed from their common lifecycle

9P keeps an accepted guest session and fid namespace across guest suspend, but

a new destination generation.

Userspace and kernel-backed vsock stop every readiness source under the device

sources after common admission opens.  Portable checkpoint rejects live
connections or buffered host state; the kernel provider must additionally be
frozen, replay its feature epoch while still fenced, and thaw successfully
before sources can restart.  Failed freeze/thaw paths retain the fence or mark
the device `NEEDS_RESET`; they do not publish a running partial backend.

The corresponding console, 9P, and vsock snapshot/lifecycle harness cases,
the common harness, snapshot model, and source validators pass.  This is
rootless code evidence: the ledger continues to require Linux and rebuilt-5BSD

### 2026-08-06 — VirtIO-vsock transport ownership replay

The kernel VirtIO-vsock driver was replayed separately from the userspace

packet before re-registering its CID and resetting the domain.  The review

continuation freeze.  It is deliberately not yet called by the live VMCS02
loop.  Connecting only the first successful edge would let another return path
retire a common owner while retaining private residency; connecting it without
the post-entry routing would misreport a VMfail as an L2 exit.  The existing
`EOPNOTSUPP` owner fence therefore remains the correct fail-closed boundary.

The nested requirements/private-interface validator (433 and 277 entries),
the complete nested model build, and `git diff --check` pass after this replay.
The next implementation step is one audited conversion of *all* cold, resumed,
hot, event-reflection, and error-return routes to the owner transaction, followed
by Intel-host L1/L2 execution and snapshot qualification.  It must not be
enabled piecemeal or treated as a source-model success claim.

The production `vmm.ko` also builds in a fresh rootless object tree after this
review.  That is a compilation and source-contract gate only: the non-null
owner remains deliberately unavailable at runtime until the complete
transaction and its Intel-host qualification are in place.

### 2026-08-06 — shared-memory aperture boundary replay

The modern PCI shared-memory aperture was reviewed independently of device
registration.  Capability registration validates each range against its BAR,
and destination restore compares immutable topology rather than importing
source-owned BAR state.  The two backing-registration paths nevertheless used
`offset + length` overlap checks.  Those operands are valid for today’s
registrations, but the comparison itself was needlessly coupled to that
earlier validation and would be fragile if a future parser or restore adapter
provided topology directly.

Both direct-backing alias admission and callback-backing ambiguity rejection
now use one subtraction-based half-open interval helper.  It cannot overflow,
handles adjacent ranges at the `uint64_t` upper boundary correctly, and still
requires the same BAR and nonempty ranges.  A focused modern-transport test
exercises adjacent, overlapping, different-BAR, empty, and null-region cases,
including values immediately below `UINT64_MAX`.  The full rootless VirtIO
device harness and `git diff --check` pass after the change.  This is portable
common-device hardening; it neither changes an advertised feature nor claims
privileged shared-memory or DAX guest qualification.

### 2026-08-06 — portable checkpoint wire-format replay

The common checkpoint and VirtIO snapshot call graph was reviewed for
architecture leakage.  Common records encode scalar fields with explicit
little-endian helpers and fixed-width bounds.  The remaining raw-buffer uses
are intentionally byte-defined: guest-owned virtqueue memory, an opaque
administration-controller image whose producer/consumer are fenced by the
same binding, and a fixed-size, zero-tail-validated userspace-vsock pathname.
They are not native C structure serializations.  Device-private codecs retain
their own magic, version, bounded length, reserved-field, and destination
identity checks; changed capacity, export, backend, and feature contracts
fail closed rather than being coerced into a restore.

Independent fixed-byte little-endian vectors, hostile/truncated image tests,
destination-atomicity cases, and repeated-restore cases are present in the
rootless harness.  Its ASan/UBSan run completed with 1,991 checks and no
sanitizer finding.  This establishes a portable wire-format code gate; it
does not substitute for live cross-architecture restore qualification, which
remains unavailable until a non-x86 host is brought into the release matrix.

### 2026-08-06 — non-standard administration-state contract replay

The bhyve-specific administration-controller checkpoint contract was reviewed
separately from the VirtIO specification.  A binding holds command admission
in a lifecycle read lock only while quiesced; save, validation, restore, and
rollback therefore cannot race a newly admitted control command.  The common
snapshot transaction takes a backup before it attempts private restore and
uses that backup if a later section fails.  Administration resource, group,
queue-bank, and controller images are fixed-width little-endian formats with
exact-size, overlap, digest, and capability checks.  Restore validation is
performed before publication, and a destination that lacks a represented
operation or topology fails closed.

The dedicated administration, common-VirtIO snapshot, and hostile-image
harness cases passed under ASan/UBSan.  Remaining qualification is operational
rather than a rootless correctness gap: exercise administration queues,
groups, and their rollback behavior with Linux and 5BSD guests when those
optional features are enabled in the live matrix.

### 2026-08-06 — ACCESS_PLATFORM IOMMU lease and publication replay

The VirtIO-IOMMU request executor, PCI callbacks, and common DMA boundary were
traced as one transaction.  A common request first acquires its DMA lease,
then translates all descriptor addresses through the currently installed
domain, and releases the same lease on normal completion, malformed-chain
retirement, reset-stale retirement, and returned-chain paths.  The IOMMU state
records that lease per endpoint.  DETACH, mapping-removing UNMAP, endpoint
unregister, reset, snapshot, restore validation, and restore all reject or
defer while a relevant lease is active.  The final release resets deferred
state and invokes the PCI idle callback after dropping the state lock; that
callback retries a returned revoking request from a completion edge rather
than polling.

The translation authorization decision is made while holding the IOMMU mutex,
but host GPA mapping is deliberately invoked outside it.  The request lease
keeps the selected address space valid across that external callback, and the
common domain-install/clear gate keeps the callback table valid until every
request lease is retired.  New MAP operations are permitted while DMA is
active because they do not revoke an address already admitted; operations
which would revoke one return BUSY.  Fragmented readable/writable requests may
overlap only after bounded gathering into a private request buffer; response
fragments are pairwise disjoint and all metadata/live-state aliases are
rejected before state mutation or completion publication.

Focused IOMMU state/request/queue/PCI tests and the complete device harness
passed under ASan/UBSan.  Live translated-DMA, split/packed, active-I/O
checkpoint, and fault-injection qualification remain explicit privileged
gates; this source review does not claim an operational IOMMU guest matrix.

### 2026-08-06 — sound readiness and lifecycle serialization repair

The VirtIO-sound backend-ready callback serializes retained PCM ownership with
`vssc_mtx`, but the guest notification, full reset, selective queue reset, and
guest suspend paths had relied only on the common transport mutex.  Those are
different synchronization domains: a backend mevent can enter while a guest
or lifecycle callback is using the retained request.  That could race the
pending token, queue generation, stream claim, and readiness-event enable
state.

The affected paths now take the device-local mutex which already protects the
readiness and completion callbacks.  Full and selective reset therefore cancel
the retained owner under the same serialization as completion, and notification
cannot install a replacement while a stale callback retires its old event.
Suspend first closes async admission, then repeats that quiesce observation
while holding the mutex; unlike checkpoint pause, it releases the mutex before
returning because guest suspend has no paired retained-lock resume callback.
This remains event-driven and bounded: no polling or sleep was introduced.

The sanitizer-backed harness, including the direct sound PCI composition test,
passed after the repair.  A fresh snapshot-enabled `libvmmapi` plus bhyve
build also passed; the library must be built with the same snapshot option as
bhyve, because an ordinary library omits the snapshot entry points.  Live
OSS/null backend reset, suspend, packed queue,
and checkpoint qualification remain root-owned evidence, not implied by this
source-level fix.

### 2026-08-06 — filesystem backend and packed-ring ownership replay

The userspace filesystem backend was reviewed as an external asynchronous
contract.  Request admission, pending ownership, backend publication,
cancellation, queue-local reset, disconnect, and checkpoint pause take a
consistent queue-to-dispatch-to-pending lock order.  Selective reset first
retires unsent guest ownership and then cancels sent requests one at a time;
completion cannot publish into a reset queue.  Pause closes admission and
returns `EINPROGRESS` while real pending or outbox ownership remains, rather
than using a polling delay.  The stable session snapshot is taken only after
both sets drain.  No new lifecycle or publication defect was found.

The packed-ring engine was independently replayed against its
document-derived model.  It validates bounded queue geometry, uses the
two-wrap cursor space for event suppression, stages a complete multi-chain
completion before publishing any descriptor ownership, and tags outstanding
heads with both generation and wrap state.  Reset can discard staged work but
retains a live asynchronous lease until its callback retires it; a stale
callback cannot complete a new queue incarnation.  Exhaustive small-ring
threshold/wrap tests, malformed-chain tests, indirect-table tests, stale
completion tests, and checkpoint-cursor tests pass under ASan/UBSan.

Linux and 5BSD packed-ring activation, device-by-device queue-reset traffic,
and packed checkpoint-at-wrap qualification remain root-owned live gates.

### 2026-08-06 — qualification-run cancellation identity replay

The bounded qualification runner was reviewed separately from device-model
code because cancellation can leave real bhyve processes and host resources
behind.  The case wrapper captures the complete initial descendant tree before
asking the runner to perform its normal cleanup.  It now records each child as
its PID plus an exact SHA-256 digest of the process start-time and command
observation.  A later TERM or KILL is issued only if that same record still
matches, so a reused PID is not treated as an original case descendant.  The
wrapper remains event-driven from the manager's perspective: it records status
143 after bounded cleanup, and the manager releases only that case's CID lease.

`virtio-lab-selftest.sh` covers active cancellation, descendants, protected
run-directory ownership, stale-manager recovery, resume, and terminal status
publication.  It also asserts the SHA-256 identity format directly: PID reuse
cannot be made reliably fast enough for a normal test, so a future regression
to a bare PID or weak checksum fails before a managed qualification run.  It
passes after the change.  Real-VM soak remains a privileged
qualification gate; cancellation and cleanup must be exercised there with the
same managed run directory rather than by manually killing bhyve processes.

### 2026-08-06 — historical timer/APIC restore publication replay

The historical VATPIT snapshot layout stores output-latch bytes but omits the
cursor that makes a count latch pending.  Restoring such a checkpoint as an
idle latch would silently alter guest port-I/O results.  Save now captures one
locked candidate and returns `EBUSY` while any output latch is active; the
guest can consume the transient latch and retry without changing the wire
format.  Restore explicitly initializes the absent cursor to idle.

The historical VLAPIC records were also restored serially: a malformed record
for a later vCPU could publish earlier APIC and timer state.  Restore now uses
a bounded per-vCPU staging array, decodes the unchanged historical records,
validates every present vCPU, and only then publishes each timer-owned LAPIC.
This preserves the record ABI while making malformed multi-vCPU input
fail before any destination LAPIC is modified.

The requirements validator, its mutation self-test, the portable snapshot
model, and a fresh `MK_BHYVE_SNAPSHOT=yes` `vmm.ko` build pass.  Privileged
PIT active-latch and multi-vCPU corrupt-later-record checkpoint cases remain
explicit live evidence requirements.

### 2026-08-06 — nested-entry and portable-restore transaction replay

The nested-entry owner fence was replayed from the ordinary L1 lifecycle stop
through the first potential VMCS02, guest-MSR, EPT, or L2-event side effect.
The only common-owner consumption point remains the provably no-entry stop
before those effects.  Every later edge remains fail-closed until the complete
residency-specific entry/unwind transaction is integrated; this deliberately
returns `EOPNOTSUPP` instead of inventing a guest exit or consuming an owner
whose architectural outcome cannot yet be represented.

The rejected-entry resolver was checked separately.  A callback failure leaves
the context in `ENTRY_PENDING` by design, with the frozen origin and execution
identifier intact for a retry.  The resolver's unit test asserts precisely that
contract.  It is therefore not a leaked runtime owner and must not be replaced
by an unconditional cancellation path.

Portable inactive and active restore preconditions were also replayed.  Their
quiescence check is read-only; destination state, registry ownership, and
control MSRs are validated before publication.  The model covers malformed,
unsupported, occupied-owner, and output-alias cases with unchanged destination
state.  The requirements validator and portable snapshot model passed for this
review pass.  Live Intel nested execution and installed-kernel checkpoint
qualification remain separate privileged gates.

### 2026-08-06 — packed-ring oracle and lifecycle replay

The common packed engine was reviewed against the independent VirtIO 1.4
oracle rather than against bhyve layout definitions.  Descriptor availability
uses the two flag bits and the current wrap, cursor advancement permits every
legal queue size from one through 32768, and event delivery is compared with a
descriptor-by-descriptor model over the full two-wrap cursor space.  The model
also checks event thresholds at both wrap boundaries, reserved event values,
and descriptor IDs that differ from physical completion positions.

The engine's device-facing contract remains bounded: descriptor and completion
ownership is keyed by queue generation plus packed head/wrap, an asynchronous
completion is held in a queue-sized reorder table until the full logical
operation can be published, and reset retires completed records while retaining
live callbacks until they acknowledge their original generation.  Checkpoint
stores only portable cursors and wrap bits after the transient reorder table
has drained; it never serializes host pointers or callback ownership.

The rootless harness's completed visible phases reported all checks cleanly,
and the independent packed model plus the sanitizer nested model pass.  Full
Linux and rebuilt-5BSD packed activation, queue-reset-under-traffic, and
checkpoint-at-wrap remain privileged qualification gates.

### 2026-08-06 — translated-DMA restore ownership replay

The VirtIO-IOMMU state and queue paths were reviewed as the common
`ACCESS_PLATFORM` boundary.  Request gathering is bounded by the largest
defined request and produces a response only after the complete request has
been copied into private storage.  Snapshot rejects active DMA leases and
serializes only little-endian endpoint, domain, mapping, and fault records;
the mutable host generation is intentionally not portable state.

Restore decodes into private bounded arrays, checks destination geometry,
endpoint identity, mapping ranges and permissions, canonicalizes mappings,
and checks overlap before publication.  Preflight builds a separate prepared
fabric with fault and idle callbacks suppressed, so endpoint-ring validation
uses the incoming translations without publishing externally visible state.
The live fabric advances its local generation only after the full image is
accepted.  No new source-level defect was found.  Linux translated-DMA split
and packed cases, fault injection, active-DMA restore rejection, and real
multi-device `ACCESS_PLATFORM` qualification remain privileged gates.
