### 2026-08-06 — shared-memory and administration-state replay

The architecture-neutral shared-memory PCI and administration-queue paths
were reviewed from construction through BAR access, lifecycle fencing,
checkpoint encoding, restore validation, and publication.  Shared-memory
registration first proves that every nonempty region fits entirely within its
memory BAR without arithmetic wrap.  Regions can intentionally alias, but a
bound direct alias must name the same overlapping bytes with the same access
policy; callback aliases are rejected because that equivalence cannot be
proved.  Access continues past an unbound alias to a compatible bound alias,
so behavior does not depend on region-ID ordering.  Reads and writes accept
only defined widths, use little-endian byte conversion, and are fenced while
reset, quiesce, suspend, or a completed checkpoint pause owns the device.

The administration queue bank preallocates its bounded scratch buffers,
serializes a command per queue, and uses a reader/writer lifecycle barrier so
reset, snapshot, restore, and destruction drain admitted work without a
polling loop.  Its snapshot and restore records bind queue count and both
buffer capacities to a complete checksummed group-state payload.  Digest,
size, topology, storage-alias, and destination-shape failures occur before
live group publication.  The full rootless device harness was rerun under its
sanitizer configuration and completed with zero failed checks; its focused
tests cover BAR bounds, lifecycle replacement, sparse callback backing,
overlap policy, ID-independent alias lookup, queue-bank concurrency/drain,
and transactional restore.  No new source-level defect was found.  Shared
memory and administration virtqueues remain unadvertised until a production
consumer and root-owned Linux/5BSD activation evidence are available.

### 2026-08-06 — device operational-path replay

The GPU and virtio-fs snapshot paths were followed through their asynchronous
and publication edges.  The filesystem device takes a pause-owned serializer,
uses monotonic condition-variable waits for queue admission and backend
control completion, and restores against a normalized prepared destination
contract rather than image-owned identity data.  A failed post-quiesce capture
performs a real THAW rollback; a failed restored THAW preserves the exact
opaque state for retry.  The GPU decoder validates all retained resources and
destination DMA before swapping the resource table, then reconstructs
destination-local display and cursor objects outside the state mutex.  The
empty-image case clears presentation first, preventing stale scanout or cursor
state from surviving restore.

An operational sweep found no device polling loops.  `virtiofsd` uses blocking
`poll(2)` only as its descriptor-readiness event loop; device teardown and
control paths use condition variables or backend callbacks.  Queue work loops
are bounded by descriptor or I/O budgets, and reset drains have explicit
condition-variable deadlines with generation fences on timeout.  A fresh
paired source build of `libvmmapi`, bhyve, and `virtiofsd` completed with
`-Werror`.  A bare bhyve build in a new object tree is intentionally not a
valid check because it would link the older installed libvmmapi and omit the
new common memory APIs.

### 2026-08-06 — common suspend and packed-publication replay

The common lifecycle layer was replayed independently of individual device
callbacks.  Guest suspend and checkpoint pause establish a queue-admission
fence before asking a backend to drain.  Suspend failure sets NEEDS_RESET
before reopening that fence; checkpoint-pause failure either unquiesces the
administration path successfully or quarantines the device.  A failed
checkpoint resume retains checkpoint ownership for a later safe retry.  A
coalesced guest kick is replayed only after the active suspend/checkpoint
owner has released it.

The packed completion publisher was checked once more against the independent
oracle and the local requirement record.  A completed logical chain is
represented by its first descriptor with the used length, buffer ID, WRITE
result, and release-ordered ownership flags; later descriptors are covered by
the completed span.  That is the required head-publication representation,
not an accidental dependence on `VIRTIO_F_IN_ORDER`.  Requirement, private
interface, and nested requirement validators all pass after this pass, as does
the whitespace check.  The live Linux/5BSD packed, suspend, checkpoint, and
soak lanes remain explicit unexecuted evidence gates.

### 2026-08-06 — Intel nested lease and active-restore replay

The Intel-only VMCS02 resource boundary was reviewed separately from the
common startup-owner fence.  Entry materializes L1 I/O and MSR interception
bitmaps in private vCPU storage, binds an EPT02 root when required, and then
acquires the VMCS02 mapping leases.  The lease owner is copied before any
callback, callbacks run with re-entry blocked, partial acquisition is released
in reverse order, and neither a new resource generation nor a caller-visible
resource record is published until all acquisitions have succeeded.  EPT
unbind is performed before the non-fallible lease teardown, leaving a failed
unbind retryable with the complete generation still owned.

The hot-to-cold freeze operation captures a value-owned L2 continuation,
installs L1, and releases the exact resource generation.  Any failure after
detach either reconstructs the captured L2 image through the explicit rollback
operation or reports the frozen transaction incomplete; it does not silently
return with an ambiguous CPU-local VMCS02 association.  Active checkpoint
restore decodes L2 state into candidates, cross-checks VMCS12 launch epoch,
MTF and shadow-link state, constructs the continuation handoff, and selects
the destination registry owner as its final fallible step before publishing
the candidate outputs.

`vmx_nested_state_test` independently covers lease callback re-entry and
mutation, partial acquire rollback, stale release, l2-freeze rollback, active
restore aliases, and occupied-owner rejection.  The nested model, requirements
validator, and the fresh production `vmm.ko` build have passed.  The common
owner remains deliberately fail-closed for a hardware nested attempt until a
complete residency/unwind transaction is admitted; real Intel L1/L2 execution,
active restore, and soak remain root-only qualification work.

### 2026-08-06 — portable VMS2 and checkpoint-coordinator replay

The common VMS2 envelope was reviewed as a future non-x86 migration boundary.
It has a fixed little-endian header and section records, explicit version and
reserved-byte validation, ordered unique section keys, overflow-safe cursor
arithmetic, and a distinct handling rule for unknown critical records.  Common
VM/vCPU records and the x86 extension encode fixed-width fields into zeroed
wire staging; pointer-valued cookies remain only in transient coordinator,
lease, and callback objects.  The two-pass x86 transaction decoder validates
the complete source before it writes the private destination stage, and then
validates destination sparse-vCPU topology and x2APIC compatibility before a
backend can apply it.

The checkpoint coordinator fences event publishers by acquiring a group of
ingress leases under a transaction lock and in ascending vCPU order.  Waiters
use the event wait primitive rather than polling.  Group finish or abort
preflights every reopen error while all selected spin locks remain held; the
following commit loop cannot partially reopen a valid group.  Deferred event
bits are applied only by a documented non-sleeping, non-allocating,
non-reentrant callback while those locks still protect the value layer.  The
unit tests cover malformed envelopes, output aliases, duplicate/critical
sections, overflow, failed group begin/reopen, and deferred-event lifecycle.
No new source-level defect was found in this portability pass.  Live
cross-architecture migration remains a future qualification gate, not an
inference from these codecs.

### 2026-08-06 — VirtIO-SCSI event and backend-identity replay

The VirtIO-SCSI device was reviewed through its CTL source callback, guest
event queue, suspend/checkpoint fencing, and snapshot reconstruction path.
CTL records are read with a finite per-callback budget under the device lock,
validated before use, and translated into only the negotiated HOTPLUG or
CHANGE forms.  A source gap, malformed source record, source overflow, or
lost notification resets the loss-aware event state so the next delivered
guest event carries the missed indication; events received before DRIVER_OK or
for a declined feature advance source continuity without inventing a guest
event.  Multimedia parameter changes are filtered as required by the device
specification.

The pause path admits no new request callback, drains already-consumed
requests using a bounded condition-variable wait, and remembers the exact
queue incarnations it may resume.  Guest suspend transfers that ownership
without letting checkpoint resume reopen the queue early.  Snapshot encoding
uses explicit little-endian fields and a versioned opaque CTL inventory
document.  Restore validates the entire record and local topology before it
queries CTL, then requires byte-exact inventory identity before publishing
cached configuration; destination-local event subscriptions are intentionally
reconstructed as a loss-aware rescan rather than serialized.

The independent SCSI event/unit harness covers ring overflow and recovery,
sequence gaps, skipped declined events, malformed guest event chains, CTL
source validation, suspend ownership transfer, snapshot mismatch, and
guest-visible wire lengths.  No new source-level defect was found.  Root-only
Linux and 5BSD hotplug/change, active-command checkpoint, and extended CTL
event soak remain required qualification lanes.

### 2026-08-06 — VirtIO-balloon optional-queue and snapshot replay

The balloon model was replayed through the optional queue layout, retained
statistics ownership, configuration transitions, host-memory operations, and
the versioned `BAL1` state image.  Queue indices remain the fixed VirtIO
indices: enabling page reporting exposes queue 4, while each intervening
statistics or free-page-hint queue reports size zero unless its own feature is
offered.  This prevents a guest from discovering an operational-looking
optional queue without negotiating the feature that defines it.  The model
uses one event-loop timer to refresh at most one retained statistics chain;
selective reset revokes stale ownership and checkpoint pause completes valid
ownership before state is saved.  A stale retained request makes the device
request reset rather than publishing a checkpoint whose queue ownership cannot
be reconstructed.

The `BAL1` decoder validates its magic and version before treating a partial
image as a layout, validates all feature-dependent fields before publication,
and transforms the PFN bitmap through a reversible host-memory transaction.
If a host discard/undiscard operation cannot be undone, the destination is
marked restore-incomplete and requires reset.  The image records architectural
configuration such as page poison and free-page-hint command phase, but never
tries to reconstruct a live descriptor from copied request metadata.  The
independent balloon tests cover fixed optional queue topology, command and
page-buffer forms, stale command handling, retained-statistics lifecycle,
malformed and truncated state, repeated restore, and rollback failure.  No new
source-level defect was found.  Linux/5BSD split and packed activation,
memory-pressure, and long reset/checkpoint soak remain explicit root-only
qualification requirements in the ledger.

### 2026-08-06 — VirtIO-console lifecycle and backend-identity replay

The console model was reviewed through multipport feature gating, selective
queue reset, host socket ownership, suspend/resume, and its `CON1` state
record.  Port zero remains usable without MULTIPORT; control queues and
additional port queues are inactive until the defining feature is negotiated.
Receive queue reset clears the host-read readiness latch for only that queue
incarnation and disables the associated event source, so stale host input
cannot be associated with a reconfigured descriptor queue.  Resume re-arms
only queues that still contain guest descriptors, including the control queue,
without waiting for an unrelated future kick.

Checkpoint pause holds the device serializer and rejects a connected host
socket, pending buffered host output, or live connection event registration.
The passive listener is destination configuration and remains reconstructible.
`CON1` has an explicit little-endian discriminator and validates complete
feature/config/port identity before applying any state; a source image cannot
import a live host connection and an identity mismatch leaves destination port
state untouched.  The independent test suite covers control lifecycle order,
queue-local reset, suspend/rearm, partial host writes, disconnect/error paths,
multiport feature gating, malformed/truncated snapshots, active-socket
rejection, and backend name/path mismatch.  No new source-level defect was
found.  Packed and multiport Linux/5BSD live lanes, blocked endpoint races,
and backend-reconnect policy remain root-only promotion requirements.

### 2026-08-06 — VirtIO-9P request-drain and export-identity replay

The 9P transport was reviewed through request admission, callback completion,
full and queue-local reset, guest suspend, checkpoint, and export confinement.
Accepted requests retain their queue generation and either publish to that same
incarnation or are discarded after reset; the final stale callback completes a
pending selective reset without closing the lib9p connection.  Full reset
serializes connection replacement with the same monotonic condition-variable
wait used by suspend, and intentionally discards kicks belonging to the old
queue incarnation.  There is no manual sleep or unbounded spin path.

Guest suspend waits only for already-admitted requests and preserves the
connection/fid namespace after they drain.  Checkpoint is deliberately more
restrictive: active requests, a pending reset, missing connection, or any
fid-bearing session is rejected because those objects contain backend-private
host state.  The sole current `V9P2` image carries fixed-width little-endian connection
limits, mount tag, features, read-only policy, and export identity, validates
them against the destination before publication, and creates a new destination
generation rather than importing asynchronous completion ownership.  The
export root is opened as a descriptor-relative confined object before
Capsicum rights are narrowed, keeping later lib9p lookups below the configured
directory.  The independent tests cover malformed chains, stale callbacks,
queue-reset completion, full reset drain, suspend success/timeout, checkpoint
identity/truncation/repeat behavior, and active-fid rejection.  No new
source-level defect was found.  Root-only Linux/5BSD packed, confinement,
active-request reset, and long fid/reconnect qualification remains tracked.

### 2026-08-06 — VirtIO-input frame, reset, and state replay

The input device was replayed across the evdev event callback, frame staging,
queue reset, guest suspend, checkpoint pause, and `INP1` restore.  Event-loop
work is bounded to one guest-ring-sized host batch.  A normal host frame is
published only at `SYN_REPORT`, after every event has a valid writable guest
buffer; an incomplete guest frame is returned or retired in ring order rather
than partially exposed.  Host `SYN_DROPPED`, allocation exhaustion, and a
frame too large for the active guest queue all produce the minimal
`SYN_DROPPED`/`SYN_REPORT` resynchronization contract.

Full reset and event-queue reset discard staged frame state and drain the
nonblocking host descriptor while the VirtIO mutex is held.  Thus input read
before a reset cannot cross into a new queue incarnation even if the guest
rapidly re-enables it.  Guest suspend likewise drops an in-progress host frame
rather than joining it to post-resume data.  Checkpoint pause disables the
event source before taking the device mutex; `INP1` validates identity,
zero-reserved configuration, bounded frame count, and the only legal
resynchronization shapes before atomically replacing staged state.  The
independent tests cover scatter/gather byte order, malformed descriptor and
status chains, loss recovery, ring-boundary frames, reset drain/re-enable,
config selection, checkpoint source lifecycle, and malformed/repeated restore.
No new source-level defect was found.  Linux and rebuilt-5BSD packed,
IN_ORDER, multi-device, reset-under-injection, and checkpoint lanes remain
root-only promotion requirements.

### 2026-08-06 — VirtIO-RNG source and save-state replay

The entropy device was reviewed for source ownership and checkpoint behavior.
It has no private snapshot payload: the host random descriptor and every byte
obtained from it are destination-local, while common queue state is the only
state captured after normal quiescence.  This avoids treating entropy as a
replayable device resource.  Each synchronous request has a 64 KiB source-read
bound, requires writable nonempty descriptors, and preserves in-order
completion semantics.  Interrupted reads retry; zero-length, unavailable, or
other failed reads return the acquired chain and request reset because the
model deliberately has no readiness source on which to retain it safely.

The independent tests cover descriptor direction, scatter/gather and partial
fill, request/read source failures, bounded work, explicit modern packed
opt-in, in-order completion, and the common-only snapshot contract.  No new
source-level defect was found.  Linux and rebuilt-5BSD split/packed,
reset/rebind, active-checkpoint, and entropy-source-failure qualification
remain root-only gates.

### 2026-08-06 — Common packed-virtqueue ownership and publication

The shared packed-ring path was rechecked from descriptor acquisition through
out-of-order completion staging, event suppression, queue reset, and portable
snapshot restoration.  The implementation treats a packed buffer as one used
descriptor: for a direct scatter/gather chain it overwrites the chain head with
the buffer ID read from the final available descriptor, then advances both
device and driver cursors by the complete descriptor span.  This matches the
VirtIO 1.4 packed-ring chaining rule; the remaining descriptors are skipped,
not independently completed.  Group completion first validates every member
and stages all metadata, then publishes from tail to head so the head makes the
entire group visible atomically to a polling driver.

The queue-owned completion table is bounded by queue size and its owner state
contains the head wrap generation.  Completion, rollback, reset cancellation,
and restore each consume that lease exactly once.  Snapshot rejects transient
packed or split ownership, serializes only bounded cursor/wrap state in
fixed-width little-endian fields, allocates a destination-local empty reorder
cache during restore, and invalidates the destination queue generation rather
than importing source callback authority.  The engine test derives ownership,
advance, event-crossing, and cursor expectations from the independent VirtIO
1.4 fixture, including exhaustive small-ring event spaces; core tests cover
wrap, group gaps, duplicate/stale completion, indirect lists, reset and cache
replacement transactions.  No source-level defect was found.  Live packed
qualification on every advertised device, Linux and rebuilt-5BSD activation,
MSI/MSI-X, selective-reset under traffic, and checkpoint-at-wrap root gates
remain mandatory before feature advertisement.

### 2026-08-06 — VMS2 private snapshot-builder boundary

The portable VMS2 envelope and x86 transaction codecs were reviewed as
caller-owned private kernel interfaces, including range arithmetic, aliasing,
canonical ordering, unknown-critical-section behavior, two-pass decode, and
destination topology preflight.  Two defensive defects were corrected: the
builder accepted a caller-corrupted cursor below the fixed envelope header,
which could make a later `add` overwrite the header before `finalize` rejected
the resulting image; and it trusted caller-owned last-section metadata, which
could append an out-of-order section that the reader would only reject later.
A shared invariant check now validates retained section headers, payload
bounds, canonical ordering, the terminal marker, cursor, and section count
before either `add` or `finalize` mutates or publishes state.  The focused
envelope suite compiled with the normal strict warnings and all eleven ATF
cases passed, including the new corrupted-builder regressions.

The codec remains architecture-neutral: all wire values are fixed-width
little-endian, the reader exposes bounded immutable payload views only, and
the x86 material is a separate typed section rather than native-structure
serialization.  The remaining work is integration qualification, not a claim
of production migration: root-only tests still need live source/destination
restore, injected transaction copyout and event-ingress failures, destination
CPU-contract mismatch, and active device/backend reconstruction on supported
architectures.

### 2026-08-06 — Event-driven lifecycle and nonstandard-interface audit

The common device paths and the private backend boundaries were reviewed for
fixed-delay polling, unbounded hot-path work, and teardown ownership.  Network
TX, block, SCSI, 9P, pmem, and filesystem drains wait on condition-variable
predicates rather than retry sleeps.  Their deadlines are explicit failure
bounds: a timeout preserves the generation fence and either rolls admission
back or requests reset; it is never treated as a completed drain.  Network
also bounds each TX batch, so a continuously busy queue yields to the shared
worker rather than monopolising it.  The filesystem checkpoint control path
is woken by backend event completion and uses a monotonic condition-variable
deadline, not a periodic status poll.

The userspace vsock backend does have one 1000 ms event-loop timer.  It is not
a descriptor-processing poll: it exists solely to enforce protocol timeouts
for a silent guest and to detect a host peer that disappeared while host reads
were disabled by flow control.  All socket probes are nonblocking, are
rate-limited by the timer, and are disabled with every other host readiness
source before suspend or checkpoint.  Timer deletion uses the synchronous
mevent deletion path before freeing the softc, while callbacks recheck the
lifecycle fence under the device mutex.  That closes the selected-callback
versus pause/destroy race without a sleep-based grace period.

The private-interface ledger validator covers every unsupported VirtIO return
and AF_VSOCK provider boundary.  The manual audit found no additional source
defect in these paths.  Remaining promotion gates are root-only: faulting each
deadline path with a live backend, exercising event-loop teardown under load,
and long concurrent pause/reset/checkpoint soak on Linux and rebuilt-5BSD.

### 2026-08-06 — Common checkpoint coordinator lock and wakeup audit

The architecture-neutral event-checkpoint coordinator was reviewed separately
from the device models.  It serializes membership and lifecycle transitions
under its transaction mutex, then takes selected ingress spin locks in strict
ascending vCPU order.  Per-vCPU publishers and startup claim completion drop
their entry spin lock before signalling the shared wait channel, so they do
not invert the transaction-to-entry lock order.  Checkpoint readiness arms the
sleepqueue generation before testing the retained group predicate, releases
both the entry locks and transaction mutex before sleeping, and always
rechecks after a wakeup.  That prevents both the signal-before-sleep gap and a
sleepable-mutex acquisition from an interrupt-adjacent publisher.

Reopen deliberately invokes the deferred-event adapter while the selected
ingress locks remain held, before reopening becomes visible.  The callback
contract is therefore narrow and explicit: it may only perform non-sleeping,
non-allocating, non-reentrant merge work.  The amd64 adapter meets that rule:
it merges transient idempotent event bits under the vCPU event owner and
defers notification until after coordinator locks are released.  No lock-order
or missed-wakeup defect was found.  Installed-kernel races involving NMI,
ExtINT, publisher drain, cancellation, and checkpoint abort remain root-only
qualification gates.

### 2026-08-07 — Nested owner transaction and test-orchestrator replay

The staged nested-VMX entry-owner path was re-read as a complete transaction,
not as an invitation to remove the current fail-closed boundary in
`vmx_run_nested()`.  The common owner has distinct `ENTRY_PENDING`, pre-entry
deferred, and post-entry deferred states.  The Intel-private outcome adapter
then binds a hardware-attempt classification to the exact rollback,
refreeze, freeze, or terminal-detach result before it settles the common
owner.  This preserves three facts that must never be conflated: an attempted
VM entry is not proof that L2 executed; a private terminal detach overrides a
replayable guard result; and an unhandled real L2 exit cannot become
returnable before the route-specific freeze or publication completes.  The
production nested run continues to reject an attached common owner until that
whole sequence is installed source-atomically.  No safe partial connection was
identified, so none was made.

The test-lab replay also confirmed that reset verification uses the guest
driver and device-manager completion boundary rather than a fixed host sleep:
the block helper discovers the rebound PCI child and waits, with a bounded
deadline, for its actual block-special node before digest I/O.  The full soak
profile deliberately performs expensive data-path validation periodically and
the smoke profile validates every reset; neither should be represented as an
all-cycle data-integrity proof.  Cancellation remains mediated through the
supervised case wrapper so its descendant teardown and terminal status remain
atomic; it is not safe to kill the daemon supervisor directly.

The current rootless gates passed under AddressSanitizer and UndefinedBehavior
Sanitizer: the nested requirements/evidence/live-staging validators (346
model cases), the portable snapshot model (30 cases), and the host helper
self-tests.  This is source/model evidence only.  Intel L1/L2 execution,
Linux and rebuilt-5BSD feature activation, active checkpoint restore, and
bounded soak remain the recorded root-only promotion gates.

The lab now also has a rootless interruption/recovery regression.  It starts
a supervised case with a separately recorded descendant, terminates only the
lab manager, verifies that the manager lease remains until the manager PID is
gone, and resumes the same immutable run configuration.  The resumed manager
must emit `REATTACH`, wait for that original wrapper, publish one success, and
remove the recovered lease.  This distinguishes an operator interrupt (which
is recoverable through `--resume`) from `virtio-lab cancel` (which must enter
the wrapper so it can terminate its bounded descendant tree and publish status
143).  The test does not claim signal-driven scheduler cleanup; it proves the
safe recovery behavior of the daemon-supervisor model.

### 2026-08-07 — VMCS02 hardware-report boundary replay

The Intel nested hardware-return path was reviewed from `vmx_enter_guest()`
through report capture, value classification, the initial/resumed completion
adapters, and the selected private unwind.  The reader captures a VMCS02 exit
only for an actual VM exit; VMfail has no exit image.  It constructs the
report and captured exit in local candidates and publishes both only after
the entry instruction, VMCS identity, and VMfail status agree.  The pure
classifier then maps a normal exit, L1-visible rejection, and L0 failure to
distinct immutable plans.  Initial rollback, resumed refreeze, hot freeze,
and fatal hot detachment remain distinct inverse operations.  No safe point
exists to settle the common entry owner between the machine instruction and
that classification plus inverse; the installed owner fence remains
fail-closed.

The independent state test now also rejects raw hardware-report values below
and above the ABI range at both construction and classification boundaries,
and proves that each rejection preserves an already published caller output.
The complete rootless `vmx_nested_state_test` passed 163 cases after this
addition.  The source ledger validator continues to map 433 nested
requirements and 277 private nonstandard interfaces.  This is not evidence
of executing VMX instructions: Intel L1/L2, entry-failure injection,
interrupt/EPT/VPID behavior, active save/restore, and bounded multi-VM soak
remain privileged qualification gates.

### 2026-08-07 — SCSI and vsock reconstruction replay

The SCSI checkpoint callback was reviewed from the common pause fence through
its CTL dependency.  It serializes a fixed little-endian private record,
checks the complete destination topology before querying CTL, and compares the
complete CTL LUN inventory before publishing configuration.  CTL descriptors,
subscriptions, and event sequence numbers remain destination-local.  Restore
therefore emits one loss-aware rescan boundary instead of replaying stale LUN
events.  Its focused model test covers malformed/truncated records, topology
and backend drift, and repeated restore; no source defect was found.

The same review of both vsock backends confirms that a portable checkpoint
contains no host socket, kernel-provider buffer, or provider file descriptor.
Userspace checkpoint is permitted only with no connection, control, pending,
reassembly, or transmit-buffer state.  Kernel-provider checkpoint additionally
requires a successful empty-provider FREEZE and reconstructs its negotiated
feature epoch before THAW.  Provider freeze, malformed checkpoint reply,
feature replay, and thaw failures retain a retryable admission fence or mark
the device reset-required.  The rootless test now explicitly repeats the same
restore transaction for userspace and frozen-kernel backends before resume;
both paths preserve identity and allocator state.  Focused tests, the full
device harness, and its AddressSanitizer/UBSan replay passed.  This deliberately
does not claim migration of active vsock connections; that remains a
root-only live qualification requirement.

### 2026-08-07 — common VirtIO lifecycle and restore-transaction replay

This pass started at the common ownership boundaries rather than at an
individual device.  Checkpoint pause and guest suspend are independent,
nested fences: checkpoint resume releases only checkpoint ownership, retains a
guest-suspended backend, and does not restart queue sources until the guest
later resumes.  Configuration changes and notifications observed while either
fence is held are latched and replayed only after the final relevant owner
opens admission.  Failed pause or resume work publishes `NEEDS_RESET` before
the common quiesce fence is released, preventing a notifier from consuming a
new descriptor in a partially drained state.

The portable restore transaction stages the common/modern transport state,
queue mappings, and administration controller state.  It restores the admin
controller before device-private publication, rolls it back on a subsequent
failure, and quarantines an irrecoverably partial destination with
`NEEDS_RESET`.  The device callback ABI explicitly requires a failed restore
to preserve both device and external-backend state; balloon, GPU, filesystem,
IOMMU, memory, PMEM, RTC, and sound callbacks were checked against their
staged decode/restore tests.  This is reinforced by common tests for admin
rollback, malformed wire state, repeated restore, incomplete-restore
quarantine, deferred configuration, and checkpoint-inside-suspend ordering.

The nonstandard-interface, snapshot-portability, DMA-boundary, and nested-VMX
requirements validators passed in this replay (97 private VirtIO entries and
433 nested requirements, with 282 nested private-boundary entries).  The
virtiofsd control loop was also checked: it blocks in `poll`, bounds per-event
work, and handles error/hangup readiness rather than polling or spinning.
These are source/model and sanitizer-quality checks.  Linux/5BSD active-I/O
checkpoint, reset, migration, and long-run soak remain the root-only proof.

### 2026-08-07 — isolated optional-build replay

An ordinary incremental `make` in the existing object directory reported
undefined snapshot symbols because that directory contained a mixture of
objects compiled with and without `BHYVE_SNAPSHOT`.  That is an object-tree
hygiene issue, not a source-level configuration mismatch.  Clean, isolated
object trees were used to build the matching `libvmmapi` and then bhyve with
`MK_BHYVE_SNAPSHOT=yes`, and independently to build bhyve with
`MK_BHYVE_SNAPSHOT=no`; both linked cleanly with the normal warnings treated
as errors.  The build-mode validator likewise passed for both modes.  Future
package/world builds should keep one object directory per option set.

### 2026-08-07 — portable codec and kernel-module replay

The next definition-first pass inspected the portable GPU, memory, input, and
sound device codecs.  Their version selectors and scalar fields use explicit
fixed-width encodings; destination identity and capacity contracts are tested
before restored state is published, and host-side restore failures retain the
common incomplete-restore fence.  No new actionable portability or
failure-atomicity issue was found.  Production paths contain no manual sleep
or polling loops; their progress ownership is event, condition-variable, or
bounded-deadline based.

The production `vmm.ko` module also rebuilt cleanly with warnings as errors
after the nested VMX review.  This confirms compilation and linkage of the
Intel-specific implementation on this source tree; it does not replace the
pending privileged Intel VMX execution, L1/L2, checkpoint, and soak gates.

The same nonstandard-interface replay found and corrected one callback
stability gap in `vmx_nested_hardware_entry_finish()`: the event callback pair
was read after a hardware callback had already run.  It is now copied before
the first hardware operation and the transaction invokes only that immutable
pair.  The regression mutates the mutable event table from both the hardware
commit and rollback callbacks and verifies that the original entered/abort
operation, not the substituted callback, is still invoked.  This change is
local to the Intel adapter; the common state-machine contract and portable
snapshot encoding are unchanged.

The callback-table pass then extended to the two Intel capture adapters that
perform a sequence of hardware reads.  `vmx_nested_entry_environment_capture`
and `vmx_nested_software_msr_capture` now copy their read-operation table
before the first sample.  Their independent regressions replace the live
table during that first callback and require the remaining fields to use the
original reader; a substituted reader is never reached and the completed
capture remains canonical.  This is a private adapter integrity rule, not a
new architectural VMX behavior or a portable save-state field.

### 2026-08-07 — Hot-to-cold handoff immutability

The follow-on private-boundary review covered the value-only VM-exit and
VM-entry-rejection handoffs.  Both adapters previously handed a pointer into
their retained state directly to the private commit callback and assumed the
callback left the owner untouched.  Each now snapshots both the operation
table and the request, invokes the callback with only the local request, and
compares the retained handoff through semantic field equality afterwards.  A
callback that nevertheless reaches the owner through its private context and
changes either the state or payload is detected; the exact original request
is restored to `PENDING` and the operation returns `EPROTO`.  A clean success
is the only path that becomes `RESOLVED`.

`nested_handoff_callback_boundary` independently corrupts both forms of
handoff from their callbacks, checks that no altered exit/failure record is
published, then retries through the unmodified callback and consumes the
original record.  It also guards the no-native-representation rule: semantic
equality helpers are used instead of `memcmp` for Intel-private state.  The
change remains confined to the dormant Intel nested-VMX path; it adds no
guest ABI, feature bit, snapshot field, or readiness claim.

The same review then covered the hot-to-cold continuation handoff used after
an L2 exit.  It now snapshots its operation table and continuation request,
receives its result in local storage, and rejects callback mutation of the
retained owner.  On a violation it restores the complete pending request and
prior result before returning `EPROTO`; no modified exit sequence, portable
generation, or completion disposition can be consumed.  The existing
`nested_l0_continuation_handoff` regression now injects both state and
sequence corruption through the callback before proving a clean retry.  This
is again an Intel-private lifecycle hardening, not an implementation of live
nested VMX or a change to the portable save-state interface.

VMCS02 commit application received the same boundary treatment.  The apply
adapter now receives a local value copy of the prospective image and a copied
operation table, never a pointer to the retained commit object.  It rejects
operation-table aliasing and detects any callback that reaches back through
private context to change commit state, restoring the canonical image and
`PENDING` state before returning `EPROTO`.  The VMCS02 composition regression
injects that state mutation and proves the next clean apply remains valid.
This strengthens the private hardware-programming adapter only; it does not
serialize a hardware VMCS or enable nested execution.

The next review scope is the full VMX instruction-handoff engine.  It already
copies its callback table before the first frozen-vCPU operation, but its
request spans the complete VMXON/VMCLEAR/VMPTRLD/VMREAD/VMWRITE/invalidation
surface.  A correct owner-mutation detector there requires a new fieldwise
semantic comparison for that entire architectural request/result pair; a
native-object comparison would violate the project’s representation rule.
This has therefore been recorded as follow-up work rather than papered over
with `memcmp` or a partial comparison.  The current rootless VirtIO validator
passes its 232 requirements, 683 independent oracle definitions, and 97
private interfaces; its live-activation ledger still correctly reports the
privileged Linux and 5BSD feature claims that need host execution.

That follow-up is now complete.  `vmx_nested_instruction_handoff` has
fieldwise equality for every architectural request/result component and runs
the full frozen instruction transaction through a local handoff owner.  Only
after all memory, VMCS, region, and invalidation callbacks return does it
compare the retained owner and publish the local outcome.  Callback mutation
restores the original pending owner and returns `EPROTO`.  The instruction
handoff regression injects state and RFLAGS corruption during the VMXON
operand read, verifies no altered result is published, and proves a clean
retry succeeds.  No native-layout comparison, guest ABI change, or nested
execution readiness change was introduced.

### 2026-08-07 — Portable lifecycle, envelope, and nested-boundary replay

This replay rechecked the common VirtIO pause/suspend/checkpoint fence and the
portable VMS2 envelope separately from the Intel-only adapters.  Queue
admission is closed before a backend drain begins; a failed drain requests
reset before reopening admission, and a deferred notification is replayed only
after the original owner has been restored.  The envelope remains a
fixed-width little-endian, type/instance ordered container.  Its reader
continues to reject a changed image without advancing either cursor or output;
callers must nevertheless stage untrusted input in immutable kernel-owned
memory before creating a reader.  No portable code depends on an Intel VMCS,
native object layout, host pointer, host file descriptor, page size, or word
size.

The matching Intel-private replay completed the full VMX instruction-handoff
transaction.  Hardware-entry finish, environment capture, MSR capture,
VM-exit, VM-entry rejection, continuation, VMCS02 application, and the full
instruction handoff all snapshot their callback table before the first
callback.  The retained owner is compared semantically after each callback;
unexpected retained-owner mutation restores the original pending value and
returns `EPROTO`.  The production `vmx_run_nested()` boundary remains
fail-closed: these are reviewed building blocks, not a claim that nested L2
execution has been enabled.

Rootless evidence after this replay is: the 433-row nested requirement ledger,
the 282-row non-standard-interface inventory, all 12 tracked live
qualification groups, the 164-case nested state model, the portable
snapshot-envelope model, the VirtIO requirement/oracle validators, and the
virtio-lab interruption/recovery self-test.  Strict-warning builds and
`git diff --check` passed.  The required privileged evidence is deliberately
unchanged and must be run on the rebuilt kernel: Linux and rebuilt-5BSD device
activation (including packed rings and multiqueue where advertised), active
checkpoint/restore, translated-DMA/IOMMU paths, bounded reset/soak cases, and
Intel L1/L2 VMX instruction, EPT/VPID, interrupt/timer, migration, and
concurrency qualification.  A cancelled soak is not evidence of a device
failure; record its terminal wrapper status and rerun either the bounded
`soak-smoke` gate or the complete `soak` gate to obtain valid evidence.

### 2026-08-07 — owner-boundary and test-runner replay

The production `vmx_run_nested()` source was traced alongside the ordinary

after `VMX_GUEST_VMEXIT`, or abort it after a proved VMfail, because it has no
additional nested continuation to freeze.  The L2 loop cannot yet make that
substitution: a rejected initial entry, resumed refreeze, EPT walk, direct L1
reflection, a handled L0 exit followed by re-entry, and a post-entry hot
freeze each require a different private inverse before a common result is
allowed to become returnable.  The source therefore deliberately accepts a
non-null owner only for the outer no-side-effect lifecycle return and otherwise
returns `EOPNOTSUPP` before guest MSRs or VMCS02 state are touched.  The
host-only `vmm,vmx,nested,withheld` probe records that policy decision.  This
is an intentional incomplete-integration boundary, not a claim that VMX
hardware activation has been tested or enabled.

The value-model side was rerun directly: all 164 independently enumerated
`vmx_nested_state_test` cases passed, and the portable snapshot-envelope test
exports 11 cases.  The source ledger validator passed with 433 requirements,
282 private-interface records, and 12 live qualification groups.  The
aggregate runner remains a convenience wrapper; its completion must be
recorded only when it emits its final `PASS nested-vmx cases=...` line.  Do not
infer that aggregate result merely from its build or validator preamble.

### 2026-08-07 — ACCESS_PLATFORM/IOMMU boundary replay

The common DMA lease and VirtIO-IOMMU publication paths were reviewed from
topology construction through feature acceptance, request mapping, active-DMA
revocation, reset, and portable-state staging.  `ACCESS_PLATFORM` is removed
unless a modern, eligible endpoint has an installed domain; accepting it
without the installed binding is rejected during the modern `FEATURES_OK`
transition.  Domain install and removal close a detaching gate and require
the common active-request count to be zero, while each established lease keeps
the provider table valid until its release.  The IOMMU provider is deliberately
not attached as its own translated endpoint, and a multi-provider topology is
rejected pending explicit device-group ownership.

Fresh focused model binaries built with strict warnings.  The active-DMA
state-transfer fence, deferred-revocation retry, and ambiguous/empty topology
negative cases passed.  This demonstrates source-level correctness of the
common boundary, not full qualification: translated Linux and 5BSD I/O,
interrupt/reset/checkpoint interactions, and bounded concurrent-device soak
remain root-only release gates.

### 2026-08-07 — shared-memory lifecycle symmetry

The portable modern-PCI shared-memory path was traced across capability
registration, topology sealing, destination-local backing installation and
revocation, BAR access fencing, suspend, checkpoint pause, reset, and restore.
Guest BAR accesses are rejected while reset, quiesce, suspend, or checkpoint
pause owns the device transition.  The review found that revoke accepted the
two latter owner states while install rejected them whenever the guest had a
nonzero status.  That made a destination-local backing replacement impossible
during the very states which safely fence guest access, unless the device was
unnecessarily reset and its negotiated state discarded.

Installation and revocation now accept the same four fenced lifecycle owners:
reset, quiesce, suspend, and checkpoint pause.  The backing remains explicitly
host-local and is never serialized; the checkpoint topology remains only the
immutable PCI capability description.  Focused independent harness cases now
exercise direct and callback backing revoke/rebind under both suspend and
checkpoint pause, along with alias lookup.  The strict-warning focused harness
build, these cases, and `git diff --check` pass.  Live shared-memory devices
(notably GPU blobs and pmem) still require their saved root-only Linux/5BSD
activation, active-checkpoint, and destination-backend identity gates.

### 2026-08-07 — shared-memory consumer and portability follow-up

The two current shared-memory consumers were reviewed against the common
runtime-backing contract.  GPU uses a callback aperture because blob resources
are sparse and dynamically mapped.  Modern BAR dispatch holds the transport
mutex, the callback takes only the documented lock-free DMA lease, and GPU
state takes its own mutex.  Queue processing releases the GPU-state mutex
before invoking presentation callbacks, so the audit found no inverse
transport/GPU-state lock acquisition.  Focused PCI, queue, and state tests
passed for the blob endian adapter, DMA-domain lease ownership, malformed
chains, blob snapshots, and transactional restore.

Pmem instead uses a fixed, locked host mapping.  Its worker is drained before
reset, suspend, or checkpoint stabilization; its portable record contains only
the backing size and explicit identity, never the host mapping or descriptor.
The immutable shared-memory capability topology is independently compared
before a modern-PCI restore publishes state.  The review found no further
shared-memory lifecycle or host-pointer serialization defect.  Real GPU and
pmem activation, packed-ring behavior, destination identity changes, and
active-I/O restore remain root-only Linux/5BSD qualification gates.

### 2026-08-07 — multi-provider vsock ownership follow-up

The host-side `/dev/vsock` transport is intentionally one stable AF_VSOCK
transport object, not one global provider.  It multiplexes CID-hashed provider
records, resolves a provider under the protocol mutex for each transmit,
credit, reset, and receive operation, and never retains a provider pointer
after dropping that mutex.  Provider close resets only PCBs for that CID,
purges only that provider's queue, recomputes aggregate socket-type capability,
and leaves other CIDs runnable.  Feature/reset/freeze paths close admission and
wait on explicit state-change wakeups with a bounded deadline rather than
polling.  No cross-CID routing, stale-provider, or global-teardown defect was
found in this review pass.

The saved privileged gates remain meaningful: duplicate-CID attach races,
1,024-provider scale, active provider checkpoint, MAC capability isolation,
and many-VM live backend soak must still run on the test host.

### 2026-08-07 — virtio-fs and translated-DMA lifecycle replay

The virtio-fs request path was traced through submission, bounded outbox
publication, asynchronous completion, selective queue reset, cancellation,
disconnect, backend reconnect fencing, quiesce/thaw, and portable state
staging.  Quiesce and thaw use the device condition variable with a monotonic
deadline; the wait releases the filesystem device mutex so the readiness
callback can make the control transaction progress.  Completion and discard
callbacks run after the queue mutex is dropped, and a selective reset retains
its fence until the final sent request has retired.  The review found no
polling loop, owner lifetime leak, or lock inversion in that path.  Fresh
strict-warning builds covered the independent filesystem host, backend,
connection, pending, state, dispatch, chain, outbox, queue, PCI, export,
FUSE, handle, session, and server test programs.

The VirtIO-IOMMU replay separately checked endpoint/domain ownership,
request-level DMA leases, ATTACH/DETACH/UNMAP exclusion while active DMA is
present, reset deferral, address-space selection across a bypass transition,
fault publication, and the portable state boundary.  Translation is
authorized while holding the IOMMU state mutex but invokes the platform mapper
only after releasing it; the lease prevents a control-plane revocation from
invalidating that authorization mid-request.  The independent rootless
harness, including hostile-input and private-interface guards, completed 616,
496, 777, 100, and 2 checks with no failures.  Hardware-backed translated
DMA remains a root-only Linux/5BSD release gate.

### 2026-08-07 — administration/device-group composition replay

The administration owner, group, capability, resource, device-parts, PCI,
and SR-IOV lifecycle layers were rebuilt with strict warnings and reviewed as
one composition boundary.  Registration is immutable before queue service;
commands take an owner lease before invoking a group; and the SR-IOV bridge
uses a read/write lifetime fence so a PCI configuration update cannot alter
the group contract while a command is active.  Capability validation and
application execute under the capability-manager mutex by contract.  The
device-parts callbacks do not reenter that manager: validation queries the
resource manager and application publishes only atomic limits.  Its restore
path stages resource and capability values before committing them.

No deadlock, native-state serialization, or partial-publication defect was
found in this replay.  The administration and SR-IOV surfaces remain ledger
qualified rather than release-complete: they need a live PCI consumer,
negative command exercise, migration compatibility tests, and a guest driver
that actually negotiates the optional administration feature.

### 2026-08-07 — asynchronous device and lifecycle-fence replay

The pmem worker, sound readiness backend, virtio-mem host range manager, and
VirtIO-IOMMU were rechecked as separate asynchronous/stateful boundaries.
Pmem keeps its lifecycle request under the same device mutex as its completion
callback and drains ownership only after publication.  Sound serializes
readiness completion, cancellation, queue reset, and snapshot pause through
its private mutex; its state record is explicitly little-endian and binds OSS
restore to the configured paths.  Virtio-mem validates its immutable geometry
before applying a restore and rolls back only ranges created by that attempt.
The IOMMU brackets descriptor DMA with endpoint leases, serializes mapping
authorization before the external GPA mapper, and refuses a snapshot while DMA
is active.

The common modern resume-failure path now publishes NEEDS_RESET before it
releases the lifecycle owner.  This is a defense-in-depth terminal-state
ordering: `vs_suspended` already keeps queues closed, while the new order makes
the failed state explicit before observers can see the owner released.  The
source comment was checked to state that precise guarantee.  A snapshot-enabled
bhyve build, the complete rootless device harness (616, 497, 777, 100, and 2
checks), requirement/portability validators, the nested-VMX model validator,
and `git diff --check` pass.  Hardware-backed translated-DMA, packed-ring,
checkpoint, and long-soak coverage remain in the saved privileged gates.

### 2026-08-07 — packed completion and nested-exposure replay

The packed-virtqueue path was traced from descriptor availability through DMA
mapping, indirect-table validation, device-owned request claiming,
asynchronous completion staging, ordered/group publication, event suppression,
discard, and queue reset.  The implementation maintains a bounded host-owned
completion table keyed by descriptor head and wrap generation.  A request lease
must be consumed exactly once before it can be staged or discarded; queue reset
retains asynchronous owners and prevents remapping or reconfiguration until
they retire.  The independent core tests cover direct and indirect chains,
non-power-of-two wrapping, stale completion, duplicate ownership, ordered and
grouped completion, reset retention, event suppression, and zero-length used
descriptors.  No duplicate-completion, wrap-reuse, or reset/reconfiguration
defect was found in this pass.

The Intel nested-VMX exposure boundary was also replayed independently of the
hardware-entry implementation.  It is a VM-wide CPU-model switch guarded by a
boot-time host policy, a per-guest request, a complete capability predicate,
and an atomic immutable-after-run state.  CPUID hides VMX when the predicate is
not met; the snapshot envelope rejects CPU-model or capability mismatches
before any nested registry or vCPU state is staged.  This remains explicitly
Intel-specific: common snapshot and lifecycle plumbing carries only versioned
portable state and does not expose VMX semantics to non-Intel backends.  The
rootless nested requirement/model gates cover the policy, capability signatures,
instruction-state models, checkpoint validation, and negative cases.  Real
Intel L1/L2 execution, active-L2 restore, and long-run fault/soak evidence
remain saved privileged qualification gates.

### 2026-08-07 — external-backend checkpoint replay

The SCSI and vsock device callbacks were traced separately from the common
VirtIO pause fence.  SCSI quiesces each request worker with a single monotonic
deadline, retains queue-reset ownership across a checkpoint, completes an
ordinary reset's queued commands with the specified reset response, and binds
restore to a fresh complete CTL LUN-inventory document rather than to host
pointers or CTL handles.  Its tests cover a timed drain failure, partial
multi-queue acquisition rollback, selective-reset retention, guest-suspend
ownership transfer, and malformed inventory/configuration records.

Vsock stops every independent readiness source while holding its recursive
device mutex; callbacks selected before disable recheck the lifecycle fence
after acquiring that mutex.  A userspace backend is checkpointable only with
no live control or data sockets.  A kernel backend additionally freezes an
empty provider, validates its fixed-width reply, replays the negotiated device
features while admission remains closed, and thaws only after that succeeds.
Failed freeze, malformed provider replies, feature replay, and thaw keep or
restore the correct fence and require reset where recovery is ambiguous.  The
snapshot record binds backend kind, configured listener identity, CID, feature
set, and next host port; it contains neither descriptors nor host file
handles.  Focused harness cases cover each exclusion, lock transfer, failed
freeze/thaw, and retryable kernel-provider path.  No new lifecycle or portable
state defect was found in this replay.  Live cross-host reconstruction and
long concurrent backend soak remain privileged qualification gates.

The console and 9P portions of the same replay also completed cleanly.
Console holds the device mutex through its reconstructibility check, rejects a
connected socket, pending host bytes, or event registration, and saves only
validated port topology and listener configuration.  Guest suspend retains
permitted host connection state behind the common descriptor fence and
re-arms queued receive/control work only after resume.  9P uses one monotonic
condition-variable deadline for suspend, keeps fids across guest suspend, but
rejects them for a portable checkpoint because their descriptors and
credentials are host-local.  Its restore verifies export path, device/inode,
read-only mode, mount tag, protocol version, and message sizes before it
publishes a new asynchronous-completion generation.  The focused console and
9P harnesses cover malformed records, identity mismatch, active state
rejection, selective reset, and failed drain paths; no new defect was found.

### 2026-08-07 — non-standard kernel contract and test-quality replay

The Intel nested state machines and the kernel-vsock provider interface were
reviewed as private contracts rather than as substitutes for standard guest
ABIs.  Nested freeze/thaw snapshots callback tables before use, carries only a
value-only L2 continuation across the cold boundary, rebuilds host VMCS/VPID,
MSR, EPT, timer, and CPU-pinning resources on the destination, and quarantines
an incomplete rollback instead of resuming from a guessed CPU-local state.
The kernel-vsock FREEZE ioctl closes admission before its bounded in-flight
copy wait, checks caller authority and reserved fields, reports fixed-width
empty-provider metadata, and rolls admission back on every rejection.  THAW
is idempotent and reissues both poll/kqueue and transport wakeups only after
the fence changes.

The nested model suite intentionally compiles the architecture-neutral value
state modules for unit coverage, but its envelope, capability, control-MSR,
VM-entry, VM-exit, and revision fixtures use literals independent of the
production headers.  The accompanying validator checks that distinction and
also compiles the portable arithmetic under 32-bit `size_t`.  The rootless
nested model, requirements validator, non-standard-interface validator, and
diff check passed in this replay.  They cannot establish hardware instruction
semantics; Intel L1/L2 execution remains mandatory before release.

### 2026-08-07 — event-driven operational replay

The production VirtIO device models were searched for periodic sleeps and
manual retry loops in their reset, suspend, resume, and asynchronous-completion
paths.  None was found.  In particular, the block backend's reset drain uses
one bounded `pthread_cond_timedwait()` predicate loop, signalled by the I/O
completion callback.  Its condition variable uses the default POSIX realtime
clock, so its one absolute `CLOCK_REALTIME` deadline is the matching contract;
it is not a polling delay.  SCSI, 9P, filesystem, network, and pmem use the
same condition-driven shape with their explicitly configured monotonic clocks.

The new common prestarted-AP path is separately event driven.  It snapshots
the startup predicate while holding the rendezvous and vCPU owners, enqueues
an interruptible sleep before dropping those owners, and revalidates after
each wake.  The requirements validator rejects timeout or polling constructs
in that routine.  The historical one-millisecond `usleep()` remains in bhyve's
debug-exit handler to reduce spinning between userland vCPU activation and the
legacy userspace STARTUP IPI.  It is outside both the VirtIO lifecycle and the
new kernel-owned startup path; it is retained as a clearly scoped legacy
operational item, not used as evidence for the new event protocol.  The
event-driven boundary remains subject to the saved installed-kernel signal,
reset, checkpoint, and Intel startup qualification gates.

### 2026-08-07 — independent-oracle adapter correction

The administration-PCI adapter unit test was compiled through the production
common header for its private C types, but two post-DUT status assertions still
spelled production status macros.  The test now remaps those names to the
independent VirtIO 1.4 fixture only after including the device under test.  A
wrong production status definition therefore changes the adapter behavior
without changing the expected result.  This is a test-quality correction only;
it does not alter guest-visible or production behavior.

The rootless device harness and conformance guards completed after the change:
616, 497, 777, and 100 harness checks passed with no failures; the independent
oracle (683 definitions), requirement ledger (232 entries), portability,
translated-DMA, DTrace, non-standard-interface, and no-manual-sleep guards
also passed.  The existing live Linux/5BSD, checkpoint, and soak gates remain
the necessary hardware/guest evidence.

### 2026-08-07 — portable-state, provider, and reference replay

The next portability pass traced the device-private snapshot records rather
than relying only on the common envelope.  The memory, IOMMU, and GPU adapters
decode fixed-width little-endian discriminators before allocating, bound every
decoded length against destination geometry and `SIZE_MAX`, and validate their
full replacement state before publication.  GPU map ranges are additionally
bounded by the configured aperture before overlap comparison, so their end
calculations cannot wrap.  Console, 9P, and vsock continue to reject live host
descriptor state instead of serializing it.  No pointer, native-structure,
host-endian, or unchecked decoded-size defect was found in that replay.

The AF_VSOCK provider path was then replayed independently.  The direct
virtio driver publishes its global softc only after ownership registration;
the PCI, legacy, and MMIO buses all consume an attach-completed failure by
detaching the child and reporting FAILED.  Detach clears ownership before
waking blocked senders and drains RX/event handlers under the same mutex.
The CID-multiplexed `/dev/vsock` provider keeps sockets tied to a stable
transport object, and its FREEZE/THAW tests cover malformed metadata, feature
replay, and retryable thaw failure.  Its waits use socket timeout or explicit
wakeup predicates, not periodic progress polling.  The source-level review
found no new ownership or wakeup defect.

Finally, the immutable corpus validator passed for the pinned VirtIO 1.4
CS01, Intel SDM revision 092, Linux 7.2-rc4, and QEMU 300438 references; the
nested model and requirement validator rebuilt and passed after this replay,
as did `git diff --check`.  These results are rootless conformance evidence
only.  Installed Linux/5BSD split-and-packed, translated-DMA, active
checkpoint, soak, and Intel L1/L2 execution gates remain required before
promotion.

### 2026-08-07 — GPU resource-table portability correction

The GPU state constructor previously depended on `calloc()` to reject a
theoretical `max_resources * sizeof(resource)` overflow.  The same extent is
subsequently used by snapshot alias detection, so allocator behavior was not a
sufficient portability contract for a future 32-bit bhyve.  The constructor
now computes that extent once with an explicit `SIZE_MAX` bound before either
allocation or later use.  The state test directly exercises the helper with
the largest 32-bit count and verifies the architecture-dependent result
without allocating the corresponding table.  The full rootless device harness
(616, 497, 777, and 100 checks), requirements and snapshot-portability guards,
and whitespace check passed after this correction.  Live GPU activation and
checkpoint remain the separately scheduled privileged gates.

### 2026-08-07 — IOMMU table-extent portability correction

The IOMMU state constructor had the same future-32-bit ambiguity for its
endpoint, domain, mapping, and optional fault tables: `calloc()` normally
detects an overflowing product, but state construction and later reset paths
need an explicit portable extent contract.  Construction now validates each
`uint32_t` count against its element size before allocation.  The new unit test
checks the largest representable count without allocating it, verifies both
overflow and valid-width behavior, and also checks invalid helper arguments.

The complete rootless harness and validation set passed after this change:
616, 497, 777, and 100 harness checks; the independent 683-definition oracle;
the 232-entry requirements ledger; snapshot-portability; translated-DMA;
DTrace; private-interface; and no-manual-sleep guards.  This is source and
model evidence only.  Privileged translated-DMA, Linux/5BSD, checkpoint, and
soak qualification still remain explicit release gates.

### 2026-08-07 — orchestration and non-standard boundary replay

The rootless orchestration pass completed the host helper, payload-chunk, and
lab self-tests.  It covers the independent parser fixtures for ring, network
hash, IOMMU, GPU-blob, and device-ring traces; the nested-live-evidence bundle;
and all current Linux/5BSD guest helper payloads.  The DTrace wrapper guard
(58 probes), translated-DMA boundary guard, snapshot hostile-input self-test,
and non-standard interface ledger (97 entries) also passed.  The latter
continues to require separate kernel and private-boundary reviews for AF_VSOCK
and verifies that unsupported paths are ledger-mapped rather than silently
advertised.

This pass also found no periodic sleep or architecture-specific execution
assumption in the common VirtIO data path.  Host-native evdev word bitmaps are
translated explicitly into the byte-defined VirtIO input bitmap before they
become guest-visible.  The root-only live feature activation, checkpoint,
translated-DMA, and soak matrices remain pending; these model tests do not
substitute for them.

### 2026-08-07 — build-mode replay and 32-bit helper correction

The two bhyve build modes were replayed with warnings promoted to errors.
That exposed a compile-only portability defect in the new GPU extent helper:
on a 64-bit build the compiler could prove the `uint32_t` overflow comparison
false and rejected it as tautological.  The GPU and IOMMU helpers now perform
the count-versus-extent check only where `size_t` is 32-bit; the multiplication
is then demonstrably safe on either width.  The full device harness and both
bhyve build modes pass after the correction.  The nested qualification
self-tests for staging, coverage, evidence, and paired policy also pass.

No live hardware result is implied by these checks.  Intel VMX L1/L2,
Linux/5BSD device activation, active checkpoint, and bounded soak remain
privileged qualification gates.

### 2026-08-07 — GPU transfer-size portability correction

The GPU `TRANSFER_TO_HOST_2D` path previously formed the row size before
checking whether it fit `size_t`.  On a future 32-bit bhyve, a large width
could therefore wrap before the later height check.  A single checked helper
now validates nonzero dimensions and both multiplications before staging or
DMA access.  Its unit coverage includes ordinary dimensions, zero dimensions,
and maximum-width/height overflow.  The device harness and both snapshot build
modes pass after the correction.

### 2026-08-07 — GPU scanout-state invariant correction

A second GPU state pass found that the live `SET_SCANOUT` and
`SET_SCANOUT_BLOB` paths accepted a nonzero resource with a zero-width or
zero-height rectangle.  Resource ID zero is the defined disabled-scanout
representation; a zero-size rectangle with a retained resource is neither a
useful presentation state nor accepted by the portable snapshot decoder.
Worse, the renderer's scanout capture computes its row extent from that state,
so a zero width could reach a division by zero in the overflow check.

Both command paths now reject that form before mutating state, while capture
also rejects it defensively in case a future or older state producer supplies
an inconsistent in-memory object.  The independent GPU model tests cover
both ordinary and blob scanout command forms, including the still-valid
resource-zero disable command.  The current rootless device harness
(616, 497, 777, 100, and 2 checks), independent 683-definition oracle,
232-entry requirements ledger, orchestration self-test, nested VMX model and
policy validators, and whitespace guard passed after the correction.  This
does not replace the pending installed Linux/5BSD packed-GPU, active
checkpoint, translated-DMA, reset, and soak evidence.

### 2026-08-07 — cross-architecture VMM build-closure correction

The architecture-neutral checkpoint/event review found a kernel build-closure
gap rather than an amd64 runtime defect.  The reusable coordinator, startup,
ingress, wait, and checkpoint helpers are shared by the VMM implementations;
the x86 `vmm_vm.c` wrapper consumes the machine-owned startup readiness hook,
while arm64 and riscv currently compile only the portable helper set.  The
amd64 module makefile already linked those helpers, but the arm64 and riscv
kernel file manifests listed only the newer dirty-log subset.  An arm64 or
riscv kernel configured with `vmm` could therefore compile callers while
omitting the portable definitions at link time.

Both manifests now include the complete shared coordinator/startup source
set.  The nested requirements validator independently requires every member
of that set in both manifests, preventing future AMD64-only module coverage
from hiding a non-x86 kernel closure regression.  The 433-entry nested
requirements ledger, 282-entry non-standard ledger, 12-group live
qualification ledger, and whitespace check pass after the correction.
Cross-architecture installed-kernel builds and live qualification remain
separate required evidence; this source-level correction makes them
buildable rather than claiming they have run.

### 2026-08-07 — checkpoint manifest and nested-entry boundary replay

The checkpoint/release manifest was replayed through the `virtio-lab`
validator rather than treated as a collection of similarly named cases.  Each
concrete checkpoint case carries the explicit checkpoint switch; the two
apparent omissions are profile-variable definitions, not runnable cases.
The manifest verifies active-state policies for userspace and kernel vsock,
console, 9P, virtio-fs, balloon, IOMMU endpoints, GPU blobs, RTC alarms,
PMEM, and sound, and it requires separate split/packed ring evidence where a
ring-format claim is made.  Its release and checkpoint coverage contracts
also retain distinct Linux and 5BSD evidence; a result from one guest is not
relabeled as proof for the other.

The Intel nested-entry replay then traced `vmx_run_nested()` with the
startup-entry owner present.  The only owner-consuming nested return remains
the early lifecycle branch, before guest MSRs, VMCS02 selection, EPT
activation, or an L2 event transaction.  Every later nested entry currently
emits the withheld probe and returns `EOPNOTSUPP`.  The modelled
owner-outcome adapter remains deliberately unlinked from that production
path: it cannot be enabled until its complete initial/resumed/hot VMCS02
unwind and post-entry settlement transaction is installed and qualified.

Rootless evidence for this replay is the passing normal and snapshot-enabled
bhyve build-mode gate; the 433-entry nested requirements ledger, 282-entry

683-definition/232-requirement VirtIO oracle; the 97-entry non-standard

sleep/poll loop in the bhyve VirtIO device path.  These are source/model

DMA, soak, and Intel L1/L2 execution remain mandatory live evidence.

An isolated `make -C sys/modules/vmm` build with warnings promoted to errors
also compiled and linked the actual amd64 `vmm.ko`, including the complete

### 2026-08-07 — qualification-boundary and portable-state replay

The privileged WASPNest launcher was reviewed as a boundary, rather than
assuming that a successful metadata check made the later VM run trustworthy.
When `VIRTIO_REFERENCE_ARTIFACT_DIR` is supplied, it authenticates the exact

The next lifecycle/portability replay passed the independent portable

### 2026-08-07 — future-port startup-readiness boundary

`vm_startup_configure_kernel()` no longer names the amd64-only machine
readiness operation directly.  Its local adapter calls that operation only on
amd64 and otherwise returns false, so a future non-x86 user of the common
wrapper fails with `EOPNOTSUPP` instead of acquiring an undeclared machine
dependency.  The current arm64 and riscv VMM manifests still link only the
portable helper set; this is a source-portability closure, not a claim of
cross-architecture build or live qualification.

The same lifecycle pass found that a failed coordinator allocation retained
`vm->maxcpus` after leaving the coordinator null.  The common initializer now
rolls that field back to zero, preserving its all-or-nothing construction
contract and making a transient allocation failure retryable.  The nested
requirements validator now makes both the representability check and this
rollback mandatory.

### 2026-08-07 — checkpoint publication and transport-reset replay

The checkpoint manifest path was rechecked from staged member creation through
hash verification, manifest replacement, directory persistence, and restore.
All parsing and compatibility checks decode into candidates before publication;
the topology, CPU-contract, backend-identity, manifest, and portable-snapshot
tests cover malformed, truncated, duplicate, and changed-destination inputs.
One subtle result is intentional: if the final directory `fsync` fails after
the atomic manifest rename, the call reports the durability error while also
reporting the generation as published.  The visible generation must retain its
event-ingress fence and must not be cleaned up as though it were unreachable.
The corresponding manifest test injects both pre-rename and post-rename fsync
failures and checks the different outcomes.

The second transport/lifecycle review confirmed that full device reset still
uses a required status readback poll in modern PCI and modern MMIO.  VirtIO
does not provide a reset-completion interrupt, but the current kernel bus reset
method is void and child teardown immediately reclaims DMA-backed queues.  A
simple timeout would therefore convert a host wedge into possible live-DMA
reuse.  This remains an explicit architectural follow-up: introduce a fallible
reset/revocation state machine, fence queue reclamation until completion, and
then bound this wait.  It is not treated as an ordinary hot-path polling loop
or hidden by the test suite.

An isolated complete `sys/modules/virtio` build linked the VirtIO core, PCI
and MMIO transports, network, block, balloon, console, GPU, input, 9P, RTC,
and vsock modules with warnings promoted to errors.  The rootless
`virtio-lab` orchestration self-test also passed.  These checks validate source
and runner behavior only; installed-kernel Linux/5BSD feature activation,
checkpoint, reset, translated-DMA, and soak evidence remains required.

### 2026-08-07 — common management-ABI architecture closure

A follow-up architecture pass rechecked the amd64-only readiness operation in
