its complete private startup-management ABI is already enclosed by an outer
amd64 guard.  The review removed a redundant inner architecture conditional
and corrected the validator to assert the real invariant: the readiness
operation, private startup state, and startup ioctl dispatch must stay inside
that single amd64 boundary.  The common `vmm_vm.c` adapter remains necessary,
because that source is shared by the other VMM architectures.

### 2026-08-07 — VirtIO-sound retained-I/O replay

The provisional sound device was rechecked from a guest PCM kick through the
private asynchronous owner, OSS readiness delivery, control RELEASE, selective
queue reset, full reset, suspend, checkpoint pause, and audio-event teardown.
Both guest notification and the readiness callback enter the asynchronous
owner under `vssc_mtx`; cancellation invokes its terminal callback
synchronously under that same lock.  Consequently the completion can neither
publish a replacement request after reset ownership starts nor dereference an
audio event after `mevent_delete_sync()` has retired it.  The generic async
owner drops only its own mutex before calling the device completion, avoiding
an inversion with the device lock while retaining its `completing` fence until
the callback returns.

The focused production-linked test family covers retained playback and capture,
partial I/O, private-copy semantics, stale generations, progress-versus-cancel
races, RELEASE ordering, readiness-source retirement, backend failures, and
portable-state rollback.  A fresh AddressSanitizer/UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer
device-harness replay passed all lanes (616, 497, 777, 100, and 2 checks; zero
failures).  This is not an assertion of a production audio backend or live
Linux/5BSD sound-driver qualification: those remain explicit roadmap gates,
and stock 5BSD still has no virtio-sound driver to activate.

### 2026-08-07 — isolated bhyve build-closure replay

An initial isolated bhyve link correctly failed rather than silently using the
installed ABI: the fresh object tree did not yet contain the rebuilt
`libvmmapi`, which supplies `vm_create_devmem_auto()` and
`vm_distribute_memory_domains()`.  Rebuilding that library in the same object
tree and then relinking bhyve completed with warnings treated as errors.  The
successful link includes the shared VirtIO core and modern transport, packed
queues, administration support, IOMMU, GPU, filesystem, memory, PMEM, RTC,
sound, vsock, all existing device models, and generated DTrace objects.  This
is a build-closure result only; it does not substitute for the root-only live
Linux/5BSD, checkpoint, translated-DMA, Intel nested-VMX, and soak gates.

### 2026-08-07 — startup-controller lifetime and retry replay

The common coordinator constructor was reviewed together with the amd64
file-description-owned startup controller interface.  Coordinator creation
does not publish its output pointer until every constructor step has
succeeded, so rolling back `vm->maxcpus` on an allocation failure restores
the complete pre-init state and permits a later retry without an allocation
or ownership leak.  The constructor's remaining internal initializer
failures are fail-stop invariants rather than user-recoverable outcomes.

For the private startup ioctl path, a device operation pins its open file
description while it uses the embedded controller ticket.  The per-fd lock
prevents configure and final-close from racing ticket mutation; wait and
commit deliberately drop that lock only after observing an active ticket, and
the coordinator authenticates every subsequent operation.  Final close
releases the exact ticket, or cancels the coordinator before discarding it if
that release cannot complete.  Concurrent wait/commit requests remain a
coordinator concern and cannot leave a copied or stale credential usable.
No additional source-level lifecycle defect was found in this pass.  The
remaining proof is the installed-kernel concurrent close/reset/cancel
qualification already recorded in the Intel live ledger.

### 2026-08-07 — common checkpoint partial-pause rollback

The checkpoint lifecycle review found an inconsistent caller boundary.  The
checkpoint-save path eventually calls `vm_resume_devices()` after a failed
pause walk, but restore returned immediately when `vm_pause_devices()` failed.
That could leave an earlier device holding its checkpoint fence when a later
device rejected pause.  The unwind now belongs to `vm_pause_devices()` itself:
it resumes the acquired prefix in reverse dependency order, treats devices
which never acquired ownership as no-ops, and reports an unwind failure rather
than pretending that the destination is runnable.  This gives save, restore,
and future callers the same failure-atomic pause contract.

An isolated bhyve rebuild, including a fresh libvmmapi in the same object tree,
passed with warnings promoted to errors.  The rootless harness still covers
per-device idempotent pause/resume ownership and phase ordering; the pending
root-only checkpoint matrix must additionally inject a later-device pause
failure with an earlier normal endpoint and verify that the endpoint receives
its matching resume before the VM is allowed to run again.

### 2026-08-07 — coordinator construction publication boundary

The coordinator constructor was tightened once more after checking its actual

using the validated original `u_int` topology value before publishing either
`vm->maxcpus` or the startup CPU mask.  A recoverable allocation/owner-ID
failure therefore leaves the VM byte-for-byte in its pre-initialization
topology state; the successful path publishes the cleared mask and narrowed
16-bit limit only after construction.  The architecture constructors continue
to pass their un-narrowed limits into this common boundary.  The rootless
nested requirements validator checks that source ordering; installed-kernel
allocation-fault and cross-architecture build qualification remain pending.

### 2026-08-07 — sound asynchronous admission test correction

The sanitizer replay exposed a test contradiction in the sound asynchronous
lane, not a host implementation failure.  After a deliberately failed
quiesce, the test attempted a replacement stream-0 job while the original
stream-0 job was still active, even though the API intentionally permits one
owned job per stream.  It then expected both the submit and cancellation for
the new generation to succeed.  The test now cancels the old stream-0 job
first, installs the replacement, verifies a stale-generation cancellation is
rejected without a completion, and then cancels the replacement.  This proves
the intended property—failed quiesce does not close admission—without masking
the independent one-job-per-stream ownership invariant.

The complete AddressSanitizer/UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer device harness passed
after the correction, including all late sound, administration, filesystem,
network, SCSI, packed-ring, DMA, and snapshot lanes.  Expected hostile-input
diagnostics are emitted by those tests; no sanitizer or assertion failure
remained.  This remains rootless evidence and does not replace live audio,
checkpoint, Linux, or 5BSD qualification.

### 2026-08-07 — qualification-host mutation rollback

The VirtIO-lab host-preparation review found a control-plane ownership gap.
The bridge ownership record was published before mutation, but a failure to
publish its updated flags after creating a bridge or adding an uplink could
leave that mutation outside the record used by `host-cleanup`.  State-file
publication now returns an error to its caller, and each post-mutation update
rolls back the bridge creation or member addition before reporting failure.
The pre-mutation ownership record remains valid for a later retry, while a
failed rollback is reported as an explicit manual-recovery condition rather
than silently claiming cleanup is safe.

The rollback path was then re-reviewed against the generic file helper.  That
helper terminates on write errors, so it could have bypassed the new rollback
logic; the host-state writer now performs its own fallible create/write/close
sequence and returns the error to the mutation owner.  Cleanup also refuses
to destroy a lab-created bridge if its configured uplink is present but was
not recorded as lab-added.  This prevents an externally added uplink from
being detached merely because the bridge itself originated with the lab.

The rootless VirtIO-lab self-test, Lua parse/usage path, and requirements
validator passed after this change.  A privileged fault-injection run that
forces ownership-record publication failure after `ifconfig create` and
`addm` remains part of the host-control-plane qualification, because it must
exercise real interface operations without risking the development host.

### 2026-08-07 — bounded nested registry serialization

The nested VMCS registry's canonical checkpoint walker previously trusted its
intrusive-list links completely.  Although those links are kernel-owned, a
damaged self-cycle could make size calculation or encoding loop indefinitely.
The walker now bounds every pass by the immutable registry limit and reports a
malformed registry as `EPROTO`; the encoder and sizing path propagate that
failure without publication.  A focused state-model case creates a temporary
self-cycle, verifies the bounded failure, restores the exact link, and then
completes the ordinary wire-format round trip.  The full nested model passed
under AddressSanitizer and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer after the correction.

### 2026-08-07 — bounded nested registry runtime lookup

The follow-up kernel traversal applied the same availability rule to normal
registry lookup and owner resolution.  A damaged intrusive list must not turn
an attempted VMCS selection or owner release into an unbounded kernel walk.
Both helpers now bound traversal by the immutable registry limit and report
`EPROTO` to their callers on exhaustion; no malformed entry is allocated,
released, or published.  The state-model regression creates a cycle in the
relevant hash bucket, verifies that a missing-GPA select and an absent-owner
release both fail boundedly, confirms the count is unchanged, then restores
the link before running the canonical state cases.  This is a defensive
kernel-internal correction only; it does not alter the VMX guest ABI,
checkpoint wire format, or the deliberately withheld live-L2 execution path.

### 2026-08-07 — bounded nested checkpoint registry validation

The same review found three cold checkpoint helpers which independently
walked the VMCS registry to resolve a GPA or determine whether an owner was
present.  They now use explicit result parameters, bound every bucket walk by
the registry limit, and verify full owner scans against the recorded count.
Malformed linkage is reported as `EPROTO`; an ordinary absent entry remains
distinguishable as `ESTALE`.  The portable registry state case exercises both
checkpoint helpers while a temporary self-cycle is present and verifies that
they fail without changing the registry.  The focused case and the strict
warning build pass.  Full sanitizer aggregate execution remains a rootless
required gate and must be recorded only from its explicit terminal marker.

The final cold restore cross-check had a separate GPA search which was also
made bounded and count-validated.  It now scans all buckets, rejects duplicate
current-GPA entries, and requires the observed entry count to match registry
metadata before comparing VMCS fields.  This preserves the distinction between
a malformed restore owner (`EPROTO`) and an ordinary stale architectural
reference, and keeps every checkpoint registry walk finite.

The metadata-negative regression then found that the new lookup helpers had
not cleared their output pointer or boolean before returning `EPROTO`.  They
now initialize every caller-visible output before any registry validation, so
a failed lookup cannot accidentally leave a previous entry or owner result in
use.  The regression covers both result forms and passes in the strict
rootless VMX state model build.

The nested requirements negative self-test also now makes each expected
validator failure explicit before re-enabling shell error-exit behavior.  This

### 2026-08-07 — atomic nested VMCS selection

The next lifecycle pass found a cross-bucket rollback hole in VMCS selection.
GPA lookup is deliberately bucket-local, while owner uniqueness requires a
whole-registry walk.  The old ordering could link a new entry and only then
discover malformed linkage in another bucket during the owner scan.  Selection
now validates that global owner view before allocating or linking anything, so
`EPROTO` leaves the registry unchanged.  The portable state test temporarily
cycles an unrelated bucket, selects a valid GPA that hashes elsewhere, and
asserts both the bounded failure and an unchanged entry count.  The focused
strict-warning model test passes.  This is kernel-internal transaction
hardening; neither the VMX guest ABI nor the portable checkpoint format
changes.

The second traversal pass tightened the owner helper itself: it now completes
its bounded scan after a first match, verifies the recorded count, and rejects
duplicate ownership.  That prevents a malformed later bucket from evading the
pre-allocation validation.  The regression constructs duplicate owners in
separate buckets and proves selection returns `EPROTO` without retargeting or
adding a VMCS entry.  The focused model and the actual `vmm.ko` module build
pass with warnings treated as errors.

The same runtime pass now rejects a duplicate VMCS GPA in its normal hash
bucket and treats an entry stored under the wrong bucket as malformed during
the whole-registry owner scan.  These checks prevent a damaged registry from
selecting an arbitrary opaque VMCS region merely because the first matching
link looked plausible.  The ownership and portable-state cases pass after the
new duplicate-GPA regression, as does the strict `vmm.ko` build.

### 2026-08-07 — registry lifecycle topology preflight

The lifecycle review found that shape validation alone was insufficient before
destruction, replacement, or storage-alias inspection: a self-referential
intrusive link could otherwise be followed by teardown code.  Those paths now
share a bounded topology preflight which checks the recorded count, the
registry limit, and each entry's hash bucket before following links.  A damaged
registry fails closed (`EPROTO` for teardown and a conservative overlap result
for alias checks), leaving its state intact rather than freeing through an
untrusted chain.  `owner_active` performs this preflight before its output
alias check, preserving `EPROTO` for corrupted topology and `EINVAL` for an
ordinary caller contract violation.

The portable-state regression constructs a self-cycle and proves destruction

hash bucket and proves owner admission rejects it.  Both tests pass after

The kernel-only review traced each waiting allocation reachable from the

reached while an individual vCPU is serialized for an internal exit, not while
checkpoint publication holds the VM frozen.  Changing only the enclosing root
object allocation would therefore have been a false nonblocking guarantee, so
that shared API was left unchanged.

The review did find one independently recoverable allocation in the frozen
VMPTRLD path: selection of a new VMCS registry entry used a waiting allocation.
That acquisition now uses the registry's no-wait mode.  `ENOMEM` remains a
recoverable host error and is propagated to the VM_RUN boundary without

and portable-state tests passed; the complete 164-case rootless nested-state

### 2026-08-07 — SCSI event-source lifecycle review

The host SCSI event path was checked from the CTL subscription contract
through bhyve's event queue and the guest driver's received-event handling.
`CTL_LUN_EVENT_NEXT` is nonblocking: after the event-source readability edge,
it returns `EAGAIN` when the subscription queue is empty.  bhyve therefore
uses a bounded drain while holding the device mutex; that serialization keeps
the callback ordered with guest queue kicks, reset, suspend, and checkpoint
fences without introducing a mutex-held wait.  The source now records that
contract next to the drain loop.

The CTL event ATF suite exercises poll/readiness and empty-queue `EAGAIN`;
the rootless VirtIO SCSI event, device, and guest-contract suites passed.  A
fresh snapshot-enabled `libvmmapi` followed by bhyve also built cleanly with
`-Werror`.  Live Linux and 5BSD LUN add/remove/change, queue-loss
`EVENTS_MISSED`, and active-command checkpoint tests remain qualification
gates rather than being inferred from these model and build results.

### 2026-08-07 — vsock event-lifetime and descriptor-reuse review

The userspace vsock backend previously identified a dynamic connection event
only by its host file descriptor.  A readiness event can have been selected
before deletion, then wait for the device lock while the original connection
is closed.  If a later connection reuses that descriptor, the stale callback
could operate on the later connection.  Each dynamic connection and control
event now has a monotonically allocated, nonzero identity.  The event
parameter carries that identity and is retained by the generic `mevent`
machinery until a deleted event can no longer dispatch.  Callbacks require
both the identity and descriptor to match before touching connection state.
Generic event-parameter cleanup runs after dropping `mevent`'s queue lock, so
future cleanup handlers may safely retire related events without creating a
lock-order dependency.

The generic event lifecycle test verifies cleanup exactly once for deletion
both before and after an event is selected, including a cleanup handler that
adds and retires a related event.  The vsock device harness adds a
descriptor-reuse case that invokes the stale callback after a replacement
connection claims the same numeric descriptor and verifies that no receive
work is injected into the replacement.  The full rootless vsock-device and
mevent-lifecycle suites, a fresh bhyve build, and `git diff --check` passed.
This is a host-model concurrency proof; long-lived multi-VM userspace-backend
soak remains part of the root-only qualification matrix.

The same pass confirmed that 9P rejects active fids, requests, and resets and

### 2026-08-07 — common checkpoint commit-order replay

The common VirtIO checkpoint path was reviewed again with the device callbacks
for IOMMU, filesystem, GPU, and network in scope.  Restore first decodes the
common PCI/transport/queue representation into reversible destination state.
When an administration controller is present, the device-private section is
validated on a copied cursor to locate the controller record; the controller
is backed up and restored before the private device callback can publish.  A
private callback failure restores the controller and all common state.  A
different byte count between validation and restore is treated as a protocol
failure and quarantines the destination instead of attempting a generic
partial rollback.

Validation callbacks are correspondingly non-publishing: the IOMMU retains a
temporary validation-scoped translation view until the coordinator cleanup,
filesystem validates its decoded backend/FUSE contract without replacing the
session, GPU validates the complete resource graph before publication, and
network restores the previous backend framing contract if a later parser step
fails.  The portable-checkpoint validator, the VMM module build, and the
nested model/requirements gate passed after this replay.  The focused model
cases cover controller rollback after private-device failure, prepared IOMMU
view cleanup, packed-cache rollback, and restore-incomplete latching.

This establishes the source and model contract only.  It does not claim that
an external backend rollback or a live guest's active I/O has been qualified;
those remain explicit privileged checkpoint and soak gates.

### 2026-08-07 — suspend, resume, and architecture-boundary replay

The common modern transport suspend state machine was traced against the
guest PCI and MMIO counterparts.  It closes queue admission before backend
drain, invokes the device callback while that fence is held, and only then
publishes SUSPEND while clearing DRIVER_OK.  A failing drain publishes
NEEDS_RESET before reopening admission, so there is no interval in which a
lockless notifier can take a new chain from a device whose backend failed to
quiesce.  Resume keeps the queue fence until the backend operation succeeds;
failed resume stays suspended and reset-required.  Deferred configuration
interrupts and queue notifications are replayed only after the corresponding
ownership fence has opened.

The guest PCI and MMIO transports request SUSPEND only when the device offered
it and wait for the device-owned status transition; the MMIO bounded wait is
documented as necessary because that transport has no lifecycle-completion
interrupt.  Device-private lifecycle callbacks remain behind the common
VirtIO operations, while VMX is confined to AMD64 VMM sources and the
portable checkpoint envelope carries no VMCS or host-pointer state.  Existing
model cases cover suspend failure, resume failure/retry, nested checkpoint
ownership, and deferred-notification replay.  A real Linux/5BSD suspend
cycle, device power transition, and active-I/O suspend/restore are still
privileged qualification requirements.

in both modes.  The failure was stale snapshot-enabled objects being linked by

Build validation remains intentionally separate from live state validation:
the snapshot-enabled build proves that the portable save-state and device
callbacks compile together, while the default build proves that non-snapshot
installations retain their supported configuration.  Neither result asserts a
successful live migration; that remains a privileged checkpoint and restore
gate.

### 2026-08-07 — nested-VMX exposure and CPU-model replay

The nested-VMX exposure path was traced from host policy through the VM-wide
capability ioctl, CPUID/MSR/instruction consumers, ordinary `vmx_run()`, and
the checkpoint compatibility record.  Host policy is a boot-time tunable and
the guest request accepts only canonical zero or one.  The resulting exposure
state is a VM-wide atomic CPU-model value, not a per-vCPU feature bit.  Before
any vCPU can execute its first guest instruction, `vmx_run()` locks that model
atomically; a concurrent configuration request therefore either wins before
execution or receives the locked-state error.  This is the cross-vCPU boundary
that the per-vCPU ioctl alone cannot provide.

When policy is disabled or the full virtual-capability predicate fails, the
get-capability path withholds the feature, and the CPUID, VMX-MSR, and
instruction handlers follow the same disabled predicate.  When enabled, the
checkpoint CPU-compatibility record carries the virtual-capability and VMCS
schema signatures rather than host VMCS state.  The model and source validator
cover the canonical-value, first-run freeze, disabled exposure, and signature
rules.  Real CPUID/MSR behavior and L1/L2 execution remain explicitly live
Intel qualification, not evidence inferred from this source pass.

### 2026-08-07 — filesystem backend and translated-DMA lifecycle replay

The virtio-fs restore path was traced from the authenticated backend handshake
through QUIESCE, portable VFS1 encoding, destination validation, session
restore, and THAW.  The saved backend incarnation is intentionally a
source-side trace value, not a destination identity: restore compares the
stable backend identity and the complete negotiated protocol, feature, and
resource contract, then thaws through the newly authenticated destination
session.  Requiring equal incarnations would reject a safe reconstructed
backend; accepting a changed identity or capability would not.  Validation is
non-publishing, and the opaque state remains retryable while the destination
connection stays quiesced after a failed thaw.

The common ACCESS_PLATFORM boundary was also traced across request leases,
IOMMU endpoint attachment, map/unmap/detach, ring-mapping refresh, and
completion.  A request lease pins the selected endpoint address space and
keeps the domain callbacks live through the final completion or discard.
Revoking operations reject active leases, persistent queue mappings refresh
only across a stable translation generation with a finite retry bound, and
the IOMMU idle callback restarts a deferred request rather than polling.
The portable sanitizer harness and the current nested-VMX build/model gate
completed without failures after this replay.  Live Linux/5BSD IOMMU and
virtio-fs mount, reset, active-checkpoint, and soak evidence remains required
before either provisional feature can be release-qualified.

### 2026-08-07 — nested live-qualification staging replay

The nested-VMX live-qualification interface was checked independently of the
hardware run.  Its evidence, staging, coverage, and default-policy-pair
validators all pass rootlessly.  The twelve required feature groups each name
separate Linux-L2, 5BSD-L2, and host-trace evidence; the wrapper refuses to
interpret a rootless model result as that evidence and requires a reviewed
root-owned L1 runner plus immutable L1, Linux-L2, and 5BSD-L2 images.

The staging contract also retains the Intel-only boundary: host policy must be
enabled before the L1 is launched, while the VM's CPU-model request remains a
per-VM decision.  No source-only run can mark any of the twelve groups live,
and no guest image, trace, or nested-state artifact is serialized as a native

than a newly discovered source implementation hole: instruction and entry
failure behavior, exit reflection, EPT/VPID invalidation, interrupt and timer
delivery, active-L2 restore, and repeated lifecycle soak on this Intel host.

### 2026-08-07 — packed completion and activation-ledger replay

The packed completion path was rechecked independently of the per-device
models.  A direct packed scatter/gather buffer is completed by rewriting its
head descriptor with the complete buffer's used length and the final
available descriptor's ID, then advancing the used cursor across the entire
chain.  The remaining chain descriptors are skipped rather than published as
separate completions.  This is the packed-buffer representation required by
the VirtIO 1.4 chaining rules, and the independent wrapped direct-chain test
checks the exact ID, length, WRITE result, ownership flags, cursor wrap, and
event notification.  Group completion first validates the full contiguous
group and publishes tail-to-head so a driver cannot observe a partial group.

The activation ledger was also reconciled with the lab manifest.  Pending
packed RTC, GPU, memory, sound, IOMMU, filesystem, PMEM, and optional-balloon
rows already name concrete split/packed Linux (and, where a driver exists,
rebuilt-5BSD) cases.  Their state is `pending` because they lack privileged
guest evidence, not because the scheduler has omitted them.  This preserves
the distinction between rootless model coverage and live feature activation;
it does not promote any of those rows.

### 2026-08-07 — nested execution-boundary replay

The Intel nested execution path was followed through the ordinary
userland-owned VM run and the newer optional kernel-owned startup-owner
parameter.  Ordinary nested operation passes no startup owner and continues
through the VMCS02 runtime path.  The non-null-owner path deliberately stops
before guest-MSR entry, VMCS02 selection, or EPT activation with
`EOPNOTSUPP`, accompanied by the host-only `vmm:vmx:nested:withheld` probe.
It is not a generic nested-VMX rejection.

That restriction is intentional: a kernel-owned startup owner cannot become
returnable until cold entry, resumed entry, handled hot exits, unhandled exits,
and every matching rollback/refreeze/detach operation form one typed
transaction.  The current requirements ledger and state model cover those
edge classifications and keep readiness false until installed timing and
fault qualification exists.  The model, requirements, staging, policy-pair,
coverage, and evidence validators passed after this replay.  The missing work
is therefore clearly bounded implementation and Intel execution
qualification—not an ambiguity that should be bypassed by enabling the
non-null owner path early.

### 2026-08-07 — nested portable-checkpoint replay

The nested VMX checkpoint codec was reviewed from capture through decode,
destination validation, registry reconstruction, and active-L2 continuation
handling.  The wire record is bounded and fixed-width little-endian.  It
contains architectural VMXON/VMCS12 state, a VMCS registry representation,
the virtual capability and schema signatures, and an active continuation only
when its VMCS12 identity and generation agree.  It does not encode a hardware
VMCS, a host pointer, a CPU-local lease, or a host-residency identifier.

Destination validation checks the virtual capability and schema contract
before registry publication.  The runtime hardware plan and VMCS02 resources
are then destination-local reacquisitions; stale continuation, epoch, launch,
or signature facts fail closed.  Existing model cases exercise incompatible
capabilities, malformed/truncated sections, duplicate/missing registry state,
active continuation generation mismatches, and repeated restore.  This is
strong source/model evidence for the format boundary, while save/restore with
a real running L2 remains an explicit Intel privileged gate.

### 2026-08-07 — packed-ring state and notification replay

The common bhyve packed-ring implementation was traced across descriptor
acquisition, chained and indirect-buffer handling, ownership claim/release,
out-of-order completion staging, ordered group publication, wrap advancement,
event suppression, queue reset, and snapshot cursor restoration.  The queue
stores a host-owned transient completion table keyed by packed head and wrap;
it does not serialize that table as portable guest state.  Snapshot state
contains only the guest-visible queue addresses, cursor positions, wrap bits,
and notification state, and restore rebuilds host-owned transient resources.

The rootless packed model and the complete device harness passed under Address
and UndefinedBehavior sanitizers.  The independent requirement validator also
confirmed document-derived wire constants, malformed-chain handling, split
publication ordering, packed guest interrupt ordering, and the absence of
manual device-progress sleeps.  The remaining qualification boundary is live:
each device must still negotiate and exercise packed queues with an actual
Linux guest and, where a rebuilt 5BSD driver supports it, a 5BSD guest before
the feature is enabled by default.

### 2026-08-07 — model-runner result-protocol replay

The compact rootless checkpoint runner and the nested-VMX model runner now
both treat ATF's result record as part of the test outcome.  A successful test
program process status alone is insufficient: an ATF case can report a failed
body through its result protocol.  Each enumerated case is therefore required
to end in `passed`, in addition to returning successfully.  The requirements
validator checks that source contract and a mutation self-test removes the
checkpoint runner's result check from a private copy and requires the
validator to reject it.  This closes a false-green test-runner failure mode;
it does not turn model coverage into privileged hardware qualification.
The guard is also a declared installed-harness companion; a fresh
object-directory `beforedepend` build materializes both `run.sh` and the guard
before the rootless entry point can be packaged or run outside the source
tree.

### 2026-08-07 — SCSI event-queue fairness replay

The VirtIO SCSI CTL source callback was already bounded, but the independent
guest event-queue drain could continue while a guest replenished buffers.  The
drain now consumes no more than the event virtqueue's negotiated size in one
notification, matching the request-queue fairness rule.  A source-level model
case uses a one-entry queue with two pending records and two available buffers;
the first notification consumes exactly one and the second notification
consumes the retained work.  The complete portable device harness then passed
under AddressSanitizer and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer (1,998 checks, zero
failures).  Linux/5BSD hotplug, active-command checkpoint, packed activation,
and long-running CTL-event qualification remain privileged gates.

### 2026-08-07 — kernel-provider vsock fragmented-RX fairness replay

The kernel-backed AF_VSOCK provider had a queue-sized limit on packet reads,
but a single received packet could still be split into an unbounded number of
guest RX descriptors during one callback. Provider reads and fragment
injection now share a budget derived from the negotiated RX queue size. The
budget is charged for each guest descriptor actually consumed, not merely for
reading a provider packet, so a packet remains parked and resumes on the next
guest notification without starving the mevent thread.

The focused model injects a 5,000-byte SEQPACKET record into three 2,048-byte
guest buffers with a one-entry RX queue. It proves exactly one fragment is
published per callback, preserves the parked offset, and emits EOM/EOR only
on the final fragment. The complete portable device harness passed again
under AddressSanitizer and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer (2,011 checks, zero
failures), as did a clean-object `bhyve` build with warnings treated as errors.
Live long-run multi-provider fairness remains a privileged qualification gate.

### 2026-08-07 — pending-control FIFO fairness replay

The bounded pending-control FIFO is intentionally allowed to hold 128 headers,
but its previous flush routine could consume all 128 in a single readiness
dispatch even when the negotiated RX virtqueue was smaller. The flush now
uses a negotiated-queue budget. Kernel-provider packet reads share that same
budget with both pending control replies and fragmented data injection.

A new source model starts with two parked replies, a one-entry RX queue, and
two guest descriptors. It proves one reply is published per flush rather than
draining the fixed-capacity FIFO opportunistically. The full sanitizer-backed
device harness passed with 2,015 checks and the clean-object bhyve build
remained warning-free. Sustained multi-guest fairness is retained for the
privileged soak lane.

### 2026-08-07 — shared pending/data budget edge replay

Review of the new shared budget found the final control-reply edge: after a
pending reply used the last queue unit, a readiness predicate must not permit a
data fragment in that same callback. The predicate now requires budget to
remain before declaring the RX ring ready for provider data. A focused model
combines one parked control reply, one pending provider data packet, and a
one-entry queue; the first call emits only the control reply and the second
emits the data. This prevents unsigned budget wraparound and preserves FIFO
ordering. The sanitizer device harness passed with 2,022 checks and no
failures, followed by a warning-clean bhyve build.

### 2026-08-07 — portable restore and external-backend review replay

The common VirtIO and checkpoint paths were reviewed for host-architecture
leakage and backend reconstruction drift.  Portable device codecs use
fixed-width little-endian fields; architecture-specific CPU and legacy-device
state remains outside that envelope.  The checkpoint manifest intentionally
requires the destination architecture and machine ABI to match, so this is a
portable device-state contract rather than an unsupported cross-architecture
VM migration promise.  Common queue and DMA code contains no amd64-only
state or host-page-size dependency; device protocol constants are kept
separate from host memory geometry.

The external-backend pass confirmed that block, network, console, 9P, input,
pmem, filesystem, SCSI, and vsock each either bind an explicit reconstruction
identity or reject unreconstructible active state.  In particular, userspace
vsock records backend kind, CID, and listener-path identity while excluding
host sockets; kernel-backed vsock records the same portable guest contract
only after its provider is empty and frozen, then replays negotiated features
before thawing destination admission.  Preflight does not freeze, thaw, or
otherwise mutate the provider.

After this review, the AddressSanitizer/UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer device
harness completed 646, 497, 779, and 100 checks (2,022 total) with zero
failures.  The independent VirtIO ledger validated 683 independent oracle
definitions and 236 requirement entries; `git diff --check` was clean.
These are rootless model and source checks.  Installed Linux and 5BSD
activation, active external-backend checkpoint, translated-DMA, repeated
restore, multi-provider fairness, and long-run soak remain explicit
privileged release gates.

### 2026-08-07 — implementation-versus-qualification inventory

The requirements ledger was reclassified by implementation status rather than
by live-gate status.  No mandatory VirtIO requirement is currently marked
unimplemented.  The only deliberately unimplemented device feature is optional
block secure erase.  ORDER_PLATFORM and SR-IOV remain intentionally
not-applicable until a platform/IOMMU or production PF/VF owner exists; no
device advertises either feature.

Most remaining ledger entries marked pending are therefore not an excuse to
claim a feature complete: they are installed Linux/5BSD, checkpoint, fault,
or soak evidence still required.  The material implementation gaps are on the
5BSD guest side (packed virtqueue support, modern suspend rollback/MMIO
lifecycle, and drivers for the newer device types) and on future host
integrations (production virtio-fs daemon, GPU presentation/audio backends,
and real SR-IOV ownership).  Those are kept separate from bhyve's current
portable device-model contracts so a missing guest driver cannot cause a
host feature to be advertised speculatively.

### 2026-08-07 — input-frame atomicity and dispatch-fairness replay

The VirtIO input event path was checked separately because it publishes a
complete evdev frame atomically rather than treating every host event as an
independent device callback.  The apparent frame-length loop is bounded by
the negotiated event-virtqueue size before it can acquire descriptors: an
oversized frame is discarded and reported to the guest as the standard
`SYN_DROPPED`/`SYN_REPORT` resynchronization frame.  It therefore cannot turn
a one-entry or otherwise small queue into an unbounded descriptor-drain
callback.  The host evdev read side is independently bounded by
`VTINPUT_HOST_EVENT_BUDGET`, and inactive/reset queues are drained in the same
bounded slices so a level-triggered host descriptor does not spin the mevent
thread.

The source harness already covers the one-entry host-read dispatch bound,
frame-larger-than-ring loss conversion, partial-frame rollback, malformed
event descriptors, reset/queue-reset loss isolation, and checkpointed staged
frames.  No code change was warranted.  Linux and 5BSD packed-input activation
and multi-device long-run evidence remain privileged qualification gates.

### 2026-08-07 — rootless conformance checkpoint

The independent requirements validator, portable snapshot validator, DTrace
surface validator, non-standard-interface ledger, build-mode validator, and
the nested-VMX model/requirements validators were rerun as one clean review
checkpoint.  The VirtIO ledger contains 236 requirements backed by 683
independent oracle definitions; the private-interface ledger contains 97

confirmed that device progress does not contain manual polling sleeps, that

The activation ledger intentionally reports 81 Linux and 116 5BSD unresolved

implementation evidence.  They remain prerequisites for enabling packed or

release-qualified.

### 2026-08-07 — cross-device queue-drain bound replay

A mechanical source audit of all VirtIO descriptor-draining callbacks confirmed
that block, balloon, console, filesystem, GPU, input, IOMMU, memory, network,
9P, pmem, RNG, SCSI, sound, and both vsock paths consume no more than the
negotiated virtqueue size per dispatch.  Network receive additionally bounds
mergeable-buffer acquisition by the queue size and segment limit; input uses
the separately reviewed whole-frame loss policy.  The audit found no
device-specific polling loop or fixed-capacity drain that could bypass the
common fairness rule.

This is source/model evidence only.  Long-running concurrent traffic, reset,
and multi-guest fairness remain in the privileged soak lane.

### 2026-08-07 — checkpoint-preflight serializer replay

The restore transaction pauses every PCI device before parsing incoming device
records, but the preflight codec is also callable by direct compatibility and
model paths.  A source-order review found that virtio-fs and vsock already
serialized those direct calls while console and 9P did not.  Both now enter the
local device serializer before invoking the common VirtIO codec; no external
listener, export, or provider operation occurs during this validation phase.

The same review caught a lock-ownership edge in the first console wrapper:
normal restore reaches preflight while `pci_vtcon_pause()` already owns the
non-recursive console mutex.  The wrapper now detects same-thread ownership,
reuses that pause fence, and acquires/releases the mutex only for direct
preflight callers.  The focused console model proves both paths and confirms
that invalid metadata reaches no decoder.  The 9P mutex is deliberately
recursive and therefore safely composes with its existing pause boundary.

The complete AddressSanitizer/UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer device harness
completed 2,024 checks with zero failures after this correction, and a
source-matched `bhyve` build linked with `-Werror`.  This closes a rootless
restore-lifecycle defect; active console/9P restore and repeated checkpoint
remain privileged evidence gates.

The follow-up common-code review deliberately rejected a universal
`vi_pci_snapshot()` mutex acquisition.  Several device callbacks already own
their serializer (and virtio-mem must acquire it itself during a direct
checkpoint callback), while other pause/resume pairs retain a non-recursive
mutex across the common transaction.  A universal lock would therefore create
self-deadlocks.  The common layer remains the transaction/framing owner;
each device with mutable external or callback-owned state supplies a local,
tested preflight serializer.

### 2026-08-07 — sound preflight serializer follow-up

The same callback-order review was extended to the VirtIO-sound PCI device.
Its commit-time pause correctly quiesced the asynchronous PCM owner and held
`vssc_mtx` through the common/private snapshot callbacks, but its direct
restore-preflight entry still used the generic callback without that mutex.
That could race a guest submission or a backend-readiness completion while it
compared backend identity and stream state.

`pci_vtsnd_snapshot_validate()` now supplies the local boundary: it validates
metadata, takes `vssc_mtx` for direct preflight, and reuses rather than
recursively reacquiring the non-recursive mutex when checkpoint pause already
owns it.  It does not quiesce, freeze, thaw, or otherwise touch the audio
backend.  The direct sound composition case proves both ownership paths and
that the direct call releases its lock.  AddressSanitizer/UndefinedBehavior-
Sanitizer device-harness replay and a full `bhyve` `-Werror` build passed.

The subsequent inventory intentionally does not replace every generic
`pe_snapshot_validate` callback mechanically.  Some private codecs have an
internal serializer (notably virtio-mem); network needs both RX and TX
ordering; SCSI also needs its worker-drain fence.  Those devices require
device-specific proofs before conversion.  The review action is recorded as
an explicit common-save-state follow-up rather than masking a lock-order
regression with a universal lock.

### 2026-08-07 — network preflight serializer follow-up

VirtIO-net was then converted after a separate lock-order trace.  Its private
snapshot includes receive staging plus TX/control/RSS state, while backend RX

`pci_vtnet_snapshot_validate()` now uses exactly that pair for direct
preflight, reuses the pair when checkpoint pause owns both, and rejects a
partial-lock caller with `EBUSY` rather than inverting the order or producing

The direct model case proves lock acquisition/release, pause-held reuse, and

active-RX/TX checkpoint and repeated restore remain root-only qualification

### 2026-08-07 — input preflight serializer follow-up

The input codec includes a host-event frame, selector cache, and resync flags

### 2026-08-07 — balloon preflight serializer follow-up

Balloon validation reads accounting, the page tracker, retained statistics,
and free-page-hint state that normal guest callbacks update under `vbsc_mtx`.
Its checkpoint pause intentionally releases that lock after draining retained

### 2026-08-07 — GPU preflight classification

GPU was reviewed but intentionally not given another PCI-level preflight
mutex.  The 2D state snapshot-size, save, limit, validate, and restore
operations serialize their resource graph with the state object's internal
mutex.  PCI-level validation reads only fixed scanout identity and the input
record's pending-event bit; it neither reads mutable event state for a
decision nor publishes it.  Adding `vsc_mtx` would duplicate the state lock
without protecting an additional mutable validation dependency and risks
constraining the render path unnecessarily.  The existing PCI callback test
already proves validation cannot publish events, and the state suite covers
concurrent snapshot state integrity.  Live GPU checkpoint remains a
privileged qualification item.

### 2026-08-07 — remaining snapshot callback classification

The remaining generic preflight callbacks were reviewed individually rather
than converted by pattern.  VirtIO-IOMMU validates into a separately allocated
prepared fabric whose parser and topology checks take the fabric's own mutex;
the PCI callback atomically replaces that prepared view only after successful
validation, and its cleanup hook drops it after the transaction.  VirtIO-mem
serializes every snapshot operation with its host-state mutex.  GPU has the
separate internal-state serialization described above.

RTC validation only decodes an incoming alarm record and calls the pure alarm
record validator; it reads the host clock and publishes alarm state only on
restore.  RNG has no device-private mutable snapshot state, and PMEM's record
contains immutable backing identity/size while worker draining belongs to
pause.  A PCI-level mutex in these three paths would not protect an additional
mutable validation dependency.  They intentionally retain the generic
callback.  This leaves no unclassified generic preflight callback among the
currently emulated VirtIO devices; live checkpoint and backend-failure tests
remain privileged qualification, not source-model proof.

Nested VMX remains deliberately unavailable.  The implementation-stage mask

fail closed rather than exposing a model-only path.

The independent nested model now asserts both that instruction-result handling

### 2026-08-07 — nested VMX live-run retry isolation

The privileged nested-VMX qualification wrapper used a fixed
`WORKDIR/runner-tmp` directory.  A timeout, signal, or external L1-runner
failure left that directory behind, making a safe retry in the same trusted
root-owned work directory fail before execution.  The wrapper now creates a
fresh `mktemp` scratch directory under the already-validated mode-0700
`WORKDIR` and removes only that exact non-symlink directory during cleanup.
The staged evidence transaction remains separate and is still discarded on a
failed attempt.  The requirements validator pins both the unique scratch
creation and exact cleanup behavior, so a future edit cannot silently return
to fixed-name reuse.  This is operational retry hygiene only; it does not
enable nested VMX or weaken the root-only evidence requirements.

### 2026-08-07 — nested qualification descendant supervision

The local FreeBSD `timeout(1)` contract was reviewed against the live-runner
cleanup claim: default mode acts as a reaper for the command and its
descendants, whereas `-f`/`--foreground` deliberately does not.  The
qualification source gate now rejects foreground mode, requires a real
`timeout` command with the reviewed kill-after policy, and its mutation test
proves that an injected foreground option is rejected.  Literal contract
searches now pass `--` to `rg`, avoiding an option-prefixed requirement (such
as `-k`) being treated as a validator option.  This keeps a timed-out nested
qualification from silently leaving L1/L2 bhyve descendants behind; it does
not constitute hardware evidence.

### 2026-08-07 — portable common-VirtIO snapshot encoding audit

The common modern-VirtIO checkpoint record was rechecked as a cross-host
format rather than an amd64 implementation detail.  Version 2 serializes its
magic, version, flags, negotiated features, queue selector, lifecycle flags,
ISR, and MSI-X selector with fixed-width little-endian helpers; its only
current decoder accepts that exact encoding and rejects obsolete development
records.  Device-memory extension records likewise use an
explicit little-endian header and table, canonical name ordering, reserved
byte validation, checked ranges, and a full digest pass before any destination
memory is changed.  Block's logical configuration record is field encoded;
network's retained configuration is deliberately the exact guest-visible byte
image; sound and RTC use self-describing byte codecs.

`modern_snapshot_has_little_endian_golden_encoding` now checks the complete
v2 common record against literal bytes and offsets independent of production
snapshot declarations.  The focused rootless test and the requirements
validator pass.  This is source/model evidence only: cross-endian and
cross-word-size restore still require their planned non-amd64 build and live
qualification lanes.

### 2026-08-07 — lab cancellation direct-child bound

The test-lab cancellation wrapper previously applied its bounded TERM/KILL
escalation only to a recorded descendant tree.  Its direct `timeout(1)` child
received an initial `TERM`, but was outside the later escalation set; a
TERM-ignoring wrapper could therefore leave the final `wait` unbounded even
after descendant cleanup.  The supervisor now fingerprints that direct child
before signalling and includes it with the original descendant tree for both
bounded escalation phases.  If fingerprint collection is unavailable during
signal handling, the child remains waitable by this wrapper, so a final direct
`KILL` is safe before `wait(2)`.

The orchestration self-test asserts this source contract and re-runs active
cancellation, descendant-reparenting, manager-interrupt, resume, lock, and
status checks.  It completed successfully.  This is host-lab hygiene only;
the bounded `soak-smoke` and endurance `soak` VM lanes still require their
separate root-only execution evidence.

### 2026-08-07 — nested VMX owner-transaction integration boundary

The nested VMX execution path was traced again from `vmx_run()` through
`vmx_run_nested()` against the common startup-entry-owner state machine.  The
ordinary VMX path has one directly adjacent attempted-entry transaction:
prepare CPU-local state, perform the common attempted-entry guard, execute
VM-entry, classify the result, then commit or abort the owner.  Nested VMX
does not have that single shape.  Its cold, resumed, and hot paths can each
acquire or retain VMCS02, L2 MSRs, an EPT/pmap activation, debug/descriptor
state, event state, and an L0 continuation; initial rejection, EPT-walk,
direct reflection, and unhandled exits also have different publication and
inverse sequences.

The Intel-private `vmx_nested_owner_outcome` value adapters correctly model
the required pre-entry, attempted-entry, and deferred post-entry settlements,
including terminal cleanup overriding replay or a captured VM exit.  They are
intentionally test-only: the requirements validator verifies they are not
linked into `vmm.ko` and that `vmx_run_nested()` rejects a non-null owner
before guest-MSR/VMCS02 residency.  Wiring only one branch would allow common
retirement before a branch-specific inverse finished, so no partial
production conversion was made and the existing `EOPNOTSUPP` gate remains the
correct behavior.  The edge matrix now remains the implementation checklist:
`EDGE-NVMX-007` through `EDGE-NVMX-012` must be converted and qualified as one
source-ordered transaction before the exposure-stage bit can be enabled.

Rootless verification reran the nested model and requirements validators; the
remaining evidence is necessarily privileged Intel execution: L1 Linux/KVM,
Linux and FreeBSD L2s, VM-entry failures, EPT/VPID and interrupt/timer paths,
checkpoint while L2 is active, and repeated create/destroy fault and soak
runs.

### 2026-08-07 — packed virtqueue promotion audit

The common packed-ring path was reviewed as a transport prerequisite rather
than a per-device option.  Modern feature finalisation fixes the selected
layout before queue enable; packed queues accept the broader legal queue-size
range, validate their descriptor/event alignment, keep completion ownership
separate from physical descriptor positions, and clear that ownership on
queue reset or a split-layout restore.  The completion path stages a full
group before publishing ownership, so an observable packed completion cannot
expose a partially completed multi-buffer request.  Indirect, stale,
malformed, wrap, event-threshold, asynchronous ordering, ACCESS_PLATFORM,
and snapshot-cache paths are independently covered by the packed model,
engine, and focused core tests.

The requirement/activation ledgers continue to keep per-device packed-ring
advertisement opt-in and distinguish rootless behavioral proof from live
interoperability.  Linux and rebuilt-5BSD packed cases must still negotiate
the feature and demonstrate real I/O and host ring evidence for every device
and advertised queue before any release promotion; no rootless result is
recorded as guest activation.

### 2026-08-07 — ACCESS_PLATFORM and VirtIO-IOMMU boundary audit

The common DMA lease is the lifetime boundary for both direct and translated
queue accesses.  It increments before sampling a domain binding, rechecks the
detach gate and binding, and only then invokes the provider acquire callback.
Domain installation and removal require no active leases; removal closes the
gate first and keeps the old callback table alive until the final request
release.  Queue parsing, completion, interrupt suppression, and snapshot
queue reconstruction all use that common lease/map path, so a reset, detach,
or restore cannot switch address spaces partway through a descriptor-chain
operation.

VirtIO-IOMMU topology construction rejects ambiguous providers and circular
provider-as-endpoint configurations before it binds any peer.  Its failed
post-init path unwinds registered endpoints and DMA-domain bindings.  State
validation checks exact endpoint/domain/mapping accounting, ordered non-
overlapping mappings, permissions, overflow, page granularity, and prepared-
view publication before replacing the live fabric.  All focused configuration,
PCI, state, protocol, request, queue, event, topology, and VIOT rootless ATF
cases passed.  This remains a source/model result: device-specific Linux and
5BSD ACCESS_PLATFORM negotiation, translated I/O, IOMMU fault delivery, and
live checkpoint/restore still require privileged execution.

### 2026-08-07 — common checkpoint and suspend ownership audit

The portable checkpoint path was rechecked through its preflight, restore,
rollback, and resume boundaries.  Restore takes a full common/queue backup,
validates first, then publishes transport, administration, and private state
in order.  A private callback that cannot compensate an external side effect
sets a runtime-only incomplete-restore latch; rollback restores the prior
common image but reasserts `DEVICE_NEEDS_RESET`, preventing a superficially
successful rollback from hiding a backend inconsistency.  The latch clears
only through a successful full reset.

Guest suspend and checkpoint pause share a queue-admission fence but retain
distinct ownership.  A device resume callback runs while the common fence is
still held; only `resume_complete` re-enables external sources after the
fence opens.  Restore hooks transfer guest-suspend ownership only on an
actual suspended/runnable transition, preventing a repeated restore from
leaking a backend freeze reference.  Portable envelope, manifest, topology,
NUMA/CPU, compatibility, devmem, PCI checkpoint, and focused lifecycle ATF
cases all passed rootlessly.  Active-I/O, backend-loss, cross-endian/word-
size, cross-host, and repeated live restore remain privileged release gates.

### 2026-08-07 — balloon ownership and optional-feature audit

The balloon device was reviewed from the guest PFN parser through host-page
discard, selective queue reset, guest suspend, checkpoint pause, and restore.
Its accounting is deliberately not used as ownership: a page tracker records
4 KiB guest PFNs and only releases or discards a host page once every guest
PFN in that host granule has the required ownership state.  Duplicate PFNs
are idempotent, holes and invalid ranges are rejected, and a failed optional
discard or undiscard hint never changes the VirtIO ownership result that has
no per-request status field to report the host paging outcome.

The optional queue contracts are feature-gated rather than merely
queue-number-gated.  Statistics retains no more than one readable descriptor;
timer refresh, guest suspend, checkpoint pause, and queue reset either
complete or revoke that ownership before it can cross an incarnation boundary.
Free-page hinting validates the command-buffer shape and command epoch;
free-page reporting acknowledges legal ranges even when discard cannot be
applied, and preserves the guest poison pattern when PAGE_POISON is
negotiated.  Snapshot state is a little-endian, versioned representation of
PFN ownership and optional state.  It rejects unknown versions, malformed
feature/state combinations, non-empty legacy images without a bitmap, and
any live retained statistics token; restore applies host-memory transitions in
deterministic order and marks the device reset-required if compensating a
partial transition fails.

All independent parser/tracker and device-level balloon ATF cases passed
rootlessly, including fragmented little-endian vectors, malformed atomicity,
duplicate PFNs, host-granule transitions, retained-statistics lifecycle,
free-page hint/report behavior, poison handling, reset, snapshot corruption,
repeated restore, and rollback failure.  Still required before promotion are
Linux and 5BSD activation evidence for each offered optional feature, genuine
inflate/deflate under memory pressure, packed-ring operation, active-I/O
checkpoint/restore, and the explicit ineligible ACCESS_PLATFORM behavior.

### 2026-08-07 — GPU 2D resource, DMA, and state audit

The modern-only GPU device was traced across both control and cursor queues,
the independent GPU state lock, the display renderer, the optional shared
memory blob aperture, and the portable snapshot envelope.  Queue processing
requires an ordered descriptor chain with at least one readable request
segment; it preserves the command fence in an error response, prevents a
short response buffer from executing a state-changing command, and only
escalates allocation exhaustion to DEVICE_NEEDS_RESET.  The command/state
layers separately validate resource IDs, formats, backing ranges, scanout and
cursor rectangles, blob mappings, EDID, and response layout before visible
publication.

All private DMA access acquires the common DMA lease and maps with an explicit
read, write, or bidirectional direction.  This keeps the blob aperture and
backing transfer paths inside the same translated-DMA lifetime discipline as
the queue path.  The GPU state object owns its own mutex; queue execution,
render capture, aperture access, state save, validation, and publication
serialize there, so the direct common snapshot validation callback does not
race resource storage.  Snapshot decoding allocates and validates a complete
candidate resource graph before replacing the destination graph; host display
objects are reconstructed only after publication and are intentionally not
serialized.

All GPU protocol, state, PCI, display, and queue ATF cases passed rootlessly.
They cover fragmented request/response buffers, malformed commands, fence
correlation, response-size atomicity, resource/backing transactions, transfer
failure rollback, scanout/cursor cropping, EDID, blob mapping and aperture
endianness, DMA lease use, portable snapshot corruption and repeated restore.
Still required are a production display-backend exercise, Linux and 5BSD
driver activation (including EDID/cursor/scanout), packed-ring live traffic,
ACCESS_PLATFORM/IOMMU execution, queue saturation, and active-display
checkpoint/restore.

### 2026-08-08 — GPU 2D lifecycle replay follow-up

A second lifecycle-oriented pass checked the apparent device-local no-op
lifecycle callbacks against the actual PCI composition.  They do not bypass
quiescence: `vi_pci_pause()` owns common queue and DMA admission before the
GPU snapshot callback enters the independently locked resource graph.  The
state mutex covers command execution, aperture access, scanout/cursor capture,
snapshot save, validation, and publication; display callbacks are deliberately
made only after releasing that mutex.  This prevents backend re-entry from
deadlocking the state serializer while retaining atomic graph replacement.

The portable image is little-endian and versioned, validates a complete
candidate resource/backing/mapping graph before publishing it, revalidates
destination guest-memory backing addresses with the proper DMA direction, and
never serializes destination-local display handles.  It reconstructs display
and cursor objects after publication and clears old destination presentation
state first, so an empty restored image cannot leave stale pixels or a cursor.

All rootless GPU protocol, state, and queue ATF cases passed in this replay.
No new code defect was identified.  This is not live-driver qualification:
the outstanding release gates remain Linux and 5BSD activation of the offered
2D/EDID/cursor/scanout features, packed-ring traffic, queue saturation under a
real display backend, ACCESS_PLATFORM execution, and active-display repeated
checkpoint/restore.

### 2026-08-08 — RTC, virtio-mem, sound, and IOMMU lifecycle replay

The RTC replay verified an event-driven alarm design: a single absolute
`CLOCK_REALTIME` timerfd is either disarmed, set to the alarm deadline, or set
to a cancellation sentinel after a delivered alarm.  The timer callback takes
the VirtIO lifecycle lock and refuses to schedule while quiescing, suspended,
or checkpoint-paused.  Reset, guest suspend, and checkpoint pause disarm the
timer before changing the portable model; restore re-observes the destination
clock before resume.  All RTC host, PCI, and alarm-model ATF cases passed.

The virtio-mem pass verified exact little-endian geometry and bitmap records,
frozen guest-visible configuration during suspend, normal reset preservation
of plugged blocks, and the separate restore-incomplete latch for failed host
range compensation.  Host-model and PCI tests passed, including repeated
restore, aliases, changed geometry rejection, and failed rollback behavior.

The sound pass verified that asynchronous PCM ownership is generation-tagged
per stream, that quiesce closes admission and drains completions before the
private codec lock is retained for checkpoint, and that portable records keep
stream configuration and backend identity but never file descriptors, host
callbacks, or PCM payloads.  Async, host, queue, and PCI ATF suites passed.

The IOMMU pass verified map/unmap/attach/detach, request and event queue
behavior, fault delivery, endpoint topology, translated-DMA generations, and
the prepared destination mapping view used by checkpoint validation.  The
provider is deliberately ACCESS_PLATFORM-ineligible, is excluded from its own
endpoint table, and multiple providers fail closed until device groups are
implemented.  All available IOMMU protocol, state, queue, topology,
configuration, event, request, and PCI ATF cases passed.

These are model and host-process results.  The pending root gates remain real
Linux ACCESS_PLATFORM negotiation with translated DMA on each eligible device,
Linux virtio-mem hotplug under memory pressure, real RTC alarm/clock-step
delivery, sound playback/capture with a production host backend, packed-ring
operation, active-I/O repeated restore, and any required 5BSD driver
activation.

### 2026-08-08 — Common core, packed ring, and evidence-ledger replay

The common VirtIO replay ran every `virtio_core_test` case individually, then
the requirements, portable-snapshot, and non-standard-interface validators.
The expected diagnostic output exercised rejection of unmapped and unaligned
DMA, looping and malformed split/packed chains, forbidden packed indirect
forms, inconsistent descriptor ownership, feature-state mismatches, invalid
status restoration, and unsafe pending-request snapshots.  The suite passed.

The independent requirements oracle reports 683 document-derived definitions,
237 code/test ledger entries, 16 suspend producers, 16 queue-reset producers,
and 127 activation assertions.  It also verifies that functional wire tests
do not source expected values from the implementation under test; private
interfaces have 97 explicit ownership/compatibility records.  The portable
snapshot validator passed its hostile-input and architecture-neutral encoding
checks.  The remaining distinction is evidence, not a waived requirement:
the ledger currently reports 81 unresolved Linux and 116 unresolved 5BSD live
activation claims, all retained as root-run gates rather than promoted from
the model suites.

### 2026-08-07 — virtio-fs backend and checkpoint audit

Virtio-fs was reviewed as an external-backend device rather than as a simple
queue forwarder.  Request chains require ordered readable and writable
segments, use overflow-checked aggregate lengths, and retain the descriptor
when bounded pending/outgoing capacity applies backpressure.  Queue reset
uses the backend reset acknowledgement and generation records before the
common queue incarnation can be reused.  The framed Unix-domain backend
protocol authenticates the peer credentials, rejects unexpected ancillary
data and truncated frames, uses versioned little-endian headers, and keeps
request/control identifiers and incarnation fields distinct.

Guest suspend is only offered when the configured stable backend identity
makes FREEZE and STATE_TRANSFER mandatory in the authenticated handshake.
Checkpoint pause holds the device serializer across the paired resume,
quiesces or borrows guest suspension, captures the FUSE and backend sessions,
and thaws on every recoverable failure path.  Decode validates the complete
portable session against the destination tag, queue topology, negotiated
features, backend identity, and *live* destination backend contract before
replacing any FUSE/session state.  This prevents a snapshot from silently
attaching to a changed export or stale destination incarnation.

The complete rootless chain, host, backend, backend-I/O/client, connection,
pending, dispatch, outbox, queue, PCI, export, FUSE, handle, session, server,
and daemon ATF suites passed.  They cover authentication, framing, malformed
and oversized messages, cancellation, backpressure, reset, request ordering,
path and handle isolation, checkpoint reconstruction, and changed-export
rejection.  Remaining release evidence is privileged Linux virtio-fs mount
and I/O with the production backend, backend restart/identity mismatch under
load, packed live traffic, active-request checkpoint/restore, and DAX only
after a separately qualified shared-memory design.

### 2026-08-07 — virtio-mem and RTC lifecycle/state audit

Reviewed the virtio-mem host model, PCI request path, frozen configuration,
and versioned bitmap restore. Guest operations are serialized separately from
state access, ordinary reset preserves plugged blocks as required, and a
failed backend restoration remains latched rather than publishing an
inconsistent ownership bitmap. The model's independent host tests and PCI
request tests passed.

Reviewed virtio-RTC request/alarm queues, timerfd callback fencing, clock-step
handling, reset, guest suspend, checkpoint pause, resume completion, and its
checksummed portable alarm snapshot. The request, host, and alarm suites
passed. The timer is disarmed before each lifecycle boundary and rearmed only
after the relevant fence is cleared.

Remaining release evidence is privileged live Linux activation for memory
plug/unplug and changed destination capacity, a real 5BSD virtio-mem driver,
and packed-ring coverage. RTC still needs Linux and 5BSD live activation,
clock-step/alarm behavior under a real guest, packed-ring operation, and
repeated active checkpoint/restore.

### 2026-08-07 — virtio-sound lifecycle and snapshot audit

Reviewed the sound control, playback, capture, host-stream, asynchronous
completion, readiness, reset, suspend, checkpoint, and restore paths.  Data
chains are retained only while an asynchronous job owns an independently
copied payload; release drains or fails every outstanding descriptor before
freeing its stream.  Checkpoint first closes async admission, then takes the
same codec mutex used by notifications and readiness callbacks, and reopens
admission only after the paired state operation completes.  The portable
snapshot records stream and backend identity state, not host file descriptors
or live PCM buffers.

The audit found and corrected two build-gate defects: the direct snapshot
preflight's conditional lock sequence was opaque to thread-safety analysis,
and its test default-initialized a now-const snapshot ABI field.  The wrapper
now has separate locked and already-locked paths, and the test initializes the
complete immutable buffer prefix.  All host, PCI, control/data queue, and async
ATF cases pass with `-Werror`.

Remaining release evidence is real Linux playback/capture with a production
host audio backend, format/rate/channel negotiation, underrun/overrun policy,
active PCM checkpoint policy, packed live traffic, and a real 5BSD guest
driver before cross-guest sound coverage can be claimed.

### 2026-08-07 — common checkpoint lifecycle and portability audit

Reviewed the shared pause/resume and snapshot transaction path after the
device-specific audits.  Checkpoint captures common state, transport state,
queue mappings, administration state, and device state in ordered sections.
Restore takes an in-memory backup before publication; an error restores the
common state and queues, rolls back administration state where possible, and
marks the device incomplete and reset-required if recovery cannot establish a
known-good destination.  A guest-suspend owner and a checkpoint owner remain
distinct so repeated restores neither leak a backend freeze nor reopen a
guest-suspended backend.

All rootless checkpoint topology, NUMA, CPU, machine, compatibility, PCI,
identity, manifest, device-memory, and portable-image ATF cases passed.  The
snapshot-portability validator and its hostile fixture passed as well: the
fixture injects an escaped native snapshot field and is rejected.  Privileged
evidence still required is repeated live restore under active I/O for every
promoted device and cross-host/cross-architecture restore once corresponding
hardware is available.

### 2026-08-07 — packed virtqueue conformance audit

Reviewed packed descriptor ownership, non-power-of-two queue wrap arithmetic,
event suppression, indirect-table rejection rules, completion ordering, queue
reset, and checkpoint cursor/mapping restoration.  The implementation treats
the packed completion cache as destination-local runtime state and refuses a
checkpoint with retained request ownership; it never carries that cache across
a split/packed layout change.  Snapshot cursors and wrap bits are encoded as
explicit portable fields and validated before mapping replacement.

The independent document-constant packed model, production packed engine, and
common VirtIO core ATF suites passed.  The independent model deliberately does
not include bhyve ring headers, and exercises queue sizes including one and
non-powers-of-two, wrap crossings, event offsets, in-order batching, invalid
markers, reset, and failure.  Remaining privileged evidence is guest-negotiated
packed-ring operation for each promoted device on Linux and 5BSD, including
active traffic, interrupt mode coverage, queue-local reset, and checkpoint at
wrap boundaries.

### 2026-08-07 — ACCESS_PLATFORM and virtio-IOMMU audit

Reviewed the VirtIO-IOMMU protocol, request/event queues, endpoint topology,
mapping permissions, fault records, translated DMA bridge, and state restore.
Authorization and address-space selection are linearized under the IOMMU state
mutex, while the external guest-RAM mapper runs after unlocking.  A per-endpoint
DMA lease pins the selected domain/bypass view until every request using it
drains; revoking attach, detach, unmap, reset, and default-bypass changes then
returns BUSY or waits for the safe epoch transition rather than invalidating an
in-flight request's address space.

All config, protocol, event, queue, request, state, topology, VIOT, and PCI
IOMMU ATF suites passed rootlessly.  They cover reserved fields, fragmented
buffers, output atomicity, map/unmap feature gating, permissions, faults,
active-DMA revocation retries, reset retries, snapshot validation, and ACPI
VIOT topology.  Still required before release is a privileged live guest using
ACCESS_PLATFORM across each supported device, with mapping/unmapping and
checkpoint under real DMA traffic.  That evidence must be gathered separately
on each target architecture/IOMMU platform.

### 2026-08-09 — IOMMU raw-state ownership replay

The callback/lifetime replay checked the IOMMU state object separately from
its mutex-protected map tables.  GPA mapping, fault delivery, and the
DMA-idle notification intentionally run outside that mutex; adding an
internal reference count would therefore not make a caller that retained a
raw state pointer safe.  The ownership boundary is the common request DMA
lease: the publishing PCI device closes new work, drains all acquired endpoint
leases, unpublishes any snapshot-validation state, and only then destroys the
state.  The public state header now records that precondition explicitly, the
private-interface ledger records it as `VIRTIO-PRIVATE-105`, and the existing
active-DMA transfer-phase test is required by the source validator.

This is a contract clarification and regression fence, not a claim of live
IOMMU qualification.  Linux and 5BSD ACCESS_PLATFORM activation, real
mapping/unmapping under DMA, and active-I/O checkpoint remain root-only,
architecture-specific release gates.

### 2026-08-09 — sound progress callback ownership replay

The sound async-owner replay found that the nonblocking backend `progress`
callback was invoked while its owner mutex was held.  A real host readiness
callback must be able to inspect owner state without deadlocking.  Progress
now pins the stream job, drops the mutex for the callback, and reacquires it
before any job mutation or completion publication.  Cancel, quiesce, resume,
and destruction treat that pin as active ownership and return `EBUSY` until it
settles.  The focused test performs a reentrant pending-state query from the
progress callback and verifies the job remains pinned; the private ledger and
source validator record this as `VIRTIO-PRIVATE-106`.

This closes a host callback-lifetime defect in the provisional sound model.
It does not promote sound: production host audio, Linux playback/capture,
packed-ring operation, 5BSD driver support, and active checkpoint policy are
still separate release gates.

### 2026-08-07 — nested VMX boundary audit

Re-ran the nested-VMX architectural model and requirements gate, including the
entry-edge matrix that distinguishes cold, resumed, hot, synthetic, rejected,
and real post-entry VMX paths.  The current execution boundary remains
intentionally fail-closed: it returns `EOPNOTSUPP` rather than attempting an
incomplete VMCS02 entry path.  The ledger requires one atomic integration of
VMCS12 validation/composition, exact pre-entry and post-entry owner settlement,
L2 residency cleanup, exit reflection, EPT/VPID handling, and snapshot state;
the guard cannot be removed piecemeal.

The rootless model suite and requirement/evidence validators passed.  This is
not live nested-VMX qualification.  Required future evidence remains Intel VMX
hardware execution with a Linux/KVM L1 and Linux/5BSD L2 guests; VMX instruction
and VM-entry failure behavior; interrupts/APIC/timers; EPT/VPID invalidation;
save/restore while L2 runs; and repeated create/destroy, fault, concurrency,
and soak runs.  AMD SVM stays architecture/model verified until AMD hardware
is available.

### 2026-08-07 — administration queues and shared-memory audit

Reviewed the administration command owner, group/resource/capability models,
PCI queue binding, lifecycle fences, queue-local reset, snapshot controller
state, and modern shared-memory capability construction.  Administration
queues are intentionally feature-gated: the modern transport advertises
`VIRTIO_F_ADMIN_VQ` only after a device supplies both staged queue storage and
an owning PCI binding for parse, completion, drain, reset, suspend, and
restore.  No promoted bhyve device currently supplies that complete binding,
so no incomplete administration interface is exposed to guests.

The shared-memory layer registers a fixed, sorted capability topology before
the guest status handshake, seals it before discovery, validates BAR bounds
without overflow, and allows backing replacement only behind a reset,
quiesce, suspend, or checkpoint fence.  GPU and pmem use the layer; restore
compares the full region topology rather than preserving a host pointer or
file descriptor.  All rootless administration capability, device-parts,
group, PCI, resource, SR-IOV, controller, modern-transport shared-memory, and
checkpoint-compatibility ATF cases passed.  Required future live evidence is
a device that deliberately promotes an administration binding, plus guest
command, cancellation, saturation, queue-reset, suspend, and restore tests.
