## VirtQueue completion-layout replay (2026-08-08)

A source-order review of the shared completion paths found that
`vq_relchain_req()` and `vq_relchain_group()` consumed ownership using the
layout recorded when a request was acquired, but selected the publication
format from the current queue layout without independently checking that the
two still matched.  Queue generation normally changes with layout, but a
malformed same-generation lifecycle transition could otherwise consume packed
ownership and publish a split used entry (or the converse).

The common completion APIs now retire stale generations first, preserving the
ordinary reset/cancellation contract, then latch `DEVICE_NEEDS_RESET` and
retire ownership without publication for a same-generation layout mismatch.
The rootless core harness covers single and grouped malformed transitions plus
their generation-changing stale counterparts.  A caller audit found no device
completion bypass: all bhyve device descriptor paths acquire a `vi_req` and
complete, return, or discard it through the common fenced APIs.

Fresh rootless evidence: the sanitizer-backed core harness passed 752 checks;
the independent VirtIO requirements/oracle validator passed 236 entries; and
the portable snapshot model passed 30 cases.  This is shared-core evidence,
not a substitute for the remaining privileged Linux/5BSD packed-ring,
checkpoint, and soak qualification.

## Provisional activation and DMA-domain replay (2026-08-08)

The current source-level replay traced each modern feature from the device
capability mask through `FEATURES_OK` and the common DMA mapper.  Optional
packed rings and the balloon, GPU, RTC, sound, filesystem, memory, and pmem
extensions remain configuration opt-ins; administration remains withheld
unless a complete queue binding is present.  The transport removes
`ACCESS_PLATFORM` unless a modern, eligible device has a published DMA domain,
and rejects `FEATURES_OK` if such a domain exists but the driver did not accept
that bit.

The VirtIO-IOMMU path builds its endpoint topology before publishing a domain,
refuses publication while a device is running or has active common-core DMA,
and symmetrically refuses removal until those leases drain.  Its prepared
restore fabric is visible only to the validating thread and is withdrawn before
destruction.  The complete ASan/UBSan device harness passed (`646` main checks
and `497` compatibility checks, zero failures), including IOMMU protocol,
mapping, concurrency, topology, fault, and restore fixtures.  This confirms
the host model and activation boundary only; translated-DMA guests, live
Linux/5BSD device operation, restore, and soak remain required release gates.

## AF_VSOCK transport lifetime replay (2026-08-08)

The kernel transport replay rechecked the non-standard provider boundary
separately from the bhyve VirtIO model.  A guest has one active VirtIO-vsock
transport; host-side bhyve providers are independent per VM and remain the
scaling mechanism for many guests.  Attach serializes the global softc check
with transport ownership, so a failed second device cannot replace or clear a
working transport.  Detach withdraws ownership, wakes AF_VSOCK users, and
waits for an RX callback that temporarily drops the transport mutex before it
stops and drains virtqueues.  The `virtio_vsock.ko` module rebuilt in a fresh
object tree with `-Werror`.

This review does not substitute for the existing privileged ATF and
multi-VM/provider qualification: reset, hot-unplug, provider close, CID
collision, and long concurrent-connection soak still require the root-owned
kernel and live-guest lanes in the qualification handoff.

## Common snapshot ABI and packed-ring replay (2026-08-08)

A fresh `sys/modules/vmm` build produced `vmm.ko` with `-Werror`.  The
descriptor-owned checkpoint-session review then traced the fixed-width
version-1 `VM_SNAPSHOT_SESSION` management ABI from libvmmapi through the
amd64 VMM dispatcher and the common event coordinator.  Its kernel-issued
identity is transient, bound to one writable management descriptor, released
or aborted on every close path, and never included in a checkpoint record.
The source checkpoint and destination-restore transactions retain that fence
through their respective publication boundaries and leave an unresolved owner
stopped rather than resuming optimistically.

This ioctl is currently an amd64 VMM management ABI, not a cross-architecture
save-state promise: arm64 and riscv do not expose the corresponding machdep
dispatcher.  Portable device records, their fixed-width little-endian
envelopes, and the common event coordinator remain separate from this
architecture-local admission control.  A future VMM backend must either add
an equivalent owned transaction with installed-build/live evidence or reject
the operation; it must not merely copy the ioctl declaration.

The independent packed-ring model and the production packed helper were also
compared directly.  They agree on ownership bits, non-power-of-two wrapping,
descriptor-event intervals, invalid state rejection, and one-revolution
advance limits.  The common modern snapshot path persists packed cursors in
fixed-width form and rejects impossible restored status/feature combinations.
This is model and source evidence only; packed Linux/5BSD activation,
checkpoint, and soak evidence remain release gates.

## Nested-owner and portable-DMA source-order replay (2026-08-08)

The nested owner boundary was replayed directly against the complete

path that retires a supplied common owner is the initial lifecycle decision,

The portable checkpoint/DMA review traced the common modern queue codec and

IOMMU snapshots reject active DMA and storage aliases, stage a complete

## Suspend-callback and activation-ledger replay (2026-08-08)

The advertised `VIRTIO_F_SUSPEND` surface was reviewed one more time at the
actual common-status transition, rather than treating the presence of a
device callback as sufficient.  `vi_modern_suspend()` first closes queue
admission, drains any negotiated administration queue, invokes the device
callback, and publishes SUSPEND only after that callback succeeds.  A failure
reopens only the common fence after publishing `NEEDS_RESET`; resume retains
the fence on failure and requires a full reset.  The GPU, IOMMU, and RNG
callbacks are deliberately no-ops because their request paths are synchronous
and retain no worker-owned request after the common fence.  Devices which do
retain a timer, external backend, held descriptor, or asynchronous work have
their own drain/reconstruction callback.  No callback was changed in this
pass: changing a synchronous callback merely to make it look busy would not
add a correctness guarantee.

The activation ledger was independently classified by its Linux and rebuilt
5BSD columns.  It currently contains 120 non-header feature rows: exercised
entries retain exact guest and host evidence, while the remaining rows are
explicitly `pending`, `driver-gap`, or `not-applicable`.  In particular,
packed queues, multi-queue, RSS, hash reporting, block write-zeroes, SCSI
events, and stream/seqpacket vsock already have some live guest evidence, but
that evidence is never generalized to the other guest or device columns.
The remaining work is therefore visible and actionable: Linux activation for
the newer provisional devices and the rebuilt-5BSD activation matrix, plus
root-only reset, device-suspend, translated-DMA, checkpoint, and soak lanes.

The nested requirements validator (433 requirements, 282 private-boundary
entries, and 12 live hardware feature groups), ASan/UBSan nested-model build,
and rootless device harness were rerun after this classification.  They passed
without a new source-level finding.  The production nested common-owner fence
continues to be deliberately fail-closed until its full source-ordered VMCS02
transaction exists.

The common modern-transport lifecycle test now explicitly retries a completed
SUSPEND status write and a completed running-status write.  It proves that
the former does not invoke a second device drain and that the latter does not
invoke a second resume callback.  The full device harness rerun passed with
646 common/vsock checks, 501 transport checks, 786 input checks, 100 RNG
checks, and two snapshot-runner checks; expected malformed-input diagnostics
were emitted without a failing group.

## Nested model/linkage boundary replay (2026-08-08)

The Intel nested owner-outcome implementation remains deliberately a
test-compiled value model.  The requirements validator now checks both sides
of that statement: `vmx_nested_owner_outcome.c` must not occur in the `vmm.ko`
source list, and the production `vmx.c` source must neither include its header
nor reference either of its pre-entry or post-entry adapters.  A Makefile-only
check was not enough, because an accidental header import could make a partial
integration look intentional while the object was still unlinked.

This is not a permanent prohibition on the model becoming production code.
The guard is deliberately paired with the existing requirement for one
source-ordered, all-path VMCS02 owner transaction and installed Intel
qualification.  That future change must replace the guard and its fail-closed
`EOPNOTSUPP` boundary together; it must not link or call the model as an
incremental readiness switch.  The nested requirements validator passed after
the strengthened boundary check.

The complete rootless VirtIO harness was replayed after the same review.  It
validated 236 requirements against 683 independent oracle definitions,
97 non-standard interface contracts, 58 DTrace wrappers, the portable
snapshot and DMA-boundary guards, and the common/vsock (646), transport
(501), input (786), and RNG (100) sanitizer-backed checks with no failures.
The activation ledger still reports 81 pending Linux and 116 pending rebuilt
5BSD live claims; this local result does not promote any of those claims.

## CPU-contract architecture enum review (2026-08-08)

The checkpoint CPU contract now treats its architecture field as a closed,
versioned wire enum.  Previously, the generic decoder accepted every nonzero
value even though only amd64, arm64, and riscv64 have named capture and
compatibility policies.  An unknown value could not match a current host, but
accepting it still weakened the format boundary and could let a future
architecture extension be parsed by an older build.  Validation now rejects
unknown architecture values before an encode, decode, or match operation
publishes a contract.  The independent CPU-contract test corrupts the
little-endian architecture bytes and also checks an unknown in-memory tag.
The `-Werror` test build and the sanitizer-backed device harness pass with the
closed enum.

## Reference-artifact availability replay (2026-08-08)

The reference catalog itself remains complete and reproducible: it pins the
VirtIO 1.4 CS01 PDF, Intel SDM revision 092 volumes 3 and 4, and exact Linux
and QEMU source revisions with publication dates, HTTPS locations, SHA-256
digests, applicability, and normative/explanatory classifications.  The
rootless validator accepts that metadata in `--waspnest` mode without
downloading or importing any third-party source.

This checkout does not currently contain the five authenticated artifacts in
an operator-supplied cache.  That is intentionally reported as an outstanding
qualification input, not hidden by treating the independent C oracle or a
mutable web page as the primary source.  Before a release or hardware
qualification run, place exactly the five regular, non-symlink artifacts in a
private cache and invoke `validate-virtio-reference-corpus.sh` with that
directory.  The validator rejects a missing, extra, duplicated, symbolic, or
digest-mismatched artifact.  No feature claim is promoted by the metadata-only
rootless result.

## CPU-contract canonical-wire replay (2026-08-08)

The CPU-contract text format is a canonical, lower-case hexadecimal encoding,
not a permissive display format.  The hostile-input test now changes an `a`
nibble to `A` in an otherwise valid, independently constructed record and
requires decode failure.  This closes the gap where the noncanonical-input
test had only damaged the magic and therefore did not distinguish strict
canonical parsing from a decoder that normalized upper-case payload data.

The rootless replay rebuilt `checkpoint_cpu_test` with `-Werror`, passed its
five direct ATF cases, and passed both the portable snapshot guard and its

callbacks return `EOPNOTSUPP` until those architectures define versioned CPU
contracts.  Common device state remains portable in either case, but a new
checkpoint must not claim portable CPU execution state that does not exist.

## Nested policy and checkpoint-model replay (2026-08-08)

The nested requirements validator again passed its complete ledger (433

groups), and the policy-pair verifier's independent self-test passed.  A

## Architecture-selected restore-admission replay (2026-08-08)

The generic CPU-contract codec intentionally recognizes the three named wire
architectures, but recognition is not restore admission.  The restore path
must first decode the source contract, capture a destination contract through
the selected machine callback, and only then compare the two.  This ordering
keeps ARM64 and RISC-V fail-closed while their callbacks return
`EOPNOTSUPP`; a recognized source tag cannot bypass the missing native
capture policy.

The snapshot portability guard now enforces that exact source ordering in the
restore block.  Its self-test privately renames the capture call and requires
the guard to reject the fixture, in addition to the existing escaped native
VirtIO snapshot-field fixture.  The positive guard, both negative fixtures,
and the 30-case snapshot-model suite passed.  This is structural/rootless
evidence; architecture-specific restore execution remains a later live gate.

## Common checkpoint cleanup idempotence replay (2026-08-08)

The common VirtIO checkpoint pause and resume paths had a small but real
cleanup-order defect.  They rejected a missing backend hook before checking
whether that device had acquired the corresponding checkpoint ownership.  A
generic rollback can pause or resume the complete PCI list, so a transition
that is already complete—or was never entered—must be a no-op rather than
convert another device's failure cleanup into `EOPNOTSUPP`.  Both callback
requirements now follow their ownership tests: an inert transition returns
success, while a genuinely new pause or a genuinely paused resume still
fails closed if it lacks its required backend inverse.

The independent core test covers both pause and resume states.  `virtio_core_test` rebuilt
with `-Werror`; its targeted lifecycle cases and complete direct ATF sweep
passed.  Expected malformed-descriptor and malformed-snapshot diagnostics
were emitted by negative cases only.

## Rootless harness completion-contract replay (2026-08-08)

The VM-free device harness now publishes an optional atomic completion record
for asynchronous orchestration.  It overwrites any earlier record with
`RUNNING device harness` before validation begins, publishes `PASS device
harness all tests passed` only after the final sanitizer lane, and publishes
`FAIL device harness exit=N` from its exit trap on every earlier nonzero
return.  The host-regression gate requires the exact PASS record after the
harness command, so redirected/truncated logs and stale successful records
cannot authorize later VM work.

Both sides of the contract were tested without privileged host state: an
intentionally invalid source root produced the expected durable failure
record, then a clean AddressSanitizer/UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer harness
rerun reached the PASS record after every lane.  The latter included the
filesystem-handle lane that had encountered a non-reproducible linker-path
failure during an overlapping run; it and all later GPU, IOMMU, network, and
SCSI lanes completed with zero check failures.  The retained clean workspace
is `/tmp/tmp.nx6ErZ3ikE`; it is diagnostic evidence only and may be removed
after log retention.

The enclosing VM-free host-regression gate was then replayed with
`RUN_PRIVILEGED_ATF=no` and completed successfully after consuming that exact
PASS record.  Its independent nested-VMX portion validated 433 requirements,
282 non-standard interfaces, and 12 tracked root-only live feature groups,
then passed 349 AddressSanitizer/UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer model cases.  The
privileged kernel/MAC ATF suites were explicitly deferred by configuration;
this replay is rootless orchestration evidence, not live hardware evidence.

A follow-up interruption test found and corrected a signal-path omission:
HUP, INT, and TERM now publish failure records with their conventional shell
statuses instead of leaving a misleading `RUNNING` record.  A live TERM replay
ended with shell status 143 and the exact record `FAIL device harness
exit=143`.

## Nested qualification cleanup and evidence replay (2026-08-08)

The nested-VMX evidence transaction was re-audited from its mutable runner
output through sealed publication.  The wrapper binds every artifact to one
fresh run identifier, hashes all trusted inputs before and after execution,
checks a stable host nested-VMX policy, requires one distinct Linux-L2,
5BSD-L2, and host proof for every ledger group, then seals and rehashes the
bundle before atomically publishing it.  FreeBSD `timeout(1)` is intentionally
used without `--foreground`: in that mode it is the command's descendant
reaper, so a runner cannot successfully return while a background bhyve or
helper remains alive.  The requirements validator and its negative fixture
reject foreground mode explicitly.

The review also corrected the rootless model and evidence self-test signal
traps.  Their cleanup handlers now run only via `EXIT`; HUP, INT, and TERM
first select their conventional nonzero exit statuses.  This prevents a
signal from removing a private scratch directory and then resuming the test
against the deleted path.  Staging, completed-evidence, coverage, and

negative fixtures.  This is orchestration and evidence-contract validation;
the actual nested L2 hardware run remains blocked by the deliberate
production `EOPNOTSUPP` fence until the full VMCS02 residency transaction is

## VirtIO-lab PID-identity replay (2026-08-08)

The VM-lab scheduler previously treated daemon(8)'s supervisor and child PID
files plus their parent relationship as sufficient proof that a resumable case
was still owned by this run.  That was too weak for `cancel` and `--resume`:
PIDs can be recycled.  The scheduler now records a SHA-256 identity over each
process's start time and command from its existing control-plane scan.  Only a
matching PID, parent, and identity is live/cancellable.  A live pair with
missing or mismatched identities is deliberately stale/busy, never adopted or
signalled; a resumed run therefore cannot overwrite it with a second case.

Daemon PID publication is asynchronous, so a fast completed compiler case is
not made a false launch failure when it exits before identities are observable.
The scheduler simply waits for the already-atomic terminal status; a
nonterminal case without recorded identities is not treated as live and is
bounded by the existing supervisor failure path.  The full rootless
`virtio-lab` self-test passed, including the active cancellation and
interrupted-manager-resume cases plus a new deliberate identity-mismatch case
that proves cancellation reports zero until the original identity is restored.

## Common-device lifecycle replay (2026-08-08)

The synchronous-device lifecycle contract was rechecked against the common
checkpoint fence rather than treating no-op hooks as automatically incomplete.
GPU queue work is serialized by the common device mutex and its resource graph
has a separate locked portable-state codec; its no-op pause is therefore a
valid statement that it has no independent backend worker to drain.  Balloon
drains its retained statistics descriptor, RTC disarms/rearms its host timer,
and the IOMMU rejects late callback work through the common quiesce fence.

The IOMMU fault path was specifically traced for lock recursion: translation
records a fault while holding its state lock, drops that lock, and only then
invokes the PCI callback that takes the device lock to drain the event queue.
Request processing takes the device lock before entering the state codec, so
there is no inverted or recursive state/device-lock acquisition in this path.
The independent VM-free harness then completed with 646 core, 505 modern,
786 input, and 100 RNG checks, all passing.  Expected diagnostic messages were
from negative cases.  Live suspend, translated-DMA, and checkpoint execution
remain explicitly root-only qualification work.

## Sound status-callback lock ownership replay (2026-08-08)

The common modern VirtIO status path invokes device suspend and reset callbacks
while `vs_mtx` is held, and modern queue-reset writes invoke the queue-reset
callback with the same ownership.  The sound device deliberately aliases that
mutex to `vssc_mtx`, but those callbacks had each tried to acquire it a second
time.  A guest-issued `SUSPEND`, device reset, or PCM queue reset could
consequently self-deadlock before the register write returned.

Both callbacks now preserve an already-held transport mutex and acquire/release
it only for direct callers.  This retains the callback serialization required
for asynchronous audio admission and backend-event cancellation without
changing transport ownership.  Independent harness cases hold the concrete
mutex across all three callback paths and verify that it remains owned until
the simulated transport releases it.

The rootless sound/device harness and an isolated bhyve build pass after the
change.  Privileged evidence still required: a Linux guest negotiating
`VIRTIO_F_SUSPEND`, with an idle and an active PCM queue, must issue suspend,
resume, and reset while a host sound backend is attached; checkpoint and soak
profiles should then cover the null and OSS backends.  This is not yet claimed
as live-guest qualification.

The same callback-ownership replay found an equivalent full-reset defect in
the userspace and kernel-provider VirtIO-vsock device: its reset hook took
`vsc_mtx` even though status reset already owns that aliased common mutex.
The hook now uses the same direct-versus-transport ownership contract, and a
vsock model case covers the modern status-reset ownership form.  This closes a
real register-path deadlock rather than changing provider semantics; live
kernel-provider reset/rebind and multi-VM matrix evidence remain root-only.
The direct-call compatibility path retains its temporary lock through
`vi_reset_dev()`, whose common invariant requires `vs_mtx` ownership whenever
that mutex is configured.

The restore transition audit also found that the virtio-mem
`vc_restore_suspended` hook unconditionally acquired its aliased device mutex,
despite the common lifecycle contract allowing that hook to be entered with
checkpoint ownership already held.  It now preserves either ownership context,
and a held-lock model case verifies the restore path.  This keeps the portable
frozen configuration semantics unchanged while preventing a destination
restore deadlock.

## Nested VMX owner-transaction boundary replay (2026-08-08)

The common stack-only startup-owner state machine now has the deferred
pre-entry and post-entry primitives that a VMCS02 adapter will need.  They
retain a failed admission or a post-exit loop disposition until the adapter
has completed its private inverse, and then allow an exact terminal error to
override a result that would otherwise request replay.  The primitive itself
is architecture-neutral and the rootless tests cover its aliasing,
repeat-resolution, invalid-error, and retirement rules.

That does not make `vmx_run_nested()` ready to consume the owner.  A
source-first replay mapped its cold initial, thawed-resume, and hot re-entry
paths through the final instruction boundary.  On those paths the private
state may include VMCS02-current association, L2 software MSRs and TSC_AUX,
nested EPT activation, debug and host descriptor state, and an event
transaction before the VMX instruction result is authoritative.  Initial
rejection, resumed failed entry, synthetic publication, direct reflection,
EPT routing, normal unhandled exits, and fatal hot detach each require a
different inverse and have different replay meaning.

Consequently the present `EOPNOTSUPP` fence for a non-NULL common owner in
the nested path is intentional and remains correct.  The only direct nested
owner action is the demonstrably pre-residency lifecycle software exit.  A
future activation must install one source-ordered typed bridge which: checks
the owner after the final private pre-entry preparation; resolves deferred
pre-entry results only after the matching rollback or refreeze; commits only
a proved L2 VM exit; and resolves deferred post-entry results only after
route-specific freeze or terminal detach.  It must not be enabled by changing
the fence alone.  The edge matrix and nested requirement validator pin this
rule, and live Intel/L1/L2 qualification remains pending.

## Optional IN_ORDER advertisement replay (2026-08-08)

The optional `VIRTIO_F_IN_ORDER` bit was replayed against each host device's
completion ownership rather than inferred from ordinary FIFO request intake.
Synchronous RNG, input, and console paths complete their available heads in
the same call and retain their documented offer. PMEM completion, however,
is owned by a durable-backing worker, while sound completion can be retained
until a host readiness event and then be cancelled by lifecycle work. Their
current generation and queue fences prevent stale or duplicate completion,
but do not constitute the stronger device-wide in-order completion promise.

Both devices now withhold `VIRTIO_F_IN_ORDER`; their independent PCI-capability
tests assert the absence of the bit. This is a conformance correction, not a
loss of ordinary split or packed-ring ordering protection: the common packed
completion cache still preserves descriptor ownership and each device remains
free to add the feature only after an explicit end-to-end async-order proof.
The rootless device harness and requirements ledger passed after the change.
Live PMEM and sound qualification remains pending and must record the final
negotiated feature set rather than assuming the optional bit is present.

A follow-up source pass found that balloon, GPU, IOMMU, memory, and RTC had
also advertised the bit despite the ledger's narrower, tested policy.  Their
ordinary request paths currently consume queue heads sequentially, but balloon
statistics and RTC alarm buffers are completed by timer paths, IOMMU has
event/DMA callbacks, memory has host configuration callbacks, and GPU spans a
display-backend lifecycle.  None had an independent multi-buffer ordering
qualification across those paths.  They now likewise withhold the optional
bit.  RNG, input, and console remain the only offers because their existing
tests exercise their synchronous completion contract.  This is intentionally
conservative and preserves compatibility: guests that do not negotiate the
optional bit continue to use the normative descriptor and used-ring rules.

## Nested VMX build-membership replay (2026-08-08)

The nested source inventory now distinguishes a compiled `vmm.ko` component
from a deliberately model-only prerequisite.  The requirements validator
requires every `vmx_nested_*.c` source to be either present in the module
Makefile or to declare both its model-only role and its intentional exclusion
from `vmm.ko`.  `vmx_nested_owner_outcome.c` is the sole current exception:
it models value precedence for a future owner bridge and is intentionally
unlinked while `vmx_run_nested()` remains fail closed.  The gate prevents an
unlinked source from being mistaken for a production implementation, without
promoting the model into the Intel runtime or save-state ABI.

## Destination restore startup-fence replay (2026-08-08)

The checkpoint compatibility audit found that `bhyverun` created its vCPU
threads before the destination restore transaction began.  A newly created
thread could therefore reach `vm_loop()` with destination-local initial state
before the transaction owned the all-vCPU restore lease.  This was a real
ordering defect even though normal restores usually reached the transaction
quickly.

Restore now arms an explicit common startup fence before the first vCPU is
created.  `checkpoint_cpu_add()` registers each new thread as suspended and
waits on the existing condition variable; it never enters guest execution.
The restore transaction requires that fence, reconstructs memory, devices and
kernel state under the exact session, commits, resumes devices, and only then
releases the startup fence.  Any preflight, session, memory, device, kernel,
commit, or resume failure leaves the fence held and bhyve exits rather than
executing a partial destination.  This is common userspace lifecycle logic;
it carries no Intel-specific state and applies to future architecture ports.

The rootless portable checkpoint model (30 cases), portability negative
fixture, requirements gate, lab self-test, and full device harness passed.
The isolated bhyve build completed with `-Werror` after rebuilding
`libvmmapi` in the same object root, which resolved an initial stale-object
link mismatch.  The live checkpoint profile remains the required privileged
confirmation.

## SCSI checkpoint and event-stream replay (2026-08-08)

The SCSI device was replayed against the VirtIO 1.4 configuration, eventq,
HOTPLUG, and CHANGE requirements.  The implementation resets `sense_size` and
`cdb_size` through the ordinary device reset path, applies the legacy endian
rule through the device codec, and treats the request, control, and event
queues as distinct queue roles.  Event records are only retained after
`DRIVER_OK` and only for negotiated event features; parameter-change records
for MMC media are deliberately filtered as required by the specification.

The CTL source callback, queue kick, reset, suspend, and checkpoint paths all
serialize event state with `vss_mtx`.  Both the CTL drain and guest eventq
drain have explicit queue-sized/host-budget bounds, so they do not turn a
continuously ready source into an unbounded mevent dispatch.  Sequence gaps,
source overflow, invalid source records, and destination reconstruction reset
the local state into the existing loss-aware rescan path.  A destination does
not pretend that its CTL subscription was migrated: it compares the complete
opaque CTL inventory identity and then requires a rescan notification after a
successful restore.

Active requests drain against one monotonic device deadline while the common
VirtIO lifecycle fence blocks new descriptor ownership.  Selectively reset
queues retain their old-incarnation fence and are not reopened accidentally by
checkpoint or guest suspend/resume.  Focused `virtio_scsi_test` and
`virtio_scsi_event_test` ATF cases all passed rootlessly; the full device
harness and requirements ledger also passed.  Privileged live coverage still
needs to exercise CTL LUN add/remove/change and a checkpoint with a real CTL
backend, because those external operations cannot be faithfully reproduced in
the rootless model.

## Console checkpoint and port-lifecycle replay (2026-08-08)

The console device was checked against the VirtIO 1.4 console initialization,
multiport control, queue-direction, and legacy-endian requirements.  Its
private snapshot records only portable port lifecycle state and immutable
listener identity.  A connected host socket, retained host output, or an
in-flight socket event registration is intentionally rejected at checkpoint:
file descriptors and host-stream contents are not silently serialized as if
they were portable device state.  The destination must present the same port
layout, names, and listener paths before any mutable fields are committed.

The common lifecycle fence serializes descriptor access, while `vsc_mtx`
serializes listener accept, socket callbacks, reset, suspend, and preflight.
Resume explicitly rearms pre-existing receive descriptors and the control
receive queue, so it does not require a new guest kick after a suspend or
checkpoint boundary.  The rootless console suite covers control-port
ordering, close/reset races, selective reset callback fencing, snapshot wire
identity and atomicity, malformed lifecycle states, active-host-socket
rejection, and preflight locking.  Live multiport reconnect and an inactive
listener checkpoint remain in the privileged matrix.

## 9P lifecycle and checkpoint replay (2026-08-08)

VirtIO 1.4 standardizes the 9P transport device identity but deliberately
does not standardize the 9P protocol or backend object model.  The review
therefore treats lib9p and the export as an explicit external-backend
contract: root path, root device/inode, read-only policy, mount tag,
negotiated features, protocol version, and message limits must match at the
destination.  Fids carry host descriptors and credentials, so any active fid,
accepted request, reset/reconnect transition, or selective-reset completion
causes checkpoint refusal rather than pointer/descriptor serialization.

Guest suspend preserves the mounted fid namespace only after the common
admission fence has drained requests to one monotonic deadline.  A selective
queue reset deliberately retains the lib9p connection and invalidates only
the old VirtIO queue incarnation; full reset closes and reconstructs the
connection.  Restore creates a new local completion generation and does not
import a source asynchronous-ownership token.  The rootless suite exercises
stale notifications, queue-reset preservation and completion, reset/reconnect
races, suspend drain, snapshot identity/atomicity, preflight serialization,
and rejection of every live session form.  Privileged Linux 9P mount/reset
and an intentionally rejected active-fid checkpoint remain required live
checks.

## Input event and checkpoint replay (2026-08-08)

The input implementation was replayed against the VirtIO 1.4 input
configuration, little-endian event wire format, queue-direction, and
whole-frame loss requirements.  It invalidates the cached selector response
when the guest changes `select` or `subsel`, emits zero-length unsupported
configuration responses, and keeps fields outside the advertised response
size zero.  Event and status values are explicitly translated between evdev's
native representation and the mandatory little-endian VirtIO wire format.

Host input is staged until `SYN_REPORT`; insufficient guest descriptors,
host `SYN_DROPPED`, allocation failure, reset, and independently reset event
queues discard or resynchronize a whole frame rather than leaking a partial
pointer/keyboard update.  The host event dispatch and drain paths have fixed
budgets, avoiding a level-triggered descriptor monopolizing mevent.  Checkpoint
disables the event registration before taking the device mutex, snapshots a
validated staged frame and configuration cache, and checks both path and
device identity on restore.  Rootless tests cover wire layout, scatter/gather,
host-event bounds, frame loss/resynchronization, reset/queue-reset stale-event
removal, suspend rearming, snapshot atomicity, and malformed staged frames.
Real Linux and 5BSD input-driver activation plus injection/reset/checkpoint
coverage remain privileged qualification work.

## Vsock backend checkpoint replay (2026-08-08)

Both vsock backends share the same VirtIO device model but have different
external-state contracts.  The userspace backend can checkpoint only when its
listener is configured and every host control connection, relay socket,
reassembly buffer, and guest-to-host backlog is absent.  It records backend
kind, guest CID, negotiated features, listener identity, and next ephemeral
port; it rejects a changed destination rather than restoring file descriptors
or stream bytes.  The kernel backend uses its explicit provider FREEZE/THAW
ABI while the device mutex and common VirtIO fence stop all source callbacks.
Provider replies must certify an empty connection/queue state and reserved
fields; malformed replies are thawed or fail closed with `NEEDS_RESET`.

Restore never imports a provider's ephemeral ownership state.  It reinstalls
the negotiated device feature epoch while an empty kernel transport remains
frozen, then thaws before source callbacks are reopened.  A retry after a
failed thaw retains a clear locked/fenced state.  Rootless vsock tests cover
userspace and kernel snapshot identity, active-state rejection, lifecycle
admission fencing, provider freeze/thaw failures, malformed replies, retry,
multi-provider isolation, CID exclusivity, and reset/rebind behavior.  The
remaining privileged work is active-connection rejection and empty-backend
checkpoint validation with Linux and 5BSD guests, followed by multi-VM soak.

## RNG lifecycle replay (2026-08-08)

The entropy device has no device-private mutable state that can be portable
across hosts: entropy source identity and bytes must never be checkpointed or
replayed.  It therefore uses the common queue/PCI snapshot lifecycle only.
The common admission fence is sufficient because each request is completed
synchronously under the device mutex and no backend work or byte buffer
survives the callback.  A failed or short `/dev/random` read makes the device
enter `NEEDS_RESET`; invalid descriptor direction, length, and chain forms do
the same without publishing ambiguous output.  Notification work is bounded by
queue size.  Rootless tests cover those failures, packed/legacy offer policy,
the no-private-snapshot contract, and bounded dispatch.  Linux and 5BSD live
rebind/reset and checkpoint-after-read tests remain queued for privileged
qualification.

## Balloon ownership and checkpoint replay (2026-08-08)

The balloon review covered inflation/deflation ownership, statistics, free-page
hinting/reporting, page poison, queue reset, and the versioned bitmap snapshot
format.  PFN transitions are range-checked and idempotent, with host-memory
reclamation treated as a best-effort hint only after guest-visible ownership
has been committed.  PAGE_REPORTING without PAGE_POISON may discard reported
memory as permitted; with PAGE_POISON it deliberately preserves the required
poison value.  The device never offers an optional queue it has not configured.

Checkpoint completes the retained statistics descriptor before state is
written, because a queue token without descriptor ownership is not portable.
The inflated-page bitmap is serialized independently and restored through a
transactional old-to-new ownership transition; incompatible sizes, invalid
bits, old nonempty v1 records, malformed statistics state, and failed rollback
all fail closed.  Rootless tests cover PFN duplicates/ranges, accounting,
statistics ownership, poison/reporting behavior, queue reset, preflight
locking, snapshot corruption/repeat restore, and transition rollback.  Live
Linux balloon pressure/reporting and an active-I/O checkpoint are still
required before promotion; 5BSD activation depends on guest-driver support.

## Packed opt-in traceability replay (2026-08-08)

The activation ledger had explicit per-device packed-queue anchors, but that
alone could drift from a constructor that stopped making `RING_PACKED`
available.  The requirements validator now checks every supported bhyve data
model—9P, balloon, block, console, GPU, input, IOMMU, memory, network, RNG,
RTC, SCSI, sound, and vsock—for both its modern release anchor and a local
`packed` configuration opt-in that supplies `VIRTIO_F_RING_PACKED`.  It does
not infer support from the shared packed-ring parser, nor does it turn a
rootless source check into guest evidence.

The independent requirements validator passes with all fourteen mappings.
Linux and rebuilt-5BSD packed negotiation, traffic, reset, suspend, and
checkpoint lanes remain distinct privileged activation requirements in the
feature ledger.

## Nested startup-owner conversion boundary (2026-08-09)

The Intel nested VMX model now has independent value-level coverage for every
common-owner result class: cold and resumed failed entries, completed initial
rejection, real L2 entry, locally handled re-entry, EPT walking, direct L1
reflection, generic unhandled exits, and terminal private unwind.  That model
is intentionally not linked into `vmm.ko`.  The production nested runner
accepts a startup owner only for the initial lifecycle exit that is provably
before guest MSR entry, VMCS02 selection, EPT activation, debug residency, and
L2 event preparation.  It rejects every later owner-bearing invocation with
`EOPNOTSUPP` and records the distinct `vmm:vmx:nested:withheld` DTrace event.

This is a safety boundary, not a claim that kernel-owned nested entry is
implemented.  A production conversion must install one CPU-pinned transaction
which places the common attempted-entry guard immediately before
`vmx_enter_guest()`, reverses nested pmap/debug/descriptor state on a declined
guard, settles initial and resumed hardware-attempt provenance only after the
matching rollback or refreeze is complete, and defers post-entry owner results
until EPT/reflection/unhandled publication or hot-continuation freeze has
completed.  It must also resolve an unclassified hardware return as a terminal
error after the private unwind, never as a fabricated VM exit or replay.  The
edge matrix (`tests/sys/vmm/vmx-startup-entry-edge-matrix.tsv`) and the nested
requirements ledger map those obligations to the current source locations and
model tests.  The requirement validator enforces that the model remains
unlinked until this whole conversion is installed and then qualified on Intel
hardware.

The freshly built `tests/sys/vmm/vmx_nested_state_test` ATF program completed
165 of 165 cases successfully on 2026-08-09.  That rootless result covers the
architectural state, owner-outcome, hot/cold continuation, VMCS02 composition,
hardware-result classification, and portable-state models.  It is deliberately
not evidence of a live VMX instruction, an L1/L2 guest, or active-L2 restore;
those remain separate Intel-host qualification gates.

## GPU presentation and restore lifetime replay (2026-08-09)

The GPU 2D model invokes display callbacks and destination-DMA validation
outside its state mutex, so those paths cannot rely on the mutex alone to keep
the resource graph alive.  Review found that destruction could release the
state while an already admitted presentation callback—or a snapshot decode
performing external DMA validation—was still executing.  The state now closes
new command admission first, pins every outside-lock presentation or snapshot
operation, copies the immutable limits and callback vector needed after the
unlock, and drains those pins before destroying callback storage, resources,
or synchronization objects.  Restore rechecks destruction before publication;
a concurrent teardown therefore fails the restore with `ECANCELED` rather
than publishing into retired state.

The GPU ATF suite now uses independently encoded GPU1 version-3 bytes to hold
DMA validation in flight while another thread destroys the state, and it
separately holds a presentation reset callback through destruction.  Both
tests prove that the destroy path reaches its own callback and remains blocked
until the prior outside-lock owner releases.  `virtio_gpu_2d_state_test`
completed 18 of 18 tests successfully on 2026-08-09.  This is a rootless host
model result; Linux and 5BSD driver activation, packed-ring operation, and
active checkpoint remain privileged qualification gates in the activation
ledger.

## Memory and sound callback destruction replay (2026-08-09)

The portable VirtIO-memory host model deliberately calls the platform
`set_range` and configuration-notification callbacks without either mutable
state mutex held.  Review found that a concurrent destroy could otherwise free
the model and callback argument while one of those callbacks was executing.
The model now has a separate admission/drain fence: every public operation
pins the model, destruction closes admission, and destruction waits for the
last admitted operation before freeing the bitmaps, callback storage, or
locks.  The independent `destroy_drains_platform_callback` test holds a real
platform callback while another thread destroys the model, then verifies that
the callback operation and destruction complete in the only safe order.

The synchronous sound host had the analogous but smaller gap.  Every backend
operation already executes under `operation_mutex`, but `destroy` previously
destroyed that mutex without first serializing against an admitted callback.
Destruction now acquires `operation_mutex` and then `state_mutex` in the same
order as public operations before either lock is destroyed.  The
`destroy_drains_selected_backend_callback` regression blocks `SET_PARAMS`
inside the backend while a second thread destroys the host; release proves
that the post-callback state publication completes before teardown.

Both contracts are recorded as `VIRTIO-PRIVATE-107` and
`VIRTIO-PRIVATE-108`, with source-order validator anchors.  The complete
rootless device harness passed after the change, and bhyve rebuilt with
`-Werror`.  These are host-model lifetime corrections, not a claim that the
provisional virtio-mem or virtio-sound devices have completed their Linux,
5BSD, packed-ring, or checkpoint activation matrices.

## Filesystem connection teardown contract replay (2026-08-09)

The virtio-fs connection deliberately has no internal operation lock because
the backend event loop and synchronous completion path are caller serialized.
Its previous public comment named only lifecycle and readiness operations,
although progress, submission, and pressure queries also dereference the
connection while destruction can reclaim the queue, backend client, buffers,
and file descriptor.  The public contract now explicitly requires callers to
serialize concurrent operations and to exclude `destroy()` from every public
connection call.  A synchronous completion callback may submit replacement
work only on that same serialized path and must not destroy the connection.

This preserves the existing destruction ordering: `destroying` is latched,
the public queue pointer is withdrawn, retained requests are drained through
their normal completion path, and only then are backing objects reclaimed.
The private-interface validator pins both that order and the public contract;
the existing `destroy_withdraws_queue_before_completion` regression passed
after the clarification.  This is an ownership-contract repair, not evidence
of virtio-fs guest activation or checkpoint interoperability.

## RTC event rollback lifetime replay (2026-08-09)

The RTC alarm timer event retains the RTC PCI softc as its callback argument.
Review found that the initialization rollback used the asynchronous
`mevent_delete_close()` operation and then immediately reclaimed that argument.
An event already selected by the dispatcher could therefore still enter its
callback after the rollback freed the softc.  The failure path now uses the
shared synchronous close-delete barrier, which retires any callback before the
timer descriptor, alarm model, mutex, or softc are released.

The common mevent API now has `mevent_delete_close_sync()`: it keeps the
descriptor open until the dispatcher reaches callback retirement, then closes
it before acknowledging deletion.  The independent lifecycle test proves the
pre-dispatch retirement and descriptor-close behavior, and the RTC source
order is pinned as `VIRTIO-PRIVATE-109`.  This is a host teardown repair; it
does not claim RTC live alarm, packed-ring, guest, or migration qualification.

## Userspace-vsock initialization rollback replay (2026-08-09)

The userspace backend attaches listener, reaper, and child socket events.  A
later initialization failure can occur after dispatch has started, so merely
using the normal asynchronous connection-close routine before freeing the
device would leave a selected child callback holding an event reference to the
freed softc.  The rollback now publishes the lifecycle pause under the device
mutex, removes all child connections from lookup, releases the mutex so a
selected callback can observe that fence, then synchronously retires each
child event before reclaiming connection, control-connection, or device
storage.

The normal close path remains asynchronous because it can run on the event
thread itself; its immutable event IDs and post-lock lookup make a retired
connection callback harmless while the device remains alive.  The dedicated
initialization rollback has no such self-delete constraint and therefore uses
the stronger barrier.  `init_failure_detaches_and_retires_child_events` covers
the detach, accounting reset, callback admission fence, and synchronous
retirement sequence.  This host-model correction is ledgered as
`VIRTIO-PRIVATE-110`; live multi-VM, migration, and long-run qualification
remain separate root-only gates.

## Portable-state and lifecycle boundary replay (2026-08-09)

A fresh portability/lifecycle pass re-read the common VMS2 envelope and
common-vCPU codecs, the Intel nested checkpoint records, and the device
drain/destruction paths from their public entry points.  The portable records
continue to use fixed-width little-endian fields with explicit bounds and
alias checks.  `uintptr_t` values found in the VMM event/startup helpers are
explicitly transient storage credentials: they are neither exposed through a
snapshot codec nor retained across a checkpoint.  Intel-private VMCS02, EPT,
VPID, bitmap, provider, CPU, and callback ownership stays outside the
portable nested image; the active-L2 path reconstructs a cold continuation
and deliberately rejects run-pending and obsolete absolute-timer forms until
their destination reconstruction semantics are implemented.

The same pass found no timer-driven progress loop in the VirtIO device paths.
Operational pause, reset, suspend, and checkpoint drains use matching
`CLOCK_MONOTONIC` condition-variable deadlines where safe rollback exists.
The few intentionally unbounded waits are destruction fences for already
admitted external callbacks or administration commands; timing those out
would free their retained state and create a use-after-free.  They are
separately classified in `virtio-nonstandard-interfaces.tsv` and pinned by
source-order validators and direct drain tests rather than being mistaken for
polling.  The current focused validation pass completed the 433-entry nested
requirements ledger, 282 nested private-interface entries, standalone public
nested-header compilation, 235 VirtIO requirements, and 110 VirtIO
private-interface entries without a finding.  This is rootless source/model
evidence only; the existing Intel, Linux, 5BSD, checkpoint, and soak commands
remain the release-qualification gate.

## Nested execution/startup-owner boundary replay (2026-08-09)

The common `vm_run()` startup-owner protocol and the Intel VMCS02 execution
path were re-traced together, including each early nested return, hardware
entry attempt, unwind, hot-exit freeze, cold continuation, INIT preflight,
and vCPU teardown path.  There is one deliberately unavailable combination:
a kernel-owned startup-entry owner and an L2 VMX entry.  `vmx_run_nested()`
accepts that owner only on the pre-hardware software-exit path; otherwise it
returns `EOPNOTSUPP` before guest MSRs, VMCS02 selection, EPT activation, or
L2 event ownership are touched.  This is intentional.  The common owner
transaction has not yet been composed with all residency-specific VMCS02
rollback/refreeze inverses, so treating an attempted L2 entry as a generic
commit, replay, or synthetic exit would be unsound.

The common caller closes this refused owner through
`vmm_startup_entry_owner_fail_before_entry()` before it returns.  Therefore
the restriction cannot strand a RUNNING or RECHECK token, leave guest FPU
state live, or make a later startup event observe ambiguous ownership.  The
unlinked `vmx_nested_owner_outcome.c` remains a value-model prerequisite and
is not imported into `vmm.ko`; linking it without one source-ordered runtime
transaction would weaken the fail-closed boundary.  The fresh nested model
gate rebuilt and exercised the owner and nested state tests successfully.

The reset and cleanup replay also found that Intel-specific VMCS02, EPT02,
VPID, TSC_AUX, and callback ownership stays in the Intel backend.  The common
event coordinator and startup-owner layer use backend operations rather than
Intel state.  The explicitly x86 startup-state helper retains the documented
Intel INIT CR0 rule, which is architecture-local rather than a portability
leak into common VirtIO or checkpoint state.  Real L2 entry under the
kernel-owned startup protocol remains a pending, root-only Intel live
qualification item; it must not be advertised or made default-on before the
complete runtime bridge and its Linux/5BSD L2 tests exist.

## Shared VirtIO snapshot callback replay (2026-08-09)

A separate callback-level replay traced the common checkpoint pause/resume
pair through SCSI, console, 9P, input, and both userspace and kernel-backed
vsock.  The shared transport acquires a device checkpoint owner only when a
complete pause/resume pair is supplied.  A pause failure unwinds the
administration fence before reopening queue admission; a resume failure keeps
the checkpoint owner intact for an exact retry; deferred configuration and
ready-queue notifications are replayed only after that owner has been
released.  These are common lifecycle guarantees, independent of the host
CPU architecture.

Each reviewed device obeys a deliberately narrow external-state rule.  SCSI
retains and later releases only the queues it parked; console rejects live host
connections rather than serializing them; 9P rejects active fids and requests;
input retains a bounded partial event frame while its event source is disabled;
and vsock stops every readiness source before capture, re-creates a
destination-local kernel-provider feature epoch while frozen, and re-enables
sources only after the common queue fence opens.  No callback was found to
publish restored state before its device-local ownership boundary is held.

The independent snapshot model passed 30 cases.  The complete rootless device
harness then passed both execution lanes (659 and 505 checks, respectively),
including requirement, portability, DMA, lifecycle, negative-request, and
private-interface guards.  This validates host-model contracts only.  The
feature activation ledger continues to distinguish those results from the
pending Linux/5BSD packed-ring, active-I/O checkpoint, and long-run live gates.

## Packed completion wrap-generation replay (2026-08-09)

A focused shared-core replay separated the one legitimate packed completion
gap from corrupted reorder state.  A missing completion at the device-owned
used cursor is expected when a later asynchronous request finishes first, and
the publisher leaves that gap pending until its head arrives.  In contrast, a
valid staged completion at that cursor carrying the opposite wrap generation
cannot denote a later request: the protocol admits at most one ring traversal
of outstanding ownership.  Treating both states as a silent gap could leave
used-ring progress permanently stalled after an internal completion-state
violation.

The publisher now preserves ordinary out-of-order deferral only for an absent
head and raises `NEEDS_RESET` for a present opposite-generation head.  The
core regression directly stages that impossible state behind an otherwise
valid later completion and proves that no silent stall is retained.  The full
ASan/UBSan device harness passed 659 checks after the correction.  This is a
host-side defensive ownership repair; live packed-ring qualification remains
separately required for every advertised device and guest family.

## Packed reset lease-metadata replay (2026-08-09)

The reset replay then examined the asynchronous packed completion cache at a
generation transition.  A callback retained across reset needs exactly one
piece of cache state: its atomic ownership lease, which lets its
generation-fenced token retire once.  Request identity, completion length,
group links, wrap annotation, and `valid` are all represented by that token
or by the retired queue incarnation and must not survive as cache metadata.

The reset helper previously described that narrow contract but left every
field intact for a nonzero lease.  It now clears only the non-atomic metadata
without touching `owner_state`, avoiding both stale admission state and a race
that could revive a lease while a late callback consumes it.  The regression
injects stale completion data alongside a retained owner, resets the queue,
then proves the callback can retire normally and the cache becomes reusable.
Both ASan/UBSan harness lanes passed (659 and 509 checks), followed by a
warnings-as-errors bhyve rebuild.  This correction preserves the existing
generation-fenced late-completion contract; it does not relax checkpoint's
requirement that real outstanding requests drain before capture.

## Current-only unreleased state formats (2026-08-10)

The unreleased WASPNest checkpoint and private-control formats now accept only
their current encoding.  Compatibility readers for superseded balloon, GPU,
RTC, memory, common VirtIO, modern PCI transport, input, network, block,
manifest, nested-VMX, and virtiofsd session records were removed.  The legacy
vsock provider feature ioctl was also removed instead of retaining two private
control ABIs.  Restore tests now assert that each obsolete encoding is rejected
before destination state is published.

Earlier dated entries in this review journal that describe those obsolete
records as readable or importable are historical and are superseded by this
section.  A first and sole encoding whose numeric field is 1 has no fallback
reader and therefore is not version-1 compatibility support.  Renumbering that
same byte layout would only create a different label for the same current
contract.  The policy also does not remove standards-defined
`VIRTIO_F_VERSION_1`, ACPI VIOT format version 1, the VirtIO legacy PCI/MMIO
transports, or FreeBSD ABIs that predate this unreleased project.  Those are
standards or already-shipped interfaces rather than compatibility decoders for
superseded WASPNest formats.

The source validator now scans every private format that has advanced beyond
its first development encoding and rejects generic legacy/V1 decoder symbols,
V1-specific decode entry points, and explicit `version == 1` acceptance.  This
prevents a renamed compatibility branch from bypassing the original
symbol-specific checks.  The unreleased startup-management and generation-run
ABIs likewise expose only `VERSION` and `SIZE` for their exact-current
contract; the former `_VERSION_1` and `_SIZE_1` spellings were removed so no
public name implies a selectable historical generation.

The stricter follow-up also removed compatibility bytes which survived after
their readers were deleted.  The sole current 9P image is now `V9P2`; it omits
the ignored source request-generation field and accepts no `V9P1` record.  The
modern common queue image likewise no longer carries a source queue generation.
Both generations are destination-local ownership epochs advanced only after a
complete successful restore.  The source gate rejects either wire slot if it is
reintroduced.  First-and-only numeric version fields elsewhere remain current
schema discriminators, not alternate V1 decoders; standards-defined
`VIRTIO_F_VERSION_1` remains the required modern VirtIO feature bit.

The restore coordinator was subsequently checked independently of the
device-private codecs.  It still admitted the pre-contract metadata shape when
CPU topology, NUMA placement, memory geometry, CPU execution contract, global
device compatibility, or the whole-machine topology seal was wholly absent.
Those fallbacks are now removed: every field emitted by the sole current
writer is mandatory, direct helper calls fail closed on absence, and device
validation and commit both require the exact current compatibility schema.
The requirements validator mechanically rejects reintroducing either an
`ENOENT` metadata path or a caller that treats it as success.  The updated
portability gate, full requirements validator, and warnings-as-errors bhyve
build pass.

## Checkpoint-session copyout ambiguity replay (2026-08-11)

The post-V1 cleanup review re-traced the descriptor-owned checkpoint session
through BEGIN, COMMIT, ABORT, publication failure, and destination restore.
It found that `vm_snapshot_session_release_exact()` recovered an ambiguous
COMMIT with an exact ABORT, but did not recover when that ABORT itself consumed
the owner and then failed its `_IOWR` copyout.  In that case the kernel owner
was gone while userspace retained `session_active`, permanently keeping a
source VM stopped even though exact release was already provable.

The release helper now retries the same idempotent exact ABORT once.  Success
releases an owner not consumed by the first attempt; `ESTALE` proves an earlier
attempt consumed the descriptor credential; every other outcome remains
unresolved and keeps execution stopped.  The installed-kernel ATF case uses a
read-only mapped ioctl buffer so copyin succeeds and copyout fails after both
BEGIN and ABORT mutate ownership, then proves `ABORT_CURRENT` and exact-ABORT
recovery respectively.  The nested requirements validator pins both the
second retry and the live fault-injection case.  Rootless compilation and
validators cover the implementation shape; running the new ATF case remains
an installed-kernel gate.

## Shared-memory checkpoint compatibility coverage (2026-08-11)

An exact reinspection corrected an earlier review artifact: the current
compatibility producer already encodes each shared-memory region as its ID,
BAR, 64-bit offset, and 64-bit length.  No production encoding correction was
needed.  The review did find that this variadic formatting boundary lacked
compiler format checking and that tests covered shared-memory transport state
without directly proving the diagnostic/preflight producer's field order.

The append helper is now `__printflike` checked.  A direct producer regression
uses two regions, including an offset above 4 GiB, asserts the complete exact
decimal encoding, changes offset and length independently, and rejects a
region count beyond the fixed registry.  The requirements gate pins both the
source field order and the independent fixture.  This is coverage hardening,
not a claim that the prior current-format encoder emitted corrupt state.

## Raw checkpoint fallback removal (2026-08-11)

The current-only format pass found one remaining coordinator-level fallback
outside the device-private decoders.  When the requested restore file did not
begin with a recognized manifest, `load_restore_file()` still treated it as
raw guest RAM and discovered adjacent `.kern` and `.meta` files.  That path
bypassed the current manifest's member digests, architecture and machine ABI,
and generation naming contract despite the ledger claiming version 3 was the
sole accepted publication.

The manifest parser now returns `ENOTSUP` for both recognized obsolete magic
and arbitrary non-manifest content.  The raw file-opening helpers and legacy
cleanup branch were removed, restore requires an existing current manifest,
and checkpoint creation refuses to replace a raw old layout.  A direct
directory-relative regression proves that all three plausible raw files are
rejected without changing the caller's candidate manifest.  The source gate
rejects reintroducing either the raw loaders or a restore path that does not
require `exists && is_manifest`.

## Final current-only VIMS cleanup (2026-08-11)

The repository-wide current-format replay found one remaining compatibility
behavior in the first and sole VirtIO-IOMMU state encoding.  Its writer emitted
a zero destination-local generation slot and canonical endpoint, domain, and
mapping order, but its reader accepted a nonzero slot and silently sorted
insertion-ordered mappings.  Those inputs could only have come from obsolete
development writers.

Restore now requires the reserved generation slot to be zero and all three
variable record classes to be strictly canonical before publication.  Mapping
overlap is then rejected by one adjacent scan without a compatibility sort.
The regression independently rewrites the generation slot and swaps endpoint,
domain, and mapping records, recomputes the integrity value, and proves every
form is rejected without changing live state.  The focused ATF program passes
21/21 cases; the complete requirements and private-interface validators pass,
and the installed manual now documents that only the current manifest is
accepted.

## Shared virtqueue ownership and packed reorder replay (2026-08-11)

The next common-core pass traced every request token from descriptor claim
through grouped asynchronous completion, reset, DMA-domain retirement, and
packed publication.  It found two fail-closed paths which quarantined the
device but did not finish retiring host-owned transient state.

First, an oversized completion group was rejected before the function consumed
the independently acquired owner lease for each request.  That could leave
split owner bytes or packed owner states permanently claimed even after
`NEEDS_RESET`, preventing a later queue reset from completing.  Group
completion now consumes every supplied owner token before validating group
cardinality; invalid publication still fails closed, but every DMA and queue
ownership lease is retired exactly once.

Second, the packed reorder flush silently returned when a staged multi-request
group contained an invalid follower.  A missing follower is not an ordinary
out-of-order completion: staging is atomic and all group members are installed
together.  Returning without poisoning the device left the valid head at the
used cursor permanently blocked.  The flush now publishes `NEEDS_RESET` for a
missing, wrong-wrap, zero-length, or oversized staged follower.

Independent split and packed regressions cover the oversized group, and a
packed regression corrupts a staged follower behind an earlier completion gap
before advancing the used cursor.  The complete common-core program passes
74/74 cases, the VirtIO requirements validator accepts 239 requirements and
695 independent oracle definitions, and the full warnings-as-errors bhyve
build succeeds.

## Configuration events across lifecycle quiesce (2026-08-11)

The device-lifecycle pass traced backend configuration changes through guest
suspend, checkpoint pause, failed-pause rollback, and final interrupt delivery.
Queue kicks were already fenced for the full `vs_quiescing` interval, but the
configuration-change helpers only deferred after the final suspended or
checkpoint-paused state had been published.  A backend callback which dropped
the device mutex could therefore report a resize or other configuration change
while pause was still in progress and inject an interrupt into a guest which
the lifecycle owner was actively stopping.

Both modern and legacy configuration-change paths now treat any quiesce owner
as a delivery fence.  A failed checkpoint pause clears that owner and replays a
coalesced configuration event before replaying deferred queue notifications;
an administration rollback which fails remains quarantined behind
`DEVICE_NEEDS_RESET` and retains both classes of deferred state for reset.

The modern transport regression enters quiesce directly and proves that the
common and transport-local latches are set without MSI/MSI-X delivery, then
proves one coalesced interrupt after the fence opens.  The common-core
regression injects both a queue kick and configuration event from a failing
pause callback and proves exact-once replay.  The complete common and modern
programs pass 74/74 and 36/36 cases respectively.

## Unreleased V1 compatibility namespace removal (2026-08-11)

The private-interface sweep removed the remaining `local-v1` backend identity
namespace and versioned test identities.  Block, network, persistent-memory,
and filesystem checkpoints now bind the sole current destination identity
without advertising an obsolete development namespace.

The same sweep found that the private virtio-fs backend hello still accepted
a version range containing its current protocol version.  Although the reply
path required one exact selection, the initiating session temporarily
published the offered maximum, including versions for which no codec exists.
The hello encoder and decoder now accept only an exact-current minimum and
maximum, and session state publishes the current constant rather than an
untrusted offered endpoint.  A negative test covers a range whose maximum is
newer than the current protocol.

The source validator now covers every project-added private state family,
rejects V1-specific decoder entry points or explicit obsolete acceptance, and
forbids reintroducing a `-v1` backend identity namespace.  Numeric revision 1
is retained only when it is the first and sole current encoding, or when the
value belongs to an external standard; relabeling unchanged bytes would not
remove compatibility behavior.  The standard mandatory
`VIRTIO_F_VERSION_1` feature remains unaffected.

## Virtio-mem nested lifetime admission (2026-08-11)

The virtio-mem ownership pass found that the configuration encoder admitted a
public host-model operation and then called the public configuration getter.
If destruction marked the object as destroying between those two admissions,
the nested getter returned without initializing its output while the outer
operation remained valid and encoded the uninitialized stack object.

The encoder now uses its existing lifetime admission and reads the complete
configuration through a private state helper.  Configuration-change callbacks
receive an immutable configuration snapshot instead of re-entering the public
API while destruction may be draining the outer operation; all callbacks are
now explicitly non-reentrant.  A source gate rejects a future reintroduction
of the nested public call.  The focused host-model and PCI device programs pass
13/13 cases each, including destroy/callback draining, configuration byte
order, request fragmentation, reset preservation, and snapshot validation.

## Virtio-RTC oversized request-buffer conformance (2026-08-11)

The request queue now passes only the bounded prefix actually copied into its
local decode buffer to the protocol decoder.  The original guest length remains
available for tracing, while additional device-readable bytes are ignored as
required by VirtIO 1.4 section 5.23.6.2.  This avoids describing nonexistent
stack storage to the decoder's alias checks and prevents valid oversized request
buffers from being mistaken for overlapping request/response storage.  The
transport-level regression suite exercises the oversized form directly; all 24
RTC host, alarm, and PCI cases pass.

## Virtio-sound RELEASE completion ordering (2026-08-11)

The sound lifecycle review found a nonblocking-backend case in which RELEASE
could drain an available prepared-output request, retain it on `EAGAIN`, and
then complete the control request with `IO_ERR` while that data request was
still outstanding.  VirtIO 1.4 section 5.14.6.6.5.1 forbids completing RELEASE
while any I/O request for that stream remains pending, independently of the
reported control status.

The release path now cancels and publishes that newly retained request before
failing any remaining available requests, invoking backend release, or
publishing the control completion.  The transport regression uses a stalling
backend with an available-but-not-yet-admitted output descriptor and verifies
data-before-control completion order, `IO_ERR` on the data request, successful
release, no retained asynchronous owner, and no descriptor visible to the
backend release callback.  All 52 sound host, asynchronous-owner, queue, and
PCI test cases pass.

## Virtio-fs malformed control-reply teardown (2026-08-11)

The connection lifecycle review found that a backend control reply carrying
the active request identifier but the wrong reply type was recorded as a
completed control error.  The backend session remained in `QUIESCING` or
`THAWING`, so checkpoint admission could remain fenced even though the
operation had returned an error.

Only a structurally valid backend refusal is now treated as a retryable
control result.  Protocol-shape and local-state errors propagate through the
terminal connection-failure path, which closes the backend descriptor and
drains all retained ownership.  The focused negative test proves the wrong
reply type returns `EPROTO`, leaves no pending or outgoing work, and cannot
remain active.  All 106 virtio-fs backend, framing, connection, queue, state,
PCI, server, and daemon cases pass, and bhyve rebuilds with its warning-as-error
policy.

## Virtio-GPU retained-state and evidence replay (2026-08-11)

The GPU pass traced every resource from create or blob import through backing
attachment, transfer, scanout/cursor publication, reset, snapshot validation,
restore, and destruction.  Command mutations stage complete DMA reads before
publishing pixels, the state mutex serializes resource ownership, callbacks
execute outside that mutex under an explicit destruction drain, and restore
validates the complete resource graph and destination DMA view before replacing
live state.  The apparently uninitialized malformed-command response was also
rechecked: the decoder intentionally publishes the validated common header
before command-specific rejection, and the negative queue test proves the
fenced error response.  No production correction was required in this pass.

The same review did find overstated traceability.  The ACCESS_PLATFORM ledger
named nonexistent GPU DMA-write and blob-read/write functions and described a
sparse GPU shared-memory BAR, although this 2D implementation consumes only
device-readable guest backing and deliberately seals the shared-memory
registry.  Those false source anchors and the read/write wording are removed.
The ledger now describes the actual validation/read lease contract and
explicitly records that no GPU shared-memory BAR is exposed.

## Requirements evidence integrity replay (2026-08-11)

The requirements validator now resolves every simple production
`file:symbol` anchor against the source tree.  This prevents a renamed,
removed, or invented identifier from remaining accepted as implementation
evidence merely because the surrounding row is syntactically valid.  The
